entries.name: What It Means…
entries.text:
You are a Guardian, a warrior forged in the Traveler's Light who has chosen to defend humanity. A beacon of hope in a universe constantly threatened by forces that would see it destroyed, or worse…

Chosen by the Traveler and raised from the dead by Ghosts, Guardians are part of the rare few able to wield paracausal abilities to manipulate the world around them. For centuries they have defended the City, but now they have extended their reach to Sol, protecting all who call this solar system home. 

Retake our lost worlds, forge unexpected alliances, and harness the power within yourself. The Guardians who lead the way will save humanity—and become legend.
entries.text_zh:
你是一名守护者，被旅行者的光能所选中、铸造出的人类卫士。一道在危机四伏的宇宙中四面受敌的希望之光…

被旅行者选中，被机灵复活，守护者是能够运用超因果能力，操纵周围世界的少数人群之一。几个世纪以来，他们一直在保卫圣城，但现在他们已经把影响延伸至整个太阳系，保护所有把这个星系当作家的人。 

夺回我们业已失去的世界，建立出乎意料的联盟，并运用藏在自己心中的力量。一马当先的守护者会拯救人类，成为传奇。

entries.name: A Guardian's Best Friend
entries.text:
Created by the Traveler's Light, Ghosts seek out their Guardian companions among the dead. The Ghost can be scout, librarian, and mechanic; ancient machinery guiding their Guardians forward. In the right situations, your Ghost can even save you from death.

But Ghosts are not immortal. As far as Guardians know, every loss is irreplaceable.
entries.text_zh:
机灵由旅行者的光能创造而生，它们会在死者当中寻找自己的守护者搭档。机灵可以充当斥候、文案管理员、机械师；指引守护者前行的古老机械。在某些情况下，机灵甚至能救你一命。

但机灵不是永生不灭的存在。据守护者们所知，每次失去都无可替代。

entries.name: The Traveler
entries.text:
Everything changed when the Traveler arrived in Sol.

It gave us gifts that transformed the solar system and the nature of human life. Moreover, it ushered in the Golden Age, a renaissance of scientific and cultural achievement. Despite all the good it has done for us, we still know nothing of the Traveler's origin or the reason it gifted Lightbearers with paracausal powers.
 
Unbeknownst to us, each of those miracles came at a price. Threats greater than we could have ever fathomed have found their way to our doorstep in pursuit of the Traveler.
entries.text_zh:
旅行者抵达太阳系时改变了一切。

它赠予了我们改变太阳系和人类生命本质的礼物。而且，它开启了黄金时代，一个科学和文化成就的复兴纪元。不过在它为我们贡献这么多之后，我们仍不知道旅行者的来源，以及它为何会赋予负光者超因果力量。
 
我们当时不知道，这些奇迹都是有代价的。为了追逐旅行者，远超我们想象的威胁已经近在咫尺。

entries.name: The Threats We Face
entries.text:
The arrival of the Traveler, for all the good it brought to Sol, painted a target on the entire system. Humanity has faced enemies from all corners of the universe: the Fallen, the Hive, the Scorn, the Vex, the Cabal, and the Taken, to name a few. 

While Guardians successfully fought off each onslaught, a greater enemy was revealed: the Witness. A mysterious voice in the Darkness that led our enemies to our solar system and the Traveler. Though the Witness was cloaked in mystery, one thing was clear: it sought the destruction of the Traveler.
entries.text_zh:
旅行者的到来造福了太阳系，但也让整个星系成为了一个标靶。人类已经面对过来自宇宙各个角落的敌人：堕落者、邪魔族、嗤魅、Vex、卡巴尔、傀儡军团等等。 

虽然守护者一次次地击退了猛攻，现在又有一个更强大的敌人现身了：见证者。一个将先前所有的敌人引到太阳系和旅行者的、来自黑暗中的神秘声音。虽然见证者的真身仍不明确，但有一件事可以确定：它要摧毁旅行者。

entries.name: The Leaders Who Guide Us
entries.text:
The Vanguard is the Last City's greatest defense and first line of offense when a threat presents itself. The organization is comprised of a long, storied line of elite Guardians with a leader chosen for each of the classes: Hunter, Titan, and Warlock.

Commander Zavala serves as Titan Vanguard. A force of nature, as unyielding as he is deadly. He has led the Guardians to victory in countless battles, and the moment a threat presents itself, the Last City looks to him as both a leader and a protector.
 
Ikora Rey serves as the Warlock Vanguard. An unmatched scholar, and one of the most formidable Warlocks in the history of the Last City. She oversees the Vanguard's intelligence network known as The Hidden.

Currently, the Hunter Vanguard position remains open. The title once belonged to Cayde-6, a Guardian as quick with a gun as he was with a joke. He met his final death after his Ghost was killed—a sobering reminder that even Guardians can be slain. A statue of him stands in the Tower to keep his memory alive.
entries.text_zh:
先锋是圣城最强大的防御力量，也是在威胁出现时的进攻矛头。该组织由一群具有传奇色彩的精英守护者组成，且三种职业（猎人，泰坦，术士）各选出一位领袖。

指挥官萨瓦拉是泰坦先锋。他犹如一股自然之力，永不退缩，无人能挡。他带领守护者们在无数次战斗中取得了胜利，当威胁出现之际，圣城仰赖他为领袖和卫士。
 
艾可拉·蕾伊是术士先锋。她是一位无与伦比的学者，也是“圣城”历史上最强大的术士之一。她还掌管着名为“隐秘者”的先锋情报网络。

当前，猎人先锋的位置仍然空着。这个位置原来属于一位名为凯德6号的守护者，他的枪法和他讲段子的水平一样精湛。在机灵被杀后，他也随之阵亡——他的遭遇警示着一个事实：就连守护者也不是无敌的。高塔中有一座为纪念他而立的雕像。

entries.name: The Friends We Made
entries.text:
Over the years, our relationship to both Light and Darkness has changed. The nuance of the universe has often been ignored by Humanity in favor of black-and-white boxes that make existence easier to grasp. Just as we have begun to open ourselves up to that nuance, so, too, have we begun to understand our former enemies and even forge alliances with them.

Most recently, both Empress Caiatl of the Cabal and Commander Zavala saw the threat of the Hive as larger than the differences between her people and ours. Similarly, a group of Fallen, known in their own language as Eliksni, have put aside the bad blood between our peoples to form the House of Light under the leadership of Mithrax, Kell of Light. They now live alongside us in the City and have become trusted allies.
entries.text_zh:
这些年来，我们与光能和暗影的关系都发生了转变。宇宙的细微变化常常被人类忽视；人类更倾向于容易掌握的，非黑即白的东西。我们已经开始接受这些细微变化，也已经开始理解我们曾经的敌人，甚至与他们结成联盟。

最近，卡巴尔的女帝查厄托和指挥官萨瓦拉就邪魔族的威胁达成了共识，决定既往不咎，结成盟友。同样，一群自称“埃里克斯尼族”的堕落者也决定不计前嫌，在光之凯尔米瑟拉克斯的领导下组成光能氏族。他们现在与我们一同居住在圣城里，是一群可以信赖的盟友。

entries.name: The Golden Age
entries.text:
The Traveler changed everything. It reshaped our solar system as decisively as it shattered our scientific and philosophical frameworks. To our ancestors it must have been a hammerblow—a glimpse beyond the horizon of expected possibility.

The Traveler kindled the Golden Age. But we built it. We remember this with pride, even after so much else has been lost. 

Today, Cryptarchs and scholars work to distill the legends of the Golden Age into truth. We know now that Humans lived longer, flew further, and learned faster. We know that countless ancient diseases and hatreds were extinguished forever. Human aspiration gave birth to vast engineering projects, sweeping social movements, and even new forms of life.

The Golden Age was not without challenges. But humanity and its machine children tackled these problems with pride, vigor, and a contagious sense of pluralist compassion.
entries.text_zh:
旅行者改变了一切。它完全重塑了我们的太阳系，就像它完全粉碎了我们的科学和哲学框架一样。对于我们的祖先来说，这件事肯定是当头一棒——这让他们瞥见了在预料可能性之外的东西。

旅行者开启了黄金时代。但建立这个时代的人是我们自己。虽然已经失去了许多，我们仍自豪地珍惜着这段历史。 

今天，解密大师和学者们在不懈地验证黄金时代传说的真伪。我们现在知道那时的人类寿命更长，走得更远，学习得也更快。我们知道无数的古代疾病和仇恨都永远消失了。人类的愿望催生了巨大的工程项目，席卷全球的社会运动，甚至是新的生命形式。

黄金时代并非毫无挑战。但人类及其机器子嗣以自豪、活力和具有感染力的多元主义仁爱解决了这些问题。

entries.name: The Collapse and The Dark Age
entries.text:
The Golden Age burned bright—and the night that overtook us after the Collapse was swift and total.

Incalculable waves of destruction ripped through Sol, decimating populations all around the system. If the stories are to be believed, this event marks the arrival of the Witness and its forces in their first attack on the Traveler. That day, the Traveler saved us from certain extinction.

The tally of suffering may be beyond comprehension. But in the following decades, the City lifted itself from the ash, gathering survivors. Guardians rose to challenge alien hordes. The Dark Age swallowed so much of our history… but hope never died.
entries.text_zh:
黄金时代光芒四射——而在大崩溃后，黑夜迅速而彻底地席卷了一切。

整个太阳系遭到了不可估量的破坏，人口急剧减少。如果传闻是真的，这一事件标志着“见证者”及其军队的到来，以及他们对旅行者发起的第一次攻击。那一天，旅行者将我们从被灭绝的命运中救了出来。

这种痛苦可能超越了理解的范围。但在接下来的几十年里，圣城从灰烬中振作起来，不断招揽幸存者。守护者死而复生，对抗外星入侵者。黑暗纪元吞噬了太多历史…但希望从未熄灭。

entries.name: The City Age
entries.text:
The Last City did not rise without struggle. Lightbearers, styling themselves as Warlords, and wilderness fiefdoms clung to power. Starvation, disease, and anarchy menaced. But this struggle brought about the rise of the Guardians and the formation of the Vanguard. The organization fought tirelessly to return some semblance of order to the people remaining on Earth. 

As the City learned to walk again, it found a world overrun by alien menace. It faced disaster and defeat in the Taken War and the Red War, outlasted multiple invasions, and was plunged into an Endless Night. If not for the work and sacrifice of the Vanguard, we would have lost it many times over.

The Last City is both a reminder of all that remains of Earth's civilization, and a commitment to our future. Repairs may come in small bursts, progress may feel slow, but humanity is nothing if not resilient.
entries.text_zh:
圣城的崛起并非一帆风顺。自立为战争领主的负光者，为了掌控权利而战的割据势力都是其阻碍。饥荒、疾病、无政府主义威胁着所有人。但这段斗争催生了守护者的崛起以及先锋的组建。这个组织为了将些许秩序带回给地球上的幸存者而不倦地战斗着。 

在圣城蹒跚学步的同时，人们发现这个世界已经被外星威胁占领了。这座城市挺过了在傀儡战争和猩红战争中的各种灾难和落败，撑过了数次入侵，还被施下了永夜的恶咒。要不是有先锋的努力和牺牲，我们早就失去这座城市不知多少次了。

圣城不仅代表着残留的地球文明，也是对我们未来的承诺。缺陷或许得一点点改，进展也许有些缓慢，但人类是坚韧不拨的。

entries.name: The Tower
entries.text:
As every Guardian knows, there are few dull moments in Sol, but any precious downtime is most often spent in the hangars and hallways of the Tower. Operating as a base of operations for the Vanguard, the Tower overlooks the Last City and the Traveler, serving as a watchful eye should any threats arise. 

As the seasons change, so, too, does the Tower. Guardians looking to partake in holiday events and festivals like, Guardian Games, Solstice, Festival of the Lost, and the Dawning, will find Eva Levante leading the celebrations with special activities and decorations galore!
entries.text_zh:
所有守护者都知道，太阳系里每天都有许多事发生，但珍贵的闲暇时间一般都是在高塔的机库和长廊里度过的。作为先锋的行动基地，高塔俯瞰着圣城和旅行者，时刻警惕着威胁。 

随着季节的更替，高塔也会随之变化。想参加各种节日活动和庆典，如守护者游戏、至日、英灵日和曙光节的守护者，会发现伊娃·莱万特正带着特殊活动和大量装饰品主持庆祝！

entries.name: Raids and Dungeons
entries.text:
As they grow into their powers and skills, Guardians often find themselves in need of a challenge. Should you wish to take your adventures to the next level, treacherous dungeons and powerful foes are the perfect way to test your mettle. 

A well-equipped fireteam of three may face difficult combatants and precarious environments as they make their way through a dungeon. Should they wish for an even bigger challenge, a fireteam of six Guardians can work together to take on Sol's biggest threats in a raid.
entries.text_zh:
随着力量和技巧不断提升，守护者经常发现自己需要更多挑战。如果你想让你的冒险更上一层楼，险恶的地牢和强力敌人是考验自身能力的最佳方式。 

在勇闯地牢时，一支装备精良的三人火力战队会面对强大的战斗人员和凶险的环境。如果希望体验更难的挑战，一支由六名守护者组成的火力战队可以在突袭中协力对抗太阳系的最大威胁。

entries.name: Unanswered Questions
entries.text:
There are many entities whose motivations remain shrouded by time and space and some that exist beyond our comprehension of reality. 

Perhaps the most well-known of these are the Hive gods: Savathûn, the Witch Queen; Xivu Arath, the God of War; and Oryx, the Taken King. While we defeated Oryx when he sought to destroy the Light, and Savathûn when she sought to take it from us, the Witch Queen's true fate remains uncertain. 

The Nine are another group of entities who inhabit this solar system. Very little is known about them outside of their unique writing styles. A mysterious agent of theirs, Xûr, visits well-known locations around Sol offering rare goods for sale.
entries.text_zh:
有许多动机仍然被时间和空间所掩藏的实体，还有一些存在于我们对现实的理解之外。 

这些实体里最广为人知的大概是这几位邪魔族之神：巫妖女王萨瓦图恩、战神希乌阿拉斯、邪神欧里克斯。虽然我们击败了试图摧毁光能的欧里克斯，也挫败了萨瓦图恩尝试偷走光能的企图，但巫妖女王的真实命运仍不为人知。 

“玖”则是另一群栖息在这个太阳系内的实体。除了他们独特的书写方式之外，我们对其一无所知。他们的代理人，仄，会前往太阳系各处的著名地点，贩卖各种珍品。

entries.name: Guiding Light
entries.text:
It takes considerable skill to master the greatest challenges in Sol, but it takes a very dedicated and patient Guardian to step up and lead others through these daunting tests. Every experienced Guardian was once a New Light. You may reminisce on your own first time in the deepest pits of the Moon; what advice would you give to yourself from those early days? Those who take the time to share their expertise are an invaluable part of the Guardian community. 

Becoming a leader isn't just about being "the best," it's about dedicating the time and effort to helping others become their best.
entries.text_zh:
克服太阳系中最艰险的挑战需要拥有精湛的技艺，只有无私奉献、富有耐心的守护者才会站出来，帮助他人通过这些艰巨的考验。每位身经百战的守护者都曾经是个新兵。你可能会回忆起你自己第一次落入月球深坑的经历；你会给刚刚踏入《命运》时的自己提供什么建议？正是有了这些肯花时间分享专长知识的人，才组成了弥足珍贵的守护者社区。 

成为领袖不只意味着成为“最强”，它还意味着付出时间和心血，帮助他人成为最优秀的自己。

entries.name: A Humble Thank You
entries.text:
Though the threats to our solar system may seem never-ending, know that your skill and power in defeating the greatest enemies in Sol, your experience in leading and mentoring others, and your efforts in creating a safer, kinder Sol haven't gone unnoticed. Congratulations, Guardian. May the songs of your deeds go down in history, and may the stars forever light your path.

Per Audacia Ad Astra!
entries.text_zh:
尽管太阳系面临的威胁看似永无止境，我们希望让你知道，你为击败恶敌、带领他人前行、创造一个更安全温良的太阳系所作出的努力并没有被忽视。恭喜你，守护者。愿你的事迹被载入史册，愿星光永远照亮你的道路。

无畏征途，终抵星辰！

entries.name: Grimoire: The City—Onslaught
entries.text:
"Our enemies never relent. Neither will you." —Lord Shaxx 

——————

Despite the sharp breeze in the Tower, the air in Shaxx's outpost is uncomfortably still and weighted with tension. There is work to do: personal feeling must not interfere when certain doom hangs over all their heads. 

"We can't afford to play defense. Not now." Shaxx stares fixedly at the training plans drawn up for his Guardians. 

"Then offense will have to see us through this fight. That should come naturally to you." Saladin's posture is Legionary-perfect. 

"Then that's that." Teeth gritted under his helmet, Shaxx folds his arms. After a long moment, he adds, "Good talk." 

Saladin nods. "Good talk." 

They look at the screen in silence. There is nobody to rescue them.
entries.text_zh:
“我们的敌人从不心慈手软。你们也不会。”——领主沙克斯 

——————

尽管高塔上微风拂面，沙克斯前哨站里的空气却静得瘆人，弥漫着紧张的气氛。还有工作必须去做：当厄运笼罩在所有人的头上时，这些工作绝对不能被个人的情感干扰。 

“我们不能光顾着防御。现在不行。”沙克斯目不转睛地凝视着为他的守护者们制定的训练计划。 

“那就只能靠进攻打完这场战斗了。这对你来说应该轻车熟路。”萨拉丁摆出的姿势堪称军团士兵的模范。 

“那就这么定了。”沙克斯把双臂交叉放在胸前，头盔下的牙齿咬得咯咯作响。过了好一会儿，他补充道，“聊得不错。” 

萨拉丁点点头。“聊得不错。” 

他们默默地看着屏幕。没有人会来拯救他们。

entries.name: Grimoire: Eris Morn—Hive God of Vengeance
entries.name_zh: 魔典：埃里斯·摩恩——邪魔族复仇之神
entries.text:
Eris, tenacious Eris. Crota's Bane, Oryx's Sorrow. Ruin of Xivu Arath.  

To see you reduced once again to a minion of the Awoken queen. Examining a locked gate for signs of weakness. Rattling the bars to the afterlife, when you might have kicked the door in! 

This very plane could have been yours. 

What you lacked in natural talent you fashioned from scholarly genius. Your will is the thing, and I mistook yours. How you burned with it! The noble vindication of victory.  

Every sword ever raised against you—can I say, against us? Down through the long years of history. Vengeance killed Oryx, why not his sibling?  

But you threw the match. What good is a mortal blow, half-delivered? You whet your blade and threw it down. The throne of war, abandoned. A thousand, thousand races fed that glorious polyp. All that hard-won evidence. You didn't even look at it.  

I could have guided you. Don't you see that? 

What will you do now? Kick down their banners? Hope for vengeance without bloodshed? And through what realms have you stamped the proof of your cause?  

…I, too, avenged? Why would I want that?  

Wait. Come back.
entries.text_zh:
埃里斯，顽强的埃里斯。克洛塔的克星，欧里克斯之哀。希乌阿拉斯的毁灭者。  

你又沦为了觉醒者女王的爪牙。检查上锁的大门是否有弱点。拉扯通往来世的栅栏。而你本来可以一脚把门踹开的！ 

这个位面本来可以属于你。 

你用学术方面的天才弥补了欠缺的天赋。我误判了你的意志，而它正是关键所在。瞧你用它燃烧自己的样子！那正是胜利的崇高证明。  

每把曾对你举起的刀剑——或者该说，曾对我们举起的刀剑？在漫长的历史中徐徐落下。复仇杀死了欧里克斯，为何不把他的妹妹也杀死？  

但你放弃了比赛。半途而废的致死攻击有什么用？你磨好了你的剑，却将它扔到一边。战争王座，遭你遗弃。无数的种族育成了嘴里的那块光辉息肉。所有来之不易的证据。你看都没看一眼。  

我本可以指引你的。难道你不明白吗？ 

你现在要做什么？踢倒他们的旗帜？希望不流血就能复仇？你又通过什么领域盖上了你事业的印证？  

…我也大仇得报？为什么我会想要那样？  

等等。回来。

entries.name: Grimoire: The Ironwood Tree
entries.text:
"Not much sense memorializing anybody during the Dark Age. Anyone worth remembering, you'd hang onto them without trying."  

Drifter crouches down in front of the Ironwood tree, mindful of the offerings littering the ground. The amulet's nothing fancy—not one of those Iron Lord tokens—but handmade, and with some care. Joxer's name is easy to read. Crisp lettering. 

"Dumb heroics will get you every time. Volunteering. First one through, so the rest of us know not to try it." Drifter smirks. "He'd have had a fighting chance against a Primeval. Big payout if he made it. Cleaner death if he didn't." 

Lord Shaxx shifts his weight. His helmet cants toward the Drifter. 

"But then you wouldn't be standing there."  

There's no reply.
entries.text_zh:
“在黑暗纪元，纪念任何人都没有意义。任何值得纪念的人，你自然会牢牢记住。”  

浪客在铁木树前蹲下，注意着散落一地的祭品。这个护身符并不华丽——不是钢铁领主的信物——但却是某人用心手工制做的。乔科斯的名字刻得非常清晰，易于辨识。 

“愚蠢的英雄主义害人啊。自告奋勇。率先赴死，让其他人知道此路不通。”浪客假笑起来。“他本来有机会与古昧战斗。要是赢了就能得到大笔报酬。就算输了也能死个痛快。” 

领主沙克斯挪了挪重心。他的头盔向浪客那边倾斜了一下。 

“那样的话，你现在就不会站在那里了。”  

浪客没有回答。

entries.name: Grimoire: BRAVE Arsenal
entries.text:
Lord Shaxx? Oh, he's quite a craftsman. But then of course, he's a survivor—like us. 

He loves rewarding his pupils. With praise and, at times, with something more material. He invests great care in his designs. Still, sometimes a weapon has an unexpected kick. A side effect. He locks these away for special occasions. Other times, the Vanguard intervenes—you never know where you'll find the next Ghost-killer. 

But outside the Crucible, the rules of engagement shift. There's no sense in leaving perfectly good armaments in storage. 

Don't worry, Namrask. I do not intend to abandon the Loom. I am merely… consulting. 

I am surprised Lord Shaxx let Drifter contribute. His aptitude is not in question, but I thought— 

What? Oh, yes. 

Low-level radiation is to be expected.
entries.text_zh:
领主沙克斯？哦，他是个能工巧匠。不过他也和我们一样，是个幸存者。 

他喜欢奖励他的学生。说些表扬的话，有时则用更加物质的东西。他的设计非常用心。但是，有时一件武器会有意想不到的效果。副作用。他会将其封存，以备不时之需。有时先锋会介入——你永远不会知道下一个机灵杀手会出现在哪里。 

但在熔炉竞技场外面，交战规则会变。把好端端的武器留在仓库里根本没意义。 

别担心，拿姆拉斯克。我不打算放弃纺织机。我只是…在咨询。 

我很惊讶领主沙克斯允许浪客帮忙。浪客的能力没问题，但我以为—— 

什么？哦，对。 

预计会有低水平辐射。

entries.name: Article: Down on the Farm
entries.text:
By Ember Hadad, Senior Editor at the City Herald 

Readers might be forgiven for imagining that, after having been captured by Shadow Legion forces, EDZ residents might consider relocating to the Last City.  

I took a trip out to the famed settlement known as The Farm to talk to the civilians and FOTC officers still stubbornly posted at the edges of the world.  

"We're not fighting for one city. We're fighting for humanity," says Baishan, one of the Farm's technicians. Baishan is charged with maintaining the Farm's few precious remaining generators—and, more recently, its Ether processors. "This is our world, and we're going to keep staking a claim."  

Naomi, a pilot with Forces of the City, has been overseeing regular supply runs to the Farm in the wake of fierce bombardment by the Shadow Legion. She sees this as par for the course. 

"Humans are good at adapting to just about anything," she observes.  

For many, the true revelations have come as a result of continued cooperation with new Eliksni neighbors.  

Long-time Farm resident Carol notes, "There's a lot about Fallen tech we couldn't have guessed at. With Skiris and Riksor helping out, we've cobbled together our own solar cell network. Our energy output is five times what it used to be. The first step toward long-term projects is getting out of starvation mode." 

And the people here do think long-term. Few of the people I interviewed seemed to have much interest in returning to the safety of the city walls.  

"The Witness tore down our cities, blighted our air and water, and sent raiders and monsters after us. We're still here, waiting for the first chance we get to take it all back. The way I see it, those of us here on the Farm are just getting a head start."
entries.text_zh:
圣城使者高级编辑恩蓓尔·哈达著 

读者们完全有理由认为，被暗影军团占领后，欧洲无人区的居民可能会考虑搬迁到圣城。  

我前往被称为“农庄”的著名定居点，采访了仍顽固驻守在世界边缘的平民和圣城防卫军的军官。  

“我们不是为一座城市而战。我们是在为人类而战，”白山如此说道。他是农庄的一名技术人员，负责维护农庄仅剩的几台珍贵的发电机——以及，最近新增的乙太处理器。“这里是我们的世界，而我们会坚持宣示我们的所有权。”  

内奥米是圣城防卫军的一名飞行员，她一直在冒着暗影军团的猛烈轰炸监督农庄的定期补给运输。她认为这是理所当然的。 

“人类擅长适应任何情况，”她做出了这样的评述。  

对许多人来说，真正的启示来自与埃里克斯尼族的新邻居们的持续合作。  

农庄的老住户卡罗指出，“堕落者的科技之中藏着许多我们无法想象的东西。借助丝吉利斯和瑞克索的帮助，我们拼凑出了自己的太阳能电池网络。我们的能量输出是以前的五倍。实现长期项目的第一步是解决温饱问题。” 

这里的人们确实考虑得很长远。我采访到的那些人似乎都对回到安全的城墙内不感兴趣。  

“见证者拆毁了我们的城市，污染了我们的空气和水，派出突袭者和怪物追杀我们。但我们还在这里，等待机会好夺回一切。在我看来，我们这些住在农庄的人只是走在了前面。”

entries.name: Grimoire: Enemies—Reaver Vandal
entries.text:
"Death is the great mystery to us all." —Master Rahool 

——————

The question of Eliksni mortality is often discussed amongst members of the Cryptarchy. Stories of Eliksni arising in full health from a death or near-death state—as Mithrax did, some say—abound.  

The Reaver of Old Russia is attested to in dozens of Vanguard records. Experienced Guardians will swear on their Ghosts that they once killed a Reaver Vandal who was uncannily strong for his size, only to see him alive and well again the next day. They have given him a nickname, perhaps as a show of respect for another being seemingly immune to death.
entries.text_zh:
“死亡对我们所有人来说都是一个巨大的谜团。”——拉乎尔大师 

——————

解密大师们经常讨论关于埃里克斯尼族寿命的问题。埃里克斯尼族从死亡或濒死状态中满血复活的故事比比皆是——有些人说米瑟拉克斯就是个例证。  

在数十个先锋记录中都有记载旧俄罗斯的掠夺者。经验丰富的守护者会以他们的机灵起誓，他们曾经杀死过一个就其体型而言强壮得难以置信的掠夺者暴徒，而在第二天又看到他活蹦乱跳。他们给他起了一个绰号，也许是借此向另一种看似对死亡免疫的生物致敬。

entries.name: Article: A Darker Hour? Looking Back at the Great Disaster
entries.name_zh: 文章：一个更黑暗的时刻？回顾大灾难
entries.text:
By Emmanuil Utkin, Staff Writer for the City Herald 

Several lifetimes have passed since the Vanguard suffered a blow from which many felt it might never recover. For the Lightless among us, the Great Disaster has become a fable: a story of monsters and tragic heroes encompassing the worst the universe can bring to bear.  

For many of the City's Guardians, however, the events of that time are not simply part of the historical record, but personal memory.  

"I'd never seen anything like it," Odon Kolos says. "That army the Vanguard put together…" 

Emboldened by initial victory against the Hive at the site of Burning Lake, the Vanguard and Consensus ordered a full-scale assault on the Moon. An army of Guardians thousands-strong marched against entrenched Hive forces—only to fall by the hundreds to a single Hive champion.  

Odon was one of the lucky Guardians who managed to reach a transport before the Moon was abandoned in the retreat.  

"Turns out immortal doesn't mean invincible," Odon observes. "Just means you stand a better chance of living with your mistakes."  

The Disaster spelled the beginning and the end for the Vanguard's military prospects. Any hope of formally organizing the City's Lightbearers dissipated. Contemporary records show that many felt the Guardian population soon became ungovernable—even disloyal—in the wake of the Vanguard's failure.  

But events in recent years suggest that Guardians do not require loyalty to a military command to compel them to place themselves in danger on behalf of the City. Whether driven by hope for humanity or a desire for wealth, Guardians have continued to face off against increasingly dire threats.  

"I used to run with Future War Cult," Odon tells me. "I guess I started to think… maybe we win the little fights, but we're never going to do anything about the real enemies out there. That war will always be waiting."  

He laughs. "And then someone comes along and kicks Crota's teeth in."
entries.text_zh:
圣城使者撰稿人伊曼奴依·乌特金著 

几个世代以前，先锋遭受了重大打击，许多人认为它再也不能恢复过来。对我们当中的无光者而言，大灾难已经成为了一则寓言：那是一个关于怪物和悲剧英雄的故事，对宇宙来说太过沉重。  

然而，对于许多圣城的守护者而言，当时发生的事件不仅仅是历史记录，更是其个人记忆的一部分。  

“我从没见过那种场面，”奥登·科洛斯说。“先锋组建的那支军队…” 

在燃烧之湖取得对抗邪魔族的初步胜利之后，受到鼓舞的先锋和元老院下令向月球发起总攻。一支由数千名守护者组成的军队向据守的邪魔族部队发起远征——结果却被一名邪魔族勇士屠戮殆尽。  

奥登是在月球被抛弃之前登上了运输船的幸运守护者之一。  

“事实证明，永生并不意味着无敌，”奥登做出了这样的评述。“它只是意味着你更有可能带着错误活下去。”  

大灾难标志着先锋作为一支军队的开端和终结。任何正式整组圣城负光者的希望都随之烟消云散。当代记录显示，先锋失败后，许多人认为守护者很快就变得难以管理——甚至心生叛意。  

但近年来发生的事件表明，守护者并不需要效忠于一个军事指挥部来驱使他们为了圣城而涉险。不管是出于对人类的希望还是对财富的渴望，守护者都在不断直面着日益严峻的威胁。  

“我曾经隶属于未来战争狂热者，”奥登告诉我。“我猜我开始觉得…也许我们赢得了小打小闹，但我们永远无法应对外面真正的敌人。觉得总有战争在等着我们。”  

他笑了。“然后，有个人跑来踢飞了克洛塔的牙齿。”

entries.name: Article: United in Hope—Our Neighbors in Neomuna
entries.name_zh: 文章：在希望中团结——我们在内欧姆那的邻居
entries.text:
By Emmanuil Utkin, Staff Writer at the City Herald 

Confirmation of a Human settlement on Neptune was only one of several shocking revelations over the course of recent years. Its discovery marks a sea change in our collective access to Golden Age information and technology long thought to be lost. Perhaps more importantly, it heralds potential reconnection with the rest of our people. Who are these Neomuni? Are they anything like us?   

Real-time communication between Neomuna and Earth is still stymied by the logistics of crossing enemy lines, in addition to Neomuna's communications restrictions. Data transmissions from Neomuna are strictly controlled and scrutinized for Vex corruption. Therefore, Vanguard sources provided assistance contacting Neomuni citizens; we asked willing individuals to share their perspectives on the possibilities of a long-awaited reunion with Earth. 

Despite the dangers, many Neomuna denizens are optimistic about the curtain coming down some day in the future. A brief selection of their thoughts follows: 

"I don't know how things would have shaken out if we'd stayed on Earth. Maybe we wouldn't have the CloudArk or nanotechnology. But if we make it through this fight with the Witness, I think it's only fair we send over, you know, what we have on food production, terraforming… There's a whole planet to reclaim."  

"I'd love to read some new Earth literature. I always assumed that the stories we managed to bring with us were going to be the last of their kind. Does anyone over there like detective stories?" 

"It's been interesting to see the Guardians at work. Is everyone on Earth like that? Going at Mach 12 all the time?"  

Stay tuned for continued coverage, including a guest feature from Neomuna's very own Jisu Calerondo!
entries.text_zh:
圣城使者撰稿人伊曼奴依·乌特金著 

确认海王星上有人类定居点只是近年来的几大震惊发现之一。长期以来，黄金时代信息和技术一直被认为已经失传，而这个发现标志着我们在此方面迎来了巨大的变化。也许更为重要的是，这预示着我们可能会与其他人类重新建立起联系。这些内欧姆那人是谁？他们和我们一样吗？   

内欧姆那和地球的实时通讯仍然受制于跨越敌方前线的后勤问题，此外还受到了内欧姆那通讯限制的影响。来自内欧姆那的传输数据仍受到严格封锁，并需检查Vex污染。因此，先锋方面协助联系了内欧姆那的居民；我们向许多乐意分享见解的居民询问了他们对与地球最终重聚的可能性的看法。 

尽管危机重重，许多内欧姆那居民仍保持乐观，觉得问题有朝一日会得到解决。以下精选了他们的部分看法： 

“我不知道如果我们当时留在地球，结果会怎样。也许我们就不会有云端方舟或纳米技术。但如果我们能挺过这场与见证者的战斗，我认为我们理应把我们在食物生产、地球化方面的技术送过去…那里有一整个星球等着我们去开垦。”  

“我很想读一些新的地球文学作品。我一直以为，我们当时设法带走的文学作品将是绝唱。那边有人喜欢侦探小说吗？” 

“看守护者工作很有趣。地球上的人都是那样吗？一直以12马赫的速度到处穿梭？”  

请继续关注后续报道，包括内欧姆那的吉舒·卡莱隆多的特邀专题！

entries.name: Article: Hot Off the Shelf
entries.text:
By Ember Hadad, Senior Editor at the City Herald 

My new friend is an unassuming young man in a torn flight jacket, still coated in a fine layer of dust. His Ghost, Rivet, is looking impressively smug for a small metal being.  

"They told me I'd never find my Guardian," Rivet tells me. "That I should try my luck with the Hive! But look at him. He's beautiful!"  

Like all Risen, Rivet's beautiful new Guardian has no memory of who he was, where he is, or what his purpose might be. But he nods agreeably when Rivet explains to him that Guardians protect the Last City.  

"I'm here to fight Fallen and Cabal," the Guardian says proudly. "But only the mean ones."  

"He's still figuring a few details out," Rivet says. 

It's been a very eventful past few years in the Sol system. I ask Rivet: At this point in time, how does a Ghost go about getting their new Guardian up to speed?  

"Well, you start by warning them about what threats we'll be facing in the field, right? I haven't… really gotten into the part about the end of the world just yet, though." 

Rivet's Guardian looks confused. "The world is ending?"  

Vanguard Operative Shaw Han, my escort through the Cosmodrome and local shepherd of those he calls New Lights, has similar advice.  

"It helps to focus on the basics. Let them test out their Light, learn what they're capable of. The details can come later." 

Even now?  

"Yep. Once they've got a handle on the little things, saving the world comes naturally."
entries.text_zh:
圣城使者高级编辑恩蓓尔·哈达著 

我的新朋友是一个其貌不扬的年轻人，穿着一件破旧的飞行夹克，上面还蒙着一层细细的灰尘。他的机灵，瑞威特，身为一个小小的金属生物倒是相当得意。  

“他们说我永远找不到我的守护者，”瑞威特告诉我。“说我应该去邪魔族那边试试运气！但你瞧瞧他。他真漂亮！”  

和所有复生者一样，瑞威特漂亮的新守护者不记得他是谁，他在哪里，或他的使命是什么。但当瑞威特向他解释守护者要保护圣城时，他赞同地点了头。  

“我是来对抗堕落者和卡巴尔的，”这名守护者骄傲地说。“但只是那些坏的堕落者和卡巴尔。”  

“他还在琢磨一些细节，”瑞威特说。 

过去的几年中，太阳系里事件频发。于是我就问瑞威特：在这种时候，机灵要如何让自己的新守护者了解当前的情况？  

“嗯，你首先要警告他们，我们在战场上会面临哪些威胁，对吧？不过我还没有…跟他说世界末日的事。” 

瑞威特的守护者看起来很困惑。“世界要迎来末日了？”  

先锋特工韩潇是我在发射基地的护卫和新兵守护者的本地导师，他也有类似的建议。  

“这能帮助他们专注于基本。让他们测试自己的光能，了解自己的能力。细节可以留到以后再说。” 

即使是现在？  

“对。等他们弄清了那些小事，自然就会想去拯救世界。”

entries.name: Article: A Consensus for the Rest of Us
entries.name_zh: 文章：我们其他人的元老院
entries.text:
By Leia Terazzas, Political Correspondent at the City Herald 

Chibuike Otieno, Perica Kosar, Argus McKowen—if there is anything the current slate of Consensus hopefuls have in common, it's that they offer a very different kind of representation for the mortal population of the Last City.  

Raucous political gatherings have become a staple of the City's night-life in recent months, with potential candidates vying for the chance to make their case for candidacy in the City's parks and public squares. Chief among their demands is the urgent restoration of fair representation to the City's government. Notably absent are the old trappings of long-established faction loyalties.   

"This [move away from Guardian-driven factions] speaks to a more mortal-centric framing," claims Dina Palomo, one of several enthusiastic volunteers campaigning on behalf of McKowen. "We know the Vanguard can handle the long view. But we need the short-term perspective as well as the immortal one." 

Warlock Vanguard Ikora Rey has repeatedly pledged to restore the Consensus, promising to hold civilian elections once the immediate threat is over. Not everyone is content to wait.  

"How many citizens were exiled from the City because they got on Executor Hideo's bad side?" asks one local. "I mean, how many Guardians got the boot because they wanted Guardians ruling the City? Isn't that what we have now? If things are so desperate, why don't we invite some of our people back home?"  

Others call the excitement over elections premature.  

"If we lose the war, I'm pretty sure none of us are going to be alive to do any voting." 

It is difficult to argue the point that election turnout might be poor under the current circumstances. But if the Lightless members of our community are to have a voice in the future, it's clear that there are those ready and eager to speak.
entries.text_zh:
圣城使者政治记者莱雅·特拉扎斯著 

奇布伊克·奥蒂埃诺、佩里卡·科萨、阿格斯·麦考文——如果说目前的元老院候选人名单有什么共同点的话，那就是他们都力求以一种截然不同的方式去代表圣城的凡人。  

近几个月来，喧闹的政治集会已成为圣城夜生活的主旋律，潜在的候选人们争相在圣城的公园和广场上进行竞选宣传。他们的主要诉求是紧急恢复市政府的公平代表性。值得注意的是，长期以来形成的象征派别忠诚的旧标识已不复存在。   

“这样[远离守护者驱动的派别]才更适合以凡人为中心的框架，”迪娜·帕洛莫这样说道，她是一名宣扬麦考文的政治观点的热情志愿者。“我们知道先锋可以从长远角度考虑问题。但除了永生者的考量，我们还需要短期的视角。” 

术士先锋艾可拉·蕾伊一再保证会恢复元老院，并承诺一旦眼前的威胁结束，就举行平民选举。但并非所有人都愿意等待。  

“有多少市民因为招惹了执行者秀夫而被流放出圣城？”一名居民问道。“我是说，有多少守护者因为希望守护者统治圣城而被驱逐？我们现在不就是那样吗？如果事态如此绝望，为什么不邀请一些我们的人回家？”  

也有人觉得热衷选举还为时过早。  

“如果我们输掉了战争，我敢说我们都没法活着去投票。” 

在目前的情况下，选举的投票率应该会很低。这一点难以辩驳。但如果说我们社区中的无光者将来会拥有发言权，显然他们中的有些人已经准备好了发言，并渴望发言。

entries.name: Grimoire: Allies—Eliksni
entries.name_zh: 魔典：盟友——埃里克斯尼族
entries.text:
"We have found the Great Machine." —Mithrax, after Chelchis

——————

Known on Earth for centuries as the Fallen, the Eliksni are four-armed beings from the planet Riis. They fled their home after the Traveler's departure caused a planet-wide calamity called the Whirlwind. While many Eliksni remain steadfast enemies of the Last City, others have joined as our allies and neighbors, most notably the House of Light and their leader, Mithrax. 

Eliksni rely on the inhalation of Ether to survive and grow. Processed from organic materials and energy by Servitors, Ether is highly combustible. As such, any leaks in City tanks are to be immediately reported through emergency channels.
entries.text_zh:
“我们找到了大机器。”——米瑟拉克斯，切尔奇斯之后

——————

几个世纪以来，埃里克斯尼族在地球上被称为“堕落者”。他们是来自里斯星的四臂生物，因旅行者的离去在那里引发了一场名为“旋风”的全球灾难而逃离家园。尽管许多埃里克斯尼族仍是圣城的死敌，但也有一些已经加入我们，成为了我们的盟友和邻居，其中最著名的是光能氏族及其领袖米瑟拉克斯。 

埃里克斯尼族靠吸入乙太来生存和成长。乙太是一种通过魔眼从有机材料和能量中提取出的易燃物质。因此，圣城中的任何乙太罐泄漏都应立即通过紧急渠道报告。

entries.name: Allies: Tower—Empress Caiatl
entries.text:
"We eat the mountains. We drink the seas." 

——————

The former emperor, Calus, lived for joy, rejecting his empire's long military tradition. His sole heir, and a member of the coup that overthrew him, the Empress Caiatl makes for a different leader. A classic militarist, she trained in her youth as a fighter pilot. Caiatl has bent her considerable might to two goals: defeating the Witness and reclaiming her homeworld of Torobatl. 

Caiatl's empire is a sprawling one, composed of many peoples. It continues to expand even within Sol, with the empress accepting the oath of the empire's first Guardian, the Valus Saladin Forge.
entries.text_zh:
“我们吞噬山川，我们畅饮海洋。” 

——————

前皇帝卡鲁斯大帝摒弃了帝国悠久的军事传统，终日享乐。他唯一的继承人，通过政变推翻他的女帝查厄托，是一名不同的领袖。她是一个典型的军国主义者，年轻时曾接受过战斗机飞行员训练。查厄托将她的强大力量用在两个目标上：击败见证者和夺回她的家园图罗巴特尔。 

查厄托的帝国疆域辽阔，由许多不同的民族组成。随着女帝接受太阳系的第一名守护者，军政官萨拉丁·佛吉的效忠誓言，她的势力甚至还扩张进了太阳系。

entries.name: Article: Visitors Out of Dreams—Changing Reef Relations
entries.name_zh: 文章：梦中来客——暗礁关系变化
entries.text:
By Leia Terazzas, Political Correspondent at the City Herald 

Recent strategic summits between Queen Mara Sov of the Awoken and the Vanguard have provided our citizens with that rarest of honors: a glimpse of our Awoken neighbors.  

The City has hosted a small Awoken population for centuries, but Reefborn subjects of the queen were more commonly contained to Awoken settlements and outposts within their own territory. The queen's secrets were guarded zealously, and prior relations with the City often bordered on hostility. In the face of common threats, however, this isolationist policy has since softened.  

For today's citizens, the arrival of Awoken Corsairs is a minor spectacle.  

"I just know it's some sort of divine monarchy?" one local commented. "How are we supposed to keep up with everything in Sol these days? But they sure look impressive."  

Initial impressions of the Awoken Corsairs appear to be positive, with several residents describing them as disciplined, worldly, and surprisingly grounded.  

"We made a choice to help Earth long ago," said one Corsair. "I'm glad we can do so openly."  

While the imminent battle for the Traveler is foremost on everyone's minds, several Corsairs noted their hopes for continued cooperation, especially given rumors of a resurgence of the infamous Ahamkara.  

As another Corsair put it: "There's a lot we're going to have to figure out together in a hurry."
entries.text_zh:
圣城使者政治记者莱雅·特拉扎斯著 

觉醒者的玛拉·索维女王与先锋近日举行的战略峰会，让市民们有幸一睹我们的邻居觉醒者的风采。  

几个世纪以来，圣城一直在接纳少量的觉醒者，但女王的暗礁后裔臣民通常都被限制在其领地内的觉醒者定居点和前哨站。女王的秘密受到狂热的保护，昔日与圣城的关系往往接近敌对。然而，面对共同的威胁，这种孤立主义政策近来有所缓和。  

对于今天的市民们来说，觉醒者海盗军的到访已是见怪不怪。  

“我只知道他们是某种神圣君主制？”一名市民评论道。“现今我们要怎样做才能跟上太阳系里发生的事啊？但他们确实看起来挺厉害。”  

市民们对觉醒者海盗军的第一印象似乎是积极的，几名市民形容他们纪律严明，善于处事，而且意外地脚踏实地。  

“我们很久以前选择了帮助地球，”一名海盗军说。“我很高兴我们能公开地那样做了。”  

虽然每个人都把即将到来的旅行者保卫战放在首位，但几名海盗军也指出，他们希望能在那之后继续合作，尤其是考虑到有传闻说臭名昭著的阿罕卡拉会卷土重来。  

正如另一名海盗军所说：“有很多事情我们都得共同尽快解决。”

entries.name: These Bad Lands
entries.text:
"Don't fool yourself. These rocks and this metal may be lashed together, but they ain't tamed. This far out, the only law is outlaw. The only justice? Last rites.

"So, walk careful—head on a swivel, hand on the hilt, all that—cuz that glare you feel is the narrowed eyes of ill-intent aimed at your honor, your heart… your head.

"And know this: Your every step is set upon blooded ground. The whole of the Shore… This is a wasteland built where a few sought to survive. In the dim light of a lost age, this wild frontier was a fleeting hope-turned-final restin' place—a graveyard at the end of existence.

"Some say you can still hear the screams—echoes of the lost and damned ringing from just out of sight. Don't believe 'em. That's just the stretching and bending of the supports—old metal moaning in the celestial breeze, the grinding of scrap and stone calling out, giving warning.

"These tethered lands be not safe. This twisted reef be not kind."

—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's Translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"


"There's no way that's a direct translation."
—Cayde-6
entries.text_zh:
“不要自己骗自己。这些岩石和金属或许是被连接在了一起，但它们并没有屈服。在如此遥远的地方，唯一的规则就是没有规则。那唯一的正义呢？那就是临终祈祷了。

“走路的时候要小心——四处张望，手握刀柄，全身上下都要戒备——因为你所感受到的那道目光，正是来自那些图谋不轨想要夺取你的荣光、你的心脏……甚至你的头颅的人。

记住：你踏过的每一步，都染满了鲜血。整个海岸……这是一处少数人挣扎求存的荒芜之地。在这个失落时代的微光之下，这一处狂野的边境已经成了稍纵即逝希望的破灭之地——一处位于存在尽头的墓场。

“有人说，你还能听到那些尖叫声——迷失者和被诅咒者的回响，从目不能及的地方传来。但请不要相信他们。那只是地基伸展和弯曲的声音——老旧的金属在微风中呻吟，瓦砾和石块的摩擦发出呼喊般的声响，让人有所警觉。

“这片被束缚的大地很不安全。这片扭曲的暗礁也相当不友善。”

——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》


“这些东西肯定不是直译来的。”
——凯德6号

entries.name: By Thy Tongue Be Damned
entries.text:
"Even here, the whispers persist.
Faint, but present."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

A Dreg fell. Left to die. A forgotten pirate set on a path toward salvation. His crew had raided the Moon looking for Ether. They found only death. And then he was alone.

Hiraks, the small. Hiraks, the timid, the weak was lost to the depths of the Hellmouth. A solitary scavenger down among the hollows where dead things dwell. How he survived is a story untold, an impossible tale known only to Hiraks himself.

In that secret is his strength.

For poor, weak, pathetic Hiraks came out of that hell as something other. Still Fallen. Still alone. But changed by all he'd seen and learned—his mind opened, set adrift through the wonders of all the nightmares he had never imagined.

Some say he spent his time hidden in the shadows of that cruel land scouring the mysteries of the Worlds' Grave. Others suggest he peered into a hateful shrine and found truth in the unutterable horrors whispered from the abyss.

Truth is, only Hiraks knows. Truth as simple as it is puzzling: Yes. Yes, he did. Scour the Grave. Hear the whispers. Only then could all that followed transpire.

For a lowly Dreg to rise from their docking to stand as a Baron is rare enough, but that a Fallen of any stature could crack the layers of understanding that barricade the known universe from the ascendant plane is more than improbable. It was impossible.

Until it wasn't.

For Hiraks succeeded where so few have. He crafted his own throne world and began a monstrous quest to expand his knowledge, etching its harshest truths upon his enemies. And his work has progressed unchecked.

It is his name the children do not speak when sharing tales of the Haunting of Nemesis. It is his blood that Paladins and Corsairs alike wish to spill for the Slaughter at Gaspra.

Hiraks, the Twisted. Hiraks, Ascendant. The mindbender whose tongue is a weapon, whose experiments seek to unravel sanity and reshape imagination that his subjects may become other—tools of his vile bidding.

And so, the warnings spread…

When the Fallen who speaks in the language of the damned calls, do your best not to listen, for once his words take hold, your will shall fade, replaced by its antithesis.

And then, like that poor, weak, fallen Dreg… you too will know darkness.

You too will be alone.
entries.text_zh:
“即使在此处，耳语仍在。
微弱，但存在。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

堕落士兵倒下，等待死亡。被遗忘的海盗军启程寻找救赎之路。他的船员袭击了月球，想寻找乙太。他们只找到了死亡。在那之后他便孤身一人。

瘦小的赫拉克斯，怯懦的赫拉克斯，迷失在了地狱之口的深处。一个孤独的拾荒者，深陷亡者徘徊的洞穴。他的幸存是一个不为人知的故事，一个只有赫拉克斯自己知道的不可能的传奇。

这个秘密，是他的力量源泉。

在弱小而可悲的赫拉克斯从那个如同地狱般的地方出来的时候，他已经成了另一个人。虽然还是堕落者，虽然还是孤身一人，但他的所见所闻改变了他——他的心智被那些他以前根本无法想像的梦魇打开了，漂浮不定。

有人说他一直躲藏在残酷土地的阴影中搜刮世界之墓的秘密；还有人认为他窥探到了一个邪恶的祭坛，从来自深渊的低语所带来的难言恐惧中找到了真理。

而真相只有赫拉克斯自己知道。真相是如此令人费解，但又如此简单。是的，是的，这些他都做了。搜刮墓穴，聆听低语。只有这样，这一切才会发生。

一个卑微的堕落士兵从码头工人走到公爵的位置上已经够罕见了，但一个能打破阻隔已知宇宙和上维国度理解层次的堕落者就不仅仅是不太可能了，那简直就是不可能的。

但事实并非如此。

在这个鲜有成就的领域，赫拉克斯确实成功了。他打造了自己的王座世界，开始疯狂拓展自己的知识，使最残酷的事实降临到他的敌人身上。而且他的进展没有受到任何阻挠。

在说起难忘的复仇女神的故事时，孩子们甚至不敢提及他的名字。圣骑士和海盗军都希望在小行星大屠杀的时候将他杀之而后快。

扭曲的赫拉克斯，上维赫拉克斯。作为以舌为刃的心灵操纵者，他一直在进行瓦解理智和重塑想象的实验，企图将他的实验对象变成其他——他邪恶行径的工具。

于是，警示传开了……

如果这个堕落者用被诅咒的语言召唤你，最好捂上耳朵，因为一旦你听清了他的话，你的自我就会消失，被邪恶的内心所取代。

然后，就像这个可怜的、懦弱的、堕落的堕落士兵一样……你也将尝到黑暗的滋味。

你也将变得孤身一人。

entries.name: Riddled with Lies
entries.text:
"Trust is your shield.
Trust is your weakness.
In the end, we all fall to betrayal."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

A simple riddle for you to consider…

"Only truth can conquer lies. But what is truth? And in whose eyes?"

What then of the Butcher of Bamberga? What then of the Psyche Hordes' slayer? The Terminus of the Gray Legion? The Sliver of the Shadowed Veil? The Bandit of Old Bassa? The Dire Siren of Valian's Reprieve?

What then of so many who are one—a single scourge, responsible for many varied tragedies?

The Trickster. The liar. Silver-tongued Araskes, the Wit.

She who bartered with the Spider and nearly cost him his life. She who swindled a dozen bounty hunters that she alone may profit. So many tales of Araskes' sleight of hand and tongue and mind. The enemy who has won battles where no battle was fought. Who has killed more rivals than have ever risen to her challenge.

What is known and unknown? None can say. And the sly prankster would have it no other way.

Of all the Barons marked by scorn, it is Araskes to fear, for her greatest weapon is the dissolution of truth. She will give you certainty, only to reshuffle the deck. She will grant you your desire, only to reveal it is truly regret.

If this realm can allow for gods, then she may be the first among devils—unknowable, unpure. Her tongue will cut you down long before your body falls. If you don't believe—if you find yourself questioning the depths of her deceit—ask yourself a simple question:

Did you kill her? And if you did, did she die?

If the answer is yes, her trap is set.

If your answer is…

It's okay. You don't have to say it. Maybe you will survive out among these wild shores longer than most.

Though maybe not as long as you'd like.
entries.text_zh:
“信任是你的盾牌。
信任是你的弱点。
最终，我们都将沦落背叛。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

出一个简单的谜语你来思考一下……

“只有真理才能征服谎言。但什么是真理？在谁的眼里是真理？”

班伯加的屠夫是什么？那灵魂部落的凶手又是什么？灰色军团终结者？暗影面纱撕裂者？老巴萨的强盗？瓦里安缓刑的可怕警笛？

如果这么多外号都属于一个人——一个需要为诸多不同惨剧负责的灾星呢？

骗术师，骗子，巧舌如簧的“智者”阿瑞斯克斯。

她跟蛛王做交易差点儿要了他的命。她把一群悬赏猎人耍得团团转，最后坐享其成。关于阿瑞斯克斯的手腕、口才和头脑，有着太多太多的传说。她是一个让你不战而败的敌人。她的对手还未崭露头角便被消灭于萌芽之中。

什么东西既已知，又未知？谁都不知道。这个狡猾的恶作剧者也别无他法。

在嗤魅所标记的所有公爵中，阿瑞斯克斯是最可怕的，因为她最强大的武器就是瓦解真理。她会给你确定性，但那只为搅浑水。她会给你你想要的东西，但你只会深深地后悔。

如果这个国度中真的有神灵存在，那她一定是第一个邪神——不可知，不纯洁的神。在你的身体不支倒地之前，她就能凭三寸不烂之舌让你支离破碎。如果你不相信——如果你质疑她的骗术——你可以问自己一个简单的问题：

你杀了她吗？如果是你杀的，那她死了吗？

如果答案是肯定的，那她的陷阱就完成了。

而如果你的答案是……

没关系，你不用说出来。也许你能比大多数人在这个狂野的海岸上生存得更久。

虽然不一定能如你所愿那么久。

entries.name: Anguish, Ten-Fold
entries.text:
"Be wary of those who would do harm.
Yourself included.
Mind that you do not become undone.
For once infliction is tinged with joy, you are not but a beast.
And are we not more than that?
Do we not strive for better?"
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

It was Reksis Vahn who saw to the final days of the House of Wolves. With cold hatred, he hunted and slaughtered their Servitors until none remained, and thus a rabid House did fall.

But Reksis Vahn's rage was not sated, as the Wolves alone were not the architects of his fury—all Fallen who clung to the ritual of House politics were his enemy, total and complete.

It is told that he was starved as a young Dreg. He watched in agony as others grew strong while he and his closest brothers and sisters were kept low. They were unworthy, pathetic, unwanted. But Reksis was ever aware. He saw the lie of the Archon's worship—how Servitors were revered upon a pedestal of godhood as a means to control the masses.

Maybe there was a time when the Fallen theology was one with greater concerns. No more. The Houses fractured, at war with one another. Old graces long since neglected in favor of a more desperate purpose—survival.

While cast low, Reksis found strength in his growing hatred. Only when he found common disdain among those twisted outcasts who would call themselves Scorned—who wore their hated derision as a badge of honor—did Reksis also find an outlet for his anger. His new brothers and sisters saw great value in his unchecked aggression. They were all a bit mad in their own right. All a bit twisted.

But where others slipped toward insanity, Reksis's mind and intent were clear—the agony of a terrible death was his aim. The target of his wickedness, the very Servitors he had been denied. The very machines that sustained the Fallen.

He would tear and slice and rend their metal until their hissing deaths rang across the Shore, the Reef… the entire system. He would make all who do not stand with the Scorned Barons feel the anguish he once felt, tenfold.

And he would do so gleefully, watching the life drain from their eyes.
entries.text_zh:
“小心那些伤害别人的人吧。
包括你自己在内。
记住，你的所作所为是无法收回的。
一旦你施加伤害时感受到快乐，你就成了野兽。
然而，我们不只是野兽吗？
我们没有努力变得更好吗？”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

瑞克西斯·瓦恩见证了恶狼氏族的最后时光。带着冷酷的仇恨，他将他们的魔眼猎杀殆尽，这个疯狂的氏族终于陨落。

但瑞克西斯·瓦恩的愤怒依然没有得到满足，因为恶狼们并非他的愤怒之源——所有坚持氏族政治仪式的堕落者都是他的敌人，完完全全的敌人。

据说，在还是一个年轻堕落士兵的时候，他就经历了饥荒。他和他最亲密的兄弟姐妹们一直吃不上一顿饱饭，于是只能痛苦地看着其他人变得强壮起来。他们毫无价值，命运悲惨，无人问津。但瑞克西斯一直很清楚。他看穿了执政官崇拜的谎言——将魔眼像神一般崇拜只是控制大众的手段。

也许曾经有一段时间堕落者神学是大家更担心的问题。但现在不是了。氏族四分五裂，彼此交战。以往的装腔作势也早已因更紧迫的目的——生存而被忽视。

但虽然流落至此，瑞克西斯还是从不断增长的仇恨中找到了力量。而当瑞克西斯在那些自称为“嗤魅”的心灵扭曲的恶棍——那些以仇恨为荣的人——发现同样的蔑视之情时，他也找到愤怒的宣泄口。他的新兄弟姐妹们在他那无可抑制的侵略性中发现了巨大的价值。他们甚至对自己的正义感到生气，感到纠结。

但当其他人走向疯狂的时候，瑞克西斯的理智和意图都很明确——他所追求的目标，就是可怕死亡的痛苦。他罪恶的对象，是那些拒绝他的魔眼，是支撑着堕落者的那些机器。

他会将这些金属撕成碎片，直到他们的死亡之音响彻整个海岸，整个暗礁……甚至整个星系。他会让所有与嗤魅公爵站在对立面的人感受他曾经感受过的痛苦，十倍奉还。

而且他会很高兴地看着生命从敌人的眼睛里慢慢消逝。

entries.name: A Blind Eye Toward Tomorrow
entries.text:
"They who draw, mustn't always draw first.
For it is not speed that kills, but the eye—keen and sharp.
So, then, do not feel death.
See it. Know it.
And it shall manifest upon the trigger's embrace."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

Pirrha, the Phantom. Pirrha, the Blind. The Fallen Baron with the all-seeing eye and the crack-shot. The Awoken link him to the legend, "The Ghost of Hellrise Canyon," believing it was Pirrha, and Pirrha alone, who haunted the winding depths, picking off intruders and holding off Corsair raiding parties as his fellow Barons planned their violent reign in the maze of caverns near the canyon's heart.

He was unseen during the Wolves uprising, but many credit him with the assassination of the Queen's palace guard. None can verify, but each fell to a single shot—clean, precise, fatal.

But how can a blind pirate who had been discarded and scorned by his House become the deadliest shot this side of Mars?

This is where the Barons' true strength hides. They are each a devil worthy of your hate, but together they are so much more. Not simply devils, but Hell itself—manifest, angry, and aggressive.

Rumors and legend merge to tell of the Machinist's expert hand, the Rifleman's cybernetic eye and a link between his sight and the tracking systems on his rifle.

What he sees, he hits.

What he hits, he kills.

There is evidence of Fallen giving themselves to technology. Becoming other—becoming more—as they marry their physical selves to enslaved mechanics. The mercenary Taniks is one example—more machine than Fallen now, an abomination in the eyes of traditional Fallen belief. The Splicers and their augmentation through SIVA—a twisted experiment brought low by the mighty hand of the heroes of Iron. Is Pirrha any different?

The Barons and Taniks and the Splicers are each and all individual dangers, driven by their own ambition. They are more likely to wage war with one another than see their commonality.

Yet are they not of a kind? Are they not evidence of something greater wending its way through the Fallen's dying culture?

Are they not the warning signs of a new terrible evolution?

One can only wonder—and hope—these horrid amalgamations of life and technology are simply outliers and not a promise of tomorrows yet to come.
entries.text_zh:
“拔枪并不一定要是最快的。
杀人靠的不是速度，而是眼睛——锐利的眼睛。
所以，不要去感受死亡。
要去观察死亡。了解死亡。
这样你才能回应扳机的拥抱。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

幽灵匹拉，盲者匹拉，有着全知之眼和神枪手本领的堕落者公爵。觉醒者将他和“狱涌峡谷的幽灵”传说联系到一起，认为这个故事说的就是匹拉：他孤身一人独守在蜿蜒的深渊，将入侵者逐个消灭并阻拦海盗军的劫掠，让其他公爵在峡谷深处如同迷宫般的洞穴中规划他们的邪恶统治。

他在恶狼氏族起义时消失无踪，但还是有很多人认为是他暗杀了女王的王宫卫队。没人能证实这个说法，但人人都是被一枪毙命——干净，准确，致命。

但一个被氏族抛弃和蔑视的盲眼盗匪是如何成为火星这一端最危险的枪手的呢？

这里隐藏着公爵们的真正力量。他们都是值得你憎恨的恶魔，但如果他们联合在一起，意义要大得多。他们已经不只是恶魔，而是整个地狱——显眼，愤怒，具有侵略性。

关于机械姬的专家之手、枪客的机械眼和他视野与他步枪上的追踪系统，有着许多的谣言和传说。

他能看到什么，就能打中什么。

他能打中什么，就能干掉什么。

有证据显示，一些堕落者献身于科技。然后变成了别的东西——比原来更强大——因为他们用自己的身体来奴役机械。雇佣兵坦尼克斯就是一个例子——他现在更像是个机器而不是堕落者，在传统的堕落者看来他就是个怪物。熔岩军团和他们通过湿婆——一个被机械英雄的强大力量所压制的邪恶实验——进行强化。匹拉又有何不同呢？

公爵、坦尼克斯和熔岩军团都是各有野心的危险人物。他们更有可能彼此开战，而不是和平共存。

但他们难道不是一类人吗？难道他们的存在不恰恰证明了有更厉害的事物导致了堕落者文化即将灭亡吗？

他们难道不是向世人警示着一个可怕的新进化的到来吗？

我们只能想象——并希望——这些生命与科技的结合体只是昙花一现，而不是必将降临的未来。

entries.name: The Ragged Valley Sprint
entries.text:
"Many are lost to the Shore's wayward ebb and flow.
The shifting mass gives and takes—pulls and tears.
The ground beneath ever uncertain, so tread carefully, as other dangers distract.
But death lingers, its grip loose but present.
Waiting to take hold. 
Waiting to embrace all who walk these tangled lands."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

The Ragged Valley is long and harsh and no valley at all. Not by traditional definition. Its hollow length runs between a series of lashed asteroids on the Shore's far western edge.

They call it a "valley" to be poetic, but in truth, it is simply the chaotic space between massive rocks that scrap and smash into one another in a violent dance. The distances from mass-to-mass ebb and flow without warning—a constant, deadly repositioning of the landscape. That ever-changing hollow is the Valley. Only the mad and desperate would dare run its length. With one exception…

Yaviks. The Rider.

The reason she made the run changes with the telling. You know she is neither mad nor desperate what with her skills on a Pike and killer determination. But the run itself—it's a legend as awe-inspiring as any Guardian's, save the fact Yaviks is a wicked beast and better off dead. The story goes…

She was running Ether… or making off with lost Golden Age tech. Some say Clovis Bray science. Others tell it was drivers from a forgotten Warmind. Or maybe she'd just dropped a Guardian and was running full-throttle from a fireteam set on revenge—a common theme this far out. Or was it pride? Did a Captain or a Kell or an Archon challenge her ability to ride? Did Fikrul? After all, their relationship is… complicated.

None of that matters. Not to me. Each version of the start is as interesting as the next. But the run itself? Her ride through the gnashing jaws of death?

Most Guardians who have heard it dismiss it. Don't want to give credit to one so infamous—the Scorned Baron with the blood on her hands, the loot in tow and her burners set to top speed—but she deserves it. Don't believe me. Ask Marcus Ren.

He wasn't there that day, but he'd heard tell and couldn't believe. So he made the run himself. Four goes. No dice. One resurrection. Four Sparrows busted to rubble.

Marcus Ren, the Sparrow Racing League champion and hero to speed junkies and race hounds City-wide, couldn't sprint that Valley. "Too random," he said. "Too chaotic. Can't read the rock one minute to the next. Can't read the angles."

But he tried again, and on the fifth go, he scraped through a narrow as the collision hit. He'd made it. The impossible was possible, though he refused to admit Yaviks could've done the same. Not that it mattered.

That Ren had come out alive proved it could be done, and if it could—why not Yaviks?

Not that Yaviks ever cared for validation. Not yours. Not Ren's. Not any Guardian's. Not any Fallen's. Not anyone's.

She took pride in recognition from her brother and sister Barons and no others.
entries.text_zh:
“许多人都迷失在海岸那反复无常的潮汐之中。
那不断变化的物质——将人拉扯、撕裂。
地面的世界更具不确定性，所以走路请小心，其他的危险可能会让你分神。
但死亡之手依然在此徘徊，手指放松但仍旧存在。
等待着收网的时机。
等待着拥抱那些走在这片纷争之地上的人。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

嶙峋峡谷漫长而难行，根本不像峡谷。至少不是传统意义上的峡谷。它蜿蜒在海岸西部边缘的小行星带上。

人们把这里称为“峡谷”是为了体现出诗意，但事实上，这里只是一片相互碰撞的危险巨大岩石之间的混乱空间。巨大的潮汐之间没有任何警示——也让这里的景象不断产生致命的变化。这不断变化的空洞就是峡谷的本质。只有疯子和绝望之徒有胆量走完全程。不过也有个例外……

那就是骑师，亚维克斯。

关于她进入峡谷的原因有好几个版本。在驾驶派克的技巧和杀人的决心上，她从来不是一个疯狂或者绝望的人。但这趟行程本身——作为一个令人敬畏的传奇——已经像守护者一样振奋人心。当然，亚维克斯本人实在是一头邪恶的怪兽，还是一死了之的好。据说……

她是在走私乙太……或是遗失的黄金时代技术。有人说是克洛维斯·布瑞的技术；有人说是被遗忘的战争思维的驱动；还有人认为她刚刚干掉了一个守护者，正急于摆脱复仇的火力战队——这也是大家比较认可的一个说法。或者说她只是为了自负而战？是有队长、凯尔或者执政官挑战她的驾驶能力吗？是费克鲁吗？毕竟他们的关系比较……复杂。

不过这都不重要。起码在我看来，每个故事的开头都很有趣。但这一趟行程本身呢？她真的从死神的牙缝里钻了过去吗？

大多数听到这个故事的守护者都不愿意相信。他们不想称赞这个如此臭名昭著的人——这个手上沾满鲜血的嗤魅公爵，那个拖着战利品将推进器开到最高速度的人——但这个名誉确实是她应得的。你可以不信我，但去问问马库斯·伦吧。

那天他不在现场，但他听过故事之后也不信。于是他自己也跑了一趟。四次，失败，还复活了一次。四辆快雀撞成了碎片。

马库斯·伦，赛雀联赛的冠军，全圣城竞速迷们的英雄，连他都跑不完那个峡谷。“太随意了，”他说，“太混乱了。一瞬间就看不到岩石的走向了，转角也看不清楚。”

但他又试了一次，在第五次的行程中，他在碰撞之前勉强蹭了过去。他成功了。不可能完成的任务确实可以做到，但他拒绝承认亚维克斯也有如此能力。不过这都不重要了。

伦活着证明了这条路是走得通的，既然走得通——为什么亚维克斯就不行呢？

亚维克斯又不在乎什么验证。不用你来验证，不用伦来验证，不用守护者来验证，不用堕落者来验证，不用任何人来验证。

她只接受其他公爵的认可，并为此自豪。

entries.name: Truth Tinkered
entries.text:
"Out here, they who craft their own fate see tomorrow, while they who depend on faith rarely make it through today."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

If you had not heard of the Machinist before, know that others had. While her crimes may not live in infamy in the hearts of City-dwellers, the Reef and its Awoken know all too well her long reign of terror.

Elykris, the Bandit, they call her. Elykris, the Scourge. The Scorned Machinist—tinker-lord of a Houseless crew.

But should those names be new to your ears, there are others you trust who have felt the pain of her vile campaign.

Ask your Arach of the Machinist's deeds. Ask him about the Siege of Arran—the hijacked ship, its stolen contents and its Guardian protectors lost or captured at the hands of the scorned.

Speak to your Vanguard of the Solis Descent—more Guardians felled, and an armory stripped of its cache.

The lowly Dreg who challenged tradition only to be cast aside. The lowly Dreg who found her own strength in a troubling bond with forsaken kin. She grew strong as an outcast—grew mean. Then found her purpose with the guidance of a preacher of sorts and a new, more driven crew.

Now, then… the questions you must ask yourself…

Had you known of the Baron's deeds, had you heard tell of the Machinist's crimes—could you have changed the path tread from there to here? From yesterday to today?

Better yet… your Vanguard, your factions, your friends and allies—what all have they kept from you? If they spoke not of the Scorned Barons, if they issued no warning, is it because they simply did not see the full scale of the danger? Were they too distracted by wars within wars and interests of their own to issue the guidance needed for you to see the Shore for the threat it has always been? Perhaps given guidance that may well have saved countless lives?

Or at least one life in particular…
entries.text_zh:
“在这里，那些能决定自己命运的人才能看到未来，但那些单单依靠信仰的人却很难撑过今天。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

如果你以前没有听说过机械姬，请记住，别人听说过。她在圣城居民的心中可能不算声名狼藉，但暗礁和住在暗礁的觉醒者心中都很清楚她长久以来的恐怖统治。

大家称她为盗匪埃里克瑞斯、灾星埃里克瑞斯、嗤魅机械姬——一群无家可归手下的工匠领袖。

你可能从未听说过这些名字，但应该有不少你信任的人曾经感受过她的邪恶行径带来的痛苦。

去问问蛛族朋友这个机械姬的事迹吧，问问他雅兰围攻事件——那艘被劫持的飞船上面失窃的东西，还有被嗤魅杀死和俘虏的守护者。

问问你的先锋关于旭日沦陷的事吧——更多的守护者死去，军械库被洗劫。

挑战传统的卑微堕落士兵只会被抛在一旁。而从与失落的亲属之间的苦恼联系中获得自身力量的卑微堕落士兵，像流浪者一样变得强大——变得刻薄。然后在某个传教士和一群新的、更激进的船员的指引下，她找到了自己的目标。

现在……你需要问自己几个问题……

你知道公爵的所作所为吗？你知道这个机械姬所犯下的罪孽吗？你能改变她在两者之间的转变吗？你能改变从过去到现在的发展变化吗？

还有……你的先锋，你的阵营，你的朋友和盟友——他们都对你隐瞒了什么？如果他们都不肯谈论嗤魅公爵，如果他们都不给你任何警告，是因为他们看不到全部的危险吗？他们是不是被战争中的战争和自身的利益所拖累，以至于无法给出你需要的指导，让你无法看到海岸中一直存在的威胁？如果他们给予指引，或许能拯救无数的性命呢？

或者，起码能救上一条命……

entries.name: An Evolution of Faith
entries.text:
"Find your honor not in your station, nor the words and gifts of those who seek control, but in yourself—in your actions, deeds, and soul. To look anywhere else is a lie."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

Fikrul was an Archon.

Then Fikrul took a fall—beaten, docked, and banished for heresies against Eliksni faith.

He should have died—alone and starved of precious Ether.

He did not. Instead, he found kin in the form of seven scorned. With them, he found purpose and power. As their legend grew, he found believers and new truth. His banishment was not penance, it was reward—for his convictions, for his courage.

Fikrul, the crazed fanatic. Fikrul, the heretic Archon who spoke against the very faith he once held dear. Scorned and forgotten—but only for so long.

Fikrul was a Dreg.

Before his banishment—before his clarity of purpose—Fikrul was a celebrated leader of Fallen faith and a savior to those who embraced his teaching.

Archons had long been elevated in Fallen society, but their stature grew, and their role shifted following the Whirlwind. As desperation took hold and the last of the Fallen raced across the stars in search of salvation, their dependence on machines evolved into a deep-rooted need—their weapons to fight, their ships to fly, their Servitors to survive.

That need became worship. That worship became faith. And the Archons—those who oversaw the care and consecration of the Servitors—were looked upon to provide hope through their words, teachings, and interpretations of the machines' wants, needs… desires.

But Fikrul saw another path—one that would later be mimicked and twisted by the techno-deviant Splicers in the Plaguelands of Earth while he and his explored their own darker interpretations of faith.

Fikrul is a Fanatic.

Scorned and abandoned.

Fikrul is all who strive to regain strength of self and purpose. He is a survivor. He is the outcast priest of the broken plains, and his sermon is death and all the glory that follows.

In Fikrul's eyes, and those of the outcasts who rallied to his philosophies, machines were not superior. They were not gods. They were tools. Instruments to be mastered and controlled and manipulated in service of Eliksni pride. None should grovel for Ether. None should have their honor bound to the whims of manufactured deities.

But the evolution of Fikrul's faith did not end there. If the machines—the very things that had regulated the whole of their existence—were tools, why not life itself? Why not death?

There are many tales of the time between Fikrul's fall and his rise again as spiritual leader of the Scorned Barons—his struggle to find strength as a battered Dreg, his journeys across the system to challenge his faith, his joining with the other outcasts who were scorned, and his eventual union with his "father." The only thing that matters, however, when confronting the dangers of Fikrul is this: He is a creature of faith.

His faith is the antithesis of all who stand in the Light. That faith has raised an army. That army will baptize all who challenge its purpose in an unending sea of death. They will never stop. They will never give in. Because they know they are right.

And everything you stand for is wrong.
entries.text_zh:
“不要在意你的地位，也不要在意那些企图控制别人的语言和礼物，只有在你自己的身上——你的动作上、你的行为中、你的灵魂里——找到自我的荣耀。企图在其他任何地方寻觅，都不过是谎言。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

费克鲁曾经是个执政官。

后来他失败了——作为异端反对埃里克斯尼族的信仰而被击败和放逐。

他本应死去——既孤独又缺乏珍贵的乙太。

但他并没有死去。相反的，他在七个嗤魅身上找到了相似之处。和他们一起，他找到了自己的目标和力量。随着他们的传奇不断增长，他又找到了信徒和新的真理。放逐对于他而言不是惩罚，而是奖励——对他的信念和勇气的奖励。

费克鲁，疯狂的狂热者。异端执政官费克鲁现在已经背叛了他曾经珍视的信念。他曾被蔑视和遗忘——但也只持续了短短一段时间。

费克鲁曾是个堕落士兵。

在他被放逐之前——在他明白自己的目标之前——费克鲁也曾经是众人敬仰的堕落者领袖，他所引导的人们的救世主。

长久以来，执政官在堕落者社会里的地位不断提高，但在旋风灾难后，他们的声誉提高，角色也改变了。满心绝望的最后堕落者穿越星辰来寻找救赎，他们对机械的依赖演变成了一种根深蒂固的需求——他们用武器战斗，他们用飞船飞行，他们依赖魔眼生存。

这种需求终于转变为崇拜，崇拜又变成了信仰。而执政官——这些负责魔眼的护理和奉献的人——人们希望通过他们的言语、教导以及对机械需求……欲望的理解来找到希望。

但费克鲁看到了另一条道路——一条后来他探索自身的黑暗理解时被地球瘟疫之地上的技术异端熔岩军团所模仿和扭曲的道路。

费克鲁现在是个狂热者。

一个被蔑视和抛弃的狂热者。

费克鲁是一个只为重获自己的力量和目标而活的人。他是个幸存者。他是破碎平原上的流浪牧师，他所传播的是死亡之道，以及跟随死亡而来的荣光。

在费克鲁和那些信仰他哲学的流浪者看来，机械并没有什么所谓的优越性。它们不是神。它们只是工具，被埃里克斯尼族掌控和操纵，并为之服务的工具。谁都不应为乙太而卑躬屈膝，谁的荣耀都不应该被人造神的信念所绑架。

但费克鲁的信仰的演变并未在此结束。如果机械——这些规范他们自身存在的东西——都只是工具，那生命自身是否也是工具？死亡是否也是工具？

从费克鲁的陨落到他再次成为嗤魅公爵的精神领袖，对于那段时间所发生的事有着各种各样的传说——他以一个被击败的堕落士兵的身份努力寻找力量，他穿越星系企图挑战自己的信仰，他找到了那些同样被蔑视的流浪者，还有他与“父亲”的最终重逢。但是，唯一重要的是，你所面对的费克鲁是一个如此危险的角色：他是信仰的产物。

他的信仰是光能的绝对对立面。他靠着这种信仰组建了一支军队。这支军队会用无尽的死亡之海来淹没所有胆敢挑战他目的的人。他们永不停歇。他们永不放弃。因为在他们的心里，他们就是正道。

而你所代表的一切，都是错误的。

entries.name: A Scorned Path
entries.text:
"Surviving is a whole lot easier when your enemies are dead."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

It was Elykris, the Machinst, who'd begun hoarding the Servitors. And Reksis, the Hangman, who slaughtered them at every turn. Two allies driven by opposing forces—one science and the unmaking of faith, the other rage and its relentless push to destroy.

There had long been tension between the two, as Reksis had, more than once, slipped into the Machinist's workshop to inflict himself on the Servitors caged there.

Fikrul, the Fanatic—their spiritual leader and one-time Archon Priest—watched patiently as their rivalry grew. He saw strength in their ire. He saw fire and fury, but also more—a new path forward. One that could join their passions and drive them further—a whole stronger than its warring parts.

Fikrul waited, biding time as tensions rose and threatened to splinter the Barons' loyalties. Only when Elykris could take no more, on a night when she caught the Hangman prepared to slaughter her latest haul of lesser Servitors, did Fikrul step in.

Fikrul motioned to Elykris and said, "Bring me a Servitor." As Reksis hissed with anticipation, she hesitated, but Fikrul was patient. "Where is your trust?"

Elykris released a Servitor from its bondage.

Fikrul motioned the Servitor closer, then turned to Elykris. "You have gathered many, Machinist. Hundreds. Maybe more. Our own supply—our life force fed by slaved mechanics." Elykris nodded to the Servitor as it inched closer to the Archon's open arms—welcoming the once revered orb as one would a child.

The other Barons began to bark, a rhythmic warriors' chant.

"For all the value in your work… it is not enough to feed ourselves." Fikrul hugged the Servitor. There was a tenderness to the embrace. A sorrow. "We must also starve our enemies, as you were once starved." With a blur, Fikrul's lower arms unsheathed and triggered a pair of polished, sparking Shock Blades. "As were we all."

The Servitor, still held with the clutches of the Archon's powerful upper arms, cried a shrill, digital wretch—pain mixed with confusion as the blades carved its outer shell and plunged deep into the core of its systems. Ether hissed and sprayed.

Fikrul released the machine's silent shell, and it clanged lifeless to the ground. He turned to Elykris. "Do you see?" Elykris smiled. She was ever the brightest among them, though her focus could lose clarity when she became frenzied.

The Barons had long been trouble for the Awoken and Fallen of the Reef, but that trouble had been limited to hit-and-run tactics. What Fikrul had just presented was a new way.

Fikrul stepped to Reksis. "Do you see?" The brute barked in response, "Kill them all!"

Fikrul laughed. "Not 'all,' Hangman. Just the ones we do not need." 

The Barons cheered as Fikrul continued, "Every Servitor—any Servitor—bound to a House is now a target. Until none remain but those upon whom we feed."
entries.text_zh:
“如果敌人死了，想活下去就简单多了。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

最初开始囤积魔眼的是机械姬埃里克瑞斯，而刽子手瑞克西斯一有机会就会屠杀它们。由对立力量驱使的两个盟友——一个崇尚科学和信念的破灭，另一个崇尚愤怒和无情的摧残。

两者之间长期以来关系非常紧张，因为瑞克西斯不止一次地溜进机械姬的工坊里亲自虐杀被关押的魔眼。

而狂热者费克鲁——他们的精神领袖和曾经的执政官牧师——只是耐心地看着双方的竞争不断升级。他在他们的愤怒中看到了力量。他看到了怒火，但不只怒火——还有一条前进的崭新道路。让他们更具激情，促使他们开拓更进一步的道路——远比战争更加强大的道路。

费克鲁耐心地等待着，等候紧张局势的加剧，等待公爵的忠诚几乎产生裂痕。一天晚上，在埃里克瑞斯发现刽子手正准备屠杀她刚抓来的一批幼年魔眼而忍无可忍时，费克鲁出手了。

他向埃里克瑞斯说道：“给我带一只魔眼来。”看到瑞克西斯发出期待的嘶吼声，埃里克瑞斯犹豫了，但费克鲁很有耐心。“你的信任哪儿去了？”

埃里克瑞斯释放了一只捆绑着的魔眼。

费克鲁示意魔眼靠近，然后转向埃里克瑞斯说道：“你收集了很多，机械姬。数以百计。也许还会有更多。这是我们自己的补给——由被奴役的机械所带领的生命力。”埃里克瑞斯点头示意魔眼靠近执政官张开的双臂——像欢迎孩子一般欢迎这个曾经被崇敬的球体。

另一位公爵开始大叫，仿佛有节奏的勇士们在吟唱。

“你的工作所制造的价值……不足以养活我们。”费克鲁抱了抱魔眼。那是个温柔的拥抱，却带着感伤。“我们必须让我们的敌人也挨饿，就像你所经历过的那样。”费克鲁的下臂一闪而出，伸出一对闪烁着火花的电光之刃。“就像我们都经历过的那样。”

魔眼仍然抱着执政官强有力的上臂，发出一阵刺耳的机械悲鸣声——迷惑而痛苦，眼睁睁地看着利刃刺穿它的外壳，深深地扎进它的系统核心。乙太嘶嘶地喷薄而出。

费克鲁放开了机械已悄无声息的外壳，已经失去生机的它跌落在地面。他转向埃里克瑞斯：“看到了吗？”埃里克瑞斯笑了。她一直是他们当中最聪明的，虽然她在变得狂热时可能会失去理智。

公爵长久以来都是觉醒者和暗礁堕落者们的威胁，但这种威胁仅限于游击战术。费克鲁刚才展示出了一种全新的方式。

费克鲁走向瑞克西斯。“你看到了吗？”这个莽夫大吼着回应：“杀光它们！”

费克鲁大笑。“不能杀光，刽子手。只杀那些我们不需要的。”

费克鲁在公爵们的欢呼声中继续说道：“每个魔眼——任何与氏族有关联的魔眼——现在都是目标。只留下供养我们的那些。”

entries.name: A Gift of Madness
entries.text:
"The song of the grinding stone calls like pained sirens—shrill and uneven.
Its melody is a warning, yet still they come…
Adventurers. Bounty hunters. Scoundrels. And unwanted.
Here they find purpose.
Or hide from those worlds beyond.
Those polite lands, which 'heroes' strive to reclaim.
There is no reclamation here.
The Shore is ever-wild, and so shall it remain…
Ever the broken land where madness dwells and violence reigns."
—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"

The questions no one asks…

Was the Bomber always mad? Or was he driven to it? Was the madness a gift—or a curse?

Did the struggle for survival outside the structure and ritual of the House system crack his mind? The things he'd seen? Done? The Shore asks much of those who call it home. Most simply find their end through the harsh will of these harsh lands or by the hand of the hardened agents who stalk its fractured expanse—bandits, cutthroats, cannibals, Awoken patrols, Guardian "heroes."

There are a billion ways to die among the jagged wilds of the Tangled Shore. To challenge those odds is no small feat. To do so while maintaining self, rarer still.

However, isn't it also possible the Bomber was this all along? Mad. Deranged. Eager to inflict destruction. Lustful for the chaos and death to follow.

The Seeding of the Accretion Fields. The Bombing of the Origin Libraries. Kaniks's handiwork has been linked to numerous tragedies, both as a rogue enemy of the Reef and in league with his scorned brothers and sisters with whom he grew strong—with whom he found the purpose he once lacked.

These points—an examination on the birth of madness—I raise to address a lingering concern.

Seek the Awoken libraries. Speak to Cryptarchs with knowledge of the Reef… the Shore. Scour the records of the Bomber's deeds. Feel the pain of those who suffered the fire of his devastation. Remember the Fields. Weep at the unimaginable loss when the Libraries fell.

Allow yourself the comfort of knowing the sinister creature is now dead and gone by Guardian hand. But linger on victory's pride for only a short while, because the truth I seek to tell has yet to be revealed, and it is this…

The Mad Bomber is dead—Kaniks is no more. Yet the Shore remains ever untamed. Despite valiant effort. Despite your incredible strength.

And if the Shore remains tangled, its edges ever shifting, ever dire… Then who else may it drive to madness? First long-lost survivors of the fabled Golden Age, then stray Awoken and discarded Fallen…

Maybe next, the warriors of the Light. Guardians.

After all, more will surely come. And with more, however righteous you may be, the odds shift further in the Shore's favor. In the favor of madness.

And if not another, Guardian… why not you?
entries.text_zh:
“磨盘之歌如痛苦的塞壬一样——刺耳而杂乱。
它的旋律是一种警告，然而他们还是来了……
探险者、悬赏猎人、恶棍、还有那些不速之客。
他们在此寻求目标。
或逃离外面的世界。
那些‘英雄们'渴望开垦的上流世界。
这里没有开拓。
海岸是片荒野，也将恒为荒野……
这里永远是潜藏着疯狂的，由罪恶统治着的破碎之地。”
——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

没人问过这些问题……

炸弹客一直是这么疯吗？还是说，他是被逼的？疯狂到底是他的天赋……还是诅咒？

难道是在氏族系统的架构和仪式之外挣扎求存使他发了疯？他见过什么？做过什么？海岸对于以之为家的人索取甚多。大多数人都只是被这片严酷的土地上的残酷意志或是那些遍布在广阔的破碎之地上的老练暴徒——强盗、杀手、食人族、觉醒者巡逻队、守护者“英雄们”了结。

在纷争海岸这一片伤痕累累的荒野里，有上十亿种办法能让你随时死去。不是什么人都能够挑战命运的。在此过程中还能保留自我意志的人，就更少了。

但是，有没有可能炸弹客一直以来就是这样呢？疯狂，错乱，热衷于破坏，渴求随之而来的混乱和死亡。

吸积场的播种事件，起源图书馆的炸弹事件，无数悲剧事件都与卡内克斯的杰作有着千丝万缕的联系，上述两者都是暗礁的潜在敌人，再加上那些帮助他成长起来的嗤魅兄弟帮——正是在他们身上，他找到了自己身上曾经缺少的人生目标。

我提到的这些关键点——关于疯狂者诞生的考虑——也是希望解决一个悬而未决的难题。

寻找觉醒者图书馆，与了解暗礁……和海岸的解密大师谈话，搜集炸弹客的所作所为，感受那些遭受他毁灭之火的人的痛楚，铭记吸积场，为图书馆的毁灭所导致的难以想象的损失痛哭流涕。

在得知那个邪恶的生物已经被守护者杀死时松一口气。但胜利的骄傲只停留了片刻，因为我想要说出的真相依然未被揭露，那就是……

疯狂炸弹客死了——卡内克斯已经不存在了。然而海岸依然野性难驯，哪怕有着这些英勇的努力，哪怕你们有着无与伦比的力量。

如果海岸依旧纷争不断，它的边缘永远在变化，永远那么可怕……那么谁又会被再逼到发疯呢？先是传说中黄金时代失联很久的幸存者，再是流浪的觉醒者和被抛弃的堕落者……

也许接下来就轮到光能的战士——守护者了。

总之，问题一定会源源不断。长此以往，无论你有多么正义，海岸的败率必将越来越高，在疯狂的指引下。

如果其他人没疯，守护者……发疯的为什么不会是你呢？

entries.name: No Heroes Here
entries.text:
Every inch of ground beyond the City walls is dangerous—safety not guaranteed—and of all the inches across every world in this dead and dying system, none are harder than every single inch of the Tangled Shore.

This is not simply untamed space. It's worse. It's outlaw territory, where the worst of a bad lot come to find their fortune, ply their trade, or run from their sins.

No one who has ever walked the Shore's broken stone has come back clean. Out here you've gotta break the rules just to get by. Oh, your moral compass? You better hope it's on the fritz, 'cuz doing the right thing will only get you killed. Unless you're strong enough to do it the wrong way.

So, walk tall—the locals can sense the meek. Stand firm—backing down will only see you trampled. And aim true—each miss could be your last. Otherwise, go home.

The Shore ain't no place for heroes, anyway.
entries.text_zh:
圣城高墙外的每一寸土地都布满危机——安全得不到保障——但是这个死亡与将死的星系里的每一寸空间，都不如纷争海岸的任何一寸土地那么可怕。

这里已经不仅仅是一处桀骜不驯的所在。比那还要更糟糕，这里是不法之徒的地盘，只有恶徒中的佼佼者才能到这里来寻求财富，进行交易，或者逃避他们所犯下的罪行。

踏足过这个海岸上碎石的人，没有任何一个还能保持清白。在这里，你只有靠打破规则来挣扎求存。什么，你有道德准则？你最好祈祷它已经烟消云散吧，因为做好事只会让你死于非命。除非你有足够的本领来逆势而为。

总之，挺直腰杆——这里的人能感觉到你的温驯。坚定立场——退让只会让你惨遭蹂躏。准头要好——你射偏的每一枪，都有可能是你人生开的最后一枪。如果做不到，还是回家去吧。

海岸反正也不是什么英雄该来的地方。

entries.name: The Lonely and the Dead
entries.text:
"Out here, the lonely fall in the company of those bound by the purest need: survival.

"Find this truth. If not in your heart, in your mind. If not your mind, then your soul—the deepest part of you that connects to the most basic truths. To live for tomorrow, you have to fight for today.

"Know this. Understand it. Live it. Find those likeminded survivors you can look to as kin. Only then can survival be within reach, because to walk the Shore unbound is to invite death."

—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's Translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"
entries.text_zh:
“在这里，孤独与那些只有最纯粹的需求——生存的人为伴。

“记住这个真理。没世不忘，乃至铭诸肺腑。铭诸肺腑，乃至铭记于心——让你内心的最深处与最基本的真相相连。想要为明天而活，就必须为今天而战。

记住，理解，并以之为生存之道，以志同道合的幸存者为伴。只有这样，才有可能生存下来，因为独自行走在海岸便是在向死亡招手。”

——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

entries.name: The Sad Story of Eldred Rush
entries.text:
"I'll tell ya of Eldred Rush. He didn't come out this way looking for trouble. He ain't a fool, neither. He knew trouble waited. He just didn't care. Couldn't, some would say.

"Eldred was a prospector of sorts, digging around these parts in search of memories he considered gold. He had a mission, personal and pure: Find the rock on which his people fell. Some tell that he was the first Guardian to walk this deep. It's not true, but fits his tale and makes for a better legend.

"Lonely Eldred walked these lashed lands cycle-upon-cycle, avoiding conflict when he could, but always hitting back when push came to shove. He was a gentle man, but violent when riled.

"Eventually he found the spot where ancient survivors of an ancient collapse huddled and died. There, at the site of all he had lost—in an old life that was long since beyond his grasp—Eldred buried the dead he could not remember but felt in his heart.

"Never saw Eldred again. No one did."

—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"
entries.text_zh:
“我来跟你们说说艾卓·拉什吧。他并不是大老远来这里找麻烦的。他也不是傻瓜。他知道麻烦在这里等着他。他只是不在乎罢了。也许有些人会说，他是没法在乎。

“艾卓从某种意义上来说是个勘探者，想从这些零件里找到那些被他视之为黄金的记忆。他有一个很私人很纯粹的任务：找到那块让他的同胞跌倒的石头。有人说，他是第一个走到如此深远的守护者。真相并非如此，但很符合他的故事，也能编出一个更有意思的传说。

“孤独的艾卓在一次次循环中行走在这片被束缚的土地上，尽可能地避免冲突，但危急关头时他也会反击。他是个绅士，但愤怒时也很暴力。

“最后他还是找到了远古的幸存者们聚集和死亡的地点。在那里，在他所失去的一切存留的地方——在一个早已不在他掌控之中的古老人生中——艾卓埋葬了这些他已经忘却但仍存有爱意的亡者。

“那之后就再也没见过艾卓了。谁都没再见过他。”

——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

entries.name: Gotta Do More than Shoot
entries.text:
"A lotta things to consider when sizing up a gunfight. Most just focus on steely eyes and steady nerves, and those have value—but the best of 'slingers weigh so much more.

"The light in the sky or lack thereof. The temp and the breeze—how cool, how warm, which direction is the wind hitting and how hard? Further still: the ground beneath your boots. Is it solid or soft? Shifting or slick? All elements that speak to the moment of truth.

"The wear of the holster. The feel of the grip.

"But first and foremost, the best 'slinger will say never pick a fight with unfamiliar tools—unless the situation dictates an unavoidable outcome or in those instances when honor comes a-callin'."

—Excerpt from C.C. LaGrange's translations of "Writings and Observations from the Tangled Shore: A Fallen Text"
entries.text_zh:
“枪战发生时要考虑许多事情。大多数人都专注于坚定的眼神和坚韧的神经，还有那些有价值的东西——但最好的枪手要考虑的东西会多得多。

“天空中的光线，甚至光线的缺乏。温度和风——天气是冷是热，风吹向哪个方向，风力有多大？还有：你脚下的土地。地面是软是硬？是粗糙还是光滑？真相揭晓的那一刻，这一切的元素都在考虑之中。

“枪套的磨损程度。枪把的握感。

“但最最重要的是，最优秀的枪手会说，绝对不要用不熟悉的武器来挑起斗争——除非在不可避免的情况下，或者听到了荣耀的召唤。”

——摘自C.C.拉格朗译制的《纷争海岸的观察与记录：一份堕落者文本》

entries.name: Deal
entries.text:
All joking aside—maybe I've made mistakes. Maybe some more recently than others.

Hard to believe, I know, but maybe it's true. Maybe.

Here's the thing about mistakes: you learn from them. Again, this is assuming the theoretical concept of me having made some mistakes is true. So, yeah, maybe that's what I'm doing. Trying to learn from these very hypothetical slipups. Turning inward, they call it. "They" being Ikora. Eris calls it something different. Eris calls a lotta things something different. 

I miss that girl.

But here I am stalling—buying time.

This ain't easy for me.

Thought it would be. Easy, I mean. Or, at least… easier than this. Thought a lot of things would be easier. Hell… Thought a lotta things about a lotta things. But maybe that's what makes me the person I am. Makes any of us part of humanity—all our big thoughts and big plans, hopes and dreams and all that squishy nonsense.

OK, fine, look: If I'm playing at honesty, and I think that's what I'm doing here, maybe those hopes and dreams are all that really matters. Just, not losing sight of them is the hard part. Life is full of those little distractions that fudge the edges, make those hopes and dreams a little blurrier.

That's the power of "maybes," I suppose—the temptation of… playing both ends against the middle.

Maybes provide… wiggle room. And I like my edges fudgy. And I loooooves me some wiggle room. But if I'm gonna stay true to this whole rambling "dear diary" how-do-ya-do business, guess what I'm sayin' is…

Guess what I'm saying is, I'm sick of "maybes." And, if I'm a straight shooter—and I'm nothing if not—then I gotta shoot straight… even when there ain't a gun in my hand.

So, let's… let's keep this between me and you, OK?

Here's the deal: My name is Cayde-6…

And this is my story.
entries.text_zh:
不说笑了——我可能真的犯错了。有些错误可能就是最近犯的。

难以置信吧，我也这么想，但可能确实如此。可能吧。

错误有一个特点：你可以从中吸取教训。再重复一遍，这是在假设我犯错这件事是事实的情况下。是的，我也许是在这么做。从这些假设的错误中吸取教训。她们管这个叫内省。“她们”指的是艾可拉。埃里斯还有别的叫法。埃里斯对很多东西都有不同的叫法。

我想念那姑娘。

但是我是在拖延——拖延时间。

对于我来说这很不容易。

我之前可不这么想。我是说，觉得会容易。或者至少……比现在要容易。我以为很多事情都会更容易。管他呢……我还以为过很多东西。但也许正是这一切造就了我这个人。造就了我们的人性——我们的伟大想法和计划、希望和梦想，还有那些软弱的废话。

好吧，好吧，这么说吧：如果要我老实说，当然，我觉得我已经很老实了，也许那些希望和梦想才是最重要的。但是，困难的是如何不失去希望和梦想。人生充满着各种虚幻的困惑，会让你的希望和梦想变得更加模糊。

我猜，那就是“可能”的力量——鱼与熊掌都想兼得的诱惑。

“可能”会让你有……回旋的余地。我喜欢边界模糊，也爱极了回旋的余地。但是，如果要我在这个“亲爱的日记”里说真话，那我只能说……

我觉得我会说，我讨厌“可能”。还有，如果我是个直肠子——否则我就什么都不是——虽然我的肠子是弯弯曲曲的，但我也直说了。

我们……这事除了你我，都得保密，明白吗？

这么说吧：我叫凯德6号……

这就是我的故事。

entries.name: Call
entries.text:
Now, to be clear, yeah, the plan is to tell it like it is, but don't expect every little detail to play out. I'm gonna hit the important stuff, sure, but what I'm really after here is a sense of… a sense of me. Because once you understand me, you just might understand where I'm coming from, why I do the things I do, and why I've done the things I've done.

So, read between the lines if you have to, but end of the day? Everything that matters should be readily apparent. If not, you're not paying attention.

So here goes…

Us Exos are haunted.

Sounds ominous, I know, and maybe a bit of a stretch. But really, it's the best word—kinda sets the stage in a way the raw facts don't.

See, Guardians have all got past lives. But unless you returned with any definitive info on your person or in proximity (I'm looking at you, Bray), that past life, or lives, was, or were, wiped clean. Gone. Reborn in the Light and all, you become what you become.

Exos, though?

We've got ghosts in our machines. Not capital-G "open doors and know things" Ghosts. I mean, like fragments of— I don't know, pieces of something that could be memory. Whatever it is, it's enough to give us a starting point to maybe, possibly, imagine who we were before we became who we are. And then there's the dreams—but I ain't touching that with a ten-foot Arc Staff.

Me? I'm one of the lucky few. The fudgy flashes of that old Exo life weren't all I had to go on. See, the "me" that was in my life before my trusty capital-G Ghost found me kept journals, like mementos—fragments of my prior life that give me a baseline of who I was.

The journals are personal, and I keep personal close to the chest. I've shared a few pages, sure, but only with right-minded types who could find a little value in seeing the man behind the myth.

Yeah, "myth," I said it. Who are we kidding? You've heard of me. Who hasn't? Point is… I don't make a show of personal business.

First, because it's MY fuel to burn. Second, because Big Blue ain't a big fan of his Guardians poking around what they used to be—something about duty, rules, not losing sight of why we were chosen. But more than any of that… most of us "Chosen Ones" don't have the luxury of a past, so rubbing it in doesn't seem right.

Look, all I know is…

When I rejoined the land of the living, the pre-Light version of me was kind enough to lend a guiding hand. I took that hand, gave it a high five, and followed its example the best I could.

All this time later, I may not know my true purpose—I leave the big-ticket, existential questions to the Warlocks—but I know this…

My calling is to do good. Maybe not always to "be" good, ya know, but do good. There's a difference.

And if I don't always go about it in a manner that fits the textbook definitions of "hero" or "team player"—I'm looking at you, Big Blue—just know…

I might dance to my own tune, but we're all at the same hoedown…

Or something like that.
entries.text_zh:
首先要说清楚的是，我会尽量还原事情的真相，但你也别指望我把每个细节都记的清清楚楚。我肯定会把重要的事情说清楚，但是我更想表达的是……我的一种感觉。因为一旦你了解我，你可能只了解我的出处，我为什么要做、为什么会做那些事情。

总之，如果有必要的话，多想想言外之意吧。不过要我说呢，所有重要的事情应该都很显而易见。如果你看不出来，只能说你不够用心。

那我们就开始吧……

我们Exo身上都有鬼。

我知道这么说有些邪门，有些牵强。不过真的，这已经是最恰当的词汇了——说明了很多原始的事实无法表述的东西。

你们应该知道，守护者都有前世。但除非你回来的时候有明确的信息在你身上或者附近（我说的就是你，布瑞），否则那一段或者几段前世，都会被清除，都会消失。在光能中重生，你会成为一个全新的存在。

不过Exo呢？

我们的机械中是有鬼魂的存在呢。不是那种“会开门，能答疑”的机灵。就像是一种碎片——我觉得可能是记忆的碎片。无论如何，它也许、可能会让我们能够了解和想象自己在这一世之前的样子。然后就是梦——不过我就不用十尺长的电弧法杖去碰它了。

我？我是少数幸运者之一。我所经历的不仅仅只有前世Exo的虚幻闪回。这么说吧，在我信赖的机灵找到我之前，我的前世会写日记——那些前世的片段能让我基本了解前世的自己。

日记是很私密的，我一直保存在胸前。我给别人看过一些，但只给那些能从我这个隐藏在神话中的人身上看到一丝价值的正直的人看过。

是的，“神话”，我是这么说的。谁在开玩笑？你听说过我。谁没听说过？重点是……我不喜欢显摆自己的事。

首先，因为那是我自己的事。其次，因为大蓝人也不喜欢他的守护者打听前世的消息——据说跟职责和规则什么的有关，不能忘记我们被选中的原因。但更重要的是……我们这些“天选者”中的大多数都没有过去，去戳别人痛处似乎并不太好。

我只知道……

在我重回生者的这片土地时，前世的我很慷慨地向我伸出了指引之手。我接受了他，然后尽力跟随着他。

哪怕现在，我都还不知道自己真正的人生目标——我把这个存在主义的大问题留给了术士去解答——但我知道……

我的使命就是行善。用不着永远“做”善人，但需要行善事。这两者是有区别的。

如果我没有一直按照教科书般的“英雄”和“团队精神”准则来做事的话——我说的就是你，大蓝人——这么说吧……

我也许能按我自己的节奏跳舞，但我们大家都在同一个舞池里……

大概是这样吧。

entries.name: First Stake
entries.text:
Made a deal with myself, long ago…

If people needed help and I could do the helping, I would—so I do.
