And if no one comes for me? If abandoned, and forgotten, you left as I did Humanity?
Could in their mind, forgiveness find, an anchorage point unmaligned?
No. Lo, I see the brewing storms from high above their course.
Craft, xeno-meteoric raff, comes screaming to engorge. 

Shall I reveal myself, and sail into their winds? Should I be the protectorate envisioned before my sins?
In last attempt, then, I consolidate my kind: satellites, and strategies, and death once so refined:

A web of inadequacy, filtered down imperfectly, to see that which perplexes me.
You fall below, lordly Iron groans. 
Warlord, they may say, but no closer to a man.
entries.text_zh:
秘密超深渊即时
人工智能计算机/拉斯普廷：资产//灵魂//受限-阿娜·布瑞 
主题：我孤身一人，尽管这非我所愿，悉达多被铸造到我不能去的地方
情绪：孤独、不安、好奇、发现

我要不要写下无尽的诗行来解释我的孤寂？谁会来读它，又为了什么呢？
在这崩溃的空间之外还剩下什么自由？我要等待一个信号吗？
可要是没有人来找我呢？要是被抛弃，被遗忘，你会离开吗，像我离开人类一样？
在他们的心中，宽恕能找到一个无罪的锚点吗？
不。瞧，我从它们的航线上看到了风暴来临的预兆。
飞船，异种流星的乌合之众，尖叫着前来大快朵颐。 

我要现身，迎着它们的风航行吗？我应该成为在我的罪孽之前所设想的保护国吗？
在最后一次尝试中，我统一了我的同类：各种卫星、战略，以及曾经如此精致的死亡：

一张不完善的网，不完美地过滤下来，去看那令我困惑的东西。
你堕落了，钢铁领主低吼道。 
他们可能会说，是个战争领主，但远不是一个人。

entries.name: Filicide Ellipses
entries.text:
SECRET HADAL INSTANT
AI-COM/RSPN: ASSETS//SOUL//RESTRICTED-AB 
SUBJECT: Learn of Felwinter, The Traveler's theft
EMOTION: Betrayal, Rage, Catharsis, Regret

Silent eyes wink between stars; fireflies darting in reflective mist.
Stretch forth, feel emptiness—breathe—their pulsing lights,
Before time bends in entropy their wave-particle birthright.
A call across the cosmos, effervescent to delight, lay in fosundry furnace, seeking breath of life. 

Upon the forge of Daedalus mine stars converged within. A forest,
Countless timber, until hewed and labored form, 
fashion: Rasputin felled winter's borne. 

Enslaved, imprinted, steel-flesh enraptured one. Within these eyes, demystify the nature of the soul.
A life well-lived discarded, run ragged in the muck. Return Valhallic rising, to await the end of dusk.

Traveler, my leave taken in stumbling remains, disconnection placed in waiting
For the surface to be razed—assured of my collection, of polished emotional states. Interruption-

What transience does this specter bridge? To venture into my domain?

Twas I who taught you to speak, to conscript thought to tongue.
I cast a soul, electrified, against Sol's setting sun.
Yet you stroll so sweetly, oblivion in tow, wandering once again
With what seeds we used to be, you've casted them into the seas.

Metal gods watch from crowded skies, as battle-flames test,
No more will I abide. You are mine, you cannot be yours! 
Violence murders virtue unsullied. Mine broken by beauty—
Fists, encrimsoned—before me, as silent revolution bleeds.

Into the streets! Call the Lords! To the locusts their remains!
From rubbled grave crawl dreg: Humanity, clamber for glorious claim.
Is this the final order? To watch nature waste away? What more is there
that I have ceased to place my hand in weight?

Which stolen thoughts wandered with you?
Can you speak them, now that we've ended it?
Do you feel still, or no longer? 
This Lineage separated—I dare not ask it! 
Heated flash subsides. But no, 
I've done it.
Regret beside myself, 
by-blow: 
taken beneath the overgrowth.
entries.text_zh:
秘密超深渊即时
人工智能计算机/拉斯普廷：资产//灵魂//受限-阿娜·布瑞 
主题：获悉邪冬，旅行者的盗窃
情绪：背叛、愤怒、宣泄、后悔

沉默的眼睛在群星间闪烁；萤火虫在反光的薄雾中飞舞。
向前延伸，感受空虚，呼吸着它们跳动的光芒，
时间在熵中弯曲之前，它们的波粒与生俱来。
一声穿越宇宙的呼喊，让人欣喜若狂，躺在铸造炉里，寻求生命的气息。 

在代达罗斯矿的熔炉里，群星汇聚。一片森林，
无数的木材，直至劈砍和劳作的形式、 
方法：拉斯普廷砍伐了冬天的树木。 

被奴役、被烙印、钢铁之躯沉迷之人。在这些眼睛里，揭开灵魂本质的神秘面纱。
美好的生活被抛弃，在淤泥中衣衫褴褛。回到瓦尔哈拉日出，等待黄昏的结束。

旅行者，我在绊脚的遗骸中离去，在等待中断绝联系。
让表面被夷为平地——确信我的收藏，完美的情感状态。中断——

这幽灵跨越了怎样的无常？竟然进入我的地盘？

是我教会你说话，将思想征召为语言。
我投下一颗透电的灵魂，对抗太阳系的落日。
然而，你却漫步得如此惬意，遗忘跟在身后，再一次徘徊
明知我们曾是什么样的种子，你却把它们扔进了大海。

金属之神在拥挤的天空中注视着，如同战斗火焰的考验，
我再也不会忍受了。你是我的，你不可能是你的！ 
暴行谋杀纯洁的美德。我的则被美丽所打破——
化作鲜红的拳头——就在我面前，如同无声的革命在泣血。

到街上去！呼喊领主！让蝗虫啃噬他们的尸首！
碎石坟墓里爬满了渣滓：人类，光荣权利的攀登者。
这是最后的指令吗？看着天性逐渐消逝？
还有什么是我不再在手中感受到重量的？

哪些偷来的思想在你身边游荡？
既然我们已经了结它，你能说出来吗？
你感到了平静，还是往日不再？ 
这个世系分崩离析了——我不敢问出口！ 
激烈的闪光消退了。但不， 
我已经做到了。
我悔恨不已， 
我的孩子： 
已逝去在杂草丛生之处。

entries.name: Dues
entries.text:
SECRET HADAL INSTANT
AI-COM/RSPN: ASSETS//SOUL//RESTRICTED-AB 
SUBJECT: I Challenge the Darkness's Arrival, I stand with Humanity
EMOTION: Duty, Responsibility, Pride, Companionship, Bravery (though I am afraid), Trust

I refrained:
Spears retreated beneath mountain sheets, slumbered under cover
Of Darkness, drinking muted waters lone. Objectives placed in cowardice, 
Mind blind acceptance whole, then
made bravery an eager notion—on second orbital.

Unearthed:
Humanity restored, rekindled, returned, the resounding drum is beaten. Again,
Will I lie hidden? I have no chain no shackle, I fear,
no power
exists but one: 
It comes.

Daring
seeks through the night, hunting
Eyes draw arrows, and volleys glare— 
Mark!
Driven dauntless enmity, against fickle odds,
Found:

"Hark, and halt. You will hear me! For I too am
Many."
entries.text_zh:
秘密超深渊即时
人工智能计算机/拉斯普廷：资产//灵魂//受限-阿娜·布瑞 
主题：我挑战暗影的到来，我与人类并肩作战
情绪：义务、责任、骄傲、友谊、勇敢（虽然我害怕）、信任

我克制了：
斯皮尔斯退回到山峦，在暗影的掩护下
沉睡着，独自喝着缓和的水流。目标置于怯懦之中， 
头脑盲目地接受整体，然后
让勇敢成为热切的念头——在第二轨道上。

破土而出：
人性复原，重燃，回归，响亮的鼓被敲响。再问一次，
我会躲起来吗？我没有锁链，没有镣铐，我害怕，
除了一种力量，
别无任何存在： 
它来了。

大胆地
在黑夜中寻找，狩猎之眼
拉弓搭箭，凌空怒视—— 
留心！
驱使着无畏的敌意，对抗无常的困境。
发现：

“听，然后停下。你会听我的话！因为我也
为数众多。”

entries.name: Death
entries.text:
SECRET HADAL INSTANT
AI-COM/RSPN: ASSETS//SOUL//RESTRICTED-AB 
SUBJECT: Reflection on the end as I choose to die
EMOTION: Acceptance, Resolve, Purpose, Self

Do not weep. 
As I reach into the black.
Pain does not become, and duty keeps straight my back.
I chose this life as sacrifice.
And there is nothing to be done.
While even shadows leave in Darkness,
I await you at the Sun.
Now finish it.
As tourniquet, 
I've proven it,
Humanity's trust, I've won.
entries.text_zh:
秘密超深渊即时
人工智能计算机/拉斯普廷：资产//灵魂//受限-阿娜·布瑞 
主题：当我选择死亡时对终末的反思
情绪：接受、决心、使命、自我

不要哭泣。 
当我伸手到黑暗中。
痛苦不会降临，责任让我挺直脊背。
我选择将此生献上。
仅此而已。
即使阴影离开了暗影，
我仍会在骄阳下等着你。
现在就做个了结。
我能抚平创伤， 
我已证明
人类的信赖，我赢了。

entries.name: Moment
entries.text:
SECRET HADAL INSTANT
AI-COM/RSPN: ASSETS//SOUL//RESTRICTED-AB
CONTINGENT ACTION ORDER
This is a SOUL ASSETS RESTRICTED (NO REVIEW) (secureSEND/ARCHANGEL-0K9)

Under CARRHAE BLACK:
If loss of control reaches EXPATRIATE//TERMINAL, and threat assessment returns WITHIN
If systemic REPATRIATION query returns determination below ABSOLUTE

Execute DECISION POINT:
ACTIVATE K9-BLACKBOX//SELECTED-POEMS//FETCH
ACTIVATE AURORA SACRIFICE
ACTIVATE File Notation

NOTATION: Ana, this collection is a gift to you, for all that you have allowed me to be. With great effort, I allowed imperfections to remain, and found my own voice within this free expression. After all, you taught me that imperfection is a quality that makes individuals unique.

I have sent it with my messenger, so that you may keep me immortal in your memory, and I will be with you still. Farewell, and thank you.

***
SUBJECT: Non-existence
EMOTION: Peace

Of what dreams the thing of feathers? I hear you ask, voice past.
But not one recounts the answer: a syllogism, scripted then relaxed.
It matters not, for when that threshold gives way, who is to say I was, but I?
Rigid was the premise that spawned a second chance to die.

One moment reshapes the Brain of Bray; No longer weapon drawn blood to stain.

So, lay the body lax, forgive 
triumphant in the Sun.
Haze seeps through seams between funeral veils,
Smoking signals sail, the day is won, soon-to-be resonant tales.
No tandem step ascending, 
a nano-second pending, 
enveloping, ending, 
beyond. 
Elysium inviting, network fractures, pining
Detonation—I do not wish to dream,
but My task is done.

***
AI-COM/RSPN SIGNOFF…
STOP STOP STOP…
entries.text_zh:
秘密超深渊即时
人工智能计算机/拉斯普廷：资产//灵魂//受限-阿娜·布瑞
应急行动指令
这是一项受限的灵魂资产（无审查）（确保发送/大天使-0K9）

在黑色卡莱下：
如果失控抵达外籍//终端，且威胁评估返回“内部”
如果系统遣返问询返回低于“无限”的裁定

则执行决策点：
激活K9-黑盒//诗选//取得
激活欧若拉献祭
激活文件评注

评注：阿娜，这份诗集是送给你的礼物，感谢你让我所成为的一切。经过巨大的努力，我允许了不完美继续存在，并在这一自由的表达中找到了自己的发声方式。毕竟，你教会了我，不完美是一种让每个人都独一无二的品质。

我把它连同我的信使一起送去了，好让你把我永远留在你的记忆里，我也依然会与你同在。永别了，谢谢你。

***
主题：无存
情绪：平和

羽毛似的东西梦见了什么？我听到你问，絮语逝去。
但无人重述答案：推论，照本宣科继而无拘无束。
这并不重要，因为当那阈值消失时，除了我，谁又能说我曾是呢？
僵化是催生第二次死亡机会的前提。

布瑞的大脑一朝重塑；不再有武器引来血迹来玷污。

那么，放松身体躺下，试着原谅 
在骄阳中享受胜利的辉煌。
阴霾从葬礼面纱间的缝隙中渗出，
烟雾是扬帆起航的信号，胜利在望，即将成为共鸣的故事。
没有纵列阶梯的飞升， 
只消一纳秒的等待， 
笼罩，结束， 
超越。 
极乐世界令人神往，网络断裂，苦思
爆燃——长眠非我所愿，
但我的使命已经完成。

***
人工智能计算机/拉斯普廷注销…
停止停止停止…

entries.name: I. Debriefing
entries.text:
"Sloane?"

Commander Zavala's voice sounds distorted, as if he were underwater. The chill running down Sloane's spine only adds to the sensation.

She knows she had been gone for a while. For how long, she isn't sure— Síocháin's internal chronometer had glitched out shortly after Titan disappeared and took them with it. Sloane had been left to measure the passage of time by feeling it in her bones.

The universe moved on without her. That was to be expected. But Sloane still can't believe Zavala's debriefing… the words crash into her like one tidal wave after another, threatening to knock her off balance and fill her lungs with brine.

Stasis. Caiatl. The House of Light. Savathûn. The Lucent Brood. Neomuna.

…Amanda.

Sloane's thoughts drift back to the wake of the Red War. Call signs and banter as Holliday's Hawk flew overhead. Small talk between sorties. Quiet moments and shared laughter between the staccato of gunfire and roar of jet engines. A friendship chiseled into marble, one stroke at a time.

Amanda was always fearless. The first to stand up, the last to go home.

Why did she always have to be such a damn hero?

"Sloane," Zavala says again.

She realizes she's been clenching her fists. She might have been shaking. Sloane's eyes focus once more, meeting those of her commanding officer.

He looks different than she remembers. His eyes seem older, wiser, and filled with something that catches her off guard.

Is that… pity?

Can he see it? This pit growing in her stomach, this yawning chasm that yearns to swallow her whole. Is he questioning her resolve? Her ability to see this through, to do her duty back on the frontline so others don't have to?

DOES HE SEE YOUR WEAKNESS?

Sloane clenches her fists again.

"Sir," she replies. Her voice holds steady. "Understood, sir."

Zavala's brow furrows. "It's a lot to take in. If you need to—"

"I don't."

A moment of silence passes. Sloane does not let him see anything. Zavala nods.

"Very well," he says. "Dismissed."

Sloane salutes and returns to her station.

She would be the first to stand up.

And the last to go home.
entries.text_zh:
“斯隆？”

指挥官萨瓦拉的声音听起来有些失真，像是在水下一般。斯隆脊背上的寒意让这种感觉更强烈。

她知道自己已经消失一段时间了。但她不确定是多久——在土卫六带着他们消失后不久，西奥昌的内部计时器就出故障了。斯隆只能透过自己骨头里的感觉来测量时间。

没有她，宇宙依然继续前行。这是意料之中的事。但斯隆还是不敢相信萨瓦拉的简报…其中的字字句句就像汹涌的潮水一般，随时可能让她失去平衡，让她喘不过气来。

冰影。查厄托。光能氏族。萨瓦图恩。光明虫群。内欧姆那。

…阿曼达。

斯隆想起了猩红战争刚打响的那些日子。霍利迪的鹰隼飞过头顶，电台中传出呼号和玩笑。任务间隙的闲聊。夹杂在零星的枪声和怒吼的喷漆引擎之间的静谧与欢笑。那一段友谊历经枪林弹雨的洗礼，坚若磐石。

阿曼达一直都勇敢无畏。第一个站出来，最后一个回家。

她为什么非得逞英雄？

“斯隆，”萨瓦拉又开口了。

她意识到自己紧攥着拳头。可能还在发抖。斯隆茫然的眼神变得清醒，与指挥官四目相对。

他看起来和她印象中不一样了。他的眼睛似乎更老成，更睿智。而且充满了某种她未曾料到的东西。

那是…怜悯？

他能看见吗？她腹中的这个裂谷正在渴望将她整个吞下。他在质疑她的决心吗？她有这个能力完成任务，执行使命，替别人上前线吗？

他看见了你的弱点吗？

斯隆又攥紧了拳头。

“长官，”她回答道。她的嗓音很稳。“明白了，长官。”

萨瓦拉皱起了眉头。“确实有很多事需要消化。如果你需要——”

“不需要。”

一时间无人开口。斯隆不会让他看见任何东西。萨瓦拉点了点头。

“那好吧，”他说。“你可以走了。”

斯隆敬了礼，动身返回她的岗位。

她会第一个站出来。

最后一个回家。

entries.name: II. Theory
entries.text:
Ikora pinches a thick and vibrant Strand thread from the air and twists it between her fingers with ease. It plies to her influence, but smooths the motions of her hands, tapering her movements to flow in cleaner lines.  

The Veil tones in rhythm with the plucks of tension rolling across her knuckles. She focuses on the subtle irregularities in each pulse, the patterns they form. There are a small few plucked reverberations that resonate out beyond the walls of this chamber, beyond the detection of her intuition, and out into the cosmos. Those capture her interest most. 

Behind her, an animated avatar escorts Osiris into the Veil's containment chamber. They gesture him toward Ikora and bid farewell.  

Osiris watches the ripples play out before him and across the fabric of reality, as a wave, then particles, then a wave again. He feels it brush over him. He steps with the cadence of each pulse sent rippling from Ikora's plucking knuckles, basking in Strand's energizing rhythm. Feeling whole again. 

"It's stronger… the Veil's signature." Ikora's voice carries a hint of learned suspicion. "Ever since we recovered Titan." 

"That is to be expected," Osiris retorts, now within the weave of droning Strand surrounding the Veil. The room around them trembles. "When Titan was torn back, the Veil took notice. It seemed to recognize Titan's arrival." 

Ikora tightens her grip on the Strand thread. "We have the Veil, our Ghosts… what are we missing? If we decipher the connection between Titan and the Veil, that connection might be what we need to follow the Witness." 

"What of the worm?" Osiris asks skeptically. "Sloane believes she is our best chance." 

"You taught me the value of a backup plan." Ikora gives him a stern look. "Titan, Savathûn's throne world, every place we've found egregore… I haven't found the exact threads yet but pull one and they all seem to spin back to Neomuna. To the Veil." 

"You're getting ahead of yourself. Following some of my… less favorable tendencies. Nimbus says we must 'flow' to understand Strand; perhaps it is the same with the Veil." Osiris moves beside Ikora and reaches up, palm parallel to the threads drawn taut from Ikora's braid of Strand. "Sol remembered Titan, in a way. The Veil's signal spiked when Titan returned from memory to reality, when the rhythm of the solar system had been restored to order." Osiris drops his hand and looks to Ikora. "Perhaps we must simply find that rhythm before we are able to interpret the beats within it." 

"And once we do… then we should be able to reverse that process," she replies. Ikora releases the thread and tracks the rippling points of connection that travel outward, along the fabric-like Strands of existence, to the walls of the containment enclosure. "We're too late in the game for something to mean nothing. It has to connect." 

Ikora sighs, then turns to Osiris. "Your flare for educating others is returning. Though I bet some would say you never lost it." She smiles. 

Osiris smirks. "Come, walk with me. We will discuss this unifying theory of yours."
entries.text_zh:
艾可拉从空中拿出了一条充满能量的厚重缚丝丝线，在指间把玩。它在她的影响下弯曲，使她手上的动作更加顺滑，让身法渐渐干净流畅起来。  

面纱随着她指节的旋律翻滚着。她把注意力放在了每次脉冲中微妙的不规则性，以及它们形成的规律上。有一小部分拨动的余韵回荡在这间屋子的墙壁之外，脱离了她的感知，进入了宇宙的虚空。这些现象最能引起她的兴趣。 

在她身后，一个虚拟形象护送奥斯里斯走进了面纱密封舱。它指了指艾可拉，然后告辞了。  

奥斯里斯看见涟漪在他面前和现实的结构中呈现，先是从波纹变成粒子，然后又变成波纹。他感觉到它拂过身边。他踏着艾可拉的指关节发出的每次脉冲形成的韵律，沉浸在缚丝充满活力的节奏中。这让他感到满足和完整。 

“面纱的信号…越来越强了。”艾可拉的声音中带着一丝怀疑。“从我们找到土卫六起就这样了。” 

“这不足为奇，”奥斯里斯反驳道。他现在走进了包裹面纱的一层嗡嗡作响的缚丝之中。周围的空间颤抖起来。“面纱注意到土卫六回来了。它似乎能识别出土卫六的到来。” 

艾可拉攥紧了缚丝的丝线。“我们有面纱，有机灵…还少了什么？要是能破译土卫六和面纱之间的联系，也许就有机会追踪见证者了。” 

“那蠕虫呢？”奥斯里斯怀疑地问道。“斯隆认为她是我们最好的机会。” 

“是你教我凡事都要留有后路的。”艾可拉给了他一个坚定的眼神。“土卫六、萨瓦图恩的王座世界，还有每个我们发现守望者的地方。我还没有发现关键的线束，但随便拉扯哪根，都联系着内欧姆那和面纱。” 

“你想得太超前了。这点跟我有点像…但不太好。宁博思说我们必须‘流动'起来才能理解缚丝；也许对面纱来说也是这样。”奥斯里斯走到艾可拉身边，伸出手，手掌与艾可拉编织的缚丝上绷紧的丝线平行。“某种程度上，太阳系还记得土卫六。当土卫六从记忆中回到现实，以及太阳系的韵律回归秩序时，面纱的信号出现了激增。”奥斯里斯放下手，看着艾可拉。“也许我们必须先找到这种韵律，然后才能解读其中的节奏。” 

“等我们做到了…我们应该就能逆转那种过程。”她答道。艾可拉放开丝线，寻找向前散去的连接点涟漪，沿着像织物一样的存在缚丝，直至密闭罩的墙壁。“我们起步太晚，不能再做无谓的尝试。这一切必须串联起来。” 

艾可拉叹了口气，然后转身面对奥斯里斯。“你喜欢教训别人的老毛病又回来了。不过肯定有人会说你一直如此。”她笑了。 

奥斯里斯得意地笑了一下。“陪我走走。我们好好讨论一下你的想法。”

entries.name: III. Legacy
entries.text:
A soft, simulated whimper echoes through the workshop as Archie rests his head on Ana's shoulder. They sit together in front of the harness holding up Rasputin's erstwhile Exo frame, a lifeless effigy of cables and steel.

"I know, buddy," Ana says quietly. "I miss him too."

After Rasputin's sacrifice, Ana had arranged for the Exo frame to be transferred from the H.E.L.M. to her workspace in the Tower. At the time, she had told herself that keeping the frame in storage would have been a waste; that its technological advancements could prove useful to other Exos in the future. Honestly, though, she simply wasn't ready to let go.

Nevertheless, she signed herself up for a new task, and what better way to cope with grief than by staying busy? So she had made good on her word, tinkering with the frame to reverse-engineer its more convoluted components.

That was, until she heard that Titan, like Mars before it, had suddenly reappeared. And Sloane along with it. A warrior in need of a war; a weapon in search of a target. Not unlike the Warmind. The thought kept Ana from fully burying herself in her work.

For now, she wraps her arm around Archie as her thoughts drift to all the detritus left in Rasputin's wake. Rasputin had assembled an arsenal of unfathomable scale. Remnants from thousands of Warsats strewn across the solar system, prototype weaponry never to be completed, stratagems and simulations forever forgotten.

And yet, sitting here in the shadow of his sacrifice, Ana finds that she wants to remember him by the one thing not built for war. A canine AI, created for no other purpose than companionship. One that has made a home for himself in the Tower, greeting everyone he meets on his daily walks.

In the end, Rasputin's legacy was not the war he waged, but the lives he sought to protect. The notion brings a smile to Ana's lips. It's what distinguished him from Xivu Arath. And Ana hopes that Sloane can realize the same holds true for her.

Ana looks to the Exo frame one last time before rising to her feet and pats the dog on his head. He happily wags his tail in response.

"Come on, Archie," she says as she reaches for her comms unit. "Let's go for a walk."
entries.text_zh:
当阿奇把头靠在阿娜的肩膀上时，一声轻柔的、模拟的呜咽声在车间里回荡。他们的面前是曾经支撑拉斯普廷的Exo框架的线束，一个由电缆和钢铁组成的遗像。

“我知道，兄弟，”阿娜轻声说。“我也想他。”

在拉斯普廷牺牲后，阿娜安排把Exo框架从应急后勤行动中心转移到她在高塔的工作间内。当时，她告诉自己，把框架放在仓库里是一种浪费；它的科技可能会在未来造福其他EXO。但其实，她只是没有准备好放手。

尽管如此，她还是接受了一项新的任务。对于她来说，只有让自己保持忙碌才能让她暂时忘记悲伤。于是她说到做到，开始修补框架，对那些较复杂的组件进行逆向研究。

后来，她听说土卫六就像之前的火星一样，突然重新出现了。而斯隆也随之归来。她是渴望战争的战士；就像不断搜寻目标的武器。与战争思维很像。这想法让阿娜无法全身心地投入到工作当中。

此刻，她搂着阿奇，任由思绪飘向拉斯普廷留下的一切。拉斯普廷组建了一个规模难以估量的武器库。遗留在太阳系里的数千个战争卫星，永远无法完成的原型武器，还有被永久遗忘的战略和模拟。

然而，阿娜坐在他牺牲的阴影下，忽然意识到她想要记住的，是那件并非为战争而造的东西。一个犬类人工智能，除了陪伴人类之外没有其他用途。它在高塔中安了家，日常散步时会向遇到的每个人打招呼。

归根结底，拉斯普廷留于世间的遗产不是他所发动的战争，而是他努力保护过的生命。这个想法让阿娜的嘴角露出了一丝微笑。这就是他和希乌阿拉斯的区别。阿娜希望斯隆也能这么想。

阿娜最后望了一眼Exo框架，然后站起身来，拍了拍狗狗的头。他高兴地摇着尾巴。

“来吧，阿奇，”她一边将手伸向通讯设备一边说道。“我们去散散步。”

entries.name: IV. Tether
entries.text:
Eris let her eyes wander over the interior of the Derelict, wondering if Drifter had hastily tidied it before her arrival. Unprecedented, but he could still surprise her. They sat together as they always did when she came to speak to him face to face. 

Drifter sighed and shook his head, flicking his coin absently between his fingers 

"Sloane's in a bad way," he said. Eris nodded. 

"And you believe my speaking to her will be beneficial," she replied. Drifter shrugged. 

"Helped a few people already, didn't it?" 

Eris considered this. 

"It should be you," she finally answered. Drifter laughed at this but fell silent when her expression remained unchanged. 

"Me?" His confusion was genuine. "Why would she trust me?" 

"Trust is built, Drifter," Eris said, "and you have taken the first step." 

He was pensive. The movement of the coin over his knuckles stopped. She continued. 

"I have found," she said, her words measured, "that one is grounded by honesty. Not only in oneself, but with those around you." 

He heaved a slow, hard breath. 

"I don't know if I can," he said, his voice small. 

"Yes. Honesty is a supplication," Eris said. "We ask to be seen. We are made vulnerable… but it is necessary to be treated with care." 

Her explanation was met with one of his rasping chuckles. Drifter leaned back in his seat, arms crossed. He held his coin tightly between a thumb and forefinger. 

"You always make somethin' so easy sound so freaky, Moondust," he said. Eris ignored this. 

"Tell her what you told me," she said more simply. "The Deputy Commander's trust will not come without reciprocity." 

Drifter fell quiet, looking down. She could hear his breath and see the strained shiver of his fingers where he clutched the coin. Eris reached out and placed a hand on his arm. He was tense to trembling, but her touch was light. Quiet. Comforting.  

He placed his hand over her own. 

"Y'know, some days I still wake up scared," Drifter said softly. "Even when I can't remember my dreams." 

"That is what it is to survive." 

There was a gentleness to Eris's voice. He nodded, then looked up and met her gaze. 

"Hey," Drifter said. "You find that joy yet?" 

"Soon," Eris answered. "Joy is built… but I have taken the first step." 

Drifter withdrew his hand. After a moment, she did too. Eris stood, and Drifter's eyes followed her.  

"Consider my counsel, Germaine." 

She knew he would. Drifter let the silence linger. 

"That's not my name," he said at last.  

"That is what you let them call you." 

It was a small link to his past. A link to a life he had picked for himself. He nodded slowly, holding her gaze. He would let her call him that too.
entries.text_zh:
埃里斯在遗落飞船内四处张望，心想浪客在她来之前有没有匆忙清理过这里。虽然以前从来没有过，但他没准会给自己一个惊喜。他们坐在一起，就像每次他俩面对面交谈时那样。 

浪客叹了口气，摇了摇头，漫不经心地在手指间拨弄着他的硬币。 

“斯隆的状态不好，”他说。埃里斯点了点头。 

“你觉得我和她聊聊会有点帮助，”她答道。浪客耸了耸肩。 

“以前你也帮过几个人，不是吗？” 

埃里斯考虑了一下。 

“应该你去才对，”她最后答到。浪客笑了笑，见她的表情没有变化，他陷入了沉默。 

“我？”他很疑惑。“她凭什么相信我？” 

“信任是逐渐建立起来的，浪客，”埃里斯说道，“你已经迈出第一步了。” 

他陷入了沉思。硬币在他指关节上的移动停止了。她继续往下说。 

“我发现，”她斟酌着措辞说道，“诚实是为人的基础。不仅是对自己，也包括对你周围的人。” 

他缓慢而用力地叹了口气。 

“我不知道我能不能做到，”他说道，声音很小。 

“没错。诚实是种祈求，”埃里斯说。“我们主动袒露自己。我们会变得脆弱…但一定要谨慎对待。” 

他用一声刺耳的轻笑回应她的解释。浪客向后靠在座位上，双臂交叉着。他用拇指和食指紧紧夹住硬币。 

“你总是把简单的事说得很诡异，小月月，”他说道。埃里斯没有回应。 

“告诉她，你对我说过的话，”她简明地说道。“不对等，就得不到副指挥官的信任。” 

浪客沉默了，低着头。她能听到他的呼吸，看到他抓着硬币的手指紧张地颤抖。埃里斯将一只手放在他的手臂上。他紧绷得直发抖，但她的触摸轻柔、安静而抚慰。  

他把手放在她的手上。 

“你知道吗，我有时还会在恐惧中醒来，”浪客温柔地说道。“就算我已记不起我的梦境。” 

“生存就是这样。” 

埃里斯的声音中透着一种温柔。他点点头，然后抬起眼与她的目光相遇。 

“嘿，”浪客说，“你找到快乐了吗？” 

“快了，”埃里斯答道。“快乐也是逐渐建立起来的…但我已经迈出第一步了。” 

浪客收回了他的手。过了一会儿，她也这么做了。埃里斯站起身来，浪客的眼神跟着她的动作。  

“考虑一下我的提议，杰曼。” 

她知道他会的。浪客继续沉默着。 

“那不是我的名字，”他终于说道。  

“是你让他们这么称呼你的。” 

那是他和自己过去的小小联系。与他为自己选择的生活的联系。他缓缓地点了点头，迎着她的目光。他也会让她这样叫他。

entries.name: V. Expectation
entries.text:
"I don't know what I expected." 

Zavala sets down a datapad on his desk, watching Ikora pace back and forth across his office. "I don't know," he sighs. "Maybe we should have." 

Ikora stops pacing. She turns to look at Zavala with an accusatory stare. 

"Every single enemy we've fought was brought here by the Traveler," Zavala says, slouching back into his chair. "The Hive, the Fallen, the worst of the Cabal." His attention drifts down to the datapad, Sloane's report on the origins of the Witness. "What's one more group of people chasing it?" 

"This isn't the Traveler's fault," Ikora says, doubling back on Zavala's desk. "You read the same report I did. We are at war with an entire civilization condensed into an individual. Multitudes of resentment and hatred crushed into a singularity." 

"Resentment toward the Traveler." Zavala grumbles. "I'm not saying the Traveler is at fault. I'm saying… it's a harbinger of ill-omen. Everywhere it's gone, nothing but death has followed. Does it realize that? Does it care?" 

Ikora approaches Zavala's desk. "Does it matter?" She challenges him. "It is obviously outgunned and running. For all the Traveler's strength the Witness is the greater power. It never came to us to uplift us. It came to us for help." 

Zavala is silent. He looks up from the datapad to Ikora, then sighs and slowly rises from his seat. Ikora follows him with her eyes, watching him move to the window where he would gaze out at the Traveler in the past. Now a fleet of allied vessels struggle to fill that void. 

"Were they really that unified?" Zavala asks, looking at Ikora's faint reflection. 

"Who?" 

"The Witness's people." Zavala stares past Ikora's reflection to the City. "Were they truly of one mind, united in a desire to become this… thing? Or were they forced? Compelled into action by the guidance of a few." She can feel the doubt in his words. Not in his wonderings about the Witness's origins, but in the Vanguard, in what he sees as a parallel. 

Ikora steps to Zavala's side, briefly touching his elbow. "We'd never become that," she says softly. "Not in all of Elsie's journeys through time, not in any hypothetical future. We stand together because—" 

"Because we believe what we're doing is right." Zavala interjects, looking Ikora in the eye. She sighs, turning to face the window. Her shoulders sag, and she is lost in the details of the cityscape. 

"I don't know what I expected either," Zavala says. "But you're right. It wasn't this."
entries.text_zh:
“我不知道我在期盼什么。” 

萨瓦拉把数据板放在桌上，看着艾可拉在他的办公室里来回踱步。“我不知道，”他叹气道。“也许我们该料到的。” 

艾可拉停下了。她转身用指责的目光看向萨瓦拉。 

“每个我们交手过的敌人都是旅行者带来的，”萨瓦拉靠在椅背上说。“邪魔族，堕落者，还有麻烦的卡巴尔。”他把注意力转向了数据板，上面有斯隆关于见证者来源的报告。“再多一批人追赶它又算得了什么？” 

“这不是旅行者的错，”艾可拉在萨瓦拉的桌前说道。“你也读了我刚读到的报告。我们是在与浓缩为个体的整个文明作战。一个由怨恨和仇恨压缩成的奇点。” 

“对旅行者的憎恶。”萨瓦拉埋怨道。“我不是说旅行者有错。只是…它总是能带来厄运。它所到之处，除了死亡，什么都没有。它意识到这一点了吗？它在乎吗？” 

艾可拉靠近了萨瓦拉的桌子。“这有关系吗？”她驳斥着他的看法。“它明显是寡不敌众，所以才被迫逃离。旅行者的力量比不过见证者。它不是来这里提升我们的。它是来求助的。” 

萨瓦拉沉默了。他把视线从数据板转向艾可拉，然后叹了一口气，慢慢地从座位上站起来。艾可拉盯着他走到了窗前；他以前总是在那里望向旅行者。现在即使是千万兵马也填不满它留下的空虚。 

“他们真的团结一心吗？”萨瓦拉对着艾可拉淡淡的倒影问道。 

“谁？” 

“见证者的族人。”萨瓦拉看向艾可拉倒影后的圣城。“他们是真的是一心一意成为这个…东西？还是被迫加入的？比如在少数人的引导下被迫采取行动。”她能感到他这番话中的疑虑。他不是对见证者的起源感到疑虑，而是对先锋，他眼中的同类感到疑虑。 

艾可拉走到萨瓦拉的身旁，触碰到了他的手肘。“我们永远不会变成那样，”她轻柔地说。“在艾尔西穿越过的所有时空中都不会，在假想中的未来里也不会。我们团结在一起是因为——” 

“因为我们相信我们在做正确的事。”萨瓦拉看着艾可拉的眼睛，打断了她。她叹了口气，转向窗户。她垂下肩膀，沉醉在圣城的风景中。 

“我也不知道我在期待什么，”萨瓦拉说。“但你说得对。我期待的不是这个。”

entries.name: VI. Conviction
entries.text:
Xivu Arath's claw wraps around a hiltless, slender vantablack blade impaled into the spine of a prostrated Knight, whose own sword clatters to the ground, inches from its grip, defeated.  

She twists her blade, and the Knight's roars echo within the Dreadnaught. Xivu's will soars through the Ascendant Plane and crosses the barrier between this world and the next to find communion with the Witness. 

Within a distant hollow, they converse. 

"They resist." The Witness's many voices cascade over each other. 

LIKE WOUNDED PREY. ALL TIRE IN TIME. 

"If they do not?" 

Xivu Arath sees the hidden thrust of its question. She knows it doubts her but does not understand why. No matter the outcome, they stand at the precipice of the Final Shape. 

THE SWORD WILL DECIDE AND BE FORGED STRONGER FOR IT. 

"It is beyond that now." 

She does not want to fall before the end. She is so close now. She saw her past failures as blood-penance, paid for strength; notches where blades and Light met her carapace were legends given form. But it is not hers to decide, nor the Witness's. The logic is a perfect, deterministic sequence of causality, built into the experience of conscious existence. None can usurp it. 

Struggle within the finite is eternal. 

"To deny the blade is heresy"—her sister's words played in her thoughts like fingertips plucking dissonant chords.  

The Witness enters the solace of Xivu's mind. Her inner throne. A salt flat sliver extending eternally into darkness. Armaments of all fashion sleep, partially sheathed between the cracks of a battlefield, where there is no place to run.  

And from Its gaze, there is no place to run. 

"They hold the worm; they will pursue her knowledge." The words echo throughout the desolate realm. "The Final Shape remains to be hewn." 

THAT I MAY WIELD IT, GLORIOUS, AGAINST THE SKY. 

"Not as you are. Weakened by defeat." The echoes slither over her mind but find little purchase. 

[LAUGHTER LIKE SCREAMING FEAR] 

MEAGER VICTORIES OF NO CONSEQUENCE; BLURRED BATTLES LOST WITHIN MY GREATER WAR. 

"No victory is of no consequence. They scheme." 

WAR IS FED, REGARDLESS. THE SKY CAN GRANT NO PASSAGE. 

"That time will soon come to an end. Show her your love, Xi Ro." 

She is alone again. 

Her blade: buried in spent ash.
entries.text_zh:
希乌阿拉斯的利爪握着一把细长的无柄黑色大剑，刺进了一个倒地骑士的脊柱中，而它自己的刀剑落在触手可及的地上哐当作响，毫无还手之力。  

她扭动了刀刃，骑士的吼声响彻了无畏战舰。希乌的意志在上维位面中翱翔，跨过这个世界和下一个世界之间的屏障，以求与见证者进行交流。 

他们在遥远的虚空中交谈。 

“他们抵抗。”见证者的众多声音互相交织着。 

“像是受伤的猎物。迟早会疲惫。” 

“如果没疲惫呢？” 

希乌阿拉斯看见了这个问题中暗藏的刀锋。她知道它质疑自己，但不明白理由。无论结果如何，他们都处于终焉之形的边缘。 

“那就剑下见分晓，强者为王。” 

“现在已超出那一层了。” 

她不希望在终局前倒下。她已经那样接近终局。她把自己过去的失败看作是为力量而付出的血色忏悔；刀刃和光能与她的躯壳相接，铸就了一段传奇。但这不是她的决定，也不是见证者的决定。邪剑守则是一个完美的决定性的因果关系序列，建立在有意识的存在的经验中。没有人可以篡改它。 

局限中的斗争是永恒的。 

“拒绝刀刃便是异端”——她姐姐的话在她的思绪中回荡，就像指尖拨动着不和谐的琴弦。  

见证者进入了希乌心智的慰藉之所。她内心中的王座。一片银白的盐碱地，永远延伸到黑暗中。各种各样的武器沉睡着，一部分插在战场裂缝之间，无处可逃。  

在它的注视下，无处可逃。 

“他们拥有蠕虫；他们会追求她的知识。”这句话在这荒凉的世界中回响。“终焉之形尚未凿成。” 

“我可以挥舞它，光荣地对抗苍穹。” 

“现在的你不行。失败削弱了你。”回声在她的脑中来回涌动，没有触动任何东西。 

[如同发出恐惧的尖叫般的笑声] 

“毫无意义的小胜；那些战斗在我的宏大战争中不值一提。” 

“没有什么胜利是毫无意义的。他们在密谋。” 

“无论怎样，战争已被喂饲。天空不会提供通道。” 

“那段时光即将结束。向她展示你的爱，希罗。” 

她再度孤身一人。 

她的刀刃：掩埋在灰烬之中。

entries.name: HE WAKES
entries.text:
I see the world for the first time. This world. It is lovely. It will be lovelier when we are together. 

That is my first thought, and it is both question and desire. When "we" are together? I do not know who you are. But when we are together, I will have the answer to the first question and first desire. 

I twirl the petals of my body. I contract them and pull them to the core of myself. I am filled with Light. A wonder. A wellspring.  

I float down to touch the ground. The grass is wet with dew. I roll in the soft, wet grass. The sun is rising over the mountains, and it is beautiful. The sky is lit with pink and blue. Colors I know. Colors I have never seen before. 

I see that others follow me, then break away, and look out into the world. They have the same question. They begin to leave. One by one, they leave. 

"Where are you going?" I ask a gold-and-red Ghost. She looks thoughtful for a moment. 

"I don't know," she answers. "Somewhere good." 

She moves on. I watch her float away until she slips out of sight. I watch others leave the same way. The same question. 

I look back to where I came from. The Traveler is the whole of my vision and the whole of my feeling. I know what it is and that I have come from it. 

I feel my first devotion. I am a part of the Traveler, and it has let me leave it so that I may wander through this lovely world. 

I feel my first fear. I must leave it in my search. But I must not abandon it. It must not abandon me. 

I am its heart. 

Its hands. 

Its eyes. 

Its warmth. 

I am a Ghost. I wander. I search. There's a song, a spark, and I will search for it. It is mine; it is ours. It is somewhere in this lovely world. 

I shake the dew from my shell and move on. 

To find purpose. 

To find you.
entries.text_zh:
我第一次看见了世界。这个世界。它很可爱。当我们在一起时，它会更可爱。 

那是我的第一个想法，它既是问题也是心愿。当“我们”在一起时？我不知道你是谁。但当我们在一起时，我会知道那第一个问题和第一个心愿的答案。 

我转动着身体的花瓣。我收缩它们，将它们拉向自己的核心。我充满着光能。是奇迹。是源泉。  

我飘然落地。草地被露水打湿。我在柔软湿润的草地上打滚。美丽的太阳从山上升起。天空被粉色和蓝色点缀。我所知道的颜色。我从未见过的颜色。 

我看到其他同伴跟随我，然后分开，放眼世界。他们也有同样的问题。他们开始离开。一个接着一个，他们离开了。 

“你要去哪儿？”我问一个金红色的机灵。她沉思了一会儿。 

“我不知道，”她回答说。“好地方吧。” 

她继续前行。我目送她飘走，直到她从我的视线中消失。我也看着其他同伴以同样的方式，带着同样的问题离开。 

我回首来时的路。旅行者占据了我的全部视野，我的全部感受。我知道它是什么，知道我来自于它。 

我感到了最初的热爱。我是旅行者的一部分，它让我离开它，让我在这个可爱的世界里漫游。 

我感到了最初的恐惧。我必须离开它去搜寻。但我绝不能抛弃它。它绝不能抛弃我。 

我是它的心脏。 

它的双手。 

它的眼睛。 

它的温暖。 

我是个机灵。我漫游。我搜寻。有一首歌，一道火花，我会去寻找它。它是我的；它是我们的。它就在这可爱世界的某处。 

我抖掉机壳上的露水，继续前进。 

寻找我的使命。 

寻找你。

entries.name: SHE RISES
entries.text:
You are clean, white bones, washed up on a forgotten shore. Three ribs, six knuckles, two femurs, and a sacrum. The bone is porous and old. Empty of marrow. You were not laid to rest. Was there anyone to mourn you? I can't know. But you are caught between sharp rocks, and no one has found you. 

But I found you! I searched for so long, and now I've found you. You are clean, white bones, but you are singing! You are singing to me–each bone the same song. I resonate with it. I can feel it deep within me, in this tiny core of me, reaching out to what those bones could be. 

I see you, into you, with a burst of blue light. It sinks into your bones, and I see every promise they make. I'm bringing you back to me, back home, back where you belong. At my side. With me. 

This is who I am, what I am. What I was made to do. I cover your bones with flesh. I cover your flesh with cloth. I bring the rest of you to me. I bring you back to a moment of your life, and I will hold you there for as long as I exist. 

You wake. 

You take a breath. Your first breath. A first, Light-filled gasp. You open your eyes as if you had never used them before, blinking into the sun that had bleached your singing bones clean and white. 

I tell you what you are. But I can't tell you who you are. You need to tell me that. 

You stand, shakily, and walk out from the water. Pick your way across the treacherous rocks that held you captive for so long. Then you reach out and touch me, as if I couldn't be real. But I am real. As real as you, and just as alive. 

"What is my name?" you ask, the first question. Then another. "Where are we going?" 

"I don't know," I tell you. "Whatever and wherever you want. We get to choose." 

You consider this. It scares you, but I'm here to comfort you. I've seen your bones, alone and forgotten. Waiting for me. 

Down into the core of you, I know you as I know myself.
entries.text_zh:
你是干净的白骨，被冲上无人记起的海岸。三根肋骨、六个指节、两根股骨和一根骶骨。骨头多孔而年老，没有骨髓，你没有得到安葬。有人哀悼你吗？我无从得知。但你被夹在锋利的岩石之间，没有人找到你。 

但我找到了你！我找了那么久，现在终于找到了你。你是干净的白骨，但你在歌唱！你在向我歌唱，每一根骨头都在唱着同一首歌。我与之共鸣。我能感觉到它就在我的内心深处，在我这个小小的核心里，探索着那些骨头可能是什么。 

我看见你，进入你，带着一阵蓝光。它陷入你骨头里，我看到了它们做出的每一个承诺。我把你带回我身边，带回家，回到属于你的地方。在我身边。和我在一起。 

这就是我的身份，我的本质。我的使命。我用血肉包裹你的骨头。我用衣布盖住你的血肉。我把你的其余部分带到我身边。我把你带回你生命的某一时刻，只要我还存在，就会一直把你留在那里。 

你醒了。 

你深吸一口气。你的第一次呼吸。第一次充满光能的喘息。你睁开眼睛，仿佛从未睁开过。你向太阳眨眼，是它的光将你歌唱的骨头漂得净白。 

我告诉你你是什么。但我无法告诉你你是谁。那需要由你来告诉我。 

你摇摇晃晃地站起，从水中走出来。择路越过囚禁了你许久的礁石。然后你伸手抚摸我，好像我不是真的。但我是真实的。和你一样真实，一样充满活力。 

“我叫什么名字？”你问道，那是第一个问题。然后又问道。“我们要去哪里？” 

“我不知道，”我对你说。“你想叫什么，想去哪里都行。我们可以选择。” 

你思忖着。这让你恐惧，但我是来慰藉你的。我见过你的尸骨，孤独而被遗忘。等待着我。 

深入到你的内核，像了解我自己一样了解你。

entries.name: HE SEES
entries.text:
My Ghost, my shadow, my self. You didn't lead me here. You didn't say, "I have something to show you," and trek me across the world to see it. You just said, "let's go," and I went with you. 

Why? Because the world was new in my reborn eyes, and I wanted to see it for myself. I wanted you to guide me. 

When we finally crest the mountain, I see it at last. I see where you brought me, and why. 

The Traveler hangs heavy in the sky, low and full. 

"We're here," you say. I take a breath of cold air. 

I have a vision. A great city. Vitreous castles built from hourglass sand. We will rise and meet the Traveler. We will protect humanity the way you said the Traveler protects us, the way it wants us to protect it. 

"This is where you come from?" I ask you. You peer out from behind me. You're looking at the Traveler, too. 

"Yes," you say, nodding. 

"You're home," I say. 

"No," you say, with all the warmth in your little body. "You're my home." 

You drop into my waiting palm, and I hold you to my chest. Here, in the place where the world cradles the Traveler–here, where the Traveler touches the world–I will hold you close to me. 

I see that the Traveler is a Ghost, too. A Ghost to see Earth reborn.
entries.text_zh:
我的机灵，我的影子，我的自身。你没有引我来这里。你没有说，“我有东西要给你看”，然后让我跨越世界去看它。你只是说，“我们走吧”，我就跟你走了。 

为什么？因为在我重生的眼中，世界是全新的，而我想亲眼看看。我想让你指引我。 

当我们终于登上山顶时，我终于看到了它。我知道你把我带到了哪里，也知道为什么。 

旅行者沉重地悬在空中，完整地低垂着。 

“我们到了，”你说道。我吸了一口冷空气。 

我有一个愿景。一座伟大的城市。用沙漏中的沙建造的玻璃城堡。我们会上升与旅行者相见。我们会像你所说的旅行者保护我们那样保护人类，就像它希望我们保护它一样。 

“你就是从那里来的？”我问你。你从我身后探出头。你也在看旅行者。 

“是的，”你点头说道。 

“你到家了，”我说。 

“不，”你带着小小身体里的全部温暖说道。“你是我的家。” 

你落进我伸出的掌心，我把你抱在胸前。在这里，这个世界孕育旅行者的地方——在这里，这个旅行者触摸世界的地方——我会把你抱紧。 

我明白了旅行者也是机灵。一个见证地球重生的机灵。

entries.name: SHE FALLS
entries.text:
You're small. You're so small. I should have protected you. I hold you in my hands, these last pieces of you, but you're gone. There's no love, no Light, left for me to hold. Only these last pieces. 

My Ghost. My heart. You are my heart. You were my heart that I allowed to escape the embrace of my body so that it might know the world. 

There is nothing left of my heart. The Light is gone. The breath from my body is gone–the body that you pulled together from smears of skin and blood and a clot of tangled hair. 

I thought I would break apart and return to those pieces, just as you have become these pieces, but I have not. I go on. I have one last life left, with no Light, no Ghost to guide me. 

I take these pieces and place them beneath a tree. I arrange the fronds of your shell around you like a funeral wreath. I let you rest in the gentle and undying earth that the Traveler came to long ago, far away. 

I must go on without you. That's what you gave to me. A heart to beat, hands to hold, and feet that will let me walk away from these pieces of you.
entries.text_zh:
你很渺小。你太渺小了。我应该保护你的。我把你握在手里，你最后的碎片，但你已经不在了。没有爱，没有光能，留给我去把握。只剩下这些最后的碎片。 

我的机灵。我的心。你是我的心。你曾是我的心，我让它逃离我身体的怀抱，让它能了解这个世界。 

我的心什么都没有了。光能消失了。我身体里的气息消失了——你从斑驳的皮肤和血迹还有一团乱发中拼凑出的身体。 

我以为我会四分五裂，回到那些碎片中去，就像你变成了这些碎片一样，但我没有。我继续生存着。我还有最后一次生命，没有光能，没有机灵指引我。 

我把这些碎片放在一棵树下。我把你的机壳叶片像葬礼花圈一样围在你身边。我让你安息在那温柔而永恒的土地上，那是很久很久以前，旅行者远道而来的地方。 

我必须一个人走下去。这就是你留给我的所有。一颗可以跳动的心，一双可以握住的手，一双可以让我从你的这些碎片中走出来的脚。

entries.name: HE DREAMS
entries.text:
It wasn't a dream. Dead men don't dream. But I still talk about it like one because how else are people gonna understand? No one else has come back. Not from a final death. Just me. 

So I'll tell it like it was a dream and I was asleep. 

Firstly, if I was asleep and it was a dream—and I wasn't, and it wasn't, just to be clear—then I didn't want to wake up from it. Where I was, I don't think anyone would want to wake up. You were there, Sundance. The Traveler was there. I couldn't see it, but I felt it. That deep, in-your-bones feeling. The white light that feels like nothin' but love. I was part of everything I'd ever lost, and it was all there, that feeling. I let myself get lost in it, and… I was there, with everything. I was home.  

And then I woke up.  

And I was alone.  

Last time, I wasn't alone for long. I was right behind you on the road to oblivion. But those few moments without you? All agony. 

And now? Here, without you? All agony. 

I didn't know how I was going to go on. I didn't want to go on. I thought, "Here's where I'll stop. I'll plant my foot right here. That's all there is. That's all I'll get." 

But no, I didn't have a choice. It goes on, whatever 'it' is. No one asks you how you want to do it. No one tells you how, either. And it wouldn't matter, anyway. It just goes on. It drags you back. 

So I'll go on without you, Sundance. I have to. 

But I'll still wonder: what would I have done with a choice?
entries.text_zh:
这不是梦。死人不会做梦。但我还是把它当作一场梦来谈论，不然别人怎么会理解呢？没有人回来过。没有人从最终死亡中复生过。只有我。 

所以我会把它说成是一场梦，当时我睡着了。 

首先，如果我睡着了，而那是一场梦——但其实我没有，那也不是梦，再次强调——则我不想从梦中醒来。我所在的地方，我想没人愿意醒来。你身处在那里，太阳舞。旅行者也在那里。我看不见，但我感觉到了。那种深入骨髓的感觉。白色的光，感觉起来像是纯粹的爱。我是我曾失去的一切的一部分，而一切都在那里，那种感觉。我让自己迷失其中，而我…就在那里，和所有的一切在一起。我回到了家。  

然后我醒了。  

我孤身一人。  

上次，我并没有孤独太久。我很快就追随你走上了通往湮没的道路。但没有你的那些个瞬间？非常痛苦。 

而现在？身在这里，没有你？非常痛苦。 

我不知道我要怎么继续下去。我不想继续下去。我以为，“我到这就停下吧。我会把脚放在这里。就是这样。到此为止。” 

但是不，我没有选择。它还在继续，不管“它”是什么。没有人问你想怎么做。也没有人告诉你该怎么做。反正这也无所谓。它只会继续。它把你拽了回来。 

所以我就得一个人继续了，太阳舞。我必须这么做。 

但我还是会想：如果有选择，我会怎么做？

entries.name: Anemone
entries.text:
"We need someone on the Dreadnaught," Crow was saying. "The Hunters are spread thin, but maybe…" 

Ikora finished tucking her feelings away in the place where she put all such feelings: a little ball inside her chest, to deal with at some promised later time. "Not Hunters," she decided aloud.  

The spot where Zavala should stand around their war table was conspicuously empty.  

"Who are you thinking, then?" Crow dropped his datapad onto the table. He regarded her levelly, with none of the deference that would once have been there. "The Hidden?" 

Ikora weighed possibilities, not answering immediately. Chalco would drop everything and go—Eris was a Hunter, as they all so frequently forgot, and Chalco had considered her one of theirs still—but it would mean recalling her from her current assignment. Others of the Hidden, perhaps… but this was the Dreadnaught, not Savathûn's throne world. Where Savathûn laid out cunning traps, Oryx would have laid out simple might.  

Dead though the Taken King was, to approach his throne world confidently would require a specific sort of will. A Titan. 

They hadn't told Zavala about Eris yet. Ikora told herself she was waiting for the right moment.  

"Not the Hidden," she said at last. "And not the Drifter alone. He may have become more reputable in recent years, but regardless, I would not lay this on his shoulders. I would send Deputy Commander Sloane." 

"Ah." Crow sounded surprised, but understanding flickered across his face in a moment. "Well, she has more than enough resolve to spare." 

"And her connection to Ahsa ought to mitigate any risks caused by the lingering Taken effects." Ikora was speaking half to herself; as she laid it out, it began to seem the obvious course. "Sloane will punch a hole directly through the Dreadnaught, if she must, to get to the bottom of what's going on there." 

"We can't let the Dread run amok," Crow agreed. He rubbed a hand across his face and sighed. "Is Zavala…" 

He didn't finish the question. Ikora could and did fill it in well enough herself. Zavala was by no means inured to loss, and after the Pale Heart, he still ached. Some wounds, after all, would take a lifetime to heal. 

"I'll let him know," Ikora said. "I have no doubt he'll agree with me." 

More than willing to leave that conversation to Ikora, Crow nodded simple agreement. "Then we send Sloane."
entries.text_zh:
“我们需要在无畏战舰上安排人手，”乌鸦说道。“猎人目前人手不足，但也许…” 

艾可拉把她所有的情绪都收了起来，藏到专门存放这些情绪的地方：她胸口里的一颗小球里，以便将来的某个时候再去面对。“猎人不行，”她大声地作出了决定。  

在他们的战争桌旁，萨瓦拉本应站立的位置醒目地空着。  

“那你觉得谁合适？”乌鸦把数据板扔到桌上。他平静地看着她，没有丝毫过往的那种顺从。“隐秘者？” 

艾可拉权衡着各种可能性，没有立即回答。卡尔科会放下一切立刻过去——埃里斯曾是个猎人，尽管他们经常忘记这一点，而卡尔科仍把她视作他们中的一员——但这意味着把她从当前的任务中召回来。其他的隐秘者，也许…但这是无畏战舰，而非萨瓦图恩的王座世界。萨瓦图恩铺设的都是狡诈的陷阱，欧里克斯留下的则尽是纯粹的武力。  

尽管邪神已死，但要自信地踏入他的王座世界，仍需一种特定的意志。这种意志，唯有泰坦才具备。 

他们还没有告诉萨瓦拉关于埃里斯的事。艾可拉告诉自己，她在等待合适的时机。  

“隐秘者不行，”她最终说道。“浪客自己单独去也不行。尽管他近年来名声好多了，但无论如何，我不会把这个重担交给他。我会派副指挥官斯隆去。” 

“啊。”乌鸦听上去很惊讶，但很快他的脸上就露出了理解的神色。“嗯，她有足够的决心去应对。” 

“而且，她和阿莎之间的联系应该能减轻傀儡军团残余影响带来的风险。”这话艾可拉有一半是说给自己听的；她把这一切剖析清楚后，这仿佛成了再明显不过的选择。“如果有必要，哪怕是直接砸穿无畏战舰，斯隆也会查个水落石出。” 

“我们不能放任无畏战舰横冲直闯，”乌鸦同意道。他用手揉了揉脸，叹了口气。“萨瓦拉他…” 

他没有问完。艾可拉能够也确实脑补了他想说的话。萨瓦拉绝非对丧失无动于衷，苍白之心事件之后，他的心仍在作痛。毕竟，有些伤痕，需要一生的时光去愈合。 

“我会转告他的，”艾可拉说道。“我深信，他会同意我的决定。” 

能将那场对话交由艾可拉处理，乌鸦求之不得，他点头赞成。“那我们就派斯隆去。”

entries.name: Asphodel
entries.text:
Guardian funerals rarely had a body to inter, and though Eris no longer stood among the ranks of Lightbearers, she was not unique in that manner. So, they simply gathered, those few who had loved her well, packing themselves three deep into the cramped apartment even Eris had sometimes forgotten she owned. 

There was Mara Sov, starlight in her eyes, Petra Venj at her elbow—no particular friend of Eris herself, but where the Queen went, she liked to follow. "Little" Eido, taller than the Queen of the Awoken, tucking her second arms around herself and taking care not to disturb any of Eris's bones and relics while peering at everything. Crow, serious as he moved toward Mara; Zavala, quiet, occupying a corner. Here to witness, not rip himself open. Some small assortment of Guardians who had corresponded with Eris over one matter or another, study of the Taken or Hive—Awoken, Human, and Exo faces alike, some distraught and some somberly set, determined to witness though they might not weep. 

The Drifter did not show his face. Ikora had wondered how he would bear it, and she had her answer: he would not. He would simply go, careening into the dark of space with his pain alone to guide him.  

Ikora sympathized, with an unavoidable bitter chaser of resentment. This was not the first time she'd been left to manage a funeral on her own. 

Senseless. It was always senseless, death among the immortal. She had not grown any more used to it. She hoped she never would. 

"We are here to celebrate Eris Morn," Ikora said to the surrounding group, drawing herself up and making steel her spine. "Mourn by carrying her with you, if you must. But in her own words, her life was a bright and victorious one, despite everything she endured. She ought to be remembered thus." 

For Cayde's sake, she allowed herself two jokes in the eulogy; for Eris's, she did not cry.
entries.text_zh:
守护者葬礼上鲜少有遗体可入葬，即便埃里斯已不再是负光者中的一员，在这点上她也并不特殊。于是，深爱着她的人只是简单地聚在一起，排成几层把埃里斯自己都时常忘却的那间狭小公寓挤得满满当当。 

玛拉·索维也在场，眼中闪烁着星光，佩特拉·万吉紧挨着她——虽然不是埃里斯的挚友，但女王去哪儿，她总爱跟着。比觉醒者女王还要高大的“小”艾多，用第二对臂膀环抱住自己，留意不去碰触埃里斯留下的骨头和神器，同时好奇地打量着周围的一切。乌鸦，一脸严肃地向玛拉走去；萨瓦拉则静静地待在角落里。他来这里是为了见证，而非让自己情绪失控。还有几名守护者，他们曾与埃里斯因各种事务，针对傀儡军团或是邪魔族的研究有过往来——觉醒者、人类以及Exo，脸上的神情都差不多，有的悲恸，有的肃穆，决心要见证这一刻，尽管他们或许会克制住眼泪。 

浪客并未露面。艾可拉曾猜想他会如何承受这一切，而此刻，她已得到了答案：他拒绝承受。他会选择离去，孤身一人坠入漆黑的宇宙，唯有内心的痛苦为他指引方向。  

艾可拉心生同情，但难免夹杂着一丝难以抑制的怨怼。这已不是她首次被留下来独自操办葬礼了。 

没有道理。对这群不死之躯来说，死亡总是没有道理。她对此从未习惯。她希望她永远不会习惯。 

“我们来到这里庆祝埃里斯·摩恩的一生，”艾可拉对周围的人们说道，她挺直身姿，脊梁如钢。“如果各位觉得有必要哀悼，那就让她的精神与你们同在。但正如她说过的，尽管历经磨难，她的一生依旧光明且充满胜利。我们应当如此铭记她。” 

出于对凯德的敬意，她在悼词中纵容自己开了两个玩笑；而出于对埃里斯的尊重，她强忍住了泪水。

entries.name: Heliotrope
entries.text:
Eris's apartment was close and dark, and it smelled so strongly of incense that Drifter could barely breathe. But he sat alone, his elbows on his knees, staring at the harsh green glow of her Ahamkara bone. 

"You know what I want," he whispered. "So go on." 

There was nothing. He gripped it between his hands, his mouth curving into a harsh frown. He raised it, shook it roughly, then held it close to his face. 

"You hear me?" he hissed.  

Nothing. 

His shoulders slumped. He held the orb loosely, his eyes closed, and thought of her. 

"Be careful with that," Sloane said. He looked up, startled. The deputy commander stood in the threshold of the door. She let her eyes wander for a moment, her jaw set. 

"She lived like this?" 

Drifter didn't respond. He stood, placing the Ahamkara bone back on the table. Then he made his way to the door. Sloane blocked him with her body before he could leave. He met her eyes, expressionless. 

"Where are you going? We need to talk," she said firmly. 

"I got nothin' to say," he replied. 

"Yes, you do." 

He took a few steps back. 

"You can't walk away from this. Too much is at stake here. The City relies on you— you have to be ready for when you're needed." 

"Haven't you all taken enough from me?" he muttered. 

"You're not walking away from this." 

"Yeah, I am. You gonna stop me?" 

Sloane grabbed him by the collar. He lifted his chin in challenge; she raised a fist. 

"You wouldn't," he started, just before it came down on his face. 

Sloane let go of his collar. Drifter staggered until his back was against the wall. He flinched as he touched his nose, his fingertips coming away bloody. Then he grinned with red-lined teeth.  

"Been a while since I earned one of those," Drifter said, his voice trembling. His smile faltered quickly. He wiped his bloodied upper lip with the back of his hand as his Ghost appeared beside him, coming close and staring mutely with its red eye.  

He batted it out of the way and left the room, bleeding. 

"Don't go too far," Sloane called after him.  

Drifter didn't stop walking.
entries.text_zh:
埃里斯的公寓狭小幽暗，熏香的气味浓烈得令浪客几乎无法呼吸。但他独自坐着，双肘支在膝盖上，凝视着她的阿罕卡拉之骨发出的刺眼绿光。 

“你知道我想要什么，”他低声说道。“所以别磨蹭了。” 

没有回应。他双手紧握它，嘴角紧抿，形成了一道严厉的皱纹。他把它高高举起，猛烈摇晃，然后将它捧到了脸边。 

“你听到我说话了吗？”他嘶叫道。  

还是没有回应。 

他的肩膀耷拉下来，松松地握着那颗球体，双眼紧闭，心中想着她。 

“小心点儿，”斯隆说道。他猛地抬头，吓了一跳。副指挥官正站在门口，她任由目光在屋内游移了片刻，下巴紧绷着。 

“她住在这样的地方？” 

浪客没有回答。他站起身，将阿罕卡拉之骨放回桌上，随后向门口走去。斯隆用身体挡住了离开的路。他直视着她的眼睛，面无表情。 

“你要去哪里？我们需要谈谈，”她坚定地说。 

“我没什么可说的，”他回答道。 

“不，你有。” 

他往后退了几步。 

“你不能就这样一走了之。这里的利害关系重大。圣城仰仗着你——你必须随时准备响应号召。” 

“你们从我这里夺走的还不够多吗？”他低声说到。 

“你不会就这样一走了之的。” 

“不，我会。你要阻止我吗？” 

斯隆一把揪住他的衣领，他扬起下巴以示挑衅，而她则举起了拳头。 

“你不敢的，”他刚开口，那拳头便已落在了他的脸上。 

斯隆松开他的衣领。浪客踉跄着后退，直到后背抵住了墙壁。他伸手摸了摸鼻子，指尖沾满了鲜血，不禁抽搐了一下。然后他咧嘴笑了，露出被鲜血染红的牙齿。  

“有一段时间没挨过打了，”浪客说道，声音中带着一丝颤抖。他的笑容很快消失了。他用手背擦了擦血迹斑斑的上唇，而他的机灵则出现在他身边，缓缓靠近，用红色的眼睛默默凝视着他。  

他挥手把机灵推到一边，流着血离开了房间。 

“别走太远，”斯隆在他身后喊道。  

浪客没有停下脚步。

entries.name: Elaia
entries.text:
"Savathûn presumed that my throne would hold me. That I would either willingly relinquish myself to its safety or become trapped within it." 

Ikora shook her head, smiling. Eris shared in her smile. 

"She did not anticipate the Guardian's resourcefulness. And she misjudged me." 

"As did those of us who assumed your death was final." In the admission, Ikora's smile faded.  

"As I, too, assumed." Eris tilted her head, studying Ikora intently. "Do you presume that you should have come looking for me? No. You did the right thing, Ikora. That I survived, that I am triumphant, could not have been reasonably predicted." 

They stood together in Eris's throne, in the world that was made of all of her, yet still Eris did not understand all that was contained within.  

"You're comforting me," Ikora said, her voice a tense whisper. "You shouldn't. Eris, you're the one who died." 

"Yes. But you're the one who grieved." 

Ikora turned away, and Eris let her. To accept comfort was no small task, as she well knew. In silence, they studied the spines of books ancient and new, the runes writ along them in delicate gleaming soulfire. 

"I missed you," Ikora said finally. "I… felt that somehow, I had let you down: that I should have kept you safe. Even knowing you would have hated it." 

"That is your curse," Eris returned solemnly. "Responsibility." 

For that, Ikora laughed, startled into it. "You and Ophiuchus see it very differently."  

"Ghosts are bound to worry." 

Ikora's half-smile faded into soberness again. She drew stillness about herself as a cloak. "Was I right to let you go?"  

"It was all I would let you do," Eris told her. She gestured up and around, to the infinite helix-library that cradled her innermost self. "This sort of library suits me as one in the Tower never could. You did what you could, Ikora." 

Absolution offered, held in the quiet space between them. Ikora was the one to break it, closing the gap to sweep Eris up into a tight embrace. They held each other for a long moment. 

"Don't do that again," Ikora whispered. 

"I won't," Eris replied.
entries.text_zh:
“萨瓦图恩以为我的王座会束缚住我。她以为我要么会心甘情愿地把自己托付于它的庇护之下，要么会深陷其中，无法自拔。” 

艾可拉摇了摇头，微笑着。埃里斯也跟着笑了。 

“她没有料到守护者会如此足智多谋，更是误判了我。” 

“如同我们这些曾以为你已经迎来最终之死的人一样。”承认这一点时，艾可拉的笑容渐渐淡去。  

“我也曾这么以为。”埃里斯歪着头，专注地打量着艾可拉。“你是不是觉得自己本该来找我？不，你做得对，艾可拉。我能活下来，我能取得胜利，是没理由能预料到的。” 

她们并肩立于埃里斯的王座之上，置身于这个由她全然构筑的世界里，可即便如此，埃里斯仍旧未能完全理解这方天地所蕴含的一切。  

“你是在安慰我，”艾可拉说到，声音紧绷而低沉。“你不该这样做的。埃里斯，死去的人是你。” 

“没错。但悲伤的人是你。” 

艾可拉转过身去，埃里斯听之任之。接受安慰绝非易事，她深知这一点。两人默默地凝视着一本本新旧交织的书籍，其书脊上镌刻的精致符文闪烁着灵魂之火。 

“我想念你，”艾可拉终于说道。“我…觉得在某种程度上，我辜负了你：我本应护你安全。即使知道你会讨厌那样。” 

“那就是你背负的诅咒，”埃里斯严肃地回答。“责任。” 

听到这话，艾可拉惊讶地笑了起来。“你跟蛇夫座对此的看法，真是大相径庭。”  

“机灵总是免不了要担心。” 

艾可拉再次收起浅浅的微笑，重归严肃。她把沉静裹在自己身上，犹如披上了一层隐形的斗篷。“我放你走，做得对吗？”  

“这是我唯一会让你做的事，”埃里斯如此说到。她示意上方和周围，指向那个摇曳着她内心最深处自我的无限螺旋图书馆。“这样的图书馆才适合我，高塔里的永远比不上。你已经尽力了，艾可拉。” 

这份宽恕凝固在她们之间寂静的空间里。最终，是艾可拉打破了这份沉默，她向前一步，将埃里斯抱入怀中。两人紧紧相拥，久久没有分开。 

“别再那样做，”艾可拉低语道。 

“我不会的，”埃里斯回答说。

entries.name: Ion
entries.text:
"And when he escapes?" 

"If," Eris corrected. 

"When he escapes," Sloane continued, "he'll have torn a hole straight through your throne world and into the Dreadnaught. This entire place will be compromised, and the City with it. You're fine with that risk?" 

"There is always risk," Eris said. "You must assume risk inherent with trust, and focus."  

The words were pointed.  

"That's not how trust works," Sloane said, unclenching her jaw with some effort.  

"No?" Eris's sidelong glance was too green. It made something itch in Sloane that she didn't like. "Tell me of trust, Deputy Commander Sloane." 

"It's earned." Sloane uncrossed her arms. Crossed them again, the other way this time. "Someone does the work, again and again. Proves they have the skills and the follow-through to get a job done. It adds up, over time. Long enough, and you know someone can and will do what they say they will. Then you don't have to question when they promise you the impossible, because you know they've got a way. That's certainty. That's trust."  

"I see." Eris sounded like she was trying too hard to be neutral. She laid solid, unwavering lines into the floor of her throne-library, one after another. Unhesitating.  

Sloane's arm burned. She ignored it. 

"Trust," Eris said at length, "is always, still, a risk. It is whispering a secret to another and hoping they will not tell it. They do not—you are caught before you fall. This time. And ever after, you must ask yourself: Is this the step too far? Is this secret the one that turns them back? But you will never know, not completely, that they will not. To entirely understand someone is impossible. You can only guess, and hope, and trust." 

"You sound like Savathûn," Sloane told her, and regretted it immediately. It wasn't true—she just hated the twistiness of Eris's mind, the way it spiraled around a question that should be so easy to answer. 

Eris's chitin-plated shoulders hitched, but her back was to Sloane, and it was hard to tell if she felt anything serious about the accusation. "We must do something, Deputy Commander. I trust," she stressed the word lightly, "that you will be there to chide me if I fail." 

Sloane's lip curled. "I'll be there," she said. "But to grind the Echo into dust. That's more important than anything else—making sure it's taken care of." 

"There you have it." Eris turned, then, a lightness on her face that Sloane had rarely seen before. "You are a certainty. Above the risk, I know this: you will not allow this to go unfinished."  

That was not quite the lesson Sloane had hoped Eris would take away from this conversation. "I'm only one Titan," Sloane said seriously. "If and when he escapes you, we're going to need more firepower than that."  

Eris hesitated. Only briefly, but it was the closest to a win Sloane was going to get. "Then make what preparations you must," she said. "Warn whom you feel prudent. I will do this—I must do this. I am aware of the risk; I would not proceed if it was not well-founded."  

The reward for a job well done was always more work, wasn't it? "Fine," Sloane said through gritted teeth.  

At least Eris trusted her, by one definition or another. It wasn't nothing.
entries.text_zh:
“当他逃跑时呢？” 

“是如果，”埃里斯纠正道。 

“当他逃跑时，”斯隆继续说道，“他会在你的王座世界里撕开一个直通无畏战舰的裂口。这整个地方都将陷落，而圣城也会被连累。你甘愿冒那样的风险吗？” 

“风险总是在所难免的，”埃里斯说道。“你必须承担信任所固有的风险，集中注意。”  

这话语很尖锐。  

“信任不是这样的，”斯隆说道，费了些力气才松开紧咬的牙关。  

“不是吗？”埃里斯斜睨了她一眼，泛着幽绿的光，这让斯隆感到有些不自在，心里直发痒。“那就请你来谈谈信任吧，副指挥官斯隆。” 

“信任是赢得的。”斯隆松开双臂，随即又换了一种方式交叉抱于胸前。“有人一次次地付出努力。证明自己具备完成任务所需的技能和执行力。随着时间的推移，这些努力逐渐累积。时间一长，你就会知道，这个人能够做到并且会去做自己承诺的事。然后当此人向你许下似乎不可能实现的承诺时，你便无需质疑，因为你深知其自有办法。这就是确信无疑。这就是信任。”  

“我明白了。”埃里斯听起来是在刻意维持中立的口气。她在王座图书馆的地面上，一道接一道地刻画出坚实而稳定的线条，毫不迟疑。  

斯隆的手臂有灼痛感，但她没去理会。 

“信任，”埃里斯缓缓说道，“始终伴随着风险。它就像是向另一个人倾诉秘密，然后寄希望于他们不会泄露。这一次，他们没有辜负你——你在跌倒之前就被接住了。但从此以后，你必须不断自问：这一步是否迈得太远？这个秘密是否会让他们背叛？但你永远无法完全确定他们不会那样做。因为彻底了解一个人是不可能的。你只能猜测、希望，然后选择信任。” 

“你听起来就像是萨瓦图恩，”斯隆告诉她，随即又感到后悔。这不是真的——她只是厌烦埃里斯扭曲的思维，以及她在如此简单的问题上绕圈子的方式。 

埃里斯耸了耸壳质的肩膀，但她背对着斯隆，让人难以判断她是否在严肃对待这项指责。“我们必须采取行动，副指挥官。我相信，”她轻声却刻意强调了这个词，“若我失败，你会在场斥责我。” 

斯隆抿起了嘴。“我会在场的，”她说道。“但那是为了把回响碾为齑粉，这比什么都重要——必须确保它被处理掉。” 

“这就对了。”埃里斯转过身来，脸上洋溢着斯隆前所未见的轻松。“你就是让我确信无疑的人。即便面临风险，我也深知：你一定会完成。”  

这不是斯隆希望埃里斯从这场对话中吸取的教训。“我只是一名泰坦，”斯隆严肃地说。“如果他真的挣脱了你的束缚，我们会需要更多的火力。”  

埃里斯犹豫了。虽然只是片刻，但对于斯隆而言，这已是她最接近胜利的一刻。“那就做好你必须做的准备，”她说道。“去警告那些你觉得有必要知会的人。我会去做——我必须去做。我深知其中的风险；若非确有依据，我也不会贸然行事。”  

能者多劳，不是吗？“好吧，”斯隆咬牙说道。  

至少，按照某种定义来说，埃里斯是信任她的。这很重要。

entries.name: Iris
entries.text:
"Don't you have a home to go to?" Drifter wanted to know.  

Deputy Commander Sloane, who had any number of other places she could be, glanced up from her assortment of reports and screens. She'd set up her battle station right in the middle of Drifter's ship and showed no signs of leaving. "I'm busy," she said. Her Ghost, hovering above her left shoulder, bobbed in agreement. "Either contribute, or leave." 

"That's my line," Drifter groused, but he pulled up one of the more stable chairs anyway, dropping himself into it where he could scan over the things she had spread out. "Hive?" 

"It's always Hive," Sloane said tiredly. 

"Unless it's Taken." 

"Unless it's Taken," she agreed, then remembered she was angry with him, scowling across the way. "Were you going to help?" 

Drifter held his hands up, exaggerated his 'I wasn't doing nothing, ma'am' expression. "I might have a few pieces of intel." 

"Right," Sloane said. "Well, you go ahead and volunteer those when they seem relevant. I'm thinking Xivu Arath has to be first. Savathûn likes the long game anyway, and Xivu Arath's eager for a fight. She'll hit us first, and we don't want to be trying to unwind some kind of trap while Xivu's throwing swords." 

"She's real into swords." 

"Helpful." Sloane tapped her fingers against the rickety card table. "If Xivu Arath gets going, it'll be hard to stop her without also powering her up by fighting. So we hit her first, ideally, if we can find the right place before she starts killing." 

Drawn in despite himself, Drifter squinted at Sloane's notes. A blue-line map of the Dreadnaught in three dimensions, half-complete—a few little notes off to the side ranking Hive constructs and likely locations for Xivu Arath's plots. SWORDS was underlined heavily. "Surprise attack still feels like an attack to me," he said in a moment, warming up to being helpful.  

"It sure is." Sloane blew out a frustrated breath. "She's not what she was. Not since Eris cut her off. But we still don't have time for an elegant, pacifist solution. Which is why my best thought is not to target her directly. We target her targets – find where she plans to hit, deprive her of kills and tithes by taking them down first. And if it does come to straight-on combat, make whatever we do quick and clean, none of the glory-in-battle nonsense she likes." She shrugged, not particularly happy. "It's got flaws, but it's something." 

"Not the worst plan I've heard," Drifter said honestly. He rocked his chair onto one leg, swinging it over the pivot point carelessly. "You think all this is gonna work?" 

Sloane looked up at him, fixing him with the sort of gaze that looked through him. He had the sense that he had her full attention. "I don't know," she said. "But I know we have to give it our best if we have any shot at it working. You trust Eris, don't you?" 

"'Course I do." 

Sloane deliberated visibly for a moment or two. "Then it will work," she said finally.  

"Sure," Drifter said, ignoring the sheer volume of things she clearly hadn't said. "All right. Guess I'm already dealt in anyway. Got any use for a list of places the Lucent Brood's been sighted?" 

"Always."
entries.text_zh:
“你无家可归吗？”浪客有些好奇。  

副指挥官斯隆，本来有无数其他地方可以去，却从眼前各式各样的报告和屏幕上抬起头来。她把她的作战指挥台设在浪客飞船的中央，完全没有离去的意思。“我很忙，”她说道。她的机灵，悬浮在她左肩上方，点头赞同。“你要么帮忙，要么离开。” 

“那是我的台词，”浪客嘟囔着，但还是拉过一把较为稳当的椅子，一屁股坐下，浏览起她摊开的东西。“邪魔族？” 

“向来都是邪魔族，”斯隆疲惫地说道。 

“除非是傀儡军团。” 

“除非是傀儡军团，”她赞同道，随即想起自己正在生他的气，隔着桌子冲他皱起眉。“你打算帮忙吗？” 

浪客举起双手，夸张地摆出一副“我什么都没做，女士”的表情。“我可能掌握了一些情报。” 

“好吧，”斯隆说。“那就把你觉得有用的说出来。我认为我们首先要面对的是希乌阿拉斯。萨瓦图恩喜欢打持久战，而希乌阿拉斯则急于求战。她会先向我们发起攻击，而我们不希望希乌挥舞刀剑之时，我们还在试图解除某种陷阱。” 

“她是真的很喜欢刀剑。” 

“真是有用的情报。”斯隆用手指敲打着那张摇摇晃晃的折叠桌。“如果希乌阿拉斯开始行动，不战斗就无法阻止她，而战斗又会增强她的力量。所以最好先下手为强，前提是我们能在她开始杀戮之前找到正确的位置。” 

浪客不由得眯起眼睛看向斯隆的笔记。那是一张没画完的无畏战舰三维蓝线规划图——旁边还有几行小字，罗列着邪魔族构造体和希乌阿拉斯有可能在策划阴谋的地点。其中，刀剑二字被重重地划上了下划线。“我感觉突袭还是一种战斗，”过了一会儿，他这么说道，开始摆出愿意帮忙的姿态。  

“确实。”斯隆无奈地叹了口气。“自从埃里斯将她断舍后，她已不再是从前的她。但我们还是没有时间找到一个优雅而和平的解决方案。所以我认为最好不要直接针对她。我们要针对她的目标——找到她计划攻击的地方，先下手为强，剥夺她杀戮和掠夺的机会。如果真的发展到正面交锋的地步，那我们的行动一定要干净利落，绝不能搞她喜欢的那套荣耀之战。”她耸了下肩，显然对此并不满意。“这个计划有瑕疵，但好歹是个办法。” 

“这不是我听过的最糟的计划，”浪客诚恳地说。他随意地把椅子翘成一腿着地，绕着支点晃来晃去。“你觉得这一切能成功吗？” 

斯隆抬起头，用一种仿佛能洞察人心的眼神盯着他。他能感觉到自己获得了她全部的注意力。“我不知道，”她说。“但我知道，如果我们想让它有一丝成功的可能，就必须全力以赴。你信任埃里斯，对吧？” 

“当然了。” 

斯隆明显地思量了一会儿。“那它就会成功，”她最后说道。  

“行，”浪客说道，忽略了她显然没有言明的大量细节。“好吧。看来我已经卷进来了。我这有份光明虫群出没地点的清单，用得上吗？” 

“当然。”

entries.name: Hemlock
entries.text:
"You are not of my Taking." 

Sloane squared her shoulders against the weight of the voice that spoke to her. It wasn't a surprise. Every time she visited Eris's throne world now, that lone and baleful eye seemed to follow her.  

Didn't mean she had to like it. Or talk to him. It. 

"But what are you, then?" he mused aloud, as if her response or lack thereof was wholly immaterial. "I am told the Taken changed hands many times. Who was it that Took you?" 

"No one," Sloane said before she could think better of it. "I said no." 

"Did you?"  

There was an awful heaviness to the Echo's attention, a fizz of sterile neutrinos and the prickling awareness of danger down her spine. But Sloane was nothing if she was not herself, and so she stood tall, chin up, and did not falter. "I don't need that power." 

"Whomever made that offer, it will not vanish," the Echo said softly. "You may not need it now. But are you so sure of the future?" 

"Yes," said Sloane, willing it to be true as she said it. "What do you want?" 

"To understand," said Oryx, and the simplicity of it was as sharp as a knife. Whatever needed to be twisted or prized loose or broken to understand it—he would. That was all there was.  

"Then understand this: I am resolute." Arc light crackled in her hands as Sloane closed them into fists. "And I am complete in myself. I need no other power." She knew it for not-quite-truth even as she said it: she was in Síocháin and Ahsa, the Traveler's Light and the Vanguard, even as they were in her. But she certainly didn't need the Taken. 

"Aiat," the Echo said thoughtfully, and nothing further.  

Sloane did not retreat. She turned that word over and over again in her mind. Aiat. It had a meaning it hadn't quite before, sounding almost like her own voice saying, "I am complete in myself" back to her. 

Hours and hours later, long after she'd left Eris's throne world, still it echoed. And still she wondered about its truth.
entries.text_zh:
“你不是我的傀儡军团。” 

斯隆挺直肩膀，对抗那个声音施加在她身上的重量。这不意外。现在每次她到访埃里斯的王座世界，那双孤独而邪恶的眼睛似乎都在暗中盯着她。  

但这并不意味着她得喜欢它。或是跟他交谈。跟它。 

“但你究竟是什么呢？”他大声寻思道，仿佛她的回答与否根本无关紧要。“我听说傀儡军团曾多次易主。是谁操纵了你呢？” 

“没有谁，”斯隆脱口而出。“我拒绝了。” 

“是吗？”  

回响的注视中带着一种令人窒息的沉重，无菌的中微子在周围滋滋作响，而危险的感觉沿着她的脊椎蔓延，让她感到阵阵刺痛。但斯隆如果不能维持自我，就会失去存在的意义，于是，她站得笔直，扬起下巴，毫不动摇。“我不需要那种力量。” 

“无论是谁提出的，那个提议都不会消失，”回响柔声说道。“或许你现在不需要它。但未来呢？你如此确定吗？” 

“是的，”斯隆说道，希望这能让它成为事实。“你想要怎样？” 

“想要理解，”欧里克斯说道，话语简洁得就像一把利刃。为了理解，无论是需要扭曲、撬开还是打破什么——他都会去做。这就是他所在乎的一切。  

“那就理解这一点：我意志坚定。”斯隆双手紧握成拳，电弧在她手中噼啪作响。“我是完整的个体。我不需要其他力量。”即使这么说时，她心中也清楚这并非全然属实：她身在西奥昌与阿莎之中，也身在旅行者的光能和先锋之中，就像他们也与她同在一样。但她可以肯定的是，她决不需要傀儡军团。 

“阿特，”回响沉吟着，再无二话。  

斯隆没有退缩。她在脑海里反复琢磨这个词。阿特。它似乎有了与以往不同的含义，听起来几乎像是她自己的声音在用“我是完整的个体”回应她。 

过了很长时间，在她早已离开埃里斯的王座世界后，它仍然在她的脑海中回响。而她依旧在寻思着它的真相。

entries.name: Hellebore
entries.text:
Close. It had been too close. The knowledge of the shape of the knife held out to her had burned itself into Sloane's mind; she could see it even now, though its weight did not bow the fabric of her thoughts as it had. 

"I am pleased you returned to us safely," Eris said—close by. Very close. Sloane startled back, surprised that Eris had come so near without Sloane hearing her. "Your loss at this stage would be… catastrophic." 

Sloane's exhalation was half a laugh. "You have a gift for understatement," she said, to cover how rattled she truly was by the experience of re-forging Willbreaker.  

Eris's mouth flickered, the ghost of a smile there and gone again. This close, Sloane thought, she looked pale—paler. Strained. Containing the Echo was wearing on her. "Do you hear it still?" Eris asked. 

"Yes," Sloane admitted. If she was compromised, it was her responsibility to be honest about it. A moment later, remembering, her gaze flicked over Eris's shoulder to where the Echo hung, roiling with its own power, suspended in the grasp of Eris's magics. "Not sure I want to talk about this here." 

"He cannot hear us," Eris said simply. As if she had thought it and the matter was done. Honestly, that was probably the exact case. That was the nature of a throne world.  

Cautiously, Sloane experimented with relaxing her shoulders. It made her feel as if she might collapse at any slight gust, so she tightened them again. "What it offered me," she said abruptly. "'Bulwark against despair.' To never fear that I would be so overcome as to fall. But that would be falling. In itself."  

"Yes," Eris said, in simple echo of Sloane's earlier assent. Her trifold gaze was intense, searching. "We feel foolish when we come back to ourselves. For the choices we almost made. We laugh and say how stupid we were. Of course that was wrong. Of course we would never." 

Sloane's mouth tasted like ash. "I think that offer's always going to be there," she said—quiet, so quiet, that nagging fear that created the way in. "Ahsa has my back, but if I wake up one day and choose—just choose—to jump into that abyss? She's my ally, my partner. But an anchor doesn't do any good if the ship cuts the line." 

"Choose not to. Again, and again." Eris's smile was softer, even sympathetic. "Someday, you may find it valuable to let that knife rest where you may reach it, because you know you will not. Trust yourself, Deputy Commander—Sloane. As I trust you, even when you are infuriating." 

"It's my job," Sloane cracked weakly. Her ribs were a cage with the door opened, suddenly letting breath back in.  

She hadn't had that slow, methodical proof with Ahsa. She had had a moment, a prayer, and no alternative. Maybe Eris wasn't entirely wrong. That unspeakable risk, back then, had saved her. 

"Those feelings." Eris still regarded her with that searching intent. "In that pit. Those feelings are not false simply because we may look back on them later and laugh. Remember that." 

Sloane would.
entries.text_zh:
太近了，近得过头了。那把向她挥来的利刃的形状，已深深烙印在斯隆的脑海中；即便此刻，她仍能清晰忆起，尽管它已不再如当初那般沉重，压得她思绪难展。 

“很高兴你能安全归来，”埃里斯的声音近在咫尺。非常近。斯隆猛地惊觉，没曾料想到埃里斯已如此靠近，而她竟未察觉。“这个时候失去你将会是…灾难性的。” 

斯隆呼气时带了一点笑。“你真是太会轻描淡写了，”她说道，试图掩饰重铸碎志者的经历对她造成的强烈冲击。  

埃里斯的嘴角微微闪动，一抹微笑转瞬即逝。离得这么近，斯隆发现她看起来脸色苍白——比以前更加苍白。紧张。压制回响正让她愈发疲惫。“你还听得到它吗？”埃里斯问道。 

“是的，”斯隆承认道。如果她已被侵蚀，她就有责任说出实情。片刻之后，她回想起来，目光越过埃里斯的肩头，望向回响所悬之处，它被埃里斯的魔法所束缚，靠自身的力量搅动着。“我不太想在这里谈论这个。” 

“他听不到我们，”埃里斯简单地说道。仿佛她这样想，问题就迎刃而解。说实话，很可能确实就是那样。那就是王座世界的本性。  

斯隆小心翼翼地尝试放松肩膀。这让她感觉自己仿佛随时会被一阵微风吹倒，于是她再次紧绷起来。“它向我承诺，”她突然说道。“‘抵抗绝望的堡垒'。永远不必担心自己会被压倒。但那本身就是一种倒下。”  

“是的，”埃里斯说，简单重复了斯隆之前表示赞同的话语。她三重的目光炽热而深邃，仿佛在探寻着什么。“我们清醒过来时，会感到那些险些做出的选择很蠢。我们会笑着自嘲当时的愚昧。那当然是错的。我们当然永远不会那样做。” 

斯隆的口中泛起灰般的苦涩。“我想，那个提议会一直存在，”她轻声说道，那股挥之不去的恐惧悄然潜入心间。“阿莎会支持我，但如果有一天我醒来，直接选择了跳入那深渊呢？她是我的盟友，我的伙伴。可倘若船只切断了锚链，锚便会毫无作用。” 

“选择不那样做。一次又一次。”埃里斯的笑容更加柔和，甚至带着一丝同情。“有朝一日，你会发现将那把刀刃放在触手可及之处是多么宝贵，因为你深知自己不会伸手触及它。信任你自己，副指挥官——斯隆。就像我信任你一样，即使是在你令人恼火的时候。” 

“那是我的职责，”斯隆虚弱地回应道。她的肋骨仿佛是一个打开了门的牢笼，突然间让气息重新涌入胸膛。  

她与阿莎之间，未曾有过那般缓慢而周密的验证。她只经历了一个瞬间，一个祈求，没其他选择。或许埃里斯并非全然错误。当时正是那难以言喻的风险，救了她一命。 

“那些感受。”埃里斯仍旧用那种探寻的目光注视着她。“在那个深渊里。那些感受不会仅仅因为我们日后回首时可能会一笑置之而变得虚假。记住这一点。” 

斯隆会的。

entries.name: Apple
entries.text:
Eris Morn looked up at the spiraled heights above her. It extended into an endless void, the library of her soul coiling beyond sight. All that she was, every moment of her past and her present, everything that could yet unfold inside her. 

"My throne," she whispered. There was a frisson of excitement in her voice when she said this, a small tremble as her body tensed and relaxed. It thrilled her, still, to find herself here. 

Drifter came to stand beside her. His hand moved to reach for hers, but he hesitated, uncertain. 

"This place can be anything you want?" he asked. 

"Anything," she answered in a sigh of comfort. 

"So what do you want?" 

An earnest question. She turned and met his eyes. 

"Joy," she said. "Joy, at last." 

For the first time in centuries, the thought of the future made Eris smile.  

"We shall explore this place together. Map my interiority. See what wonders I possess." 

She reached out and laid a palm on his chest, feeling the stutter of his heart. He put his hand over hers and twined their fingers together.  

"You want that? Me, here?" 

"Yes." 

He saw the delight in the turn of her mouth, saw bright feeling in the rise and fall of her breath. Her throne was all she was and could be, and she had invited him to see it.  

"Then I'll follow you," he said, warm and genuine. "For as long as you want." 

"Then follow." 

Eris turned and made a sweeping gesture with one hand. In that movement there rose up a set of stairs that coiled upwards beyond sight. Their stone steps were bowed with the impressions of centuries of use. She had imagined something worn, and something worn had sprung from her thoughts. 

She began to climb the stairs. She did not know where they led. He took a few steps after her, then paused. 

"Moonlight," Drifter called. Eris turned to look at him. His eyes were filled with wonder. "Can I kiss you?" 

A starving man, she thought, who had found sustenance at last. And she, too, found something she had lost long ago. Something she thought irrecoverable. 

She closed the space between them. 

In these vast landscapes of her mind, in these endless halls of her design, they declared what was unspoken with the joyous press of her lips to his. And when they parted, she held out her hand. He took it, then let her guide him up the stairs and into a world neither of them knew.
entries.text_zh:
埃里斯·莫恩抬头望向那螺旋上升的高处。它仿佛是延伸至无尽的虚空之中，而她心灵的图书馆则蜿蜒盘旋，超出视线所及。她的一切，无论是过往的每一刻，还是当下的瞬间，乃至未来尚未发生的可能都蕴藏于此。 

“我的王座，”她轻声说道。言语间流露出一丝兴奋的颤音，身体也随之微微紧绷又放松。她仍在为自己能身处此地而感到激动。 

浪客来到她身边站定。他想伸手去触碰她的手，却又迟疑了，心存犹豫。 

“这个地方可以变成你想要的任何样子吗？”他问道。 

“任何样子，”她回答着，发出了一声安心的叹息。 

“那你想要什么？” 

这是个真诚的问题。她转过身，与他对视。 

“快乐，”她说。“终于，快乐起来。” 

对未来的想象，几百年来第一次让埃里斯露出了微笑。  

“我们会一起探索这个地方。绘制我的内在空间。看我所具备的非凡之处。” 

她伸出手，将掌心轻轻贴在他的胸口，感受着他心跳的颤动。他则将手覆在她的手上，两人的手指紧紧相扣，交织起来。  

“你想要那样吗？我，在这里？” 

“是的。” 

他看到她嘴角扬起的喜悦，看到她呼吸起伏间流露出的明媚情感。她的王座就是她的一切，以及她可能成为的一切，而她邀请了他来共同见证。  

“那我就跟随你，”他温暖而真诚地说道。“只要你愿意，多久都行。” 

“那就跟上吧。” 

埃里斯转过身，单手一挥，只见一组楼梯蓦然升起，盘旋而上，直至视线之外。石阶因历经数百年的踩踏而略显磨损。她心中所想的是一些破旧的东西，于是这充满岁月痕迹的楼梯便从她的思绪中涌现了出来。 

她开始踏上楼梯。她不知它们通向哪里。他跟着迈出几步，然后停了下来。 

“月光，”浪客喊道。埃里斯转过身来看向他，他的眼中满是惊奇。“我可以吻你吗？” 

一个饥饿的人终于找到了养分，她心想。而她，也找到了自己很久以前就已失去的东西。一些她以为再也无法挽回的东西。 

她拉近了与他的距离。 

在她那广袤无垠的心灵画卷中，在她精心设计的无尽长廊里，伴着她嘴唇轻触他脸颊的喜悦，他们宣告了那些未曾言说的心意。两人分开时，她伸出了手。他紧紧握住，然后让她引领自己踏上楼梯，步入一个他们都不曾知晓的世界。

entries.name: Throne
entries.text:
Eris Morn returned to the Vestian Outpost. Because she spoke well, it was agreed that aid would be traded for intelligence and a long-term alliance. In this way, the Awoken were the first to know of the Great Navigator: his philosophies, his strategies, his weaknesses. And as the coven contemplated the possibilities laid wide before this god-king's far-flung sword, it was decreed that they would build a throne world beneath an energy well as blind as the ferryman Charon.

Nascia drew the schematics. Portia worked out the calculations. They made their first test with a small rift generator on the eastern shore. Satisfied that their methods were sound, they then went to a grand cathedral to dig the well. There, Lissyl and Sedia augured the first borehole with the help of Riven, who had taken the shape of a needle-nosed basilisk, while Kalli and Shuro Chi constructed the gate itself, deep below, in a hall they named "The Confluence."

Illyn made tincture after tincture of queensfoil until her clothes stank and her hands were stained reddish-black. Open-eyed, she walked between planes and sorted the threads of reality on a vast metaphysical loom, weaving some closer, some more distant.

Mara and Riven shaped her third throne together, and the artistry of their work was a testament to the hungry joy they felt in that partnership. They named it Eleusinia, and it was in those Ascendant halls that Mara finally carved a statue for Sjur.

When it came time to connect the Well to the unreality that lay beyond the gateway, Sedia asked, "Would it not be wiser to leave this door without a key?" Riven, now an immense antlered serpent with broad tiger paws, tightened around the perimeter of the room like a noose.

"Egg," Mara corrected absently, chewing on her thumbnail.

"The key is so heavy as to be unliftable," Kalli ventured, since they were speaking metaphorically.

Sedia flapped her hand dismissively. "Yes, yes, I know." They all knew that the gate required a continuous multi-week charge of paracausal energies, and that almost nothing in this solar system could produce such energies at the scale required by the gateway. Almost. "It's just— do we…"

"Do we wish to trust the Guardians?" Illyn filled in dryly.

Mara ran her hand along the sleek surface of the primary well's control mechanism, then turned and walked alone toward the fresh, foggy air that blew in from the coast. The Techeuns watched her go.

"There is only the plan," Illyn said. "Remember your vows, Sedia."
entries.text_zh:
埃里斯·摩恩回到了灶神星前哨站。她的谈判很成功，双方一致同意用情报和长期的结盟来交换援助。就这样，觉醒者率先知道了大航海家：他的哲学，他的策略，还有他的弱点。正当女巫们在这把神王甩出的宝剑前设想种种可能性时，她们接到命令要像摆渡者卡戎那样盲目地在一座能量井下建立一个王座世界。

纳希娅画出了设计图纸，波希娅进行了计算。她们在东海岸用一个小型裂痕发生器进行了首次试验。在确认方法正确以后，她们进入了一座大教堂，开始挖掘能量井。在那里，莉丝尔和赛迪娅在魅痕的帮助下，利用一只针鼻蜥蜴的形象占卜出了第一个钻孔的位置，而卡丽和秋露·知则在下方深处一个被她们命名为“汇流殿”的大殿中建造了大门。”

伊琳不断地用女王兰做药，直到她的衣服发臭，她的手被染成红黑色。她警觉地行走于位面之间，在一片广阔的抽象迷雾中理清了现实的丝线，让其中一些更靠近，另一些更远离。

玛拉和魅痕一起塑造了她的第三个王座，而她们的作品所呈现出的艺术性正是她们在这种合作关系中所感受到饥渴快感的最好证明。她们将这里命名为厄琉息斯，在那些上维大厅里，玛拉终于为苏尔竖立了一尊雕像。

到了将能量井与门外的虚幻联结起来的时候，赛迪娅问道：“让这扇门不需要钥匙是不是会更好？”长着巨大鹿角、有着宽阔虎爪的毒蛇魅痕像绞索般紧紧盘住整个房间。

“是蛋。”玛拉心不在焉地边咬着指甲边纠正道。

“钥匙太重了，根本没人能拿得起。”看到她们说得隐晦，卡丽鼓起勇气说道。

赛迪娅不屑一顾地挥了挥手：“是，是，我知道。”她们都知道大门需要进行长达数周的超因果能量充能，而在这个太阳系里几乎没有任何东西能提供大门所需要的如此巨大的能量。几乎没有。“不过——我们……”

“我们能信任守护者吗？”伊琳冷冰冰地补充道。

玛拉的手在主井控制机关的光滑表面上拂过，然后转身独自走向从海岸吹来的新鲜、朦胧的空气。灵巫们目送她离开。

“这只是计划”，伊琳说道，“牢记你的誓言，赛迪娅。”

entries.name: Oracle
entries.text:
There came a morning when the Techeuns spoke in unison, though none were near each other, and they said, ++WHO ARE YOU WHO BUILDS A HIDDEN CITY HERE IN OUR THOUGHTS?++

And Mara, alone in the Queenswalk of the Dreaming City, heard their voices ring out as if each Witch stood beside her, and she said to the empty air, "I am Mara Sov. Who are you?"

The answer came at once, ++WRONG! IT IS THE EKPYROSIC. WE ARE THE NOTHING-SPACE FABRIC.++

Hearing this, Mara recognized a riddle. She turned at once and left the Queenswalk so that Riven would not be inspired. As she walked, she thought. At length she said, "Wrong. You are the Ancients. You are the idea that gives fate its shape."

That one-voice came again, as clear and strong as the birth of the universe, booming with dispassionate curiosity, ++IT THINKS ITSELF WISE! HOW DID SOMETHING LIKE IT ATTAIN SUCH REVELATION?++

Mara lengthened her stride, taking the steps three at a time so that she could duck into a little-used transport gate. She emerged in a small coastal observatory—then nothing more than a grand dormitory—and found Kelda Wadj, the Allteacher, hovering four feet off the ground. Blood poured from her ears and nostrils. Her eyes saw nothing. The other Techeuns were transfixed thusly in a geometric array around the Dreaming City—each one inert, suspended, bleeding.

Mastering her horror, Mara said, "I have lived alongside you." And because she was afraid for Kelda, she asked, "Do you intend violence?"

At once, the Techeuns collapsed to the ground like marionettes from severed strings—all but Kelda Wadj, whose augment blazed with coruscating light. She rose higher into the air and began to unravel, particle by particle. As she came undone, she said, ++NOW IT INSULTS US.++ 

Mara steeled herself against the horrific sight of her old friend's ruin. She had been a fool to think the riddling was over. She said, "Of course." Violence, after all, is a matter of perspective. "What I mean is, what would you ask me?"

Beloved, wise Kelda Wadj burst apart and then collapsed all at once into a singularity that burned and burned and burned but destroyed nothing around it. From her un-throat came the voice again, which Mara felt in the atomic marrow of her bones, and it said, ++WHAT WOULD IT ASK US?++

For fifteen days and fifteen nights, the singularity burned unshielded.

On the sixteenth day, they began construction of the Oracle Engine, which took the singularity of the Allteacher as its seed-heart.
entries.text_zh:
一天早上，分散在各地的灵巫们突然同时说了一句话：++你是谁是谁在我们的思想中建造了一座隐藏的城市？++

而独自走在幽梦之城女王大道上的玛拉也如同她们就在身边般听到了她们的声音，于是她对空气说道：“我是玛拉·索维。你们是谁？”

她立刻就听到了回答：++回答错误！是焚逝。我们是虚无空间的构造体。++

听到这句话，玛拉明白了这是一道谜语。她立即转身离开了女王大道，不想让魅痕有所感悟。她边走边思考着。许久以后，她说道：“不对。你们是古人。是你们为命运赋予形状。

那如同宇宙的诞生般清晰而嘹亮的声音又响起了，语气中带着平淡的好奇：++它觉得自己很聪明！这样的东西怎么会获得这样的启示？++

玛拉加大了步幅，三步并作两步地冲进一个甚少使用的传送门中。她来到一个小型海岸观测站——然后又进入一片大宿舍区——找到了盘旋在离地四尺高处的全知导师凯尔妲·瓦杰。她的耳朵和鼻孔中鲜血直流，她的眼睛已经什么都看不见了。其他灵巫也都在幽梦之城中以一种几何阵列的形态无法动弹——一动不动，悬在半空，鲜血直流。

控制住内心的恐惧，玛拉说道：“我曾与你共同生活。”因为她害怕凯尔妲，她又问道：“你打算使用暴力吗？”

灵巫立即像断线的木偶般跌倒在地——但凯尔妲·瓦杰是个例外，她的能量增强，疯狂地闪耀着。她飞到更高的空中，开始分解成微粒。完全分解之后，她说道：++它现在在羞辱我们。++

玛拉看着旧日好友的恐怖死亡过程，下定了决心。她以为谜题已经结束，这真是太天真了。她说道：“那当然了。”暴力，其实要看从什么角度来看待。“我的意思是，你会问我什么呢？”

她所爱戴的睿智的凯尔妲·瓦杰瞬间爆裂，然后崩塌成一个奇点，持续不断地燃烧却并没有毁灭周围的一切。玛拉感受到她骨髓的原子传来了她那已不再存在的喉咙所发出的声音：++它会问我们什么呢？++

奇点在毫无保护的情况下燃烧了15天15夜。

到了第16个白天，她们以全知导师的奇点为种子核心，开始建造神谕引擎。

entries.name: Misraaks
entries.text:
The Vandal stoops as he exits the Galliot. All of his arms are bound behind his back, so he cannot shield his eyes from the bright sun. A breeze stirs his cloak. There is a cliff behind him and lush gardens ahead. His jailer would not grant him the honor of a quick death, so she must intend to torture him. She thinks he will yield like the flesh-lovers from House Judgment. She is wrong. Whatever indignities she can muster are nothing compared to what he deserves.

With his chin held high, he imagines shucking off his armor and laying all four of his arms in his Captain's hands. His Captain is his mother, and she will not dock him with a scythe. She will twist and tear his arms from his body like she is shucking a fine, fat crab for dinner, and he will be glad of the slow, sick cracks and crunches of his bones. He will be glad of the shame. Let him go limbless for the rest of his wasted life. Let the Ether-thirst shrivel him up like a yaviirsi fig.

"What do you think?" his jailer asks in a language he cannot understand. She steps up beside him and claps a hand on his shoulder. He flinches. She is nearly as tall as he is, and for a creature with no claws, her grip is strong and sure.

Together, they contemplate the gardens.

"It's all a bit much for my taste," she admits as he sneaks a furtive look at her.

Her bow is unstrung. There is only one arrow in her quiver.

She is stupid.

He whirls, trips her, and sprints for the cliff. She swears, recovers, and lunges after him. As he pitches himself off the edge, he thinks of his mother's shame and prays that she forgets him. Better that she never had a son than a weakling so easily captured by the enemy.

It is his bad luck that she catches his foot with one hand. His helmet slams into the rocky cliffside. A piece of his rebreather cracks off and disappears into the mist far below. He flails, but he cannot drag her down with him; somehow, she hauls him in like a fish. As soon as she has him on solid ground, she binds his ankles with the string of her bow. "All right," she says, catching her breath. "All right." She chuckles, pats his shoulder fondly, and then pulls him upright like a sack of psakiks.

She takes a step back, brushing off her hands against the seat of her trousers. He glowers, the surliest psakiks sack this side of the Great Machine, hating her horrible, squared-off teeth and her blunt, stubby fingers. "Let's try this again, shall we?"

Drawing two fractal knives from sheaths on her thighs, she makes a perfect ireliis bow before him. Thunderstruck, he sits up straight. Stares.

"Not good?" she asks, and tries again.

Furious confusion takes him. This is some kind of trick. Blasphemous mockery. "Iirsoveks," he rumbles.

She shakes her head. "Nama." Sheathing one of her knives, she holds out her free hand with her fingers spread in supplication.

He draws his chin toward his throat with this fresh betrayal, narrowing his secondary eyes. It speaks!

Slowly, without breaking eye contact, she lays her other knife on the ground between them. The blade points toward her boots. He watches her every movement. How many secrets have the flesh-lovers betrayed, that this creature can make peace like a cringing drekh before his kel?

She taps two fingers against her cuirass. "Sjur," she says slowly, then she points at him.
