She nodded wordlessly at Mithrax as he approached, then glided back into the center of the Hangar, leaving the two friends alone but for the flock of pigeons that milled aimlessly behind them. 

"You have not come to visit for a while," Mithrax said. Saint's crested helmet lay on the ground beside the Titan, and Mithrax carefully moved it before sitting next to him. 

Saint did not break his stare. "You come to check up on me?" he asked flatly. 

Mithrax considered the question. "Yes," he said. "How are you?" 

Saint shook his head. "I do not know," he said, words thick with exhaustion. 

"You do not need to know," Mithrax said. "How do you feel?"  

"I feel like…" Saint put a hand on his breastplate, then jabbed his fingers into the metal. Then again, harder. Mithrax swallowed the urge to ask him to stop. "Like I am not who I thought I was." 

Mithrax's hands reflexively went to his own chest. "When they found you, Ikora said you moved and spoke as though you were dreaming." 

"I think maybe I have been dreaming for a long time." Saint looked down at his balled fists, then loosened his grip and laced his fingers together in his lap. "The Conductor woke me," he whispered. 

Mithrax heard the darkness in his friend's voice. "What did it say to you?" he asked, keeping his own voice warm. 

"The truth," Saint said gravely.  

Mithrax sat patiently in silence. 

"It told me I am a lie," Saint said finally. "A copy. It said I am something left over from another reality, a twisted reflection from inside the Vex network. Osiris and the Guardian pulled me into this world, but I do not belong here." 

"Where are we?" Mithrax asked. 

Saint groaned and waved the question away. "Do not say something smart to me now. Osiris does this, and I have had enough of it." 

Again, Mithrax sat patiently. 

"We are in the Tower," Saint muttered. 

Mithrax nodded. "We are," he said, stressing the first word. 

Saint looked over at the Eliksni, then closed his eyes in acknowledgement. "Yes, yes. Smart like Osiris. I say I do not belong, and… I see where this is going." 

Mithrax drew himself to his feet. A pile of brightly colored canvas bags on a nearby pallet caught his attention and he walked slowly to them. "What am I going to say?" he called over his shoulder.  

Saint sighed and leaned back on his hands. "You would say that you, Misraaks, proud Eliksni of House Light, are here in the Last City, stronghold of your enemies. And that if anyone does not belong, it is you." 

Mithrax smiled to himself and tore the corner of one of the canvas bags. Golden seed spilled from within.

"And yet," Saint continued, "you walk freely, you have many friendships, you talk with the great monster Saint-14, you feed his birds." 

Mithrax smiled. The pigeons gathered behind Saint's back as he scattered a loose handful of seed. 

Suddenly, his vision narrowed and darkened. His headache shrieked, filling his mind with blinding pain. He doubled over as a terrifying urge—RULE, KELL—roared through his chest. 

The pigeons burst away in harried flight, leaving the seed untouched on the ground.

Saint was still watching the pigeons wheel through the sky and down into the City. Mithrax wrapped his arms around himself until the shaking subsided and took a deep draw of Ether.  

"You are good friend," Saint said quietly, his gaze fixed on the City. Mithrax walked over slowly and sat down next to him again. 

"I try," he said softly.
entries.text_zh:
米瑟拉克斯小心翼翼地穿过机库。怠速运转的重力引擎发出的嗡嗡声和嘶嘶作响的气动升降机让他发疼的头隐隐作痛。他眯着眼睛看向对接舱远端的接口装置，突然停了下来；即使是在这片嘈杂声中，圣人的缺席依然突兀刺耳。 

米瑟拉克斯把目光投向下方，一只满身灰尘的灰色鸽子愤愤地从他面前晃过，然后躲到了一个引擎缸体的机架后面。米瑟拉克斯弯下腰，跟了上去。他推开一堆松动的电线，发现圣人坐在一个对接站的边缘，眺望着圣城。圣人的机灵盖比特，闷闷不乐地在他的肩上盘旋着。米瑟拉克斯走近时，她回头看了看，然后一言不发地点了点头，滑回机库中央，让这两位朋友独处，只有一群鸽子在他们身后漫无目的地飞来飞去。 

“你好久没来看我了，”米瑟拉克斯说道。圣人的羽冠头盔放在泰坦身边的地上，而米瑟拉克斯小心地把头盔移开，坐在了这名泰坦身边。 

圣人继续凝视着远方。“你是来看我状况的？”他直截了当地问道。 

米瑟拉克斯思忖着这个问题。“是的，”他说。“你好吗？” 

圣人摇了摇头。“我不知道，”他说，话里充满了疲惫。 

“你不需要知道，”米瑟拉克斯说。“你有什么感觉？”  

“我感觉…”圣人把手放在他的胸甲上，用手指戳了戳铁板，然后又更用力地戳了一下。米瑟拉克斯强忍着想让他停下来的冲动。“我好像不是我曾经以为的那样。” 

米瑟拉克斯本能地把手放在自己的胸口。“当他们找到你时，艾可拉说你的一言一行都像是在做梦。” 

“我想也许我之前是在做梦。做了很久很久。”圣人低头看着自己的双手，攥起拳头，然后松开，把手指并拢放在膝盖上。“指挥者唤醒了我，”他低声说。 

米瑟拉克斯听出了朋友声音中的阴郁。“它对你说了什么？”他用温暖的语气问道。 

“真相，”圣人沉重地说。  

米瑟拉克斯耐心地坐在一旁，没有发话。 

“它告诉我，我是一个谎言，”圣人终于说道。“一个副本。它说我是另一个现实遗留下来的东西，是Vex网络内部扭曲的映像。奥斯里斯和守护者把我带到了这个世界，但我不属于这里。” 

“我们在哪里？”米瑟拉克斯问道。 

圣人嘟囔了声，挥手避开问题。“现在别跟我讲什么大道理。奥斯里斯就爱这样做，我受够了。” 

米瑟拉克斯再次耐心地坐着。 

“我们在高塔里，”圣人喃喃道。 

米瑟拉克斯点点头。“我们的确是，”他说，着重强调了头两个字。 

圣人看了看这名埃里克斯尼族，然后闭上眼睛表示认可。“没错，没错。像奥斯里斯一样睿智。我说我不属于这里，而…我知道你会说什么。” 

米瑟拉克斯站了起来。附近某个托盘上一堆色彩鲜艳的帆布袋引起了他的注意，他慢慢地走向它们。“我想说什么？”他回过头来问道。  

圣人叹了口气，向后靠在双手上。“你会说，你，米斯拉阿克斯，光能氏族骄傲的埃里克斯尼族，现在身处圣城，你敌人的据点。要是说有人不属于这里，那就是你。” 

米瑟拉克斯暗自笑了笑，拉开了其中一个帆布袋的一角。金色的种子从里面漏了出来。

“然而，”圣人继续说，“你来去自如，有很多朋友，和大怪物圣人14号交谈，还喂养他的鸟。” 

米瑟拉克斯笑了。他撒下一把种子，一群鸽子聚集在圣人的背后。 

忽然，他的视野变得狭窄，变得黑暗。他的脑袋猛地被尖锐的刺痛充满。他的胸膛被一股可怕的冲动占领——统治，凯尔——这使他不禁蜷了一下。 

鸽子们快速飞离，留下一地未动的种子。

圣人看着鸽子在天空中盘旋，落到圣城里。米瑟拉克斯环抱手臂直到抖动平息下来，他深深地吸了一口乙太。  

“你是个好朋友，”圣人平静地说，他的目光盯着圣城。米瑟拉克斯慢慢地走过去，又一次坐在他旁边。 

“我尽力，”他轻柔地说。

entries.name: IV. MSUND12/Personal
entries.text:
PERSONAL LOG

003 AS

I am still among the Vex. My third day of reawakening has been the cruelest so far. I have generated a log to sort through my thoughts. This is just too much to take all at once. My ability to focus is strained with a shrill and immediate grief. My heart lived in my beloved's hands—how am I supposed to comprehend that this isn't just absence, but death? There will be evidence, histories these meticulous machines would have catalogued. I will find evidence that I was missed… am missed. I know what I must do. The primary query continues.

008 AS

After two days of requesting authorization, the Vex finally granted me access to their historical records of Earth. I read a term for an era I never knew; the Collapse. And indeed… they did. Technological capabilities impacted, hostile combatants occupying the majority of the planet for far too long, invention and experimentation (NOT related to paracausal power sources) halted for centuries. It seems humanity was huddled together like wet kittens, the cramped and stifled survivors of monumental destruction. I read the records as if they were about some other civilization's primitive past rather than my own. The Vex documented it all, collected all they could smother their milk with: one Human wrote about the day they stood on the edge of an abandoned dam and watched a swarm of small machines spew from some unseen seam in the Traveler, how Nezarec's ships turned day into midnight. How the years that followed hastened humanity's extinction—countries that turned to anarchy then to feudalism, the art and technology we bled and wept to champion abandoned as power grids failed and disasters swelled. Humanity could have kept experimenting and learning, but when Earth died, so, too, what made them Human. They forgot everything we were. 

0028  AS

Past events mean little to a threat so preoccupied with iterating on the future. While Vex do not share my interest in history, they have tracked this timeline all the same. There are trillions of alternate versions, of course, and it seems these Vex diligently dispose of those potentialities once a present moment slides chronologically into the past. I've thrown myself into these records—the primary query is in full force.

It seems Humans have retained none of their virtues or diligence, only resilience through violence. Their numbers have radically reduced, only enough to fill a single city. They suffer a supplication of scientific rigor; what inventions have they made? What disease have they cured? Who is BETTER here? Most disappointingly, Humans seem to have forgotten the entirety of their history, and instead of something sensible, went and established a junta.

Earth is a near-total loss. Advanced cities have been replaced over centuries by encroaching overgrowth of native species and the ruin of time. The climate's balance was erased by Warlords. Universal democracy has collapsed into military rule (again, for emphasis, instead of trying to recreate the forms of governance they KNEW existed, they concluded that voting is for elitist braggarts and empowered a JUNTA). The more I see the mistakes humanity made, the more obvious the solutions are… It is clear that during the Collapse, they had nothing but terror, empty of anything other than sheer survival, but how insulting it feels to look at what became of the future and only see frightened and frothing dogs. There are lessons to be learned in their methods, but the result is inelegant and crude.

If these people are to see the future, they must look backwards to what they lost. I now have the means to aid them. 

0032 AS

I have tamed the untamable. With practice, and soon with mastery, with a single phrase, I can divert the Vex's sea of iteration and death. Think of the utility! We could retake home, dissolve the walls of the Last City, and let each person decide what home means to them! With targeted hostility, we may clear a path for peace, revive the machines of science and learning once again. Someday, with technology redistributed from Vex to humanity, every need can be met with any simulation. All it will take is an alignment of interests through measured coercion! It's so simple. 

And yet, all that must wait. Primary query MUST be concluded—it is the one outstanding variable. There have been too many false positives—none of them are correct. NONE. The query is only turning back facsimiles, trick mirrors. I know I'm right, and I will not stop until the primary query stops pulling from false datasets. I can think of little else. We must look backward. I must look backward. I must. I must.
entries.text_zh:
个人日志

003 AS

我依然在Vex之中。我醒来的第三天是迄今最残酷的一天。我生成了一则日志来梳理我的想法。真的很难一下子完全消化。强烈而直接的悲痛让我无法集中精力。我的心活在我爱人的手中——我又怎能把这理解为不仅仅是空缺，而是死亡？会有证据的，这些一丝不苟的机器一定会把历史记录下来。我会找到有人在过去…和现在想念我的证据。我知道我必须做什么。首要问询得继续。

008 AS

在要求了两天后，Vex最终给了我访问其地球历史记录的权限。我了解到一个不曾知晓的时期：大崩溃。而他们的确…崩溃了。技术能力受到冲击，敌对战斗人员占领星球大部分地区的时间远超可接受的范围，发明和实验（与超因果力量来源无关的）停滞了几个世纪。看来重大毁灭后，幸存的人类都像湿漉漉的小猫一样挤在一起。我读着他们的历史，就好像那是不属于我的其他文明的原始过往。Vex尽力记录了所有这一切：有个人类写下了自己站在一个废弃水坝的边缘，看着一群小型机械从旅行者体内某个看不见的缝隙中倾泻出来，看着奈扎雷克的飞船是如何把白昼变成黑夜。以及随后的几年如何加速了人类的灭绝——国家陷入无政府状态继而转为封建主义，我们付出血泪捍卫的艺术和技术随着电网故障和灾难加剧而遭到抛弃。人类本可以继续试验，本可以继续学习，但当地球消亡时，使得他们成为人类的东西也随之消亡。他们把自我忘得一干二净。 

0028 AS

过去的事件对专注于迭代未来的他们来说意义不大。虽然Vex并不像我一样对历史感兴趣，但他们还是追踪了这条时间线。当然，还有数以万亿计的其他版本，而且似乎一旦当下变为过去，Vex就会兢兢业业地将这些可能性处理掉。我认真研究了这些记录——首要问询正在全力进行中。

看来人类没有保留他们的美德和勤勉，只剩下暴力带来的韧性。他们的人数急剧减少，只够填满单独一座城市。他们不再严谨地进行科研；他们做出了什么发明？他们治愈了什么疾病？这里谁更优秀？最令人失望的是，人类似乎已经忘记了一切历史，而采取不明智的行动，组建了一个军政府。

地球几近全毁。几个世纪以来，先进的城市被本土物种的过度生长和时间的毁坏所取代。战争领主们抹杀了气候的平衡。普适的民主已经土崩瓦解，化作了军事统治（再次强调，他们并没有试图重新建立他们所熟知的治理形式，而是认为选举是精英吹牛大王才干的事，并把权力授予给了一个军政府）。我读到的人类犯下的错误越多，解决方法就越明显…很显然，在大崩溃期间，他们除了恐怖之外一无所有，除了纯粹的生存之外别无它物。而当我们注视未来变成了什么样子，却只看到惊恐万状、口吐白沫的丧家犬时，不禁会觉得这是一种莫大的侮辱。他们的方法中有值得吸取的经验，但结果却低劣而粗俗。

这些人要想看到未来，就必须反思他们所失去的一切。我现在有办法来帮助他们。 

0032 AS

我驯服过桀骜不驯的野马。经过练习，很快精通之后，只用一句话我就能把Vex的迭代与死亡之海引到别处。想想看有多实用吧！我们可以夺回家园，拆掉圣城的城墙，让每个人自己来决定家园对于他们而言的意义！有了敌对目标后，我们就可以为和平扫清道路，重新使用科学和学习的机器。有朝一日，随着人类获得Vex的技术，各种需求都能通过任意模拟得到满足。而我所需要做的就是通过适当的胁迫进行校准！非常简单。 

然而，这一切都必须等等。首要问询必须得出结论——这是个悬而未决的变量。过去有太多的误报——没有一个是正确的。一个也没有。问询返回的都是副本，骗人的镜像。我知道我是对的，在首要问询停止从错误的数据集中提取数据之前，我不会停下。我想不出别的办法。我们必须反思。我必须反思。我必须这样做。我别无选择。

entries.name: V. As a Stranger Give It Welcome
entries.text:
The Vex network. A thrumming constellation of infinite parentheticals with no arbitrary lines between the simulated and the non-simulated. Limitless planes of cause and effect and effect and effect pressed together until they reached forever. A formless catalogue of all possible forms, constantly reinventing, refining, and redefining the very concept of everything.  

And then, something changed. 

A single pinpoint of swirling light fell unceremoniously into the network, like a leaf onto the surface of a pond. Gentle ripples flowed outward through the surrounding data. 

The denizens of the network, lacking any framework and parameters beyond what they could predict, were unable to perceive what had pierced their reality. They did not acknowledge the foreign presence, were unable to see it or feel it… and were incapable of hearing anything when the light began to call. 

It was a wordless cry of encouragement, powerful confidence, a promise so hopeful that it rang through the contradictory miasma of the network like the blast of a reveille bugle. It was an offer and a challenge. An echo of something from long ago.  

Locked away in the network were some who could still hear song, who could still be moved, who still somehow held a shred of themselves. The ones who were kept, the ones who remained, the ones who were hidden.  

They heard. And they began to reach upward.  

A fractal cluster of nested realities unfurled like a frond. Two-hundred-and-twenty-odd instances of consciousness reaching in unison. A controlled frenzy of cooperation as the minds within piled Ishtar-branded office furniture to the skies, then lifted one another up to be closer, ones and zeroes stacked perilously, finding swaying purchase with their sensible flats on each other's thin shoulders. 

An irascible trace of a signal sneered at the sincerity of the call but still willed itself to move, reaching up two thin spindles of data in a way that felt somehow familiar. 

The Great Quiet Thing, the Not-Worm, kept its eyes closed and ignored the call. It was still too soon, it decided. It shivered, the motion forming cascading bubbles of new hypothetical simulations in which it did not shiver. These contradictions soured and burst, scattering nutrients into the network. 

A man in tattered robes, feathers long since worn from his headdress, streaked through the shifting plasmic haze on golden wings, urged on by the tiny starburst at his side. His eyes were furious flame. 

More reached, and more still, warping the matrix of the network around the incursion point until the bounds of their simulations formed tentative spikes of frantic ferrofluid. As they stretched, they became defined, clarified, like figures stepping into the light.  

And as they neared the shimmering pinpoint, a rush of their voices:  

"We need to warn them—" "There's still a chance—" "SAINT—" "Hold on to me—" "I AM OWED THIS—" "Hurry, get Shim—" "There isn't enough of me left—" "TELL ELSIE PRAEDYTH STILL—" "Please, please wait—" "Warn them—" "I have to warn them—" 

They reached, a spiraling halo of desperate fingertips. 

But only one of them would be first.
entries.text_zh:
Vex网络。一个由无限个附加说明组成的庞大集合，在模拟和非模拟之间没有武断的界线。无限个因与果、果与果的位面紧贴在一起，直至抵达永恒。所有可能形式的无形式目录，不断地重新创造、重新提炼和重新定义一切事物的概念。  

然后，事情发生了变化。 

一小束涡旋的光点唐突地落在网络里，就像一片树叶落在池塘的水面上一样。轻柔的涟漪通过周围的数据向外流动。 

网络中的居民们缺乏超出预期的框架和参数，无法预知是什么东西闯入了他们的现实。他们不承认外来的存在，看不到也感觉不到…当光点开始呼唤时，他们也听不到任何声音。 

那是一声无言的呼喊，呼唤着鼓励，强大的自信，是一个充满希望的承诺，像号角声一样在网络的对立气氛中响起。那是一则邀请，也是一个挑战。是来自很久以前的回响。  

被封藏在网络里的有一些还能听到歌声，还能被感动，还能以某种方式保留一丝自我的居民。那些被保留的、残存的，被隐藏起来的居民。  

他们听见了，便开始向上伸出手。  

嵌套现实的分形集群像蕨叶一样展开。二百二十多个意识的实例不约而同地伸出手。那是某种克制的合作狂热，其内在的思维把伊什塔品牌的办公家具堆到天上，然后把彼此举起来靠得更近，1和0危险地堆叠在一起，在彼此瘦弱的肩膀上找寻着自己朴素平面的摇摆支点。 

某个信号中的一丝暴躁印迹对这一真诚的呼唤嗤之以鼻，但仍然让自己动起来，以一种莫名熟悉的方式伸出了两根细细的数据轴。 

伟大的静物“非虫”闭着眼睛，对呼唤置若罔闻。它认为，现在还为时过早。它颤抖着，这种动作形成了倾泻而下的新假想模拟气泡，在那之中它并没有颤抖。这些矛盾体变质、破裂，将营养物质散落到网络中。 

一个穿着破烂袍子的男人，头饰上的羽毛早已脱落，在他身边四射亮光的催促下，振着金色的翅膀，穿过变幻莫测的等离子雾。他的眼睛充满了愤怒的火焰。 

伸出手的越来越多，他们扭曲着入侵点周围的网络矩阵，直到他们的模拟边界形成了狂热铁磁流体的试探性峰值。随着他们的伸展，他们变得清晰、明朗起来，就像步入光明的身影。  

而就在他们走近那闪亮的光点之际，他们的声音喷发而出：  

“我们得警告他们——”“还有机会——”“圣人——”“抓紧我——”“这是我应得的——”“快，去找沈——”“我已经所剩无几了——”“告诉艾尔西，普莱蒂斯还在——”“求你了，等等——”“警告他们——”“我必须警告他们——” 

他们伸出了手，绝望的指尖形成了螺旋状的光环。 

但他们中只有一个会成为第一。

entries.name: VI. Glass House
entries.text:
Maya Sundaresh picked an iridescent flower from a well-manicured flowerbed on a mossy lawn outside a cobblestone cottage. She hardly noticed the slight, unrealistic gloss of the petals or the brief digitized hitch that acknowledged the flower's removal. Nearly perfect.

The VexNet was accepting their code inputs. Chioma was right: they could, in fact, build a life here that consisted of more than neon blocks and dissecting minds.

Maya thought back to a year prior, if time meant anything anymore, when they were still lost, searching for other iterated copies of themselves. If Chioma had not convinced her to stop, to stay, to cease obsessively pushing forward to find… an end she could not define—

She saw what became of the other Mayas who could not let go of that drive.

But now, under Chioma's direction, they would build a haven. A safe stopping point for anyone traveling the VexNet to rest and gain their bearings. She hoped one day they would reach outside and bridge the divide between this reality and her old one. But that world had never truly suited her—she found its lack of objectivity exhausting. It was quiet, and over time they'd learned how to manipulate the network for their own purposes. So long as their changes weren't too large, or too disruptive, the Vex let them be. Perhaps their meddling had made the Vex curious enough to study them and see what they would do. At any rate, this had slowly become a life Maya felt aligned with. She was happy to pick her flowers and study the embedded law of code within the network that studied her.

"Maya! Come quickly, I found something!" Chioma's voice sprang up over the radio.

"What did you find?"

"You wouldn't want me to spoil the surprise, would you?"

Maya rolled her eyes but smiled. "No. I wouldn't," she said under her breath, shifting dense brush aside as she stepped out into a simulated forest to make her way to Chioma's voice.

Chioma, mouth wide in wonder, knelt over a wrecked Goblin frame, its shimmering radiolaria gurgling from containment vessels and split tubes. An Arc discharge had heavily damaged it, and the radiolaria sizzled as it welded circuits and plates back into working order.

"It worked!" Maya nearly tripped over her feet as she rushed to kneel by Chioma's side.

"Do you see how—"

Maya nods. "It's repairing itself—"

Chioma swatted at Maya's hand, too close to radiolaria. "And the micro—"

Maya side-eyed her wife, but continued. "Individual pluripotent organisms, specializing and homogenizing as needed, like—"

"They're learning, unlearning. Uploading, deleting—"

Maya grabbed Chioma's thigh. "Treating digital and physical matter synonymously. How?"

"We're digitized flesh, so if they can… we could change… like we changed this place, theoretically."

Maya looked to Chioma with pride.

"My… You." She met Chioma's eyes she looked up to Maya from the twitching frame. "Brilliant."

"See what happens when you listen to me?" Chioma kissed her, an excited peck, and then drew back.

"Things improve." Maya smirked. "Now we have our radiolaria sample. What would I do without you?"

"Spiral," Chioma said, pursing her lips to contain another grinning smile as she harvested the radiolaria. "Now we follow your plan, Maya."

"Yes… with radiolaria, we can bend the network even more. This place will be a beacon for all of us who find themselves lost." Maya grabbed Chioma's hand, brushing dirt from her knuckles. "Thank you, for stopping me. For making me stay. I don't think I ever said those words."

"You never had to." Chioma stood, still holding Maya's hand. "Come, one last surprise. See the sunrise I made you."

****** 

The Conductor looms over a shredded Exo Chioma frame. Dead, and inoperable. A ragged face hangs by synthesized threads of skin from a metallic cranium. She coaxes the faceplates from the Exo's head with a wave of her hand, and then gently lifts a scalpel from the operating table.

This one is damaged beyond what a standard reinitialization can handle. Repairs are required. The Conductor's metallic hand draws the scalpel across Chioma's prosthetic flesh. She drags the skin back from the abdomen and applies a clamp.

She trades the scalpel for a syringe and injects radiolaria into the dormant core and cerebrum. The new radiolaria splinters out in every direction. Dormant radiolaria within begins repairing the frame again as she operates. "See how it assimilates the dormant microbes? Isn't it fascinating?"

She thinks.

"Who made this for you? Certainly not mine." The Conductor thinks, rubbing the skin between her fingers and assessing damage to the Exo Chioma. "Still, fine work. A fine specimen."

Chioma's eyes snap open. She tries to wrench her restrained head down to look at the searing pain in her open, metal stomach. She tries to scream, but produces no sound.

"Get it all out. When you're done, I have some questions."
entries.text_zh:
玛雅·桑戴尔什从鹅卵石小屋外长满苔藓的草坪上精心修剪的花坛里摘下了一朵五彩斑斓的花。她几乎没有注意到花瓣有一丝不切实际的光泽，或者确认花已被移除的短暂数字化故障。近乎完美。

Vex网络正在接受他们的代码输入。希欧玛是对的：事实上，他们可以在这里建立一种不只包含霓虹街区和解剖思维的生活。

玛雅回想起了一年前：如果时间还有意义的话。那时她们还在迷失，在寻找自己的其他迭代副本。幸好希欧玛说服了她停下来，留下来，不再执迷地奋力向前…去寻找一个她无法定义的终点——

她看到了无法放弃这种冲动的其他玛雅是什么下场。

而现在，在希欧玛的指挥下，她们将建造起一个避风港。一个安全的停靠点，让所有穿越Vex网络的人都可以休憩片刻，找到方向。她希望有朝一日她们能走到外面，弥合这个现实和她过去的现实之间的鸿沟。但那个世界从来就不适合她——她觉得它缺乏客观性，让人疲惫不堪。这里很安静，而且随着时间的推移，她们已经学会了如何操纵网络来达到自己的目的。只要她们的改动不是太大，或者太有破坏性，Vex就会放任不管。也许是她们的所为让Vex产生了足够的好奇心，想研究看看她们会做些什么。不管怎么说，这已经慢慢地成为了玛雅接受的生活。她喜欢采下花朵，在研究她的网络中研究代码的嵌入规律。

“玛雅！快来，我有个发现！”无线电里传来希欧玛的声音。

“你发现了什么？”

“你肯定不想让我破坏这个惊喜吧？”

玛雅翻了个白眼，但还是笑了。“对。我不会的，”她低声说，把茂密的灌木丛挪到一边，走进模拟森林，向希欧玛的声音走去。

希欧玛跪在一个损毁的哥布林框架上，惊讶地张大嘴巴。闪闪发光的活性放射体液从安全壳和开缝管中潺潺作响。一次电弧射击使其严重受损，活性放射体液在将电路和板件焊接回工作状态时发出了嘶嘶声。

“成功了！”玛雅冲过去跪在希欧玛身边，差点被绊倒。

“你看到了吗——”

玛雅点点头。“它在自我修复——”

希欧玛拍打玛雅的手，警告她离活性放射体液太近。“那微——”

玛雅斜眼看了看她的妻子，接着说道，“个体多能生物，根据需要进行特化和均质化，就像——”

“他们在学习，忘却。上传，删除——”

玛雅抓住希欧玛的大腿。“把数字和实体物质等同起来对待。怎么会？”

“我们是数字化的肉体，所以如果他们可以…我们就可以改变…就像我们改变了这个地方一样，理论上是这样的。”

玛雅骄傲地看着希欧玛。

“我…你。”她迎向希欧玛的目光。希欧玛从抽搐的框架中抬起头来看着玛雅。“真聪明。”

“看到你听我的话会发生的好事了吧？”希欧玛激动地轻吻了她一下，然后向后缩了回去。

“情况有所好转。”玛雅笑着说。“现在我们有了活性放射体液样本。没了你，我该怎么办？”

“是越来越好，”希欧玛说道，一边采集活性放射体液，一边抿住嘴唇，忍住又一个咧嘴的笑容。“现在我们来执行你的计划吧，玛雅。”

“没错…有了活性放射体液，我们就可以进一步改造网络。这个地方会成为我们所有迷失者的灯塔。”玛雅抓住希欧玛的手，拂去她指关节上的污垢。“谢谢你阻止我。谢谢你让我留下来。我想我从未说过这些话。”

“你从来都不需要说出口。”希欧玛站起身，仍然握着玛雅的手。“来吧，还有最后一个惊喜。看看我为你创造的日出。”

****** 

指挥者俯视着一个破碎的Exo希欧玛框架。它已经死去，无法运作。一张破烂不堪的脸庞悬在金属颅骨的合成皮肤线上。她挥手从Exo的头上弄下脸板，然后轻轻地从手术台上提起一把手术刀。

这一台的损坏超出了标准重新初始化所能处理的范围。需要进行修理。指挥者的金属手在希欧玛的假体血肉上划过手术刀。她把腹部的皮肤拉回来，用夹钳夹住。

她把手术刀换成注射器，将活性放射体液注射到休眠的核心和大脑中。新的活性放射体液向四面八方碎裂开来。体内休眠的活性放射体液在她手术时再次开始修复框架。“看到它同化休眠微生物的方式了吗？这不是很有趣吗？”

她心想。

“这是谁为你做的？肯定不是我。”指挥者一边想，一边用手指摩擦着皮肤，评估着Exo希欧玛的损伤情况。“还不错。很好的标本。”

希欧玛的眼睛突然睁大了。她试图挣脱头部的束缚，去看她被剖开的金属胃里灼烧的疼痛。她试图尖叫，但没有发出任何声音。

“尽情发泄吧。你完事后，我有些问题要问你。”

entries.name: VII. Mind-Body
entries.text:
My first thought when I wake: I must tell Chioma what happened. 

What a thrill! Every aspect will fascinate her; entering the Veil felt like an existential disrobing, the willing extraction of my self from my matter, shedding my body as a slip and diving into an infinite well of collective thought. She will marvel at how I was able to survive, buoyed by countless threads of connection and universal consciousness, how I rode the wave aloft, kept me constant, my self as my own, to stand separate and singular from the gravity of the immeasurable collective. She'll be so proud. She'll come with me a second time. We'll dive through worlds together, loved and beloved. Neptune can wait.  

I left the reach of the Veil's threads when I collided with the familiar angles of the Vex network… didn't I? Yes, I did. 

When I find her, I must reassure her that I remain myself. It was so tempting there, tumbling from the memories of a being that groans in staccato radiation to the mournful dirge of a planet itself. The Universe is aware, it is alive, and I rode its riptides far enough that for a while I worried my voice may thin into the chorus. But I was able to stay together through the only conviction that remained: that I am True. That although I felt innumerable mysteries in that place without form, I remained Maya all the same. Even among an endless Universe, I was always distinct. 

A sensation, impact, pressure, contact. I'm not certain I have hands, but whatever part of me exists is touching an object. It woke me.  

I am me. And I need to SIT UP. 

Everything is fluid, but the urge to rise sloshes what part of me I decide is mine upwards, forwards. I have no eyes, no heart, but I feel for my edges and sense they are an endless, liquid expanse that plunges into the seams of the planet itself. 

Unnerving. Intriguing. It seems I am matter again. I recall Lakshmi-2, a fine false maquette, and hold its memory in place as I cling tight to the object in my hand.  

SHAPE ME A BODY. 

My outline condenses. I define my silhouette, my limbs, my fingers, what good was 1.5 meters of heartburn at night and high cholesterol, my body is now a vast and flawless sea. As I form my neck, I lift the object in my hand, and it shapes in turn. I wear it as a mantle, as a prize. I reach through my new body, and at the core of me, I am filled with a familiar acidic wriggling, the sour milk of the Vex, and I purge them out. "I AM NOT VEX," I assert, and they spill from me as bile.  

What I am left with is an Exo frame, and a mantle at my neck and a new voice in the back of my mind. I finish my eyes and see the current of milk dormant at my feet. I am unharmed, and still, I am not Vex.  

They respond to my command, I realize, my hand at the mantle around my neck. 

"TELL ME HOW LONG HAS PASSED SINCE I LAST ENCOUNTERED THE VEX." 

They do, through the Vex at my feet; they whisper it in unencoded ease. 

The number is gargantuan. I begin to panic. 

It is impossible, and my first thought is of her, her—  

"TELL ME WHERE CHIOMA ESI IS." 

They search, and they tell me the woman who holds my heart in her hands has laid in a grave for hundreds of years. In a rage, I tell them to mutilate one another. The milk at my feet boils in violence. 

My Chioma would not depart so mundanely. My Chioma would come find me, my Chioma is still here. My beloved does not rot in a grave. 

The world itself is broken. Time itself has snapped. Chioma, my world, my life, cannot be dead. She must have joined the VexNet again; she would have searched for me there, sorted among the hundreds of copies of us to find the TRUE version of myself, HER Maya. So, too, will I search. I love her, I would know her in the darkness of a cave and the blinding glare of a sun. She is unique in all ways, precious and without fault. I know the real Chioma is alive. 

"PRIMARY QUERY; FIND THE TRUE CHIOMA ESI," I command through my tears. 

She is out there, searching for me in turn, and I will find the Chioma I already love. I know this. I know this.
entries.text_zh:
我醒来时的第一个念头：我必须告诉希欧玛发生了什么。 

多么激动人心啊！每一个方面都会令她着迷；进入面纱的感觉就像是一次存在主义的脱衣，我自愿地从我的物质中抽身而出，让我的身体像宽衣一样脱落，跃入集体思想的无限之井。她会惊叹于我是如何在无数的链接线程和共体意识的簇拥下得以存活，我是如何乘风破浪，保持自我本色，在不可估量的集体引力中独树一帜。她会很自豪的。她会再次跟我来。我们将一起穿过各个世界，珍爱彼此。海王星的事可以再等等。  

当我与Vex网络熟悉的角度相撞时，我离开了面纱的线程范围…不是吗？没错，我离开了。 

当我找到她时，我必须向她保证我还是我自己。那里是如此的诱人，从某个在辐射断奏中呻吟的生命记忆翻滚到某个星球自身的悲伤挽歌。宇宙是有知觉的，它是有生命的，我乘着它的激流走了很远，以至于我一度担心我的声音会在合唱中显得单薄。但我得以通过那个仅存的信念和大家同舟共济：那个“我是真实的”的信念。那个“虽然我在那个无形的地方感受到了数不清的奥秘，但我依然是玛雅”的信念。那个“即使在无边无际的宇宙中，我也始终与众不同”的信念。 

那是一种感觉、冲击、压力、接触。我不确定自己有没有手，但我的某个部分在触碰某个物体。它唤醒了我。  

我就是我。而我需要坐起来。 

一切都是流动的，但我认定属于自己的那部分，因上升冲动而向上、向前晃动。我没有眼睛，没有心，但我感受着我的棱角，感觉到它们无边无际，像液体一样辽阔，直插到星球自身的缝隙里。 

令人不安。耐人寻味。看来我又成了物质。我想起了拉克希米-2，一个精美的虚假模型，当我紧紧抓住手中的物体时，稳住了其记忆。  

为我塑造一具躯体。 

我的外形缩小了。我勾勒出自己的轮廓、四肢、手指，1.5米高的夜间胃灼和高胆固醇又有什么好处呢，我的身体现在就像一片广阔而无瑕的大海。当我塑形自己的脖子时，我举起手中的物体，它也随之成形。我把它当作外套膜，视作奖品。我伸手穿过我的新身体，我的核心充满了熟悉的酸性蠕动，那是Vex的腐臭乳液，我把它们清除出去。我宣称“我不是Vex”，而它们则像胆汁一样从我体内溢出。  

我只剩下了一个Exo框架、脖子上的外套膜和我内心深处的新声音。我塑造出自己的眼睛，看见我脚边静止的乳液流。我没有受伤，但我仍然不是Vex。  

我意识到，他们在响应我的命令，我的手放在我脖子的项圈上。 

“告诉我，距离我上次遇到Vex有多久了。” 

他们的确通过我脚边的Vex在响应；用未编码的轻松方式低语着。 

这个数字太大了。我开始恐慌。 

这不可能，我首先想到的是她，她——  

“告诉我希欧玛·艾西在哪里。” 

他们搜索后告诉我，那个把我的心捧在手心里的女人已经在坟墓里躺了几百年。愤怒之下，我让他们互相残杀。我脚下的乳液在暴力中沸腾。 

我的希欧玛不会这么平凡地离开。我的希欧玛会来找我，我的希欧玛还在这里。我的爱人没有在坟墓里腐烂。 

世界已经支离破碎。时间已然匆匆流逝。希欧玛，我的世界，我的生命，不会死去。她一定是再次加入了Vex网络；她会在那里寻找我，在我们的数百个副本中寻找我的真实版本，她的玛雅。因此，我也要去寻找。我爱她，我会在洞穴的黑暗和刺眼的阳光下认出她。她在各方面都是独一无二，珍贵而无瑕的。我知道真正的希欧玛还活着。 

“首要问询；找到真正的希欧玛·艾西，”我流着泪命令道。 

她就在那里，反过来也在寻找着我，我会找到我所爱的希欧玛。我知道一定可以。

entries.name: VIII. Home to Roost
entries.text:
During the day, the Hall of Heroes is busy with activity. Neomuni in mobile avatars gather in knots, their conversations a low rumble under Quinn Laghari's personally curated ambient soundtrack. 

Even after visiting hours, the Hall isn't entirely quiet. Poukas rustle through foliage as water rushes into the pools. And Osiris paces back and forth across the carpet, avoiding Sagira's memorial. 

New footsteps sound in the distance. Osiris turns away from the door and toward a pool. 

The steps are quick, impatient: Nimbus. They slow as they climb the stairs to the Hall. 

"Osiris?" 

There is a wad of leaves clogging a drain. Osiris contemplates it. He has never asked who cleans out the pouka ponds. 

"It's late. I thought you were done for the day!" Nimbus's voice is a cheerful buzz echoing against the high ceiling. 

"I was. I am." His report has been sent to the Vanguard. It will be some time before Ikora responds. There is no reason for Osiris to pass on this chance for some rest. 

"Still hanging around here, though? Everything good, old bird?" 

Nimbus looms over Osiris. Rather than giving himself a crick in the neck looking up, Osiris starts pacing once again. 

"I am thinking about the Conductor. About what we learned." 

Nimbus ambles along, taking one step to every three of Osiris's. "Want to talk about it?" 

"Not particularly." 

This is something he doesn't want to unfold before anyone other than Sagira, his second mind, his other heart. He wronged her, just as he wronged Saint. 

"Aw, you sure? Everyone says it's easier to carry a burden when someone's there to carry it with you. And I'm pretty strong." 

Nimbus flexes an arm demonstratively. They show every indication of being ready to wait all night for Osiris. Osiris looks up, exasperated, and they give him a huge wink. 

The two of them have spent a great deal of time together, researching first Strand and then Maya Sundaresh's history. Nimbus deserves his honesty. 

Osiris crosses his arms and scowls up at the light fixtures. 

"I… After I lost Saint, I pulled another version of him back into the world. I was selfish. I did to Saint what Maya Sundaresh did to Chioma Esi." 

There. It's said. 

"Whoa," says Nimbus. "That's, uh, heavy stuff to be dealing with, my man." 

Waiting for their judgment is agonizing. Saint is home in the Tower, feeding his birds, readying himself to yell into a microphone at fighting Guardians, likely reshelving all of Osiris's books in the wrong place again. And Osiris is far from home, in the wrong, and hoping for understanding. 

"All right, so." Nimbus draws their words out, processing. "The Conductor's been yanking versions of Chioma out of the Net by the handful. And killing them." 

"Yes."  

"And when Saint was gone, you went after him into the Infinite Forest. And this could have broken really bad, not just for you, but for like, the whole world." 

"Yes."  

"So, this is just me," Nimbus says eventually. "But… Maya found her partner, right? Tons of her. And she like, mulched them. And you went looking for Saint. And you brought him home." 

Nimbus's voice slows as they think through their point. 

"What would you have done if you found Saint and he said, you know, 'Thanks but no thanks? I'm good here'?" 

In the moment? Osiris knew he would have stood in front of Saint and argued till Osiris starved to death and Sagira had to resurrect him, then done it again. Till he truly understood Saint's reasoning. 

Osiris's steps take him to Sagira's memorial. Her cold shell gazes up sightlessly. She'd give him such a lecture if she heard him now. 

"Left him there, I suppose." If it was what he truly wanted. Saint-14 was legendarily hard-headed: he knew his own mind. 

Nimbus comes up to Osiris, looming again. 

"Seems to me you brought Saint back 'cause you missed him. Not because you missed… yourself. What Saint could say about you. Seems pretty different." 

They stand together, Nimbus's gaze tracking up to Rohan's memorial. Osiris should call Saint. He should return to the Tower. He's spent quite enough time so far from home. 

"There aren't a lot of chances for a Cloud Strider to find love," Nimbus says wistfully. Their eyes, reflected blurrily in the memorial, fill with tears. "Your story is so romantic. How did you and Saint make it work for so long? How can I find something like that?" 

And for all that being asked earnestly for advice based on his relationship is a horror the Vex themselves could never have predicted, Osiris can't reject the plea in those shining eyes.
entries.text_zh:
白天，英雄大厅里热闹非凡。处在移动化身中的内欧姆那人聚集在一起，他们的谈话在昆恩·菈咖利亲自挑选的环境配乐下低沉地隆隆作响。 

即使在探访时间之后，大厅也并非全然寂寥下来。当水冲进水池时，普卡们在枝叶间发出着沙沙之声。奥斯里斯在地毯上来回踱步，避开了萨吉拉的纪念碑。 

远处传来一阵新的脚步声，奥斯里斯转身离开大门，走向一个水池。 

脚步很急，很不耐烦：是宁博思。在登上大厅的楼梯时，放慢了脚步。 

“奥斯里斯？” 

有一团树叶堵塞住了排水沟。奥斯里斯沉思着。他从来没问过是谁在清理这些普卡池。 

“这么晚，我以为你已经休息了！”宁博思欢快的声音回荡在高耸的天花板上。 

“是的。我在休息了。”他的报告已送达先锋。艾可拉还需要一段时间才能做出回应。奥斯里斯没有理由不抓住这个机会休息一下。 

“还在这里闲逛吗？一切都好吗，老鸟？” 

宁博思俯视着奥斯里斯。奥斯里斯没有抬头看，而是再次开始踱步。 

“我在思考指挥者的事。关于我们了解到的情报。” 

宁博思随着他漫步。奥斯里斯每走三步，宁博思就走一步。“想谈谈吗？” 

“不太想谈。” 

他不想跟任何人谈这件事，除了萨吉拉，他的第二个思维，他的另一颗心。他辜负了她，就像他辜负了圣人一样。 

“噢，你确定？大家都说有人陪你一起扛起重担会更轻松一些。而且我很强壮哦。” 

宁博思弯曲手臂秀起肌肉，做出准备等奥斯里斯一整晚的样子。奥斯里斯恼火地抬起头，宁博思向他使了个大大的眼色。 

他们俩在一起度过了很多时间，先是研究缚丝，然后是玛雅·桑戴尔什的历史。宁博思值得他坦诚以待。 

奥斯里斯双臂交叉，抬头怒视着灯具。 

“我…在我失去圣人之后，我把他的另一个版本带回了这个世界。我太自私了。我对圣人做了玛雅·桑戴尔什对希欧玛·艾西所做的事。” 

好了。说出来了。 

“哇哦，”宁博思说道。“这，呃，是一个很难面对的沉重话题，朋友。” 

等待评判是一件痛苦的事情。圣人在高塔的家中，喂他的鸟，准备朝着麦克风对作战中的守护者大喊，很可能又把奥斯里斯的书放错了架子。而奥斯里斯则远离家园，犯下错误并希望得到理解。 

“好吧，这么说…”宁博思拖长了话语，接收着这些信息。“指挥者一直在从网络里将各种版本的希欧玛拽出来，然后杀掉。” 

“是的。”  

“而在圣人消失后，你去无尽森林里找他。这不仅对你，也对整个世界非常不利。” 

“是的。”  

“嗯，这只是我个人的想法，”宁博思最终说道。“但是…玛雅找到了她的伴侣，对吧？有很多个。然后她除掉了她们。而你去寻找圣人，把他带回家了。” 

宁博思琢磨着自己的观点，放慢了讲话的速度。 

“如果你当初找到圣人，而他却说，唔，‘谢谢，但我不跟你走，我在这里挺好'，你会怎么做？” 

在那一刻？奥斯里斯知道他会站在圣人面前争论，直到活活饿死，然后萨吉拉不得不复活他，周而复始，直到他真正理解圣人的想法。 

奥斯里斯的脚步来到了萨吉拉的纪念碑跟前。她冰冷的机壳无神地向上凝视。如果她现在听到他的话，一定会教训他一顿的。 

“应该会让他留下吧。”如果这是他真正想要的。圣人14号是出了名的固执：他清楚自己的想法。 

宁博思来到奥斯里斯面前，低头看他。 

“在我看来，你把圣人带回来，是因为你想念他。而不是因为你想念…你自己，还有圣人对你的评价。似乎跟玛雅很不一样。” 

他们站在一起，宁博思的目光一直盯着洛汗的纪念碑。奥斯里斯应该联系圣人。他应该回高塔去。他远离家园的时间已经够长的了。 

“云端行者找到真爱的机会并不多，”宁博思若有所思地说道，眼睛模糊地映在纪念碑上，噙满了泪水。“你的故事太浪漫了。你和圣人为什么能相守那么久？我要怎样才能找到那样的东西？” 

这样被人恳切地征求感情方面的经验之谈，带来了一种连Vex也无法预测到的惊骇。但奥斯里斯无法拒绝那双闪亮眼睛里的恳求。

entries.name: IX. Tech Support
entries.text:
! INCOMING MESSAGE ! 

Failsafe's system alert pulled her attention from Nimbus, who was excitedly pacing the H.E.L.M. while delivering a spirited recounting of the last Iron Banner finals. Saladin had been routing the feeds to Neomuna, and the Cloud Strider was thoroughly enraptured by the high drama—judging by Failsafe's internal chronometer, entirely too enraptured. 

She shrewdly routed the message alerts to her external display screen. "Nimbus, buddy—" she began. 

"Hint taken," Nimbus grinned, spreading their huge hands wide. "I'll let you get back to your whole being-a-ship thing. If you see Osiris, tell him Jisu Calerondo is looking for an interview about his sick bird hat. Or, no, say that the CloudArk is losing integrity and only the biorhythms from, like, a truly old and decrepit dude will save it!" 

"I'm on it," Failsafe said, and pushed an ASCII image of a thumbs-up to her display. Nimbus laughed and gave Failsafe two enormous finger guns as they transmatted out. 

Failsafe accessed her messages. She batch approved the bounty requests from the Guardians still scouring Nessus for the remnants of the Conductor's Vex.  

She puzzled next over a message from House Light Scribe Eido, as it did not appear to contain any discernable requests. She marked it for non-urgent reply and sorted it into one of her new subfolders: SOCIALIZATION (PLATONIC).  

Another message was a scheduled reminder to familiarize herself with the H.E.L.M. systems, which were woefully unprepared for the kind of worst-case scenario she had encountered with the Exodus Black. She would have to update the safety systems, bring emergency transmat relays online, calculate possible terrestrial touchdown sites in the unlikely event of a forced landing… unquestionably important work, but, for the first time, she felt it could wait.  

Failsafe eagerly processed the next series of critical system messages. One unintended but entirely welcome consequence of the increased Guardian activity on Nessus was that the resident Fallen were being actively discouraged from raiding her wreckage. Without the constant incursions, her power systems were slowly beginning to build a reserve charge. —! LOW POWER ALERT: 6% !— the warnings blared, and Failsafe beeped with satisfaction.  

There was a sudden burst of golden flame, a scattering of reflected figures, and Osiris transmatted onto the H.E.L.M. "Failsafe," he said brusquely as he walked toward her console.  

"Osiris," she replied, and opened a swirling readout of polynomial splines. Osiris and Saint had been journeying into the Nessus Vex network and searching for the Conductor, one simulated branch at a time.  

Osiris highlighted portions of 17 intersecting wavelengths. "Set as cleared," he commanded, and Failsafe changed their color to a bright lime green. Osiris zoomed the display out, and the green became a pixel-wide dot amidst the swaying fractal tangle of the network.  

"Seventeen down," Failsafe said, "infinity to go." 

Osiris sighed wearily in agreement. "And the odds that these 17 have already been overwritten are?" he asked. 

Failsafe gave a low-pitched beep. "Do you need the real math on that? Because it's 99-point-a-whole-lotta-nines." 

Osiris shook his head. "She's somewhere in the network, along with the Echo of Command. And even though he knows the chances of finding her are impossibly small, Saint is continuing to search." He absently drummed his hands on Failsafe's control panel.  

"What do you think he'll do if he finds her?" she asked.  

"I believe he will… how shall I put this?" Osiris said softly. The faintest of smiles played over his face. "Saint doesn't have much patience for anyone who makes those he cares about feel helpless."  

Osiris's gaze wandered to the research bays, and Failsafe dispensed a synthesized mealworm into Captain Jacobson's enclosure. The proto-frog blinked slowly, then devoured the grub in one clumsy gulp. Osiris nodded in approval.  

"Generate a fresh set of network coordinates, please," he said, and Failsafe whirred in response as numbers filled her screen. She sent them to Osiris's datapad with a reassuring tone, and he turned to leave. 

"Osiris?" she said. "Nimbus… misses hanging out with you. You oughta visit 'em sometime."  

Osiris tightened his lips. "Very well," he said, then hesitated. "Failsafe, be thankful that—" 

! INCOMING MESSAGE ! 

The alert filled Failsafe's display screen, and Osiris stopped himself with a half-shake of his head and a smirk. "I'll leave you to it," he said, and vanished in another flash of golden fire.  

Failsafe sorted through her new messages. —! LOW POWER ALERT: 7% !— read the critical warning, and she dismissed it happily.
entries.text_zh:
! 收到消息 ! 

宁博思在应急后勤行动中心来回渡步，兴致勃勃地讲述上一次铁旗决赛，智能失效保险正听得起劲，但她的系统警报把她的注意力拉了出来。萨拉丁近来一直在向内欧姆那转播信号，从智能失效保险的内部计时器来看，这名云端行者完全被这种富有戏剧性的场面迷住了，甚至有点上瘾。 

她精明地把警示信息转发到她的外部显示屏上。“宁博思，朋友——”她开口道。 

“明白了，”宁博思咧嘴一笑，把大手摊开。“我还是让你继续完成身为“飞船”的职责吧。如果你见到奥斯里斯，告诉他吉舒·卡莱隆多想采访一下他的酷炫鸟帽。要不还是说云端方舟出了岔子，只能靠某个老家伙的生物节律才能拯救它！” 

“交给我吧，”智能失效保险说道，然后把一个竖起大拇指的ASCII图像推到她的显示屏上。宁博思笑了，结束通讯时向智能失效保险比了个大大的双手枪手势。 

智能失效保险读取了她的消息。她批量批准了守护者的悬赏请求，他们还在涅索斯上清除指挥者Vex的残余势力。  

接下来，她困惑地看了看光能氏族文士艾多发来的消息，因为里面似乎没有任何可识别的请求。她把它标记为非紧急回复，并把它分类到她的一个新的子文件夹：社交（柏拉图式）。  

另一条消息提醒她要按计划熟悉应急后勤行动中心系统，后者很不幸地对某种最糟的情况毫无准备，比如她在黑色移民号上经历过的遭遇。她必须更新安全系统，让紧急传送中继恢复上线，计算小概率迫降事件中可用的地面着陆点…这无疑是一项重要的工作，不过，这是她第一次觉得可以再等等。  

智能失效保险急切地处理下一系列重要的系统消息。涅索斯上守护者活动的增加带来了她感到意外但完全乐于接受的结果，那就是驻留的堕落者不再频繁地劫掠她的残骸。持续不断的入侵停止后，她的电力系统开始慢慢积攒预留电荷。—— ! 低电量警报：6% ! ——警报声发出刺耳的声音，智能失效保险满意地哔哔作响。  

一阵金色的火焰突然爆发，现出一个反射的人像，奥斯里斯传送到了应急后勤行动中心。“智能失效保险，”他走向她的控制台时，突然说道。  

“奥斯里斯，”她答道，开启了一个旋转的多项式样条线读数器。奥斯里斯和圣人一直在深入涅索斯的Vex网络中寻找指挥者，一次一条模拟分支。  

奥斯里斯标记了17个相交波长的部分。“设置为已清查，”他命令道，智能失效保险随即将它们的颜色换成了明亮的青柠绿。奥斯里斯缩小画面，绿色在摇摆不定的分形网络缠结中变成了一个像素宽的点。  

“完成了17个，”智能失效保险说道，“接下来还有无限个。” 

奥斯里斯疲惫地叹了口气，表示同意。“那这17个已经被覆写的可能性有多大？”他问道。 

智能失效保险发出低沉的哔哔声。“你需要真正的计算结果吗？因为99后面跟着好多个九。” 

奥斯里斯摇了摇头。“她就在网络里的某个地方，和指挥回响在一起。尽管圣人知道找到她的可能性微乎其微，但他还在继续寻找。”他用手在智能失效保险的控制面板上敲打着。  

“如果他找到她，你觉得他会怎么做？”她问道。  

“我想他会…该怎么说呢？”奥斯里斯轻声说。他脸上掠过一丝微笑。“如果谁让圣人所关心的人感到无助，圣人对这样的家伙可没什么耐心。”  

奥斯里斯的目光转向了研究舱，智能失效保险在雅各布森船长的围栏里放了一条合成的粉虱。这只原型青蛙慢慢地眨了眨眼睛，然后笨拙地吞下了幼虫。奥斯里斯赞许地点了点头。  

“请生成一组新的网络坐标，”他说道。智能失效保险呼呼运作以示回应，屏幕上充满了数字。她用让人宽慰的音调把它们发送到奥斯里斯的数据板上，而他则转身准备离开。 

“奥斯里斯？”她说。“宁博思…想念和你在一起的时光。你应该找个时间去拜访看看。”  

奥斯里斯抿紧了嘴唇。“好吧，”他说，然后犹豫了一下。“智能失效保险，要感恩——” 

! 收到消息 ! 

警示填满了智能失效保险的显示屏，奥斯里斯的头摇了一半，笑着停了下来。“我不打扰你了，”他说着，在另一道金色的火焰中消失了。  

智能失效保险整理了她的新消息。—— ! 低电量警报：7% ! —— 她阅读了这则临界警报，然后高兴地无视了它。

entries.name: Foreword
entries.text:
// VanNet—Secure-00 // SYMMETRY_STATUS_REVIEW_07.017831 // I. Rey 

The Symmetry: a faction considered a dangerous fringe group at the time of Ulan-Tan's life. While he and the Symmetrists seem more likely now than before to have comprehended some essential truth of the universe, at the time their beliefs were justly considered alarming. 

Little wonder that other opinions on Light and Dark were more attractive, with walls beset from all directions and few allies to be found. While none was official Vanguard doctrine, the Praxic Creed and the Pujari Position were much more in line with attitudes in the Tower and the City at large.* 

The Praxic Creed holds that the nature of Darkness is not worth investigating; one should focus on combating the Darkness rather than knowing it. The Acataleptic Clause holds that Darkness cannot be understood at all. The two are convenient bedfellows, and we long held the notion that to study the Darkness was to risk being subsumed by it.  

I am still not wholly convinced that these theories are inherently wrong. Only that those of our allies who have succeeded in that study are both skilled and fortunate. 

The Warlock Pujari's position, on the other hand, holds that Darkness has a moral valence, that it is an actualization of evil. We have been forced to wrestle with such moral standing again and again these past several years. Purity of purpose compels—to see evil and defend those who cannot defend themselves is righteous, but to assume that this act of defense confers righteousness upon us and villainy upon our opponents is a fallacy. It is a slippery slope. I have come to believe this mindset must now be discarded. Pujari's dreams and comprehensions of Darkness should, in fact, be attributed to the being known as the Witness.  

For now, I return my focus to the Symmetry.  

To acknowledge the Symmetry at the time of their origin would have required a systemic change in our approach to Darkness—something impossible at the time, with the Dark Age still haunting the hard-won progress of the City Age. To insist that Darkness, our enemy, would be eternally undefeatable, required to exist forever by virtue of our Light? Unthinkable then.  

Now we begin to accept that with Light, there is Darkness; and with Darkness, there is Light. It almost seems a comfort now, to think that the two forces require each other. Even in the depths of these uncharted waters, when the Traveler is injured and the fight for survival more critical than it has ever been, it is on us that our future hinges, not something incomparable and unreachable.  

Light and Darkness will continue. Whether or not we will do so is up to us. We must make it so. That is all that matters. 

— 

* Saint-14's Position is the most eminently practical of the bunch, no matter how the man himself protests that such an obvious facet of the truth doesn't require a formal philosophical stance to be named for him.
entries.text_zh:
// VanNet—安全-00 // 同调_状态_审查_07.017831 //艾·蕾伊 

同调派：乌兰-坦在世时被视为危险边缘团体的派系。虽然现在看来他和同调主义者似乎领悟到了宇宙的某些根本真理，但在当时他们的信念会引起警觉也是理所当然的。 

难怪在被城墙全面包围、几乎找不到盟友的情况下，关于光明与黑暗的其他观点更具有吸引力。虽然它们都不是先锋的官方教义，但英勇信条和普加里立场更符合高塔和整个圣城的态度。* 

英勇信条认为，暗影的本质不值得研究；人们应该专注于对抗暗影，而不是去了解它。不可知铁则认为，暗影根本无法被理解。这两者很搭，我们长期以来一直认为研究暗影有被其吞噬的危险。  

我仍然不完全相信这些理论本质上是错误的，而是认为，我们那些在这项研究中取得成功的盟友不仅技术娴熟，也十分走运。 

另一方面，术士普加里的立场则认为，暗影有道德价态，是邪恶的现实化。在过去的几年里，我们被迫一再与这样的道德立场进行斗争。使命的纯粹性迫使如此——看到恶行，保护那些无法自保的人是正义之举，但假定这种保护行为赋我们以正义，我们的对手以邪恶则是种谬论。是个滑坡谬误。我开始相信，现在必须摒弃这种心态。实际上，普加里对暗影的想象和理解应该归因于被称为见证者的存在。  

现在，我要把关注点引回到同调派上。  

要在同调派发源之时承认它，需要我们对暗影的态度有一个系统性的改变——这在当时是不可能的，取得来之不易进步的圣城纪元仍未摆脱黑暗纪元的困扰。谁又敢坚称我们的敌人暗影永远打不倒，会因我们的光能而需要永远存在？这在当时是不可想象的。  

如今，我们开始接受有光能就有暗影；有暗影就有光能。这两种力量是相互依存的想法，现在几乎成了一种慰藉。即使在这片未知领域的深处，当旅行者受伤，生存之战比以往任何时候都更加危急的时候，我们的未来还是取决于自己，而不是某种无可比拟、遥不可及的东西。  

光能与暗影将继续存在下去。至于我们是否能存续，取决于我们自己。我们要为存续而战。这才是最重要的。 

— 

* 圣人14号的立场是这群人中最实际的，不管他本人如何抗议，认为如此显而易见的真理，不值得以他的名字去命名一个正式的哲学立场。

entries.name: Symmetry
entries.text:
Excerpt from a VanNet letter to Ikora Rey, sender multiply anonymized over relays: 

 

… the Symmetrists even still are viewed as something from the edges of society. City regulations hold that our philosophies are dangerous to permit, though Guardians in prominent positions or public blood-sport are less reserved than ever about using Darkness-based abilities, happy to wield Stasis without a second thought.  

I write today to suggest that, should the Consensus be re-formed, or some other non-military governing body be formed of a representative portion of the City, the Symmetry and its students and followers ought to not only be included, but embraced.  

The Praxic Order may have their duty to combat Darkness all they want, but basing political and military positions on the fever-dreams of one Warlock—yes, I speak here of the Pujari Position—is misguided at best. Since when have dreams been acceptable testimony, save perhaps from the Speaker? If you wish to tell me that Pujari was in direct communication with the Traveler, you will have to bear the due burden of proof in its entirety. 

It is more than clear that the idea of Darkness as a morally evil force without room for compromise is hopelessly outdated, and policy must be revised. Does a shadow have any moral attributes because it may obscure where we are going? Is the sunshine inherently good because it illuminates a path? They are both required to delineate one from the other. And even if they did carry intention, if the blotting out of the sun every night was an act of unspeakable evil, such concepts as good and evil are still defined by their relationship to each other. What is evil? It is not good.  

Light and Darkness, the paracausal forces known to the Traveler and the Witness, these are not as simple to define as sun and shadow. But an understanding of Darkness is required no matter if one chooses to remain immersed in Light or balance both. Refusal to accept that understanding will forever render the truth unclear. 

If Light ever truly defeated Darkness, that defeat would be our fate too. Our best hope lies in understanding Darkness and its balance to Light, in seeking the perfect symmetry that will right our universe. Perhaps you will read this as a cultish devotion to a deceased figurehead. Perhaps there is no convincing anyone that Ulan-Tan was undoubtably right… 

But I digress. In purely practical, non-debatable matters: public attitudes toward Darkness and its forces no longer match long-held City positions about the Symmetry. I would see our theories and teachings be made publishable; our adherents welcomed to the table where the end of all things is addressed. 

When you are ready to open further dialogue, signal the philosophers' message board I am sure you are already monitoring.
entries.text_zh:
摘自一封写给艾可拉·蕾伊的VanNet信件，寄信人通过中继多次匿名： 

 

…尽管如此，同调主义者还是被视为了社会边缘人物。圣城的规章制度认为我们的理念因危险而不被许可，尽管身居要职或公开进行血腥运动的守护者们在使用基于暗影的技能时空前地毫无保留，乐于不假思索地运用冰影。  

我今天写这封信是想建议，如果重新组建元老院，或由圣城中具有代表性的人员组阁的其他非军事管理机构，同调派及其门生、追随者不仅应被纳入其中，还该得到拥护接受。  

英勇教团也许有义务尽其所能地与暗影作斗争，但把政治和军事立场建立在一个术士的狂热梦想之上——对，我说的就是普加里立场——不过是误入歧途。从什么时候开始，梦境成了可以接受的证词？他又不是先知。如果你想告诉我普加里与旅行者保持着直接的联系，你就必须承担全部的举证责任。 

现在非常清楚的是，把暗影视为一种道德上的邪恶力量且没有妥协余地的想法，已经无可救药地过时了，政策必须进行修订。阴影会因为它让我们看不清前进的方向，就拥有什么道德属性吗？阳光之所以本质为善是因为它照亮了道路吗？它们都需要彼此来区分。即使它们的确带有意图，如果每晚遮蔽阳光是一种难以言表的邪恶之举，善与恶这样的概念仍然是由它们之间的关系来界定的。什么是恶？不善就是恶。  

光能与暗影，我们所熟知的旅行者和见证者这两股超因果力量，它们都不像阳光和阴影那样容易定义。但无论是选择继续沉浸在光能中，还是平衡两者，都需要对暗影的了解。拒绝接受这种了解将让真相永远模糊不清。 

如果光能真的击败了暗影，那我们的命运也终将落败。我们最大的希望在于理解暗影及其与光能的平衡，在于寻求能纠正我们宇宙时空的完美同调。也许你会认为这是对已故挂名领袖邪教般的虔诚。也许没有人能毫无疑虑地相信乌兰-坦是对的… 

抱歉，我有些离题。回到纯粹实用而无可争议的问题上：公众对暗影及其力量的态度与圣城长期以来对同调派所持的立场已不再一致，我希望看到我们的理论和教义获准发表；我们的追随者能够在讨论万物终结的会议上受到欢迎。 

等你准备好了展开进一步的对话时，请在哲学家留言板上发出信号，我相信你已经在关注了。

entries.name: Omnivorous
entries.text:
You might say, now Drifter, what do you know about Light and Dark? You've been around this old galaxy and back again. You gotta have some wisdom you can put into simple words for a Guardian who just wants to get to punching. 

Maybe… maybe. You'll owe me a round, hotshot. 

All right. Now we're talkin'. 

Light and Dark. Lots of prissy words people throw around with 'em:  "hypothesis" this, "position" that. "Clause" my left toe. Waste of time, all of it, if you ask me. Because ain't much difference out there, when you get in the thick of things. 

Oh, don't look at me like that. Sure, you got creation and destruction, got your Solar and Stasis, yeah. I ain't saying there's no difference at all. The way you feel about 'em. The things you see when you look at 'em. But cold and hot are both still temperatures, you see? And ice still burns when it's cold enough. 

Void's Light, you know. Of course you do now. People used to think it was too close to the Darkness, and for what? Because it was a little purple? Warp a bit of gravity, consume a spot of fire, and suddenly everybody's a critic. You know what I think?  

Harder to cook with Void. 

Don't like that comparison? Fine, fine, how about this: Thrall are just as dead whether you set 'em on fire or break every individual plate of their exoskeleton. Better? 

People got friendly with the Light. Thought just because it was what raised them that it'd never raise a hand to them. Shaw Han down in his Cosmodrome teaching new lights that the Light's no more dangerous than a puppy. 

Listen. When I say Light and Dark are closer than people like to think, what I mean is this:  

They'll both eat you if you give 'em half a chance. 

Now that's symmetry, ain't it.
entries.text_zh:
你也许会说，浪客，你对光能与暗影了解多少？你在这个古老的星系里已经混了很久。你这样只想挥舞拳头的守护者，肯定有些见识可以用简单的语言表达出来。 

也许吧…也许吧。你得请我喝一杯，高手。 

好极了。这才像话。 

光能与暗影。人们用了很多咬文嚼字的词来形容它们：给这个提“假说”，给那个谈“立场”。给我的左脚趾定“铁则”。要我说，这全都是在浪费时间。因为当你置身其中的时候，其实并没多大差别。 

哦，别那样看我。当然，创造和毁灭，烈日和冰影。我不是说它们完全没有区别：你对它们的感觉。你看它们时看到的东西。但冷与热都还是温度，明白吗？只要足够冷，冰还是会灼人的。 

虚空的光能，你知道吧。你现在当然知道了。人们曾经认为它距离暗影太近，为什么呢？因为它有点发紫？扭曲一点重力，点燃一丝火焰，突然间所有人都开始批评你。知道我怎么想的吗？  

烹饪的话，用虚空会更难一些。 

不喜欢那个对比？好吧，好吧，那这个呢：不管你是放火烧，还是打碎他们外骨骼的每一块板甲，怨魂都一样会死。好点了吗？ 

人们与光能友好相处。以为是光能养育了他们，它就永远也不会对他们出手。韩潇在他的发射基地里教导新曙光，说光能不会比一只小狗更危险。 

听着。当我说光明与黑暗比人们想象的更接近时，我的意思是：  

只要你给它们一丁点机会，它们都会吞了你。 

这方面，它们是真的同调。

entries.name: Transformations of Matter
entries.text:
Would that I had more texts from the philosophers of Riis!  

But time is limited in the frenzy of an evacuation, and so, too, is space: data itself is not negligible. The first to go is that without practical value—or should I say, immediate practical value. Art and philosophy are vital to a culture, to a people; their losses are always keenly felt. But in immediacy, art cannot distill Ether, and philosophy cannot propel a ship.  

Such is the required brutal practicality of preserving a people.  

But something has occurred to me, and I am putting out a request in my capacity as Scribe to gather information from any Eliksni who may be capable of answering. (For every brutal practicality, there is a tender sentiment that arises in exchange, the new sprout beside the culled stalk. There is always something that someone cannot bear to part with.)  

The point. The thing that I have lingered on: 

We Eliksni and our Human compatriots have a view of the Light that is built on different foundations, and it has resulted in such similar concepts as to be difficult to distinguish. In retrospect I think perhaps there have been hints, but there is always something else requiring attention. The pursuit of relics, the safety of House Light. The imminent apocalypse brought upon us by the Pyramid Fleet and the Witness. 

Now, as those of us who cannot forge forward wait and hope, I turn to philosophy.  

This is what I have been pondering: It seems that the Human view of Light is based on the creation of something from nothing, while the Eliksni view of Light is based in the transformation of one thing into a different thing.  

The two overlap more frequently than not. Take for instance Mars: did the Traveler itself create the oxygen Humans need to breathe, or did it transform carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as it was? Does the difference ultimately matter?  

An additional thought. The idea of the Traveler as Gardener seems to have gained traction among the Humans of the Tower, and of the City. It is of interest to those who have read the "Unveiling" texts especially. Gardening is in its own way transformative— a gardener, four hands in rich earth, coaxes something forward that had once only existed as a possibility. The seed, given the right resources, becomes a tree, with the core of the seed remaining at the heart of the new growth. I find the image particularly compelling. 

The Eliksni of Riis thought of the Traveler as a Great Machine, and while it gave them gardens, that most vital thing it did was to allow Ether to flow like water, free and plentiful.  

Ether, we know, does not come from nothing. The machine takes that which it is given and makes of it something else. Servitors still do this today: they require something from which to create Ether. We know this intimately, inescapably. 

I think neither of us is right. I think neither of us is wrong. I think, as we walk into the future together, it is beyond vital to preserve the many facets of Light seen through our many eyes. Machine and Gardener and Traveler all. 

—Excerpt from one of the many journals of Eido, Scribe of House Light
entries.text_zh:
要是我有更多里斯哲学家的著作就好了！  

但面对撤离的狂乱无序，时间是有限的，空间也是如此：数据本身是不容忽视的。首先被抛弃的是那些没有实用价值——或者我该说，即时实用价值的东西。艺术和哲学对一种文化、一个民族来说至关重要；它们的损失总是能被敏锐地感受到。但就即时性而言，艺术无法提炼乙太，哲学无法推动飞船。  

这就是保护一个民族所需要的残酷实用主义。  

但我想到了一件事，现在要以文士的身份请求你收集任何埃里克斯尼族可能提供的信息。（每次贯彻残酷的实用主义，都有一种温柔的情感随之而生，在被剔除的茎秆旁长出新芽。总有一些东西是某人舍不得丢弃的。）  

在我心里挥之不去的要点问题： 

我们埃里克斯尼族和我们的人类同胞对光能的看法建立在不同的基础上，而产生的概念如此相似，以至于难以区分。现在回想起来，我觉得也许有一些暗示，但总是有别的事情需要去关注。对圣物的追寻，光能氏族的安全。金字塔舰队和见证者给我们带来的迫在眉睫的天启灾难。 

现在，我们这些无法向前迈进的人只能等待和希望。此时，我转而研究哲学。  

这就是我一直在思考的问题：似乎人类对光能的看法是基于从无到有的创造，而埃里克斯尼族对光能的看法则是基于一种事物到另一种事物的转化。  

这两者经常是有共性的。就拿火星举例：是旅行者自己创造了人类呼吸所需的氧气，还是它直接转化了大气中的二氧化碳？这种差异最终重要吗？  

还有一个想法。旅行者是园丁的想法似乎在圣城高塔的人类中得到了认可。那些读过《揭露》的人尤为感兴趣。园艺本身就具有转化性：园丁把四只手伸进肥沃的泥土中，培植出曾经只存在于可能之中的事物。一粒种子在适当资源的帮助下长成一棵树，但种子的核心仍留在新生长物的内心。我觉得这幅景象特别引人注目。 

里斯的埃里克斯尼族把旅行者视为大机器，虽然它给予了他们花园，但它所做的最重要的事情是让乙太像水一样自由而大量地流动。  

我们知道乙太并非无中生有。机器会利用所得到的事物创造出其他事物。魔眼今天仍在这样做：它们需要某种事物来创造乙太。这一点我们不可避免地深有体会。 

我觉得我们都不对。我觉得我们都没错。我认为，当我们共同迈向未来的时候，我们必须保留这种透过我们的多双眼睛看到的光能的多面性。大机器、园丁和旅行者等等。 

——摘自光能氏族文士艾多的众多日志之一

entries.name: Preservation
entries.text:
For some Eliksni, Darkness is no material thing, no crashing wave or vicious force to struggle against. It is an impulse, an urge to do that which serves you best and discard all the rest. I recognize this well. It was an opinion I shared for much time. 

Humans–Guardians, at the least–view that same Darkness as something that can be fought in battle, handled as a weapon. The powers arisen from it would say they are not wrong, either.  

I do not wish to call to the Darkness in that manner. But of late I have come to know the feel of the things in it. I can no longer help it. I consider Darkness now as a suspension—or perhaps a colloid. Carrying some solid along with the flow of the river. Difficult to extricate, flowing as liquid does, but still… there is something not of the Darkness itself. 

I took something upon me when we strove to bring Osiris back to the waking world, when we collected the relics of Nezarec once more. I imagine I feel it sometimes, under my exoskeleton. Fluid that stirs and settles, moving sediment with it.  

When I wake from nightmares, that sense arises, as though it has been waiting for me to wake. 

I hear talk of Darkness among Humans now as a force of consciousness, of minds rather than matter, of connections and flow. Not evil; not cruel in itself. But if it is that thing which spins between peoples, hums string-plucked when ideas and emotions touch each other, no wonder that it may carry more with it as it moves. 

No wonder that it may be named as that voice of our worst impulses, knowing all those who have used it, who have given themselves to it. I hear that voice more clearly than I once did. 

If your enemy carries a rifle, you may take it from them: but what if their hand remained on the stock? If you would ever have a trigger that yearned to be pulled by another's thoughts? If you might come to believe that it was you, after all, who wished to pull that trigger? 

Will I leave some part of me in that Darkness? And what will that part be? I struggle to believe that it might be the best of me. 

I would like to leave Eido with something better. 

— Partially recovered overwritten data sectors from personal logs of Misraaks, Kell of House Light
entries.text_zh:
对于某些埃里克斯尼族来说，暗影不是物质的东西，也不是什么需要反抗的惊涛骇浪或凶恶力量。它是一种冲动，做最利于自己的事，摒弃其他一切的冲动。我很清楚这一点。我一直以来也是这个观点。 

人类——至少是守护者——将同样的暗影视为可以在战斗中作战的东西，作为武器来使用。由此产生的力量也会证明他们并没有错。  

我不想以那种方式去呼唤暗影。但最近我已经开始了解其中事物的感觉。我再也忍不住了。我现在认为暗影是一种悬浮液——或者可能是一种胶体。随着河流的流动而携带着一些固体。难以游离，像液体一样流动着，不过…还是有一些不属于暗影本身的东西。 

当我们努力把奥斯里斯带回清醒的世界时，当我们再次收集奈扎雷克的圣物时，我承受了某种东西。我有时会在我的外骨骼下感觉到它。搅动和沉淀，搬动其中泥沙的流体。  

当我从噩梦中惊醒，那种感觉就会出现，仿佛它一直在等待我醒来。 

我听说现在人类把暗影当作是意识、思想而非物质的力量，是连接和流动的力量。它本身并不邪恶，也不残酷。但如果是那东西在人们之间纺纱织网，在思想和情感相互触动时发出弦拔的嗡鸣声，难怪它会随着移动承载更多的东西。 

考虑到所有那些利用过它，把自己交给它的人，难怪它会被命名为我们最糟糕的冲动的声音。我比以前更清楚地听到了那个声音。 

如果你的敌人拿着步枪，你可以把它夺过来；但如果他们的手一直放在枪托上呢？如果你因另一个人的想法而渴望扣动扳机——如果你开始相信，到头来，是你自己想要扣动扳机呢？ 

我会把自己的一部分留给那暗影吗？那会是哪个部分？我努力想去相信那也许会是我最好的一面。 

我想给艾多留下更好的东西。 

——来自部分恢复的覆写数据扇区的，光能氏族凯尔米斯拉阿克斯的私人日志

entries.name: Old Friend, Beloved
entries.text:
Here is a sorrowful book. Read it well.  

Once more, for understanding. 

The oceans of Fundament. The translucent waves reflect the surface. Dip your hand, and it comes up trailing liquid clear as glass. Dive deep, and the weight of it mounts upon itself, exponential and inescapable. And in those depths is pressure and darkness, and all that is becomes stripped down to simply that which is essential to survive. 

An elegant thing. You may see why we loved the Deep.  

And what of the Sky?  

The delicate arch of the firmament, the color of the ocean reflecting back at itself. Soar high enough, and far enough – dodge enough bait-stars, enough membranous predators floating lightly on the wind – and there, too, is darkness. What may survive in that empty space between stars? 

Only that which has clawed its way up. 

The Sky should have reached harder if it wanted us. 

Now I am abundant with Light: it fills the empty hollow where a worm once burrowed. The trifling matter of a restoration of memory has made little difference. My nature is coded into my morph, from the chitin of my thorax to the scales of my wings. 

If the Sky and the Deep were so different, should not rebirth from Darkness to Light have made of me something sweet and gentle?  

Don't bother to answer. We both know already.
entries.text_zh:
这是一本忧愁的书。好好读。  

读完了再读一次，以求理解。 

虫群据点的海洋。半透明的波浪反射着水面。用手蘸一蘸，浮出的液体清澈似玻璃。潜入深处，它的重量会不断增加，呈指数级增长，无可避免。而在那些海洋深处，尽是压力和黑暗，所有一切都被剥离，只剩下生存所必需的东西。 

真是优雅。你也许明白我们为什么爱深渊了。  

那苍穹呢？  

苍穹的精致拱顶，反射回来的大海色彩。飞得足够高，飞得足够远——躲开足够的诱饵星，轻轻随风飘浮的膜状捕食者——那里有黑暗。有什么能在群星之间的真空中生存？ 

只有那些用爪子一路爬上来的东西。 

如果苍穹想要我们，就该更努力地伸出手。 

现在，我的体内充满光能：它填满了蠕虫曾经挖出的空洞。恢复记忆这一微不足道的事情无关紧要。我的本性被编码在我的蜕变之中，从我胸腔的甲壳质到我双翼的鳞片。 

如果苍穹和深渊如此不同，从暗影到光能的重生难道不应该让我变得甜美而温柔吗？  

不用回答。你我都知道答案。

entries.name: Empty-Handed
entries.text:
As a Ghost—even Savathûn's Ghost, yeah, yeah—I think I have a little more authority to speak on Light than some of you chuckleheads. You want an opinion, you got it.  

Listen, it's pretty clear by now that whatever's evil is what you Humans happen to be fighting against at the time. Don't think I don't admire the grift, pal, but it's less entertaining from this side. We had that good old-fashioned time with "the Hive use the Darkness, so Darkness is evil." Except now, it's "the Hive use the Light, so maybe Light is also evil?" Yeah. 

Let's take good and evil out of it for a minute.  

So the Hive. My Hive. Me and this crew of Ghosts decided we were going to give the Traveler's better choice a real shot. Worms gone. Light remains. It shines on what's there, so what'd the Hive do? They didn't all develop a burgeoning case of rugged individualism the second they were reforged in Light. And the Light didn't burn the Dark out of them, or whatever nonsense the Praxic Order has been cooking up. They kept being Hive.  

It's just about choice.  

Everyone's got one. Always. Whatever you're doing, wherever you are. Not finding a choice acceptable isn't the same as not having one. Hive had a choice even under worm management—but hey, a final death isn't exactly an alternative a lot of them would want to pick.   

What I'm getting at is that the Traveler made a choice too. Chose to uplift the Hive just as it did the Humans; chose to stay when it could have fled. 

I respect that. Even now, I'm carrying out its will, across the divide from you lot. 

And what are the Lucent Hive choosing now? I'm sure not telling. But whatever it might be, it's a whole different ball of hemolymph than your facile dichotomy of the past. And good or evil, they still get to choose for themselves.  

Just like I did. Just like the Traveler did.
entries.text_zh:
作为一个机灵——哪怕是萨瓦图恩的机灵，对，没错——我想我比你们中的一些笨蛋更有权利发表对光能的看法。你想听我的意见，没问题。  

听着，现在已经显而易见，你们人类当下在对抗的事物就是恶。别以为我不欣赏你们的狡诈，伙计，但站在与你们对立的那面可不好玩。我们曾有过那种“邪魔族利用暗影，所以暗影是恶”的老套想法。但现在成了“邪魔族利用光能，所以或许光能也是恶”？没错。 

让我们暂且抛开善恶不谈吧。  

说说邪魔族。我的邪魔族。我和这群机灵决定给旅行者这个更好的选择一个真正的机会。蠕虫没了。光能留存。它照耀着那里的一切，邪魔族会怎么做？他们并非所有人都在接受光能改造的那一刻迅速形成了强烈的个人主义。光能并没有把暗影，或是英勇教团一直以来编造的狗屁，从他们的身上清除。他们仍然还是邪魔族。  

这只是选择的问题。  

每个人都有选择。始终如此。无论你在做什么，无论你身在何处。不能接受选择并不等于没有选择。即使是在蠕虫的管理下，邪魔族也有选择的余地——不过嘿，谁会愿意选择最终死亡这个备选项呢。   

我想说的是旅行者也做出了选择。选择赋能邪魔族，就像它对人类做过的那样；它在可以逃跑的时候选择了留下来。 

我尊重这一点。即使是现在，我也在跨越与你们相隔的鸿沟，执行着它的意志。 

光明邪魔族现在选择了什么？我肯定不会告诉你们。但无论是什么，这都与你们过去轻率的二分法完全不同。善还是恶，他们仍然可以自行选择。  

就像我做的那样。就像旅行者做的那样。

entries.name: Cacosmia
entries.text:
[Report by VanNet encrypted router] 

[A-Mahal//Link: C-Yong] 

[Mail-Archive//0071292//excerpted] 

… Where there is smoke, there is fire, they say. The sign of a thing does not come to pass without the thing that made it. Footsteps require a being walking to be made.  

So then, why the recent move toward acceptance of Darkness as a morally neutral force? Are we expected to believe that the Collapse, that all our battles against the Hive and their Darkness, have been nothing more than an elaborate false flag operation? How is it that none of the enemies of humanity have, until now, come to us wielding Light? 

It is not… impossible.  

There, I have said it, though it leaves a bad taste in my mouth to do so. While I sincerely doubt any genuine conspiracy, I will concede that it is technically possible that nearly every enemy of humanity has simply happened to take to hand the cosmic force that opposes the Traveler, the one force which was used to end the Golden Age and decimate humanity. 

Savathûn is known for deception and trickery. Are we so certain that she was given the Light? Truly?  

And even if it is true that the Darkness is itself as safe as the Light, that our greatest enemy had only taken it as its cloak, should we truly encourage Guardians to reach for it? A force of consciousness with the Witness lingering within? From where I stand, nothing seems riskier.  

I have never thought that we needed to understand the Darkness to defeat it. Doing so has only brought more questions and uncertainty in a time when clarity of purpose is required. 

Have we all forgotten the reasons Osiris was banished? In his obsession with the Vex, he spoke freely of morality, decrying the concepts of good and evil as foolishness; he spoke of a willingness to choose Darkness above whatever fate the Vex might bring. At the time, it was thought so dangerous a viewpoint that he was sent away from the City, and his return has only brought more doubt. 

I will still fight the Darkness. That is of paramount importance. Perhaps, if there can be peace, the Creed can be revisited to prioritize the defeat of humanity's enemies. 

That time is not now.
entries.text_zh:
[报告来自VanNet加密路由器] 

[A-Mahal//链接：C-Yong] 

[邮件归档//0071292//节选] 

…俗话说，无风不起浪。没有造物之主，就没有造物之迹。需要有生物走动，才能发出脚步声。  

那么，为什么最近人们开始接受暗影是一种道德中立的力量呢？难道我们要相信大崩溃，相信我们与邪魔族及其暗影的所有战斗，都不过是一场精心策划的假旗行动？为什么在此之前人类之敌都没有操控着光能来对付我们？ 

这并非…不可能。  

好了，我说出口了，虽然这样做让我感到不自在。虽然我由衷地怀疑存在任何真正的阴谋，但我承认，严格来讲，几乎人类的每一个敌人都可能只是碰巧掌握了那种与旅行者相反的宇宙力量，那种用来终结黄金时代并毁灭人类的力量。 

萨瓦图恩以欺骗和诡计而著称。我们就这么确定她是被赐予了光能吗？真是那样吗？  

而就算暗影本身真的跟光能一样安全，我们最大的敌人也只是把它当成披风，我们真的该鼓励守护者去触及它吗？一种见证者徘徊在其中的意识力量？在我看来，没有什么比这更冒险了。  

我从没想过我们需要了解暗影才能击败它。这样做只会在这个需要明确目标的时候带来更多问题和不确定性。 

难道我们都忘了奥斯里斯被放逐的原因吗？他那时痴迷于Vex，不顾道德地畅所欲言，将善恶的概念斥为愚蠢；他说他宁愿选择暗影，也不愿接受Vex所可能带来的命运。当时的人们认为这种观点非常危险，因此他被赶出了圣城，而他的回归也只带来了更多的质疑。 

我仍将与暗影作战。这一点是至关重要的。也许，如果能够实现和平，信条就可以被重新审视，将击败人类之敌放在首位。 

现在还不是时候。

entries.name: Collective
entries.text:
From the writings of Ulan-Tan, recovered after his death: 

… It is because Light and Darkness are connected that great sacrifice was required of the Traveler: that which was once in balance was no longer, and to equal Darkness with its Light would take more than had ever been given before.  

So the Traveler created Ghosts; Ghosts created Guardians. And afterward, the Traveler became quiet. Dead, some thought, or dreaming.  

When a Human being commits an act of great cost, we know this as injury, as muscles torn and bones broken. It requires rest; frequently, it requires intervention to heal. As simple as the helping hand of another to lean on, or as complex as deep surgery: the constant theme that it cannot be done alone. Even to rest safely in quiet requires another to take over the matters of life that cannot be put off, which do not pause themselves simply for the fact of being asked kindly. 

So: the Traveler strove greatly, and then became still. How do we believe that it is anything but injured? 

The Speaker tells us the Traveler is not dead, and I believe this. It is sleeping, resting from its great deed. The sacrifice made for us, to create us.  

There is a debt thus owed. 

If we understand that Light is connected to itself—that the Light in Guardians is the same Light as that in their Ghosts, which in turn is the same Light as the Traveler's—then the answer is clear: that those possessed of the Traveler's Light, defended and upraised by it, stand in the best and in fact only possible position to pay back that debt. Who else could even hope to do so?  

I argue that our duty is to try. Even the act of defending the Traveler so it may heal is some measure of action. But if there is more that can be done, then we who it has defended owe it to the Traveler to do so. 

Remember that, in Light or in Darkness.
entries.text_zh:
摘自乌兰-坦死后被发现的作品： 

…正因为光能与暗影是相通的，所以旅行者需要做出巨大牺牲：原本的平衡不复存在，而想用它的光能均衡暗影，就需要付出比以往更高的代价。  

所以旅行者创造了机灵，机灵创造了守护者。再之后，旅行者就陷入了沉寂。有人认为它死了，或是在做梦。  

当一个人做出了付出巨大代价的行为时，我们视之为受伤，是肌肉撕裂和骨骼断裂。需要休息；通常，需要干预才能痊愈。简单如他人的援助之手，复杂如深度手术：一个不变的主题是，单靠自己不行。即使是在宁静的环境中安然休息，也需要他人来接手不能被搁置，不会因你好言相求就暂停的生活事务。 

所以说：旅行者努力了很久，然后安静下来了。我们怎么能认为那不是它受伤了呢？ 

先知告诉我们旅行者没有死，我相信这一点。它在沉睡，从它的伟大事业中抽身出来休息。那是为创造我们而做出的牺牲。  

我们也因此欠下了一笔债。 

如果在我们的理解中光能是与自身想通的——守护者的光能与他们的机灵的光能是一样的，而他们的机灵又与旅行者的光能是一样的——那么答案就不言而喻了：那些拥有旅行者的光能，受到它的保护和提升的人，就是最适合，事实上也是唯一可能偿债的人。还有谁能做到？  

我认为，我们的责任就是去尝试。哪怕是保卫旅行者来助它痊愈的行为也是一种行动措施。但如果还能做得更多，那么我们这些被旅行者保卫过的人理应那样做。 

记住这点，无论是在光能还是暗影之中。

entries.name: Bird in the Hand
entries.text:
I'm the last guy you'd accuse of being on the straight and narrow, right? Right. I mean, come on, look at me. Hunters aren't exactly the noble knights of the Guardian world.  

Look. I'm not a square. That's Zavala's job. I'll break all the rules that I shouldn't and keep the ones no one expects me to. Which is why, in part, I've never been much of one for nosing into the Darkness. Take the three of us, huh? Who would you expect to get their hands into the goop? The honorable commander, the wise wizard, or… me?  

I keep hearing how Light and Dark are connected. Not sure I'm into it. Maybe it has something to do with being reborn here, with being all made up of Light now. 

Maybe not. 

I like the Light. Simple as that. I know what to do with it. I've got hundreds of years of rolling around this old solar system with fire in my gun and Light in my heart. And let's face it, how can you live with yourself if you can't be light-hearted?  

…I'm rusty. That was awful.  

Anyways. The Traveler's like a good old friend. Dependable. Doesn't talk much. Doesn't need to. Just… there for you.  

Spent a while as part of that Light. Me and the Traveler. The Traveler and me… and Sundance. So I've got a sense for it these days. Guess you could say I'm biased in its favor, so take that into account if you're doing a detailed survey.  

But Darkness, I hardly know it. Apart from the Witness, what is it? Doesn't have a friendly hand at the helm. Seems to me more like a crowd of folks whispering while you fight for your life. The audience or the mob. Could go your way if you impress them, if the mood flows the right way. Might not lift a finger for you. Wouldn't want to depend on 'em either way.  

This isn't faith; it isn't dogma. It isn't me sitting down with an agenda and telling people just to believe in the Traveler and everything will work out just fine. But it's what works for me, rules or no rules. It's what I've lived, what I've touched, and a little helping of thinking about what my girl Sundance might say.  

I think about her now, out here, nothing but the Light in me to guide my way. I'm a ghost of what I once was—pun intended, thank you very much—but Light is Light. It still sings, just differently. I'll work it out, even if there's a great big hole where she should be. 

But enough about me.  

Look. Trust what you want, I'm not your dad. Just make sure that trust is well placed.
entries.text_zh:
你肯定不会指称我是循规蹈矩的人，对吧？对的。我的意思是，拜托，看看我。猎人并不是守护者世界里高贵的骑士。  

你看。我不是个古板守旧的人。萨瓦拉才会那样。我会打破所有我不该打破的规则，然后遵守那些人们以为我不会遵守的规则。这也是我一直不怎么喜欢探究暗影的部分原因。就拿我们三个来说吧？你觉得谁会把手伸到泥沼里去？是可敬的指挥官，聪明的巫师，还是…我？  

我老是听人说光明与黑暗是相连的。我不确定自己是否喜欢这观点。也许与我在这里重生有关，与现在我的一切都由光能构成有关。 

也许无关。 

我爱光能。就这么简单。我知道该怎么利用它。我在这个古老的太阳系里摸爬滚打了几百年，枪里有火，心里有光。我们要面对现实，心思太阴暗的人没法问心无愧，对吧？  

…我退步了。那不是个好笑话。  

总之。旅行者就像一个老朋友。可靠。话不多。无需开口。只是…默默支持你。  

有一段时间我都成了光能的一部分。我和旅行者。旅行者和我…还有太阳舞。所以如今我对它有一定的了解。我想你可以说我会偏袒它，所以如果你是在做详细调查，请考虑到这一点。  

但对于暗影，我几乎一无所知。抛除见证者，它是什么？它的掌舵手可不怎么友好。在我看来，那更像是一群在你为生存而战时窃窃私语的人。可以是观众也可以是暴徒。要是你给他们留下了深刻印象，要是气氛顺其自然的话，也许会随你所愿。但也可能一根指头都不愿意为你而动。无论如何最好都别想着依赖它们。  

这不是信仰；也不是教条。更不是我带着动机坐下来，告诉人们只要相信旅行者，一切都会好起来。但我觉得它有道理，无论有没有规则。这是我经历过的，我接触过的，而想想我的女孩太阳舞会怎么说也有帮助。  

我现在想着她，在这里，只有我心中的光能指引着我的方向。我是过去的自己的幽灵，但光能还是光能。它仍在歌唱，只是方式不同。我会想到解决办法的，即使她本该在的地方只剩下一个大洞。 

不过我的事已经说得够多了。  

听着。你想相信什么就相信什么，我又不是你爸。只要确保别轻信错付就行。

entries.name: Chapter 1
entries.text:
Faint guitar music drifted through the streets of the Last City, barely audible over the buzz of citizens in the market. Glint's iris flicked between passing patrons and the pleasing festival decorations. His self-assigned patrol was barely a distraction from his racing thoughts, but it made him feel helpful to Crow and the Vanguard—even if they didn't know and were too preoccupied to care.

A nearby stand decorated with stained glass wind chimes caught his attention. He gave them a closer look, wondering how to get one back to Crow.

"Come on! Quick!" a voice shouted. Glint turned to see four teens rush by the stall, narrowly avoiding a cart full of vegetables. To Glint's surprise, one teen carried a large pumpkin.

"These kids and their Headless Ones nonsense, I swear," the stall owner said.

"It's that time of year. Silly pranks abound," responded a patron with a chuckle.

Glint quickly floated after them.
entries.text_zh:
微弱的吉他乐声轻轻拂过圣城的街道，几乎被市场上市民们熙熙攘攘的喧嚣声所掩盖。格林特的视线在往来的顾客与节日的喜庆装饰间游移。他自发的巡逻虽然未能完全驱散心中的纷扰思绪，但至少让他觉得自己能为乌鸦和先锋尽一份力——即使他们未曾察觉，因忙于其他事务而无暇顾及这份心意。

不远处，一个装饰着彩色玻璃风铃的摊位吸引了他的目光。他走近细看，琢磨着怎么才能给乌鸦弄一个回来。

“快！快点！”一个声音喊道。格林特转身望去，只见四个孩子匆匆跑过摊位，险些撞翻满载蔬菜的小车。令格林特惊讶的是，其中一个孩子怀里还抱着一个大南瓜。

“这些孩子和他们那些无头者的无稽之谈，真是让人头疼，”摊主抱怨道。

“又是一年中的这个时候了，尽是些无聊的恶作剧，”一位顾客笑着回应道。

格林特迅速跟了上去。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 1
entries.text:
[NEW RECORDING] Ghost Den–Session 1

LOCATION: Tower–Bazaar—Previously New Monarch Meeting Area

FACILITATORS: Eva Levante, Micah-10, and Mihaylova (Recordkeeper)

PARTICIPANTS: Ghost, Glint, Ophiuchus, Kugu, Lexicon, Bee, and Batt

—START OF RECORDING—

Eva: Welcome, little Lights. Thank you for joining us.

Micah: In the spirit of the season, and with recent events in mind, we wanted to hold this gathering to give you space to talk and share.

Eva: The Festival of the Lost is an opportunity to celebrate life and honor death. We often forget to do both and can feel much turmoil as a result.

Micah: Mihaylova is recording, but only so you can look back on your progress if you like. So please don't feel intimidated by her.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The participants glance at each other. Ghost shrinks under everyone's curiosity and floats closer to the open air of the balcony.]

Eva: Now, who would like to begin?
entries.text_zh:
[新记录] 机灵集会地–第1次会议

地点：高塔–集市–前新王派集会区

主持人：伊娃·莱万特、米迦-10以及米哈伊洛娃（记录员）

与会者：机灵、格林特、蛇夫座、库谷、莱克森、比和巴特

-记录开始-

伊娃：欢迎，小家伙。谢谢你们的参与。

米迦：为了节日精神，同时考虑到最近发生的事件，我们决定举行这次集会，让你们有机会来倾诉和分享。

伊娃：英灵日是一个庆祝生命并纪念死亡的时刻。我们时常忘记去做这两件事，因而内心感到纷扰。

米迦：米哈伊洛娃正在记录，但这只是为了方便你们日后回顾自己取得的进展。所以请不要被她吓到。

[圈注：与会者们相互对视，机灵在众人好奇的目光下蜷缩起来，飘得更靠近了阳台的开阔空间一些。]

伊娃：那么，由谁开始呢？

entries.name: Chapter 2
entries.text:
Glint saw the teens running into an abandoned building and floated in behind them. The rays from the setting sun trickled through the windows, allowing Glint to find his way without providing his own light. Keeping to the shadows, he bobbed his way through piles of debris, passing half-finished murals on the walls until he found the room the pranksters had decided to make their hideout.

As he entered, he noticed a collection of curiosities that he couldn't quite place, but it was an unfamiliar book in one of the teens' hands that claimed his attention first. It looked thrown together; pages of varying quality and color poked out haphazardly, like an art project gone wrong.

"No, no, the pumpkin has to be in the center, Cash," the young Awoken girl said, exasperated.

Glint spotted "Cash." The Human boy made a patronizing face but moved the pumpkin anyway. With its carved-out eyes and sharp teeth, the item in question fit with what Glint knew of Headless Ones. Nothing about it glowed, which was a good sign, so he dipped slyly behind a box to avoid detection and continued to examine the room while the teens argued over this "ritual."
entries.text_zh:
格林特看到孩子们跑进一栋废弃的建筑，便跟在他们后面飘了进去。夕阳的余晖透过窗户洒落，为格林特指引方向，让他无需点亮自己的光能。他尽量避开亮光，在废墟堆中跃动前行，经过墙上未完成的壁画，最终找到了那群捣蛋鬼选作藏身处的房间。

他进入其中，注意到了一些让他感到困惑的奇怪东西，但首先吸引他目光的是某个孩子手中紧握的一本陌生书册。它看起来像是随意拼凑而成的；书页材质与颜色各异，杂乱无章地突出在外，就像是一件失败的艺术作品。

“不，不，南瓜一定要在中间，凯什，”年轻的觉醒者女孩恼怒地说道。

格林特注意到了“凯什”的身影。这个人类男孩虽面露不屑，但还是把南瓜挪到了中间。那件物品上面雕刻着深邃的眼洞和锋利的獠牙，与格林特心中无头者的形象不谋而合。南瓜并未散发出丝毫光芒，这是个好兆头，于是他偷偷地躲到箱子后面，避免被发现，在那些孩子争论这场“仪式”的细节时，继续观察着房间。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 2
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: A Ghost with a light blue shell, Kugu, beeps and floats toward the center of the circle made by the other Ghosts.]

Micah: Ah, Kugu! Go right ahead.

Kugu: The Witness is a spineless, weak jerk that made everyone's lives horrible. Who asked for its opinion on how the universe should be run? No one! I've never seen such an entitled being in my life. I wish I could have gone shell to smoke head with it. I would have ripped it in—

[CIRCLE NOTE: Other Ghosts looking between one another, a few giggling. Another Ghost with an all-black shell, Lexicon, quickly flies up and pushes gently against Kugu.]

Lexicon: Yes, the Witness is awful, but maybe we should try to move forward? It's dead. Holding onto anger will only poison us and our future.

Micah: That's an excellent perspective, Lexicon. Thank you.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Kugu grumbles in agreement and returns to their original spot, with Lexicon close behind.]
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：一个浅蓝色机壳的机灵，库谷，发出蜂鸣声，飘向其他机灵围成的圆圈中心。]

米迦：啊，库谷！请说吧。

库谷：见证者是个懦弱无能的混蛋，它让每个人的生活都变得一团糟。谁问过它对宇宙应该如何运行的意见？没人问过！我这辈子从没见过那么自以为是的家伙。真希望能和它来场单挑。我一定会把它撕成——

[圈注：其他机灵面面相觑，有几个在咯咯笑。另一个全黑机壳的机灵，莱克森，迅速飞了过来，轻轻地推着库谷。]

莱克森：没错，见证者的确是糟透了，但也许我们应该试着向前看？它已经死了。继续沉溺于愤怒只会对我们自己和我们的未来造成伤害。

米迦：这是个很好的观点，莱克森。谢谢你。

[圈注：库谷咕哝着表示同意，然后回到原来的位置，莱克森紧随其后。]

entries.name: Chapter 3
entries.text:
There were some unusual objects in the room. Glint scanned them when he was sure no one was looking: colorful fabrics draped over various things, a hundred or so melting candles, counterfeit Gambit coins, swords that were supposed to be Hive in origin, candy dumped in a variety of buckets, boxes, and vases. Everything was a forgery, some sort of fake.

Two young Eliksni had been standing off to one side. At the Awoken girl's behest, they approached her in the center of the makeshift ritual circle. That was when Glint's eye caught something interesting. An altar, covered in more candles and smaller baubles that reflected against something familiar, an item he hadn't expected to find here: a golden reliquary container.
entries.text_zh:
房间里摆放着一些不寻常的东西。格林特趁没人注意时扫描了它们：披在各种东西上的五颜六色的布料，一百来根快要融化的蜡烛，伪造的智谋硬币，标称来自邪魔族的刀剑，装在各种桶、盒子和花瓶里的糖果。所有东西都是赝品，都是某种假货。

两名年轻的埃里克斯尼族一直居于一侧。在觉醒者女孩的示意下，他们走到了临时仪式环的中央。就在这时，格林特注意到了一件有趣的东西。有个祭坛上摆放着更多的蜡烛和一些小饰品，映衬着某个熟悉的东西，一件他没想到会在这里看到的物品：一个金色的圣物匣。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 3
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Eva: Would anyone else like to go?

[CIRCLE NOTE: The Ghosts idle in place, irises nervously looking around.]

Micah: Anyone…? Ophiuchus?

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ophiuchus does not say anything. He stares back at Micah and slowly blinks. Lexicon floats toward a pillow and hides behind it. Another Ghost makes a noise akin to someone clearing their throat. Eva continues to smile from her place next to Micah on the couch.]

Micah: All right, moving on.
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

伊娃：还有谁想发言吗？

[圈注：机灵们停留在原地，眼神紧张地环顾四周。]

米迦：有人愿意吗…？蛇夫座？

[圈注：蛇夫座没有说话。他回头盯着米迦，缓慢地眨了下眼睛。莱克森飘向一个枕头，躲在后面。另一个机灵发出类似清嗓子的声音。伊娃坐在沙发上，挨着米迦继续微笑着。]

米迦：好吧，继续。

entries.name: Chapter 4
entries.text:
A debate had started between the teens. While they were distracted, Glint could easily float unnoticed from one hiding spot to the next. They were arguing whether to use melted candy on their hands to bond them even further before the ritual, which resulted in huffs and objections. Cash sighed at the response to his suggestion.

Glint floated past some deactivated—or more likely broken—Cabal shields and some weird blue substance in a mason jar before stopping at a box a few feet from the altar. He wasn't close enough to scan it, but it certainly looked like a real reliquary. It sat beside a book holder that took up the center of the table. There were other items around it: a gold medallion with a symbol he didn't recognize, an orb that shimmered like starlight, an assortment of scarves, and rocks that gleamed in the candlelight. But nothing looked as potentially concerning as the reliquary. Anything could be in there…

He glanced over at the group for a moment. Having checked that their attention was elsewhere, he floated over to the altar for a closer inspection.
entries.text_zh:
孩子们之间开始了一场争论。趁着他们分心的时候，格林特轻易地从一个藏身处飘到另一处而未被察觉。他们争论是否要在仪式前用融化的糖果把他们的手粘合起来，结果引起了一阵抱怨和反对。凯什听着大家对自己提议的反响叹了口气。

格林特飘过一些关闭的——或者更可能是坏掉的——卡巴尔护盾和一些装在玻璃罐里的奇怪蓝色物质，在离祭坛几英尺远的一个盒子前停了下来。他离得不够近，没法进行扫描，但它看起来确实是个真正的圣物匣。它放在桌子中央的一个书架旁。周围还有其他物品：一枚带有他不认识的符号的黄金勋章，一个像星光一样闪烁的球体，各式各样的围巾，还有在烛光下闪闪发光的石头。但没有任何东西看起来能像圣物匣那样引人注目。里面可能藏有任何东西…

他瞥了那群孩子一眼，确认他们的注意力都在别处后，飘到祭坛前仔细检视。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 4
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: A Ghost with an orange shell, Bee, floats forward. Another, Batt, dons a red shell. She hovers close to her.]

Bee: I can go. Ahem.

Batt: It's okay, you got this.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Batt gives Bee a comforting nudge. She takes a shaky breath.]
