Bee: We almost died during the War. I—I know that "almost" isn't as bad as "did", but… I haven't felt the same since then.

Micah: What you experienced is just as important. No need to minimize it.

Bee: It was… terrifying. The way its limbs reached out to crush anyone in its path…

Batt: We got grabbed. It looked like that was it, but then it disappeared.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The two turn to Ghost, who can't meet their gaze. He floats a bit lower.]

Bee: We're alive because of you. Thank you.
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：一个橙色机壳的机灵，比，向前飘了出来。另一个叫巴特的红色机壳机灵紧挨着她盘旋。]

比：我来吧。呃哼。

巴特：没事，你能行的。

[圈注：巴特安慰地推了推比。她颤抖地喘了口气。]

比：战争期间我们都差点死掉。我、我知道“差点死掉”没有“死掉”那么糟糕，但是…从那以后，我的感觉就不一样了。

米迦：你所经历的一切同样重要。没必要轻视它。

比：真的…太可怕了。它伸展肢体，要把挡道的人统统捏碎…

巴特：我们被抓住了。似乎一切都完了，但它随即消失了。

[圈注：两人转头看向机灵，而他无法直视他们的目光。他飘得更低了一些。]

比：我们能活下来都是因为你。谢谢你。

entries.name: Chapter 5
entries.text:
The teens stood in a circle. At the center was a pumpkin, positioned in the middle of an intricate symbol, painted with unsure brushstrokes, smudged to fix mistakes.

"Stop fidgeting, Nirysk," the young Eliksni girl muttered, tightening her grip on the other Eliksni's hands. "You don't see Cash or Rhea fidgeting."

"I'm not fidgeting," said Nirysk as he grabbed Cash's hand.

"If you're scared, I'm sure we can do this alone—"

"Melii, I'm fine," Nirysk retorted, his tone short.

"Everyone ready?" Rhea asked. The teens nodded. In one hand, she held up the book she'd been leafing through when Glint initially arrived. The words they strung together seemed a bit nonsensical, despite recognizing a few. Glint approached the altar with the intention of scanning the reliquary… but he couldn't.

Confused, Glint tried again. Nothing happened. His sensors were jammed. He couldn't even send an SOS to the Vanguard.

A violet glow danced in his peripherals, demanding his attention. He spun around and, to his surprise, saw it was from the pumpkin head—eyes and mouth alight.
entries.text_zh:
孩子们站成一圈。中心是一个南瓜，它被放置在一个复杂的符号中央，那符号是用不确定的笔触绘制的，为了修正错误而涂抹得有些模糊。

“别动来动去的，尼瑞斯克，”年轻的埃里克斯尼族女孩低声抱怨道，紧紧握住另一名埃里克斯尼族的手。“你看凯什和瑞亚在乱动吗？”

“我没有动来动去，”尼瑞斯克边说边抓住凯什的手。

“如果你害怕的话，我相信我们可以单独做这件事——”

“梅莉伊，我没事，”尼瑞斯克反驳道，语气简短。

“大家都准备好了吗？”瑞亚问道。孩子们点了点头。她用一只手拿着格林特刚来时她就一直在翻阅的那本书。尽管他认得其中一些字，但它们连在一起似乎有点莫名其妙。格林特靠近祭坛，打算扫描一下圣物匣…但他做不到。

困惑之余，格林特又试了一次。什么也没发生。他的传感器被干扰了。他甚至无法向先锋发出求救信号。

一丝紫色的炫光在眼角边缘闪烁着，引起了他的注意。他转过身去，惊讶地发现这光芒来自于南瓜头——它的眼洞和嘴巴都亮了起来。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 5
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: The focus has now shifted to Ghost. The rest of the participants, quiet and waiting, turn their attention toward him.]

Ghost: I don't know what to say… I-I'm glad I could help. I just…

[CIRCLE NOTE: He looks around and retracts.]

Ghost: I can't. Not yet.

Glint: Hey, it's okay.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Glint floats over to Ghost and huddles beside him, shells touching for comfort.]

Glint: I can go next.
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：焦点现在移到了机灵身上。其他与会者安静地等待着，把注意力转向了他。]

机灵：我不知道该说什么…我、我很高兴能帮上忙。我只是…

[圈注：他环顾四周，然后缩了回去。]

机灵：我做不到。还不行。

格林特：嘿，没事的。

[圈注：格林特飘到机灵身边，蜷缩在其一旁，机壳触碰，以示安慰。]

格林特：我来发言吧。

entries.name: Chapter 6
entries.text:
Panic surged through Glint.

No. No, no, no. According to all the research he and Eido had done on the Headless Ones over the years, this shouldn't have been possible. It shouldn't have been allowed to happen. Nothing in this room was real, or at least shouldn't have been able to power a ritual—the book! It had to have been the book.

The teens were lost in the trance of their spell, a palpable energy lifting them slowly from the ground.

This was only supposed to be a prank! Glint tried once more to reach out to the Vanguard, to Crow, but his radio was eating static. He did the next best thing.

"Hey!" he shouted. It worked instantly. The startled teens yelled in surprise and, with their concentration broken, tumbled to the ground with loud thuds.
entries.text_zh:
恐慌涌上了格林特的心头。

不。不，不，不。根据他和艾多这几年来对无头者的研究，这本是不可能的。这种事不该发生。这房间里没有任何东西是真的，至少没可能为仪式提供能量——那本书！一定是那本书。

孩子们陷入了咒语的恍惚之中，一种明显的能量正缓缓地将他们从地面上托起。

这本该只是个恶作剧！格林特再次试图联系先锋，联系乌鸦，但他的无线电一直在受到静电干扰。他选择退而求其次。

“嘿！”他喊道。这一招立刻奏效。吓了一跳的孩子们惊讶地大叫起来，由于注意力被分散，统统砰地一声摔倒在地。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 6
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Glint: The war with the Witness was never going to end without losses. I don't think any of us wanted that, but we all knew that if it meant saving lives, we'd pay whatever price was asked.

Glint: But I've never felt a Ghost's death before.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The circle falters for a moment. Many of the Ghosts shift uneasily. They don't look at Glint.]

Glint: I didn't know Targe for very long. The nature of our mission in the Pale Heart brought everyone's Ghosts together. I've talked with Ghost a lot in the past and consider us friends, but it was nice to be around Targe and Ophiuchus. To see things from a new perspective.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Glint sighs. Ghost looks to him. Ophiuchus does not react.]

Glint: I wish I could have gotten to know him better.

Ophiuchus: He didn't have to die.

[CIRCLE NOTE: All eyes snap to Ophiuchus, shells twisting with curiosity.]
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

格林特：与见证者开战必将伴随着丧失。我想我们谁也不希望这样，但我们都知道，如果这意味着拯救生命，我们愿意付出任何代价。

格林特：但从未有过哪个机灵的死这般触动我。

[圈注：围圈的机灵动摇了片刻。许多机灵不安地挪动着。他们移开了视线不去看格林特。]

格林特：我和塔吉相处的时间并不长。我们在苍白之心内任务的性质让所有人的机灵都聚到了一起。我以前经常和机灵交谈，认为我们是朋友，但和塔格、蛇夫座在一起感觉也很好。能从新的角度看待事物。

[圈注：格林特叹了口气。机灵看向他。蛇夫座没有反应。]

格林特：我希望我能多了解他一些。

蛇夫座：他本来没必要死的。

[圈注：所有人的目光都投向了蛇夫座，好奇地扭动着机壳。]

entries.name: Chapter 7
entries.text:
"The hell is a Ghost doing here?!" Cash asked. Everyone had risen, hissing painfully, to their feet. They looked around as they brushed themselves off and checked for injuries.

"Wait," Melii said. Glint floated closer to them, and the Eliksni's eyes widened. "That's not just any Ghost, egghead! That's the Hunter Vanguard's Ghost!"

"Glint?" Nirysk asked. Melii nodded. Beside them, the flickering candlelight danced on Rhea's pale violet arms as she folded them protectively over the book.

"That doesn't answer the question," she said defensively.

"I could ask you the same," Glint said. He looked at each of them in turn, but found his gaze drawn invariably back to the book. Even from a distance it didn't look special. "What in the world were you trying to do, exactly? Summon a Headless One?"

"What? No! That'd be ridiculous," Rhea said. "Everyone knows there's no way to do that."

"Yeah, exactly," Cash said. "We were trying to speak to the dead."

Glint blinked.
entries.text_zh:
“真该死，这里怎么会有机灵？”凯什问道。所有人都站了起来，痛苦地嘟囔着。他们环顾四周，拍拍自己身上的尘土，检查有没有受伤。

“等等，”梅莉伊说道。格林特飘到他们身边时，这名埃里克斯尼族睁大了眼睛。“那不是普通的机灵，笨蛋！那是猎人先锋的机灵！”

“格林特？”尼瑞斯克问道。梅莉伊点了点头。在他们身边，闪烁的烛光在瑞亚浅紫色的手臂上跃动着，她抱紧了那本书。

“这并没有回答那个问题，”她回嘴道。

“我也可以问你们同样的问题，”格林特说道。他依次看了看他们每个人，却发现自己的目光总是被那本书吸引。即使走近了点看，这本书看上去也很普通。“你们到底想做什么？召唤无头者？”

“什么？当然不是！那太荒谬了，”瑞亚说道。“大家都知道那是不可能做到的。”

“对，没错，”凯什说道。“我们是想要跟死者对话。”

格林特愣了。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 7
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Ophiuchus: Targe was a pain, just like Zavala, sometimes… but he was a good Ghost.

[CIRCLE NOTE: A soft gust of wind passes through the circle. It sounds closer to a roar in the silence.]

Ophiuchus: You get used to someone's presence when you've been around them for so long. Even if you don't speak often.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ophiuchus sighs.]

Ophiuchus: I knew he was going to do it. Something reckless… But I thought he would make it out. He and Zavala have been in many a bind, so I foolishly thought this would be no different.

Ophiuchus: I do think I miss him.

[CIRCLE NOTE: There is a long pause. The other Ghosts share glances.]

Ophiuchus: Ghost…

Ophiuchus: What was it like when you died?
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

蛇夫座：塔格有时很讨厌，就像萨瓦拉一样…但他是个好机灵。

[圈注：一阵微风吹过机灵围成的圈子，它在寂静中听起来近似于咆哮。]

蛇夫座：跟某人相处这么久的时间后，你会习惯其存在。即使你们彼此不常说话。

[圈注：蛇夫座叹了口气。]

蛇夫座：我就知道他会去做鲁莽的事…但我以为他能成功脱险。他和萨瓦拉经历过许多困境，所以我愚蠢地认为这次也不会有什么不同。

蛇夫座：我想我确实想念他。

[圈注：一阵长久的停顿。其他机灵互相交换着眼神。]

蛇夫座：机灵…

蛇夫座：你死的时候是什么感觉？

entries.name: Chapter 8
entries.text:
"You were trying to… what?" Glint asked, taken aback.

"Well…" Melii started, then paused. She looked hesitantly at her peers. "We were talking about how many people fell during the war, and, uh, we just wanted to try to speak to them."

Glint noted the cautiousness in her voice. He floated higher to be level with their faces and saw how they all looked away from him, as if ashamed. Or… was it something more?

"We don't care about stupid pranks," Rhea explained quietly. "We had heard that this time of year was the best to try something like this…"

"The Hall Between," Glint muttered. They nodded.

Realization dawned on Glint.

They'd lost people to the Witness, and they were looking for solace. For answers. They wanted to feel close to their loved ones again after having had them taken away so suddenly and without warning. Glint could understand that.
entries.text_zh:
“你们想要…什么？”格林特震惊地问道。

“嗯…”梅莉伊开了个头，然后停顿了一下。她迟疑地看着同伴们。“我们聊到了有多少人在战争中倒下，呃，我们只是想试着和他们交谈。”

格林特注意到了她声音中的谨慎。他飘得更高，与他们的脸平齐，看到他们都把目光从他身上移开，好像感到了羞愧。或者…是有别的原因？

“我们对愚蠢的恶作剧不感兴趣，”瑞亚低声解释道。“我们听说每年的这个时候最适合尝试这样的事情…”

“腕神节，”格林特咕哝道。他们点了点头。

格林特恍然大悟。

他们因见证者而失去了亲人，正在寻找慰藉，寻找答案。他们想在亲人被如此毫无征兆、猝不及防地夺走后，再次感受到亲人的温暖。格林特能理解这一点。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 8
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Glint: You don't have to answer that…

Ghost: No, it's fine. I'm fine.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ghost's shell flexes and shakes a little. Micah and Eva watch him carefully.]

Ghost: Final Deaths are always a possibility. We all know that.

Ghost: There's a complacency we feel, a comfortability, when it comes to our immortality… But, being in the Pale Heart, fighting alongside the Guardian, feeling the damage to me increasing with each moment…

Ghost: I don't know why I came back.

Ghost: I… I don't know why it was me and not Targe. He was just as important as any of us.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Ghost's shell droops. The rest of the group look away. Some float closer to one another.]

Ghost: He should have come back…
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

格林特：你不必回答这个问题…

机灵：不，没事。我没事。

[圈注：机灵的机壳绷紧起来，微微颤抖。米迦和伊娃谨慎地观察着他。]

机灵：最终的死亡总是有可能发生的。我们都知道这一点。

机灵：每次谈到自己的不朽，我们都会感到一种自满，一种安逸…可是，在苍白之心里，与守护者并肩作战，感受到我身上的伤害每时每刻都在恶化…

机灵：我不知道我为什么能回来。

机灵：我…我不知道为什么是我而不是塔格。他和我们其他人一样重要。

[圈注：机灵的机壳耷拉下来。其余的人把目光移开。有些机灵相互靠得更近了。]

机灵：回来的应该是他…

entries.name: Chapter 9
entries.text:
"I put this book together with all the things we found during our research," Rhea said. She gently placed the book on its stand at the altar. "My mentor…" Her voice faltered. "She always said to keep your notes in one place, so they're easier to find… She never liked things to be messy."

"My sister was also like that," Cash said, eyes downcast.

Nirysk and Melii looked at each other. One of Melii's arms wrapped around Nirysk.

"Our brother went into the Great Machine as well…" Melii started.

"It should have been me," Nirysk whispered.

Glint felt their sorrow deeply. They were all so young.

"I was going to join him. I was supposed to be there," Nirysk said. "But I was a coward. I turned back. He… he didn't look at me with shame, only understanding, and that somehow makes it worse. I should have given my life to protect the Great Machine, too."

Nirysk kicked the pumpkin head just hard enough for it to tumble out of the circle they'd painted on the floor, its face dark and mocking.
entries.text_zh:
“我把我们在研究过程中发现的所有东西整理成了这本书，”瑞亚说道。她轻轻地把书放在祭坛的支架上。“我的导师…”她的声音有些颤抖。“她总是说要把笔记都放在同一个地方，这样才更容易找到…她从来不喜欢把东西弄得乱七八糟。”

“我姐姐也是那样，”凯什说道，目光低垂。

尼瑞斯克和梅莉伊互相看了一眼。梅莉伊用一只手臂环抱着尼瑞斯克。

“我们的哥哥也进入了大机器…”梅莉伊开口说道。

“本来应该是我的，”尼瑞斯克低声说。

格林特深深地感受到了他们的悲伤。他们都还那么年轻。

“我本来要和他一起去的。我本该在那里的，”尼瑞斯克说道。“但我是个懦夫。我退缩了。他…他没有用羞愧的眼神看我，而是充满了理解，这让我更难过了。我也应该献出自己的生命来保护大机器。”

尼瑞斯克踢了南瓜头一脚，力道刚好让它从他们在地板上画的圆圈里滚出来。它的脸上是一副阴沉而嘲弄的神情。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 9
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

Micah: I'm proud of you for expressing how you're feeling about this, Ghost. I know it can't be easy.

Micah: Targe's death was a tragedy. And so was yours.

Micah: No one could possibly have known you'd get a second chance.

Micah: And it's okay that you don't feel okay. Any one of us would likely feel the same.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The participants nod in agreement, empathizing.]

Micah: You're not alone, Ghost. You are here and we're here for you… We'll get through it together. It'll just take a little bit of time.

[CIRCLE NOTE: Glint nudges Ghost for reassurance.]
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

米迦：你能表达出自己的感受，我为你感到骄傲，机灵。我知道这不容易。

米迦：塔格的死是个悲剧。你的死也是。

米迦：没人能知道你还会有第二次机会。

米迦：你感觉不好也没关系。换做是我们任何人都会有同样的感受。

[圈注：与会者点头表示同意，感同身受。]

米迦：你并不孤单，机灵。你在这里，而我们支持你…我们会共同度过这个难关。只是需要一点时间。

[圈注：格林特推了推机灵，以示安慰。]

entries.name: Chapter 10
entries.text:
"You shouldn't think like that," Glint said, his tone soft and full of empathy. "I know that's easier said than done but trust me when I say, I understand. Someone I knew died, and I thought… 'Why not me?' It's so easy, isn't it? To blame ourselves and think we could have done something differently? 'If only I'd been there, maybe they'd still be here…'"

Emotion welled up within the Ghost, and he struggled to contain it.

"How do you get past that?" Nirysk asked. "It just feels like… Ether draining out of me constantly and I don't know how to stop it."

"Time," Glint said simply. "You give it time… and you lean on each other. You get through it together."

The teens were quiet. Glint knew it wasn't the answer they wanted. They were here in search of closure. Their hopes pinned on forged relics and fabricated rituals. All they wanted was closure.
entries.text_zh:
“你们不应该这么想，”格林特说，他的语气柔和，充满同情。“我知道这说起来容易做起来难，但相信我，我能理解你们。我认识的一个人去世了，我当时就想…‘为什么死的不是我？'这很容易，对不对？我们会责怪自己，认为自己本可以做得更好，‘要是我当时在场，也许他们就不会死…'”

机灵的内心涌动着情绪，他努力克制着。

“你是怎么熬过来的？”尼瑞斯克问道。“那感觉就像…乙太在不断地从我体内流走，我不知道该怎么阻止它。”

“时间，”格林特言简意赅。“给它一些时间…你们可以互相依靠。一起度过难关。”

孩子们都沉默了。格林特知道这不是他们想要的答案。他们是来寻找解脱的。他们把希望寄托在伪造的圣物和虚构的仪式上。他们想要的只是解脱。

entries.name: Ghost Den – 10
entries.text:
—CONTINUATION OF SESSION 1 RECORDING—

[CIRCLE NOTE: The other Ghosts have dispersed. Eva and Micah linger behind to watch Glint, Ghost, and Ophiuchus, who float by the edge of the Tower, looking out at the Last City.]

Glint: Are you okay, Ghost?

Ghost: No, but… I think I will be.

Glint: Good.

Ophiuchus: Maybe it's inherent for all Ghosts to want to sacrifice themselves eventually. As morbid as that sounds.

Ghost: …I'd do it again.

Glint: I know… Should we just have a moment of quiet? For Targe?

Ophiuchus: Yes.

[CIRCLE NOTE: The silence permeates the air as they float by the edge. They naturally migrate closer together.]

[END OF SESSION 1 RECORDING]
entries.text_zh:
—第1次会议记录续—

[圈注：其他机灵已经散去。伊娃和米迦留了下来，看着飘浮在高塔边缘、眺望圣城的格林特、机灵和蛇夫座。]

格林特：你还好吗，机灵？

机灵：不好，但…我想我会好起来的。

格林特：那就好。

蛇夫座：也许所有机灵最终都想要牺牲自己。也许这是天生的。虽然这听起来很病态。

机灵：…我不后悔。

格林特：我知道…要不我们默哀片刻？为了塔格？

蛇夫座：嗯。

[圈注：他们飘浮在高塔边缘，空气中弥漫着寂静。他们自然而然地靠得更近了。]

[第1次会议记录结束]

entries.name: Chapter 11
entries.text:
"We're sorry," the teens mumbled together, their voices sad.

"Are we in trouble with the Vanguard?" Rhea asked.

Glint shook his shell from side to side.

"No, you're not, but I'm going to clear this place out and make sure nothing is amiss. Get on home, ok?" They nodded and turned away. He added, loud enough for them to hear, "And no more rituals. You don't know what could happen if you accidentally mix real spells together."

"Thank you, Glint," Nirysk said, and lingered for just a moment before he joined his sister.

Glint sighed.

Any other year, he'd have been excited at the idea of a potential ritual to summon a Headless One, but this year… This year, he simply wanted some time for quiet contemplation. Figuring out what had caused such a strange phenomenon could wait. It was a problem for him and Eido to revisit at a future date.

For his own peace of mind, Glint scanned the reliquary and was relieved to find that it was just packed full of candy.
entries.text_zh:
“我们很抱歉，”孩子们低声嘟囔着，声音里充满了悲伤。

“先锋会来找我们麻烦吗？”瑞亚问道。

格林特左右摇晃着他的机壳。

“不，不会。但我要把这地方清干净，确保不会出差错。快回家吧，好吗？”他们点点头，转身离开了。他又补充了一句，声音大到足以让他们听见，“还有，别再举行仪式了。如果不小心把真正的咒语混在一起，天知道会发生什么事。”

“谢谢你，格林特，”尼瑞斯克说道，停留了片刻后才随他的姐妹而去。

格林特叹了口气。

如果是在其他任何一年，他都会因为一场也许能召唤无头者的仪式而兴奋不已，但今年…今年，他只想静静地沉思一会儿。至于是什么造成了这种奇怪的现象，可以等等再想。这是他和艾多将来要重新研究的问题。

为了让自己安心，格林特扫描了圣物匣，如释重负地发现里面只是装满了糖果。

entries.name: Epilogue
entries.text:
"Everything has been moved to a vault designated by Ikora, for future inspection," Glint reported. "She thinks one of those Hive swords might have been real, so she's sending someone to investigate the market where the kids got everything."

"Why didn't you call me?" Crow asked, arms crossed as he leaned against Amanda's old workshop table. Glint floated in front of him.

"You've been busy, and I didn't want to waste your time with what looked like a prank—"

"I'm never too busy for you, Glint," Crow said, sincerity in every word. Glint's shell slumped a little in response. "Were they alright, at least?"

"I think so?" Glint said. "As alright as one can be after everything… I think they just needed someone to talk to."

Crow considered Glint for a moment.

"Come here," Crow said and held up his hand for Glint to float to. He obliged and was taken by surprise when Crow pulled him to his chest for a tight hug. "I'm sorry I haven't checked in with you. I'll try to do better. I promise."

"Ok," Glint said and pressed himself into Crow's cloak. They remained like that for a while.
entries.text_zh:
“所有物品都被转移到了艾可拉指定的保险库里，以备将来检视，”格林特报告说。“她认为那些邪魔族刀剑里有一把可能是真的，所以她正派人去调查孩子们拿到这些东西的市场。”

“你为什么不联系我？”乌鸦靠在阿曼达的旧工作桌上，双臂交叉着问道。格林特飘浮在他面前。

“你一直很忙，我不想因为一件看起来像是恶作剧的小事浪费你的时间——”

“我绝不会忙得顾不上你的事，格林特，”乌鸦说道，每一个字都透着真诚。格林特的机壳应声微微下垂。“至少，他们没事吧？”

“我想是吧？”格林特说道。“就经历过这一切的人而言…我想他们只是需要找人倾诉。”

乌鸦看着格林特沉思了片刻。

“过来，”乌鸦说着，举起手让格林特飘上去。他照做了，而乌鸦把他拉到胸前紧紧抱住，这让他吃了一惊。“对不起，我最近没关注你的情况。我会努力做得更好。我保证。”

“好，”格林特说着，把自己贴进了乌鸦的披风里。他们就这样呆了一会儿。

entries.name: 1. Judgment
entries.text:
This being the recollection of Irrha of the House of Slayers, apprentice to the Baron Kiiraskes.

[This is so exciting! I will translate as best I can. –Eido, Scribe of the House of Light] 

It was a beautiful day at the end of the wet season, and the waters had risen high in the canals such that the Palace of Judgment sat on a limned mirror.

My pilot rowed us steadily between the raised walkways. The banners of the great Houses flanked us on either side of the channel. Nearest to the landing, the banners of Kings and Judgment cast long shadows down upon us. It was through them that our unity was possible, and we were not to forget it. 

I had spent five days traveling to reach Riis-Ath-Lodrii [1], and just as long before that receiving instruction in the formalities and proper courtesies to be observed in the presence of the Scribes of Judgment. But I was greeted at the landing not by a formal assemblage, but by a lone thin figure dressed in the layered finery of Judgment's officers.

He reached down to help me up out of the watercraft before I had time to bow, sparing only a moment to dust Ether accretion from my cloak. 

"Velask, Apprentice Irrha," he said, in a tone that conveyed I had already erred in some way. "Please hurry." 





I was led to a side entrance into the Halls of Judgment, where my escort expertly navigated a maze of corridors that led into a small, unremarkable reception room. We stepped into the hushed silence of stifled argument.

There were two figures waiting for us in the room. The first was dressed in the mantle of the city Peacekeepers and the ornamented headdress of the House of Stone [2]. 

Members of the House of Stone were the foundation upon which the city's defenses were built, and I thought then—as I still do—that the virtues of that House showed in none more nobly than its Kell, Chelchis. She stood twice as tall as I, her limbs as thick as the support beams above us. I could have believed any number of stories about her. 

The second figure was clad in a void-black cloak and a pytha-hide [3] crest. The absence of a House symbol marked her as a Baron of the Order of Slayers. 

The Slayer Barons had tamed Riis back when it grew wild and disordered in the first century of the Great Machine's Ether Flood. First Riis, and then the moons beyond our sky, which were often hostile to us. Within the hatchling-schools, the minders showed us shadow-stories of cunning hunters, adepts of the Great Machine, working in tandem to bring down the biggest monsters of their age.

I did not think so highly of Baron Kiiraskes when I saw her—leaner than Chelchis, but twice as scarred—until she raised her head and I saw the gleam of her eyes beneath her cap. There was a feverish cunning in her scrutiny.

"You brought me a hatchling," she complained. 

I felt a hot, familiar resentment—and desperation. It was more important than anything that she not turn me away.

"I have been two solar cycles studying," I pleaded.

"I think Chelchis here has carried clutches for longer than that," said the Baron.

Chelchis' irritated tolling [4] would have withered me in my shell, were it directed at me. All the same, I felt a sick humiliation for having been slighted in front of her.

Nearby, the Judgment official bobbed his head in disapproval.

"You have been assigned what you require," he said. "When was the last time that you needed to be summoned out here, that our Peacekeepers could not handle matters? Apprentice Irrha will suffice."

Kiiraskes gave little indication she heard the official's words. 
"What is your House?" she asked me.

This moment was inevitable.

"I do not have one." It occurred to me at last that I might have been brought here as an insult.

Kiiraskes regarded me steadily. "We can't all be Kings."

The official rubbed his hands together in agitation. "It will be quick work, Baron. Travel to the farm of Haaksis and dispatch the animal that troubles him. If you require reinforcements, send for the support of a House."

Kiiraskes grunted and turned away. I began to bow and felt her claws latch onto my arm like a star-steel cuff, pulling me from the room.

"Be careful, Slayer Baron." The small chimes on Chelchis' headdress rang softly as she turned her head. 

I did not see the gesture Kiiraskes made in response, but I heard Chelchis' amused hiss.



[1: "Veins of Riis," or the Channels Through the Body of Riis. One city of many!] 
[2: The famed House of Stone!]
[3: A vicious predator native to Riis. Variks says that these were delicious.] 
[4: To click a warning at an Eliksni that they can feel in their shell. I bet Humans can feel the vibration in their sternums!]  
[I was going to translate everything very literally, but Variks told me I was "ripping the soul from every word." Please forgive me some poetic license! –Eido, Scribe of House Light]
entries.text_zh:
这是基拉斯克丝公爵的学徒，杀手氏族的伊尔哈的回忆。

[这太激动人心了！我会尽力翻译的。——光能氏族文士艾多] 

雨季末的这天风和日丽，运河里水位高涨，审判宫殿仿佛坐落在一片精细勾勒的明镜之上。

我的领航员稳稳地划动着桨，带我们穿梭在高出的走道之间。航道两岸，各大氏族的旗帜在我们的侧面迎风招展。在最接近登陆点的地方，王族氏族与审判氏族的旗帜投下的长影盖住了我们。正是因为他们的存在，我们方能团结一心，而我们绝不能忘记这一点。 

我历经五天的长途跋涉抵达里斯-阿斯-洛德里[1]，在此之前还耗掉了同样的时日研习在审判氏族文士面前应遵循的礼节与得体的仪态。但在登陆之时，迎接我的并非庄重的集会，而是一个身着审判官员层层华服的孤瘦身影。

我还没来得及鞠躬，他就伸手扶我从船上起来，又花了片刻工夫拍去我披风上积落的乙太尘埃。 

“维拉斯克，学徒伊尔哈，”他的话语中带着一丝我已经犯了错的意味。“请快点。” 





我被带到审判大厅的侧门，护送我的那位官员熟练地穿过一系列错综复杂的走廊，最终带我来到了一间不起眼的小接待室。我们走进时，里头原本嘈杂的争论顿时变得鸦雀无声。

房内有两个身影在等候我们。第一个人身穿城市和平守护者的斗篷，头上戴着顽石氏族[2]的华丽头饰。 

顽石氏族的成员是城市防御的基石。我当时就在想——现在也还是这么认为——顽石氏族的美德在其凯尔切尔奇斯的身上体现得最为淋漓尽致。她的个子比我高出一倍，肢体则跟我们头上的顶梁柱一般粗壮。关于她的种种传说，我都愿意相信。 

第二个人身穿一袭漆黑如夜的披风，头戴一顶由皮塔兽革[3]制成的头冠。其上没有氏族标志，这表明她是一位隶属于杀手教团的公爵。 

在那个大机器乙太洪流肆虐的初始世纪，里斯曾陷入狂野无序，那时便是由杀手公爵们将它驯服的。他们的征服之旅，始于里斯，随后延伸至我们苍穹之外那些常常对我们抱有敌意的卫星。在幼雏学校里，保育员带我们看了许多暗影戏，戏里那些狡黠的猎人，亦是深谙大机器之道的专家，携手击败了属于他们时代的最恶怪物。

初见基拉斯克丝公爵时，我对其评价不高——她比切尔奇斯更瘦削，身上的伤疤却多了一倍——直到她抬起头，我看到她冠帽下闪烁的眼眸。她的眼神中蕴藏着一种狂热的狡黠。

“你给我带来了一只幼雏，”她抱怨道。 

我感受到一股炽热而熟悉的愤恨——以及绝望。无论如何都不能让她把我赶走。

“我已经苦学了两个太阳周期，”我恳求道。

“我想这位切尔奇斯怀卵的时间都比那要长，”公爵说道。

如果切尔奇斯生气的鸣响[4]是冲我来的，恐怕我早就萎缩进自己的壳里了。尽管如此，我还是因为在她面前受到轻视而感到难忍的屈辱。

附近的审判官员不以为然地晃了晃头。

“你已被指派你要求的人力，”他说道。“上一次因为我们的和平守护者处理不了，而需要召你来此是什么时候？学徒伊尔哈就足够了。”

基拉斯克丝几乎没有表现出她听到了官员说的话。 
“你属于哪个氏族？”她问我。

这一刻是不可避免的。

“我没有氏族。”我终于意识到自己可能是为了侮辱她而被带到这里来的。

基拉斯克丝坚定地看着我。“不是王族氏族咯。”

官员不安地揉着手。“这是一项简单的工作，公爵。前往哈克西斯的农场，解决掉那头困扰他的野兽。要是你需要增援，就派人请求氏族的支援。”

基拉斯克丝咕哝了一声，转过身去。我刚开始鞠躬，却突然感到她的爪子如同星钢打造的镣铐一般扣住了我的手臂，把我拉出了房间。

“小心点，杀手公爵。”切尔奇斯转过头时，她头饰上的小铃铛轻轻地响了起来。 

我没有看到基拉斯克丝作出回应的手势，但听到了切尔奇斯被逗乐的嘶鸣。



[1: 里斯脉城，或称里斯的体脉。众城之城！] 
[2: 久负盛名的顽石氏族！]
[3: 一种原产于里斯的凶猛食肉动物。据瓦里克斯说它们很美味。] 
[4: 向埃里克斯尼族发出让其能透过壳感觉到的警告。人类肯定也能感觉到胸骨的震动！]  
[我本来打算逐字逐句地直译，但瓦里克斯告诉我，那样做是“剥夺了每个词的灵魂”。请原谅我加入了一些诗意的发挥！——光能氏族文士艾多]

entries.name: 2. Fields
entries.text:
Kiiraskes stank strongly of sea-grass and sunsoak root [1]. I took care to sit toward the front of the watercraft, but the odor wrestled powerfully against the wind.

I did my best to focus on the task I had been given, which was to mix the contents of three flasks into a fourth. I prided myself on the steadiness of my hands, and the work was not so difficult that I couldn't steal glimpses of our route.

We followed the river as it skirted the sprawling residential districts, then turned and cut toward the listing sun. I watched the crowds thin as canal-side markets gave way to orderly arrays of residential towers and aerial traffic, then to radiating lines of transport arterials, waterways, and roads, connecting each of Riis's great cities to one another in a shimmering network.

We passed lines of pilgrims making their way to the site where the Great Machine first came to Riis, the hill at the heart of Riis-Ath-Lodrii. I saw high priests of the House of Dancers, devoted clerics who gorge themselves past satiation on Ether until they tower above their peers, then amputate their lower arms in ritual supplication to the Great Machine.

It was strange to see those shambling giants. But there was something awe-inspiring in it. The shuffling march of hundreds, unified in purpose.

Kiiraskes followed my gaze, then spat audibly into the water. "Fanaticism is what landed us in the wars. Fanaticism, pride, and Ether-thirst."

I looked at her. "You were in the Edge Wars?"

Kiiraskes hissed. "I have no war stories for you, hatchling." She gestured toward the flasks. "If this is serious, you should be prepared."

"And if it truly is only an animal?"

"You should still learn how to mix a tonic on the go. Don't drop that."





The farms of the House of Rain were among the most splendid on all of Riis, and the quadrant assigned to Baron Haaksis was no exception. There were great swathes of forest, carefully hemmed and controlled, arranged neatly around crop fields.

It could not have been done without the machines.
 
Baron Haaksis had a fleet of them: small, autonomous drones that moved about planting, harvesting, and measuring Ether uptake. The sound of their toil was that of wind across grassland. A thousand small tasks undertaken without rest or complaint.

For all this, the farm was strangely absent of workers. There should have been at least a few machine-tenders, monitoring the proceedings and providing maintenance and direction. Nor did any guards come to meet us as I lashed the watercraft to the dock.

We stepped out onto sun-fed walkways braced by beautiful, leafy plants. Kiiraskes pointed to the bags of supplies, and in my eagerness to prove my strength, I gathered all of them. They were very heavy, and by the time I managed to follow Kiiraskes to Haaksis' doorstep, I felt as if I were pinned to the earth.





Considering the lush abundance that surrounded it, the round building where Haaksis kept his office was sparse and joyless. The sole decoration was two twin sets of blades he kept on one wall: a memento of the Edge Wars. I had seen dozens like them throughout my upbringing, only some of them genuine.

More interesting was the drone on his desk, which Haaksis seemed to be in the process of repairing. It was a hybrid reconnaissance-defense drone called a "Shank," the kind that became popular during the war. Not many Eliksni still possessed them in peacetime. But such an interest suited a noble like Haaksis. 

Haaksis was dressed in the rich hues of Rain. He was of a height with Kiiraskes, if slighter in build, and stiff in his bearing.

I bowed low and formally, feeling the weight of my House-less status. Kiiraskes reached out and lifted me bodily upright by the carapace with no more difficulty than she might have plucked a flowering plant.

"I sent for Slayers," Haaksis said. He looked at me, and I felt my shell itch.

Kiiraskes spread her hands, untroubled. "So we've come. The House of Judgment mentioned an animal."

"No. I told them… I told them many times. This is not an animal," Haaksis said. At his sides, his claws clenched into fists, one after the other. "It is an old evil."

I looked up at Kiiraskes but found no sign of her thoughts. Her mandibles clicked quietly. "You've seen it?"

Haaksis sagged then, as if already weary of conversation. "It attacked my people. I tried to recover the bodies, but… And then the House of Judgment took its time—"

"Do you know where it is now?"

"No. Nothing can hide on this farm without the sensors tracking it. The forest tracts are just as well-tended. But there is a Garden-Way [2], between… we were letting that grow, re-wild for a few cycles…"

"We'll track it down," Kiiraskes said. "Tell me where the bodies are."
 
I felt relieved to hear her speak of us as "we." But the feeling didn't last long. Even as he brought up the displays and maps to guide Kiiraskes, Haaksis kept staring in my direction, and I realized he did not expect me to survive.



[1. Sea-grass seems straightforward enough, but I found few other references to "sunsoak root." Does it absorb Light?]
[2. A space around farmland where the local flora and fauna are left to grow naturally. These were carefully maintained, so you couldn't really call them wild.]
entries.text_zh:
基拉斯克丝身上散发出浓烈的海草和日晒树根的气味[1]。我特意坐在船头，但那气味却顽强地逆着风势阵阵袭来。

我尽力集中精神完成交给我的任务，也就是将三个烧瓶里的东西混着倒进第四个烧瓶里。我手很稳，这一点我一直引以为豪，而且这活不算太难，我还能偷瞄一下我们的路线。

河流蜿蜒穿过了大片杂乱延伸的居民区，我们顺着河前行，然后转向朝着落日驶去。我看着人群逐渐稀疏，运河畔的市集渐渐隐退，被整齐的住宅塔和空中交通取代，最后只剩四通八达的交通干线、水道和道路，它们将里斯的各大城市紧密相连，编织成一张熠熠生辉的网络。

我们经过了朝圣者的队伍，他们正前往里斯-阿斯-洛德里中心的山丘，那里是大机器初临里斯的地方。我看到了舞者氏族的高阶祭司，那些虔诚的教士们贪婪无度地吸收着乙太，直至身形超越常人，然后在仪式中斩断自己的前臂，以此向大机器献上虔诚的祈求。

目睹那些步履蹒跚的巨人，感觉既奇特又令人敬畏。数百人虽步伐踉跄，却因抱有共同使命而整齐前进。

基拉斯克丝顺着我的目光看去，然后用力向水里吐了一口唾沫。“正是狂热主义让我们陷入了战争。狂热、傲慢，还有对乙太的饥渴。”

我看着她。“你参加过边缘战争？”

基拉斯克丝发出嘶鸣。“我没有战争故事讲给你听，幼雏。”她指了指那些烧瓶，“如果这差事不简单，那你就该做好准备。”

“如果真的只是一头野兽呢？”

“那你也该学会怎么快速配制药剂。别懈怠。”





骤雨氏族农场的壮观程度在整个里斯都是首屈一指的，分配给哈克西斯公爵的地块也不例外。这里有大片精心围护看管的森林，整齐地环绕在农田周围。

如果没有机器，这是不可能完成的。
 
哈克西斯公爵拥有一支这样的无人机队：它们小巧且自主运行，在田间往来穿梭，负责种植、收割和测量乙太摄取量，辛勤劳作的声音如同风吹过草原一般，不辞辛劳、毫无怨言地执行着上千个小任务。

尽管如此，农场里却出奇地缺少工人。本应至少有几名机器操作员来监督作业，提供维护和指导的。我把船系好停靠在码头时，也没有任何守卫前来迎接。

我们走到阳光充足的步道上，旁边是枝繁叶茂的美丽植物。基拉斯克丝指向补给袋，而我急于展示自己的力量，便把它们都收集了起来。这些东西非常重，等我勉强跟着基拉斯克丝走到哈克西斯的家门口时，我感觉自己好像被钉在了地上。





与周围葱郁的丰饶景象相比，哈克西斯设立办公室的圆形建筑显得简朴而无趣。唯一的装饰是他挂在一面墙上的两套双刃：边缘战争的纪念物。我在自己的成长过程中见过几十件这样的战刃，但其中只有少数是真品。

更有趣的是他桌上的无人机，哈克西斯似乎正在修理它。这种名为“侦察机”的混合型侦察防御无人机在战争时期非常流行。和平年代还保有这种无人机的埃里克斯尼族为数不多。但这样的爱好正适合像哈克西斯这样的贵族。 

哈克西斯身着骤雨氏族标志性的华丽色彩。他的身高与基拉斯克丝相仿，但体型稍显瘦削，举止也有些僵硬。

我恭敬地深深鞠躬，体会着自己无氏族的卑微。基拉斯克丝伸出手，抬着甲壳将我扶起，像摘下一株花草般的轻而易举。

“我请他们派来杀手，”哈克西斯说道。他的目光让我感到一阵外壳发痒。

基拉斯克丝摊开她的手，神色自若。“所以我们来了。审判氏族提到了一头野兽。”

“不。我告诉过他们…我告诉过他们很多次。不是什么野兽，”哈克西斯说道。他两侧的爪子一个接一个地紧握成拳。“是古老的邪恶。”

我抬头看向基拉斯克丝，但察觉不出她的想法。她的下颚轻柔地咔嗒着。“你见过它？”

哈克西斯垂头丧气，仿佛已厌倦了交谈。“它袭击了我的人。我试图找回尸体，可是…而审判氏族迟迟不肯行动——”

“你知道它现在在哪里吗？”

“不知道。在这个农场里，没有任何东西能躲过传感器的追踪。林地也一样管理得井井有条。但有一片‘花园之路'[2]…我们让它自然生长了几个周期，重新野化…”

“我们会找到它的，”基拉斯克丝说道。“告诉我尸体在哪里。”
 
听到她用“我们”来称呼她和我，让我感到了一丝宽慰。但这种感觉没有持续多久。哈克西斯拿出显示屏和地图来为基拉斯克丝指路时，仍会不断盯向我这边，而我意识到他认定我必死无疑。



[1: 海草似乎很直白明了，但我几乎没找到其他关于“日晒树根”的记载。它能吸收光能吗？]
[2: 农田周围让当地动植物能够自然生长的一片区域。这些地方受到精心养护，所以并不算是真正的野生区域。]

entries.name: 3. Light
entries.text:
At the time, it seemed natural to pursue the creature at the hour of night when it was most likely to be on the hunt. I was distracted from all thought of fear by Kiiraskes, who decided to question me briefly on the qualities of Tenar, Brossk, and Liisok [1]: which excelled as purgatives, and which burned through chitin and stone alike.

At last, she said, "You said you studied. From records?"

"Yes, Baron." There were no Slayer-apothecarists left to train under. And even if any survived, none who would visit the common quadrants of the small city where I was raised.

Kiiraskes paused in her trudging progress up the path. We had divided the supplies between ourselves this time, and now she passed me a vial. "Drink this."

I was quick to obey, noting the odor of sunsoak root that clung to the liquid. I hoped this first taste of a Slayer's tonic would fill me with strength, or make me grow as if I had molted five times over.

It tasted foul. I became very aware of how little I had eaten since arriving.
 
"Come," Kiiraskes said. "I think I smell one of Haaksis' guards."

I could not smell anything but Kiiraskes. I followed her as she stepped nimbly across one of the sluices and onto the rich, loamy soil that marked the wildest part of Haaksis' property.

It was around this time that I started to feel the tonic's effects. I saw Light—a tiny luminescence at the edge of my sight. I turned to watch it drifting slowly toward the ground, and by the time it landed, I could see more motes gathered over the undergrowth in clouds, like dust. Far above, I read the flow of Ether like a river through the sky. I set my bags down, looked at my hands, and saw a glow beneath my shell, as if the tonic had illuminated me from the inside out.

But it was not just me. I looked at Kiiraskes and saw Light. The push-pull of air through spiracles, the misting of expelled Ether, the fervent radiance of her eyes.

She had stilled to observe me, and now she spoke.

"The Light is in all things. We cannot control it, but we can entice it. Draw it close." She chuffed. "Like a greedy pellauk."

I was cradled in the grip of awe, and the interruption was like a clout to the face. "The Great Machine is not a herd-animal sniffing after Yka fruit!" In my offense, I forgot that I was her apprentice, and at her mercy.

Kiiraskes laughed. "Don't you like Yka fruit?"

Annoyed, I looked away, to the sky. On a clear night like this, it was possible to watch the Great Machine drift across Riis's upper atmosphere. Under the tonic's influence, I saw it trailing Light—Life, I thought dizzily—like a comet.

The Great Machine had terraformed Riis's moons in four blinks, then brought the Ether-flood to Riis. A time of plenty, when no hatchlings starved and foundered in their development. A time of too-much, as the House of Judgment would tell it. A time without hierarchies, without sense. Our people had to change, to adapt.

In this new age, they called me a "Drekh." Useless, House-less.

"And now, the body," Kiiraskes said. 





It was Eliksni—or had been. The mangled form at our feet had been twisted into a tangle of limbs. If not for the torn mantle attached to it, I am not sure I would have known the body to belong to one of Haaksis' guards.

Worse was the emptiness of it. Every living thing around the body shone with the Great Machine's influence. I had not known this stranger [2], but their death left a void in the world which the tonic now permitted me to see. I was glad then for my empty stomach.
 
Kiiraskes crouched down near the body and at once began touching it, shifting an arm here and there, inspecting it. I stood by, uncertain of whether I disapproved, too afraid to complain in any case. The plant life here was not yet so dense, and we were exposed, though—as Kiiraskes had pointed out—any creatures would be as well.

"Was it an animal?" I asked. There were predators out here, after all. Though nothing that would voluntarily attack Kiiraskes unless it was desperate.

She gestured for me to crouch beside her. "Look," she said. And then, once I had settled beside her: "What don't you see?" 

"Light," I said, suffused again with sudden grief.

She swatted me. "Look down."
 
I did. I saw a cluster of lights—small larvae that had gathered in the footprints I'd left around the body. I brushed one absently from my leg, then realized…

"They're avoiding the body," I said.

Kiiraskes grunted, pleased. "Touch here. Tell me what you feel."

I touched the guard's carapace and felt something wet under my claws. I had long enough to recognize that the beast had cracked his shell down the middle, and to fear that I could never stomach a meal again. And then, suddenly, it was as if I had dipped my hand into a cold pond. 

I felt anger. A sharp, foreign fury that had nothing to do with my own revulsion and fear. Beneath it, there was something like… remorse [3]. Could an animal feel remorse?

"You feel it? We cannot see this evil [4], but it's there," Kiiraskes said. "Come. Judgment was wrong. I'm taking you back to the boat—if we're quick, it won't have time to follow us."
 
But the monster did not stalk us across the forest.

It poured out of the air in a cloud of billowing shadow. 



[1: For reference, I believe Brossk is the purgative. Liisok translates as Rock-Destroyer, or maybe Stone-Eater.] 
[2: Technically, the archaic word used here means "Eliksni from outside one's House."]
[3: This word is not quite right, but I don't know a better one. Guilt for something that has not yet occurred? A voluntary acceptance of responsibility that was not yours. Variks has not been forthcoming.] 
[4: I believe we would now call this "Darkness."]
entries.text_zh:
当时，在夜深人静、怪物最有可能出没狩猎的时候追捕它似乎是理所当然的，而我所有的恐惧念头都被基拉斯克丝分散了，她决定让我简单介绍一下特纳尔、布罗斯克和利索克[1]的特性：哪种作为泻剂效果最佳，哪种又能毫不费力地穿透甲壳和石头。

最后，她问道，“你说你苦学过。是从记载里学的吗？”

“是的，公爵。”这世上已经没剩下能教我的杀手药剂师了。就算有人幸存，他们也不会到访我长大的小城的平民街区。

基拉斯克丝停下了在小径上艰难前行的脚步。这次我们各自分担了补给，而现在她递给我一个小瓶。“喝了它。”

我很快就照做了，并注意到液体中附着的日晒树根气味。我希望这第一口杀手药剂能让我充满力量，或者让我像蜕了五次皮一样成长。

它的味道难以下咽。我开始清楚意识到，自从到这里后，我几乎没有吃过什么东西。
 
“走吧，”基拉斯克丝说道。“我想我闻到了某个哈克西斯守卫。”

我除了基拉斯克丝的气味什么都闻不到。我跟在她后面。她灵活地跨过一个水闸，踏上肥沃的壤土，那里是哈克西斯的农场中最为野生的地方。

就在这时，我开始感受到药剂的效果。我看到了光能——在我视线边缘闪烁的一种微弱荧光。我转过身，看着它慢慢飘向地面，当它落地时，我看到更多萤光像尘埃一样聚集成云。在遥远的上空，我看到乙太的流动像一条河穿过天空。我放下背包，看了看自己的手，只见我的外壳下闪耀着光芒，仿佛是药剂从里到外照亮了我。

不仅我是如此。我望向基拉斯克丝，也看到了光能。通过她气孔一进一出的空气，被排出的乙太形成的雾气，以及她眼中狂热的光芒。

她一直在静静观察着我，现在她开口说话了。

“光能存在于万物之中。我们无法控制它，但我们可以吸引它。让它靠近。”她哼了一声。“就像一头贪婪的佩劳克。”

我正沉浸在敬畏之中，这突如其来的话语像是一记耳光打在我的脸上。“大机器可不是嗅探着亚卡果的畜牧动物！”我如此冒犯地说道，忘了自己是任她摆布的学徒。

基拉斯克丝笑了。“你不喜欢亚卡果吗？”

我恼怒地看向别处，仰望天空。在这样一个晴朗的夜晚，可以看到大机器在里斯的高层大气缓缓飘过。在药剂的作用下，我看到它像彗星般拖着光能——恍惚间觉得那即是生命。

大机器眨眼间就完成了对里斯卫星的地貌改造，然后把乙太洪流带到了里斯。那是一个富足的时代，没有幼雏会在成长过程中挨饿或夭折。如审判氏族所言，那也是一个物极必反的时代，一个缺乏秩序和理智的时代。我们的族人必须改变，必须适应。

在这个新时代，他们管我叫“堕落者士兵”。无用，无氏族。

“现在，来看尸体吧，”基拉斯克丝说道。 





这是埃里克斯尼族的尸体，或者说曾经是。我们脚下这具残缺不全的躯体已经肢体交缠，难以辨认。要不是连着它的那件残破斗篷，我可能都不会知道它曾属于哈克西斯的一名守卫。

更糟糕的是它的空虚。尸体周围的每个生物都闪耀着大机器的光芒。我不认识这个陌生人[2]，但其死亡在这世界上留下了一处空洞，而此刻在药剂的作用下，我能够看到这个空洞。我当时很庆幸自己的肚子空空如也。
 
基拉斯克丝在尸体附近蹲下，立刻开始触摸它，挪动手臂，仔细检查。我站在一旁，不知道自己该不该反对，但无论如何也不敢去抱怨。这里的植物还不是很茂密，我们暴露在外，不过——正如基拉斯克丝指出的那样——任何生物都是如此。

“是野兽干的吗？”我问道。毕竟这里确实有掠食动物出没。不过除非走投无路，任何野兽都不会主动攻击基拉斯克丝。

她示意我蹲在她身边。“看，”她说道。接着，等我在她侧面稳住后：“你没看到什么？” 

“光能，”我说道，突然的悲痛再次袭上心头。

她拍了我一下。“向下看。”
 
我照做了。我看到了一簇光——那是一群小幼虫，它们聚集于我在尸体周围留下的脚印里。我轻轻地拂去腿上的一只，然后意识到…

“它们在避开尸体，”我说道。

基拉斯克丝高兴地咕哝着。“摸摸这里。告诉我你感受到了什么。”

我摸了摸守卫的甲壳，感觉爪子下有湿湿的东西。我花了一段时间才意识到野兽从中间撕裂了其甲壳，并担心自己再也吃不下饭了。然后，突然间，我的手好像浸入了冰冷的池塘。 

我感受到愤怒。一种强烈、陌生的怒火，这与我自己的反感和恐惧无关。在愤怒之下，还有一种情绪，类似于…悔恨[3]。野兽会感到悔恨吗？

“你感受到了吗？我们看不到这种邪恶[4]，但它确实存在，”基拉斯克丝说道。“走吧。审判氏族是错的。我带你回船上去——要是我们动作快，它就不会有时间追上我们。”
 
但那头怪物并没有在森林里追踪我们。

它凭空倾泻而出，如同一团翻腾汹涌的阴影。 



[1: 这仅供参考，但我相信布罗斯克是泻剂。利索克可翻译为碎岩者，或是食石者。] 
[2: 严格来讲，这里所用古语的意思是“某个氏族之外的埃里克斯尼族”。]
[3: 这个词不太准确，但我也找不到更好的表达。它指的是对尚未发生的事情感到内疚？或者是自愿承担本不属于你的责任。瓦里克斯一直不太愿意解答。] 
[4: 我相信我们如今称之为“暗影”。]

entries.name: 4. War
entries.text:
I do not know if I would have seen anything at all had I not been given the tonic. What I did see, I did not understand at first: a dark shape clawing its way into being, caught on the edges of reality and tearing itself apart in order to make its existence possible.
It bellowed, and I felt the force of that sound rattle through my shell.

Something collided against my shoulder—Kiiraskes, pushing me away. 
"Irrha, the tonics!"

I stumbled toward the supplies. Behind me, I heard the whine and snap of Arc energy, and I turned to see Kiiraskes draw a short rod from the lining of her cloak. In her hands, it drew apart into a thin spear, crackling with power, and this she threw into the dark heart of the thing that hung suspended in the rift.

I heard the squelch of impact. The air filled with the strange, unpleasant stink of bad Ether and wet dirt. The creature rippled, clawed, and fell unhindered to the earth. The shape of it changed. I saw it rise upon six heavy limbs. Its misshapen head turned toward me.

In the next instant, a flask burst against it, and hissing steam roiled along its flank. I saw the beast's pointed maw part as it screamed.

"The Stone-Eater!" Kiiraskes cried. She pulled her sword from her belt and scraped something over the blade's surface. I saw Light bloom where she had touched it, and then she was moving toward the monster.

I opened the pack, but in my terror, I could not read the symbols on the bottles, nor think of what to do. I stared down at the rows of tonics I had so confidently described for Kiiraskes only an hour before, and I thought of how much of a hatchling I really was. I had studied the work of the Slayers as if it were only a story, and had expected only a story. All I had wanted was an escape.

Then I heard Kiiraskes yell. I thought of my time training, hoping I might become a healer in one of the great Houses. I looked in the pack, and there it was: the vial of Stone-Eater. I pulled it free and threw it as hard as I could toward the beast's head.

My will outpaced my aim. The flask struck the monster in the leg, and at once began to eat through its flesh. I saw it stumble briefly, only to shift its weight and turn. It made no sound of pain when struck, but now it sent another thundering bellow toward me, and with that rippling wave came a cold like nothing I've ever felt.

The air stung my throat and eyes. I threw my arms over my face and leapt away blindly toward the trees. When I looked back, I saw that the Light had been snuffed from a broad line of the undergrowth, leaving a sprawling emptiness into which I too might fall. I saw the monster rear up in preparation to charge.

A flash. Kiiraskes's blade, slicing deep into the monster's throat.

I saw that great maw descend upon her. I heard her scream.

The beast had her snared in its jaws, but she was levering them apart with two of her hands. The third held fast to her blade in the thing's neck, and in the fourth, I caught the shine of glass.

She thrust the flask deep into the creature's throat. For a long moment, nothing happened. Then the creature shuddered, and I saw the shell of it—the bones—lit from within by pale fire [1]. Its jaws crashed shut around Kiiraskes, once, then parted to scream. I saw the Baron haul at the blade—heard more terrible, wet screaming as the fire caught and spread.
 
The beast writhed and fell. Kiiraskes fell with it.



[1: I think this must be Tenar: 'wrath', and presumably the wrath of Light.]
entries.text_zh:
如果我没有服用药剂，不知道我当时是否能看到任何东西。而我所看到的，起初我并不理解：一个黑暗的形体挣扎着成形，被困在现实的边缘，自我撕裂方得以存在。
它吼叫着，我感到那声音的力量震得我的躯壳咯咯作响。

有什么东西撞到我的肩膀——是基拉斯克丝，把我推开了。 
“伊尔哈，药剂！”

我踉跄地朝补给跑去。我听到了身后电弧能量发出的嗡鸣和噼啪声响，于是我转过身去，看到基拉斯克丝从披风内衬中抽出一根短棒。在她的手中，短棒分离成一根细长的矛，噼啪作响，充满了能量，她将这根长矛投进了悬浮在裂缝中那东西的黑暗心脏。

我听到了撞击的嘎吱声。空气中弥漫着变质乙太和潮湿泥土的恶臭。那怪物翻滚着、抓挠着，径直倒在地上。它的形体发生了变化。我看到它用六条沉重的肢体站起来，将它那畸形的头转向了我。

下一瞬间，一个烧瓶在它身上爆裂开来，嘶嘶作响的蒸汽沿着它身体一侧搅动着。我看到那野兽尖叫着张开了巨嘴。

“食石者！”基拉斯克丝喊道。她从腰间拔出刀剑，在刃面上刮附了什么东西。我看到她触剑之处绽放出光能，然后她就朝着怪物过去了。

我打开背包，但由于惊恐，辨认不清瓶子上的符号，也无法思考该做什么。我低头凝视着数排一小时前我还自信满满地向基拉斯克丝描述过的药剂，真切地认识到自己是多稚嫩的一只幼雏。我一直把杀手的工作当作故事来研学，而期望着的也只不过是个故事。我所想要的只是逃离。

接着，我听到了基拉斯克丝的喊声。我想起了自己期盼着成为某个大氏族的治疗师而接受训练的日子。我在背包里搜寻着，总算找到了它：食石者的药瓶。我迅速把它拿出来，用尽全力扔向了那野兽的头部。

我的准头没能赶上我的决心。烧瓶击中了怪物的腿，并立刻开始侵蚀它的血肉。我看到它短暂地踉跄了一下，但随即挪动重心转过身来。被击中时，它没有发出任何痛苦的声音，但现在它再次朝我发出了雷鸣般的吼叫，伴随着那滚滚的声波，我感到了前所未有的寒冷。

空气刺痛了我的喉咙和眼睛。我手捂住脸，盲目地跳向树林。我回头望去，只见光能已经从一大片灌木丛中消失，只剩一片我也可能落入其中的无垠虚空。我看到怪物正蓄势待发，准备冲锋。

一道闪光划过。基拉斯克丝的利刃深深地刺进了怪物的喉咙。

我看到那张巨嘴向她扑去。我听到了她的尖叫声。

野兽用它的巨嘴咬住了她，但她用两只手将其撬开。第三只手紧紧抓住怪物脖子上的刀刃，而在第四只手中，我看到了玻璃的光泽。

她将烧瓶深深地插入怪物的喉咙里。很长一段时间，什么都没发生。然后那生物颤抖了起来，我看到它的外壳——骨头——被苍白的火焰从内部照亮[1]。它猛地合上巨嘴咬住基拉斯克丝，然后再张开尖叫。我看到了公爵用力去拉刀刃，随着火焰的燃烧和蔓延，听到了更可怕、夹杂着粘液的尖叫。
 
野兽扭动着身体扑地。基拉斯克丝也随之倒下。



[1: 我想这肯定是特纳尔，即怒火，应该是光能之怒吧。]

entries.name: 5. Monsters
entries.text:
I thought her dead.
 
Kiiraskes sat up, then fell over again. She spoke a very foul oath.
 
"You're hurt!" I cried stupidly.

"I'm not," she hissed. "Help me face the Great Machine."

She was too heavy to drag anywhere she did not want to go. I helped her sit up, and saw then the extent of the damage. She had lost a primary arm at the elbow, but that was the least of it. The wound in her middle yawned wide as she repositioned herself. In my certainty that I had failed her, I did not see her reach into the pack beside us.

She slathered a foul-smelling concoction onto her stomach, then activated her Arc-knife and held it close. I think I must have shouted. I heard the popping hiss of the salve igniting, and the air filled with the stink of roasting flesh.

Kiiraskes groaned and shuddered as the dying beast had.

"Now help me up," she said.

Together, we shuffled toward the burning ruin of Haaksis's creature.

It looked ordinary after the fire had worked through it. It seemed like it might have been a river-catcher, one of several common predators that fed along the waterways. But we had both seen it cloaked in boiling shadow, wielding a power that could douse the Light of the Great Machine. And no river-catcher ever grew so large.

Amid the pile of bones, I caught the shine of something metallic. A gleaming sphere. I reached for it, and Kiiraskes pulled me back.

"Don't touch it." With the stump of her arm, she gestured toward the pack I had abandoned nearby. "Bring that here."

I watched as she tipped a canister of powder over the sphere. The effects of the tonic were fading now, but I could still see the motes as they drew together. A cluster of Light, like a frenzied swarm of fish, gathering closer and closer together over the sphere until I had to cover my eyes.

When I looked again, the sphere was gone.

"What was it?" I could not help but regret that I had not had a chance to study it.
 
"Haaksis's old evil," Kiiraskes said. "Let's see what he can tell us about it."





Haaksis prepared hot, sweet drinks for us both. Later, I would wonder at his kindness. At the time, I was too tired and sore, and the drink soothed the ache in my throat.

Kiiraskes's wound still looked terrible: a livid stretch of cauterized flesh beneath a cracked carapace. But Kiiraskes refused both food and aid; she stood at the ready, listening.

"I wanted to pilot a Ketch," Haaksis told us. "When I was young. I stole a scout-ship to prove myself. I got lost."

"I didn't have much fuel. I set down on what I thought was one of the moons. But there was no air. No life. No Great Machine. I took my mask. My Ether-pack. I stepped outside."

I watched him clench his fists again, one after the other. Helplessly.

"I found a tower. A fortress-city of tombs like nothing you've ever seen. Something monumental. Something older than us."
 
I shivered.

"And at its heart, a ship. A ship like a blade." Haaksis's mandibles scraped together. "I found a sphere [1]. And when I held it…"

I heard Kiiraskes inhale, very softly.
 
"…showed me how to get home."

Kiiraskes said nothing. I sipped my drink, saying nothing. Understanding nothing.

"It showed me everything. The storm at the end of things, Kiiraskes. The uselessness of it all. The ruin of it." Haaksis hung his head. "I still hear its Voice. Even after I cast the sphere away. Even now, after you…"

After we destroyed the sphere, I realized. I set my cup down.
There had been nothing in his demeanor to make me frightened of Haaksis until now. It was as if something had torn free inside him. He must have been fighting it, the entire time. Fighting, and losing.

"I sent for Slayers. I thought there would be more of you left. I thought… there might be a way."

"We can still fight it, Haaksis," Kiiraskes said. "You and I. Come and tell Judgment—"
 
Haaksis gestured sharply in dismissal. "You don't know what's coming for us. For our children." He groaned. Ether gusted from his mouth like fog. "We have to stop this suffering." His eyes fixed upon mine. "We have to end it all."

He came at me over the desk.

Kiiraskes met him first.

I stumbled back as they fought. Fought like animals trapped inside a cage. A display shattered under the collision of their bodies. Haaksis's bellowing rattled the walls.
I could not throw any flasks without risk of hitting Kiiraskes. I made myself small and pressed my hands over my eyes.

I do not know if they fought for long hours or mere moments. For a time, there was only terror and noise, and once it passed, I felt gentle hands tugging mine away from my face.

"Forgive me," I said.

Kiiraskes grunted. "I haven't yet taught you to fight. That's what I'm here for." She looked down at the still form that had been Haaksis. "Bring the Shank. I have to tell the House of Judgment I killed a Lord of Rain."



[1: Eris spoke of finding such an artifact on the surface of the Lunar Pyramid.]
entries.text_zh:
我以为她死了。
 
基拉斯克丝坐起来，然后再次倒下。她恶毒地咒骂了一句。
 
“你受伤了！”我傻傻地喊到。

“我没有，”她发出了嘶鸣。“帮我面向大机器。”

她太重了，没法把她拖往她不想去的地方。我扶她坐起来，这才看到她受伤的程度。她的一只主臂在肘部断掉，但那还只是最轻的伤。她重新坐好时，中部的伤口深深地裂开。我因确信自己令她失望而沮丧，没注意到她把手伸进了我们身边的背包里。

她往自己的肚子上涂了一层难闻的药剂，然后激活电弧刀刃并紧紧握住。我想我肯定是喊出了声。我听到药膏点燃时噼里啪啦的嘶嘶声响，空气中弥漫着烤肉的恶臭。

基拉斯克丝像那头野兽垂死时一样呻吟和颤抖着。

“现在扶我起来，”她说。

我们一起摇摇晃晃地走向哈克西斯的那只生物的燃烧残骸。

大火过后，它看起来挺普通，似乎曾是只河流捕食者。那是一种在水道边觅食的常见掠食者，但我们都见过它被沸腾的阴影所笼罩，操控着足以熄灭大机器光能的力量。而且，没有哪只河流捕食者能长得如此巨大。

在骨堆中，我看到了一抹金属的光泽。一个闪闪发光的球体。我伸出手去，但基拉斯克丝把我拉了回来。

“别碰它。”她用残臂指了指我丢弃在附近的背包。“把那个拿过来。”

我看着她把一罐粉末倒在那球体上。虽然药剂的效力在消退，但我仍能看到萤光聚集在一起。一簇光能，像狂热的鱼群，在球体上越聚越近，直到我不得不掩住眼睛。

我再看时，那球体已经不见了。

“那是什么？”我不禁为自己没有机会研究它而感到遗憾。
 
“哈克西斯的古老邪恶，”基拉斯克丝说道。“看看他能告诉我们些什么。”





哈克西斯为我们俩准备了热乎乎的甜饮料。事后我会对他的好意感到纳闷。但当时我太累，浑身酸痛，而饮料舒缓了我喉咙的疼痛。

基拉斯克丝的伤口看起来还是很可怕：开裂的甲壳下是一大片颜色青紫、经过烧灼处理的血肉。但基拉斯克丝拒绝了食物和援助，她保持警觉地站在那里，仔细聆听着。

“我曾立志要驾驶双桅船，”哈克西斯告诉我们。“在我年轻的时候。为了证明自己，我偷了一艘斥候飞船。结果迷路了。”

“我当时的燃料不多。我降落在一个我以为是卫星的地方。但那里没有空气。没有生命。没有大机器。我拿上我的面具和乙太背包，走了出去。”

我看着他再次一个接一个地握紧拳头。无法遏制。

“我发现了一座塔。一座由墓穴构成的要塞城市，那景象你们一定没见过。它宏伟壮丽，比我们还要古老。”
 
我打了个寒颤。

“在它的中心，有一艘飞船。一艘像刀刃一样的飞船。”哈克西斯的下颚摩擦着发出声响。“我发现了一个球体[1]。我拿起它的时候…”

我听到基拉斯克丝轻轻地吸了一口气。
 
“…告诉了我怎么回家。”

基拉斯克丝没有说话。我抿了一口饮料，也没说话。一头雾水。

“它告诉了我一切。万物尽头的风暴，基拉斯克丝。一切都是白费力气。全都毁了。”哈克西斯垂下了头。“我还能听到它的声音。即使在我扔掉球体之后。即使是现在，在你们…”

在我们毁掉球体之后，我意识到。我放下了杯子。
此前，哈克西斯的举止并没有什么让我对他感到恐惧的地方。就好像他体内有什么东西被撕裂开了。他肯定一直在与之斗争。不停抵抗，节节败退。

“我请他们派来杀手。我以为会有更多的杀手存活。我以为…可能会有办法。”

“我们还是可以对抗它，哈克西斯，”基拉斯克丝说道。“你和我，去告诉审判——”
 
哈克西斯猛地做出了一个拒绝的手势。“你不知道我们将要面临什么。我们的孩子将要面临什么。”他呻吟着。乙太像雾一样从他口中喷涌而出。“我们必须停止这种痛苦。”他的目光紧盯着我的眼睛。“我们必须结束这一切。”

他越过桌子朝我扑来。

基拉斯克丝先迎了上去。

他们打斗时，我踉跄着后退。他们像困在笼中的野兽般搏斗。在他们身体的撞击下，有个陈列柜碎裂了。哈克西斯的吼声震得墙壁隆隆作响。
我不能冒险扔出任何烧瓶，那可能会误伤基拉斯克丝。我尽量蜷缩身体，用手捂住眼。

我不知道他们是打了几小时，还是只打了片刻。一时间，只剩下恐怖和嘈杂，而当那一切都过去后，我感觉到有一双温柔的手把我的手从脸上拿开。

“原谅我，”我说道。

基拉斯克丝咕哝道。“我还没教过你战斗。被派到这里来战斗的人是我。”她低头看了看那具曾是哈克西斯，但已不再动弹的躯体。“带上侦察机。我得告诉审判氏族，我杀死了一位骤雨领主。”



[1: 埃里斯提到过在月球金字塔表面发现了这样的一件神器。]

entries.name: 6. Return
entries.text:
The artificial current did more to steer the watercraft than we did. Kiiraskes held loosely to the oar with one hand.

I held the drone carefully, mindful of the occasional splash of water from the restless river. It chimed cheerfully in my hands, perhaps sensing I wanted soothing.

"I had a son. Ah…" Kiiraskes scraped a claw along one mandible, to strike the words from her mouth. "I have a son. Not much older than you."

I looked up at her, surprised. Her gaze was on the water.
"He found a place with the Gentle Weavers. He wanted very much to… belong. I hope he will weave great things. Or else… do whatever it is he wishes to do." She looked at me, and it was my turn to feign interest in the river.

I heard her sigh. "We Slayers were never lords. We had no Kells. We came together to defend our people. We were Barons of Riis and the Great Machine, not… this House or that."
 
She touched the scar on her stomach, and I stilled in concern.

"The wars destroyed us. Nobody believes that there is anything worse to fight out there than ourselves."

I thought, without wanting to, of Haaksis. The mind-sickness that had gripped him… or else, the voice of something powerful and ancient.

"Chelchis sees it. Feels it deep in her mills. Something is coming. All those strange reports that she takes back to Kings and Judgment. But she thinks it will come from within, from… disorder."

"But… I saw the monster," I said. "I'll tell everyone what happened."
 
Kiiraskes looked up at me. Even with her helmet removed, I could not tell what she was thinking. 

"You did well, Irrha," she said.
The rest of the journey, we passed in silence. 





I knew Baron Kiiraskes was still in pain because she did not shrug off Chelchis's assistance in stepping out of the watercraft.

Kiiraskes reached out to take the Shank from my hands. "I will speak to House Judgment and report on our findings." She hesitated. "Chelchiskel can keep an eye out for you until I return."

We both watched Baron Kiiraskes pull her cloak tightly around herself and limp away toward the palace doors. Chelchis stared at me, and I worried she would ask me for an explanation. But instead, Chelchis grunted, as if something had been decided, and leaned against a nearby pillar.

I felt the weight of the past couple of days settle onto me. I was tired, but my body was not convinced it was safe to rest. I felt alert and exhausted all at once. I hugged my arms to myself and waited.

Some time into the silence, Chelchis began to sing quietly. It was not a tune I recognized, but beautiful in its lilting sweetness.

I thought of voices raised together in song in shared rooms. I thought of long nights playing find-sneak with friends, long before any of us had to worry about our purpose. In my chest, I felt a hollow ache like grief.
 
"What is it?" Chelchis asked.
 
I startled and looked up at her. What could I possibly say to a Kell that wouldn't just be wasting her time? "Oh, no, it's just… your song is sad."

Had she taken offense, she could have pulled my arms from their sockets. Instead, Chelchis touched my shoulder gently, and drew me close.

"Not sad," Chelchis said. "A song for star-sailors headed out into the dark between worlds."

"And wherever we walk, there is Light, little brother."



[Goodbye, Irrha.  –Eido, Scribe of House Light]
entries.text_zh:
人造水流比我们更能控制船只的行进方向。基拉斯克丝一只手松松地握着桨。

我小心翼翼地拿着无人机，留意着躁动的河水偶尔溅起的水花。它在我手中欢快地鸣叫着，也许是感受到了我需要安慰。

“我有过一个儿子。啊…”基拉斯克丝用一只爪子刮过她的下颚，仿佛是要把那些话从嘴里抹去。“我有一个儿子。比你大不了多少。”

我抬起头，惊讶地看着她。她的目光落在水面上。
“他在温柔织工氏族中找到了自己的位置。他非常想…融入其中。我希望他能编织出伟大的事物。或者是…做他想做的任何事情。”她看向我，这次轮到我假装对河流感兴趣了。

我听到她叹了口气。“我们杀手从来都不是领主。我们没有凯尔。我们聚集在一起是为了保卫我们的族人。我们是里斯和大机器的公爵，而不是…这个或那个氏族的公爵。”
 
她摸了摸肚子上的伤疤，我担忧地僵住了。

“战争摧毁了我们。没有谁相信这世上还有比我们自己更可怕的东西，需要我们去对抗。”

我不由自主地想起了哈克西斯。他被心灵的疾病所折磨…又或者，是某种强大而古老之物的声音在作祟。

“切尔奇斯看到了。在她的内心深处感受到了。有什么事情要发生。所有那些她带回给王族和审判氏族的奇怪报告。但她认为那会来自于内部，来自于…混乱。”

“但是…我看到了怪物，”我说。“我会告诉大家发生了什么。”
 
基拉斯克丝抬起头望着我。即使她摘下了头盔，我也看不出她在想什么。 

“你做得很好，伊尔哈。”她说。
接下来的旅程中，我们保持着沉默。 





我知道基拉斯克丝公爵还在忍受痛苦，因为她走下船时没有甩开切尔奇斯的搀扶。

基拉斯克丝从我的手中接过了侦察机。“我会跟审判氏族交谈，报告我们的发现。”她犹豫了一下。“在我回来之前，切尔奇斯凯尔可以照看你。”

我们俩看着基拉斯克丝公爵拉紧披风，一瘸一拐地向宫殿大门走去。切尔奇斯盯着我，我担心她会要求我作出解释。但切尔奇斯却哼了一声，好像已经决定了什么似的，然后靠在了旁边的一根柱子上。

我感到过去几天的重担压得我喘不过气来。我累了，但我的身体却不相信现在休息是安全的。我觉得既警觉又疲惫。我抱着双臂等待着。

沉默了一段时间后，切尔奇斯开始低声唱歌。那是我不熟悉的曲调，但它的旋律悠扬甜美，非常动听。

我想起了在共用的房间里一起高歌的声音，想起了与朋友们一起玩捉小偷游戏度过的长夜，那时我们中还没有谁需要为自己的使命而担忧。我感到胸口有一种类似悲伤的空虚之痛。
 
“怎么了？”切尔奇斯问道。
 
我吓了一跳，抬头看着她。我能对一位凯尔说什么，而不算是浪费她的时间呢？“哦，没什么，只是…你的歌很悲伤。”

要是她感觉受到冒犯，可能就会把我的胳膊从关节上拽下来。但切尔奇斯却轻轻碰触我的肩，把我拉近。

“不是悲伤，”切尔奇斯说道。“这是一首为那些驶向世界间无尽黑暗的星际水手而唱的歌。”

“而无论我们走到哪里，都有光能相伴，小兄弟。”



[再见，伊尔哈。——光能氏族文士艾多]

entries.name: Lingering
entries.text:
He lingers in the entryway. It's the sort of lingering where you pretend nothing's changed—and it doesn't have to, as long as you never go in. Eris will always be just out of reach, but at least there, real in the apartment she barely used, in the City she defended but rarely saw.  

It's a fool's dream. But what is he if not a fool? So he stays a little longer, sick with wishing.
entries.text_zh:
他徘徊在入口处。仿佛只要不进去，就能装作一切未曾改变。埃里斯将永远遥不可及，但至少她真实地存在于那间几乎不曾有人踏足的公寓里，在她守护却鲜少露面的圣城之中。  

这是一场傻瓜的幻想。但他不正是个傻瓜吗？于是，他多停留了一会儿，满心向往。

entries.name: Expanse
entries.text:
Cold out here. Reminds him—in a bad way—of that Light-forsaken planet he nearly died on.  

He scuffles around the campsite. Pathetic, he knows it's pathetic. Even if people hadn't been through here, the storms would have blown over any footprints. Any lost trinkets would long since have been found or buried deep enough that he can't hope to find them. 

Looking out on the desolate expanse doesn't do much for him, just leaves him alone with his feelings. Not a fun place to be. He moves on.
entries.text_zh:
外面很冷，让他苦涩地回忆起那个被光能遗弃的星球，而他曾在那里濒临死亡。  

他在营地周围徘徊，深知此举颇为可悲。即便无人经过，风暴也会抹去所有足迹。任何遗失的小物件早已被寻获或深埋，他不可能找到它们。 

眺望这片荒凉的广袤之地，只会让他与自己的情感独处。此地不宜久留，他继续前行。

entries.name: Schadenfreude
entries.text:
Sometimes it makes a guy feel better to make fun of someone way worse off than he is. He knows it's a mistake soon as he sets eyes on the giant robot face, though.  

Maybe somewhere else. He turns and goes, ignoring the dramatic monologue already kicking off behind him.
entries.text_zh:
有时，嘲笑境遇比自己更糟的人能带来一丝慰藉。但当他看到那张巨大的机器人脸庞时，便知道自己错了。  

或许该换个地方。他转身离去，对身后已然开始的戏剧性独白不予理会。

entries.name: Unfamiliar
entries.text:
Pretending everything's fine was never going to work. He says he's lost a shipment of new fancy guns to get a bunch of Guardians off his back and on a scavenger hunt for nonexistent weapons. Give him some peace and quiet. He takes a minute to rustle around in his stuff, grabbing what he might need for maybe a longer trip— 

Not sure where he'd go, just not here— 

He swears he can see Eris leaning against the railing, a sly little smile barely turning up the corners of her mouth. He can't stand it.
entries.text_zh:
假装一切安好是行不通的。他谎称遗失了一批新的高级枪械，让几名守护者不再纠缠他，去寻找那些并不存在的武器，给他片刻宁静。他花了一分钟时间在自己的物品中翻找，拿取漫长之旅中可能需要的东西—— 

他不确定该去哪儿，只要离开这里就好—— 

他仿佛看到埃里斯倚在栏杆上，嘴角勾起一抹狡黠的微笑。这令他感到难以忍受。

entries.name: Restlessness
entries.text:
He swings by to let the man in charge know he's going to be out of town for a while. Guy'll understand. And it's a new level of responsible; Commander should appreciate that. 

The place is empty, though. He wanders around it—sets the beads to clicking against each other, prods the gold figure on the side table until it falls over, meanders past books and blinks at the cat perched on a shelf over his head.  

Nothing. He's restless. The longer he stands still, the longer the grief has to get its hooks into him. He mutters a curse into the silence and sees himself out.
entries.text_zh:
他顺道去向管事的老大报备，说自己要离城一段时间。那家伙会理解的。这样做也更显责任心，指挥官会对此表示赞赏的。 

但这地方是空的。他在房间里来回踱步——让珠子相互碰撞，轻推边桌上的金色雕像，直至它倾倒，又在书架间徘徊，抬头望向架子上的猫。  

什么都没有。他心神不宁。停留得越久，那份悲伤就越发清晰地缠绕着他。他冲着寂静低声咒骂，自行离去。

entries.name: Preparation
entries.text:
There's a hidden little nook in the Hangar, great spot for watching Sparrow maintenance if that's what you're into. Comfortable too. Good place to get away from the noise. He breezes in and out, rooting up a cache he left there a long time ago. Never could get out of the habit of keeping emergency stashes.   

Anywhere else he needs to stop off before he leaves for good? Maybe… maybe.   

It's a short hop from there to his ship.
entries.text_zh:
机库里有个隐秘的角落，如果你有兴趣的话，可以清晰地看到快雀的维修过程。那里很舒适，是个远离尘嚣的好地方。他轻车熟路地来到那里，找出很久以前藏在那里的应急储备品。藏货的习惯，他一直都难以改掉。   

在彻底离开之前，还有别的什么地方值得去看看吗？或许…有吧。   

那里离他的飞船也很近。

entries.name: Reconsidering
entries.text:
Getting out in the woods could clear his head. Maybe he shouldn't go after all.  

Familiar energy readings. Not Darkness, not Light, but the in-between stuff. Sterile neutrinos. Makes him think of a time way back when: Moondust and him. And the arrival of the Pyramid fleet…
entries.text_zh:
步入树林没准儿会让他清醒一点。到头来，他也许并不该选择离去。  

熟悉的能量读数——既非暗影也非光能，而是介于二者之间。惰性中微子，这让他回想起了很久以前的往事：小月月和他。以及金字塔舰队的抵达…

entries.name: Committing
entries.text:
There's a little cliff that overlooks the cove's water. He settles there a spell. It's quiet. Not a lot of combat, few enough reasons for Guardians to swing through. The quiet doesn't so much remind him of her as make him wish she were there. 

Everything's just going to keep doing that, huh. He can be honest with himself about that.  

All right. One last stop.
entries.text_zh:
有个俯瞰着宁静海湾的小悬崖。他在那里安顿了一会儿。很静。战斗很稀少，守护者们也没有多少理由来这里。这样的宁静没怎么勾起他对她的回忆，反而让他更加渴望她此刻在这里。 

所有的一切都会继续如此吧。他可以坦然地承认这一点。  

好了。还有最后一站。

entries.name: Reminiscing
entries.text:
He goes into her apartment this time. Not to look through her things, really, just—prove it to himself. She's not there. She won't be. He's got to remember that.  

He brushes his fingers along a side table and tries to imagine what she'd say to him.
entries.text_zh:
这次他走进了她的公寓。不是为了寻找她的遗物，而是——想要向自己证明些什么。她不在这里，永远也不会再回来。他必须铭记于心。  

他用他的手指轻轻掠过边桌，试图想象她会对他说些什么。

entries.name: Imagining
entries.text: Probably it'd be something deep and meaningful. He doesn't have the heart to think it up. He steps into the other room, moves around the table covered in books and relics. Almost trips on the rug.
entries.text_zh: 八成是某种深刻而重要的东西，但他无心琢磨。他步入另一房间，绕过堆满书籍与圣物的书桌，差点被地毯绊倒。

entries.name: Final Curtain
entries.text:
Someone else finds him there. 

He sees himself out, mouth stinging as he takes the stairs. That's it, then. There's nothing for him here. And he was a fool to think there was.  

Time to go.
entries.text_zh:
他在那里遇到了另一个人。 

他自行离去，走下楼梯时嘴里满是刺痛。原来如此。这里没有给他的东西。他是傻瓜，才会抱有那种期待。  

该离开了。

entries.name: I. Now and hereafter
entries.text:
The fall dissolves my body because I allow it. The radiolaria takes my consciousness into the network because I command it. I do not perish; I am not swept away by outside force; the waterfall accedes to gravity only upon my word. The lingering presence of Commander Te'Qal in my C2 vertebra understands the value of a tactical retreat.

At age forty-three I stood on the edge of the Citadel with a jar full of brains. Two hundred and twenty-seven Maya Sundareshes replicated by the Vex, readied in turn as weapons against them. Sappers. Explorers. Lab rats loosed into a maze.

Venus was lifetimes ago, before Lhasa, before Neomuna. Before the network and my new becoming.

My Chioma stood at my side. Both of us in proxy suits, too fragile to walk under the shadow of the Citadel in our own bodies. Weak. Mortal. Scared for our lives and those of our copies, trapped within a linear flow of time, unable to stand aside and see that this was the happiest we'd ever be.

The only ethical choice, we believed, was to accept the copies' vote and release them into the network.

We should have crushed the drives, broken the jars, strained the tadpoles from the water and poured them into an incinerator, instead of dropping them into the pond. None of those copies were my Chioma; none were the true me. Frameshift mutations instantiated by the Vex to torment us with what they knew, and what was beyond our control. Photonegatives, skewing further and further out of alignment the longer they were allowed to exist in something approaching linear time.

Those Venus-Chiomas still walking the network, the lingering remains of the Vex's first assault on my life, are crude parasites. Mimics of the real plant. Boquila trifoliata hoping the angles of their misshapen leaves will keep them from my notice.

I know my Chioma, and she knows me.

If she does not know me with the light of an Echo around my neck, then she is not the true Chioma, she is a weed in the flowerbed choking out a true rose.

I control the variables. I command the Vex. There is nowhere that my Chioma can hide from me where I will not find her. There is nobody who can keep her from me.

The waterfall at the heart of Nessus sweeps me into the information network and reassembles my body. The mantle on my shoulders sings with purpose as sweetly as ever. Te'Qal's memory guides me yet. A setback will not stop my work; one voice silenced will not end the chorus.

I lift my hand, breathe, and let the baton fall.
entries.text_zh:
坠落溶解着我的躯体，只因我允许。活性放射体液遵循我的指令，将我的意识带入网络。我并未消逝，亦非被外力裹挟；瀑布唯我之命是从，方能顺从重力。指挥官特卡尔难以磨灭的印记藏于我的C2椎骨之中，深谙战术撤退的价值。

四十三岁那年，我伫立于要塞边缘，手持装满大脑的容器。两百二十七个被Vex复制的玛雅·桑戴尔什，正待被用作对抗它们的武器。工兵、探险者，皆是迷宫中的实验鼠。

金星上的事恍如隔世，那是在拉萨之前，在内欧姆那之前，在网络与新生的自我之前。

我的希欧玛站在我身旁，我们都穿着代理服，脆弱不堪，无法以血肉之躯行走于要塞阴影之下。渺小，凡人之躯，我们为自己与复制品的生命而战栗，被困于线性时间流中，无法纵观全局，看清这是我们一生中最幸福的时光。

我们坚信，唯一合乎道德的选择，是接受复制品的投票，将其释放到网络之中。

我们本应粉碎驱动器，砸碎容器，将蝌蚪从水中滤出，倾入焚化炉，而非投入池塘。那些复制品中，无一是我的希欧玛；无一是真正的我。Vex实例化的移码突变，以它们所知且超乎我们掌控之物，折磨着我们。底片，随其在接近线性时间中的存在愈久，便愈发偏离正轨。

那些仍游荡于网络之中的金星-希欧玛，Vex对我生命初次侵袭的残余，不过是粗糙的寄生虫，对真正植物的拙劣模仿。三叶葡萄藤妄图以畸形叶片的角度，蒙蔽我的双眼。

我了解我的希欧玛，她也了解我。

若她因为我颈间的回响之光无法认出我，那她便非真正的希欧玛，不过是花圃中的杂草，窒息了真正的玫瑰。

我掌控变量，驾驭Vex。无论我的希欧玛藏身何处，我必能找到她。没有人能阻止我找到她。

涅索斯中心的瀑布将我卷入信息网络，重塑我的身躯。我肩上的披风，如往昔般甜美地吟唱着目标之歌。特卡尔的记忆仍在指引着我，挫折无法阻挡我的脚步；一个声音的沉默，不会终结合唱。

我抬手，深呼吸，让指挥棒落下。

entries.name: II. A perfect when
entries.text:
It is not power that corrupts but time: the pressure of the world bearing down over endless seconds until what was perfect is distorted, stretched, suspended. True preservation is impossible in the face of chronology. Even silver, purest of the conductive metals, oxidizes eventually.

A prickle runs down my spine. The commander's mind blooms into gold-edged life within mine.

:advisor:ancestor:Warden:so I speak:

:find your goal, my few-limbed descendant:

My goal. Chioma. Where is she?

She's waiting for me faithfully where she has always been. Before Neptune and its failures.

We finished our contract on Venus; we concluded work with the Ishtar Collective on Earth; we parted ways for a time, working on separate problems. Hoping, above all, to benefit humanity, to extend our Golden Age beyond death. A pure note, sustained indefinitely, in the willing air.

That was the end. I just couldn't see it—a failure of perspective. The absolute threshold of my senses was not broad enough.

Time and its corruption set in. Our first encounter with the Vex sent in unanticipated directions. Who can remain whole after knowing yourself to be one of 228? What marriage can sustain so many empty futures?

To hold your own soul in your hand is to grasp the infinite. The fingers don't close.

:communion:allyship:sympathy:

:we will plan our attack with care:

Venus in the Ishtar Sink. That was when we were perfect. That was our Golden Age. The rot was sinking in by the time we reached Neptune—even before the Collapse, and the invasion from the outside.

The Guardians call today the City Age. The era of a single metropolis walled in, under siege. A global population attenuated, weakened, scratching out cooking fires in the dirt covering a buried particle accelerator.

They pick away at invader after invader, threat after threat.

:failed strategy:

They have assured the preservation of a world in ruins.

My beloved languishes in the Golden Age, a secure present shattered by the oncoming future.

She is not dead. She is not within the network. She has just unpacked her home office after years of storage. She's preparing summary papers and a slide deck for the Collective board. She is thinking of her current work, her next contract, her forty-fifth birthday in two weeks' time, which she hopes I will have remembered to plan for. And all the while the neutron bomb of Damocles hovers over her head. A fleet of Pyramid ships waiting to descend.

:consider your assets:consider your goal:build the bridge between:

:what do you have?:

A golden past. My Chioma locked in a tomb under the rubble of the Collapse.

:what do you have?:

A safe future unthreatened by the Collapse and its inciting Witness. Guidance, strategy, ability. 

:what do you have?:

A lever.

Given somewhere to place it, I could move the world.
entries.text_zh:
腐蚀万物的并非权力，而是时间：在无尽流逝的每一秒中，世界的压力如影随形，直至将完美之物扭曲、拉长、悬置。面对时间的洪流，真正的永恒不过是妄想。即便是最纯净的导电金属——银，也终将难逃氧化之劫。

一阵刺痛顺着我的脊椎蔓延开来。指挥官的思维在我脑海中迸发出镶着金边的生命之光。

:顾问:祖先:守望者:我如是说:

:找到你的目标，我少肢的后代:

我的目标，希欧玛，她在哪里？

她始终如一地在那里守候着我，在海王星尚未陨落的时代之前。

我们在金星履行了合约，在地球结束了与伊什塔集团的协作。随后，我们各自分道扬镳，投身于不同的使命。我们的初衷，是造福人类，将黄金时代的光辉延续至永恒。如同纯净的音符，在自由的空气中无限回响。

那便是结局，而我却无法窥见——视角受到局限，感官的阈值太过狭隘。

时间与它的腐蚀之力悄然降临。与Vex的首次接触，引领我们走向了意想不到的境地。当意识到自己不过是228个中的一员时，谁又能保持完整无缺？什么样的婚姻能够承受如此多的空洞未来？

紧握自己的灵魂，如同掌控无限。我的手指无法合拢。

:交流:联盟:同情:

:我们将精心策划这场攻势:

金星之上的伊什塔洼地，那时的我们无懈可击，那便是我们的黄金时代。然而，腐烂的种子早已在我们抵达海王星时悄然种下——甚至早于大崩溃与外部入侵。

守护者称如今为圣城纪元。一个单一的城市被围墙包围，处于围困之中的时代。全球人口减少，削弱，在覆盖着埋藏粒子加速器的泥土上刮擦出炊火。

他们逐一迎战入侵者，逐一化解威胁。

:失败的策略:

那不过是一个废墟世界的苟延残喘。

我的爱人在黄金时代中凋萎，一个安全的当下，被即将到来的未来无情摧毁。

她没有死去。她不在网络中。她刚刚取出尘封多年的家庭办公室物品，正为集团委员会准备摘要论文与幻灯片。她心中所念，是当前的工作、下一个合同、两周后的四十五岁生日，期望着我能记得准备惊喜。而与此同时，达摩克利斯之剑般的中子弹悬于她头顶，一队金字塔飞船正等待着降临的时刻。

:考虑你的资产:考虑你的目标:在两者间架起桥梁:

:你拥有什么？:

一个金色的过去，我的希欧玛被囚禁于大崩溃废墟之下的坟墓之中。

:你拥有什么？:

一个不受大崩溃及其诱因——见证者——威胁的安全未来。指引、策略与能力。 

:你拥有什么？:

一根杠杆。

给我一个支点，我将撬动整个世界。

entries.name: III. Down?
entries.text:
Traveling the Vex information network means metaphor superimposed on the flat planes of reality. Techno-biological synesthesia. Merkwelt, wirkwelt, umwelt. I step through a portal held open by the calculations of a Gate Lord, feel it in its true form as my Vex do, even as the Human part of me grasps for interpretation: Fourier transforming down the crest of a wave, knowing the water is angry below.

The water stills as I walk upon it, harmless to its master. My laboratory and my royal court. I incline my scepter and my Vex leap to test another variable for me.

Somewhere within the network will be a record of the fulcrum I need, the power I require. If not within the bounds of my Collective's testing, then outside of it.

What I need is to observe without biasing the results.

PAY ME NO MIND.

The light of my mantle dims, and my footfalls grow silent. Around me, my Vex forget my presence. I walk between them, a queen unmarked by any sensor.

Layer upon layer of networked simulations part for me as easily as curtains brushed aside.

A world of glass cliffs reduced to glittering sand by the furious water below. Here the Vex test the limits of aquatic life and of Klein bottle manifolds.

Eighteen thousand and sixty-four simulations stacked like pages in a book, failed attempts to predict and replicate Light. Hundreds of thousands of prior attempts crumpled and burned.

An Exodus ship-sized Minotaur—a builder of builders—tests and iterates new chassis designs for its deputies, processing capacity, sensor networks, and physical balance on varying terrain and durability. One beta-build clad in mismatched bronze plating plays jump rope with its own tails. Another carries a mechano-organic fetus within its ventral tank, radiolaria adhering layer by layer to its surface.

Something trembling and vermiform darts through the ephemeral layers of hypothesis, followed by thought-predators feeding on the swarming krill of datapoints.

Torobatl falls, rises, falls again, in tactical simulations more concerned with access to the servers of its Athenaeum worlds than anything else.

I walk, farther from home than any human before me, into simulations of worlds lit by stars, the first gleaming of which have yet to reach Earth's skies. Millions of worlds connected at unexpected points, staked out by different Collectives for their own use.

All the distance, all the storehouses of data and simulated tactics run through my fingers. And somehow, it's on my homecoming that I find what I need.
entries.text_zh:
穿越Vex信息网络，意味着让隐喻与现实的层面相互重叠。这是技术生物的通感体验——感知世界、影响世界、环境世界。我踏过一扇由门神的计算维持开启的传送门，以我的Vex那样的真实面目感受这一切，即便作为人类的部分仍在寻求解释：沿着波峰进行傅里叶变换，深知下方的水流暗藏汹涌。

当我行走于水面上时，水流归于平静，不会伤害它的主人。我的实验室，我的王室宫廷。我倾斜权杖，Vex便跃然而起，为我测试新的变量。

在这网络之中，定有我所需的支点记录，我渴望的力量。若不在我集合体的测试范围之内，那便是在其外。

我所追求的，是在不干扰结果的前提下进行观察。

无需在意我。

我的披风光芒渐暗，脚步悄无声息。在我周围，Vex忘记了我的存在。我穿梭于它们之间，宛如一位不被任何传感器察觉的女王。

一层又一层的网络模拟，如同拨开窗帘般轻易地为我分开。

这是一个由玻璃悬崖构成的世界，被下方湍急的水流冲刷成闪闪发光的沙粒。在这里，Vex正测试着水生生命与克莱因瓶流形的极限。

一万八千零六十四个模拟层层堆叠，犹如书页，它们试图预测并复制光能，却屡屡失败。数十万次尝试，皆已付之一炬。

一个与移民飞船同等大小的米诺陶——建造者中的佼佼者——正在测试并迭代其副官的新底盘设计、处理能力、传感网络，以及在不同地形上的物理平衡与耐久性。一个身着不匹配青铜装甲的测试版，正用尾巴玩着跳绳游戏。另一个则在其腹部水箱中，携带着一个机械有机胎儿，活性放射体液一层层地附着其上。

一个颤抖的蠕虫状物体穿梭于假设的短暂层面之间，身后跟着思想掠食者，它们正在捕食由数据点构成的虫群。

图罗巴特尔沦陷、崛起，再次沦陷，这些战术模拟更关心的是如何侵入其雅典娜神殿世界的服务器，而非其他任何事务。

我前行，比任何人类都走得更远，踏入由恒星照亮的世界模拟之中，这些恒星的第一缕光芒尚未照耀地球的天空。数百万个世界在意想不到的节点上相连，被不同的集合体据为己有。

所有的距离、所有的数据存储库、所有的模拟战术，皆从我指尖流淌而过。而不知为何，正是在我踏上归途之时，我找到了我所需要的。

entries.name: IV. The root of unity
entries.text:
I'm standing on a glass pier stretching out over a pale, alkaline lake. I'm crossing a static-charged field of snow. I'm sitting on a bench in front of a Parthenon frieze worn over millennia to near perfect smoothness.

:necessary change:limb in jaw-beast's maw:no lone mind is sane:

:a prudent general accepts new perspectives:a prudent general wins the war: 

You're right. I need new tools. 

:refutation:not tools:allies:listen: 

:attend your ancestor: 

I rise from the bench. Dust off my hands. Exit the museum and drop my ticket stub on the way out. My tools are waiting. 

I COMMAND YOU. 

Pull on the helix and the strand reform. Eukaryotes wriggle, swell, collapse. 

BE OTHERWISE. 

Eat the apple, leave the garden, make a choice that comes from something other than your Collective. I need variations in tactics. I need your minds to be separate from others.

RESPECT WHAT I CAN GIVE YOU.

Minotaurs kneel as I pass, my hand trailing sparks over their chassis. Hydras still their cilia in respect.

A Hobgoblin holds up useless, shining pieces of scrap to weld to its body. Its hand is very steady as it applies the solder.

TELL ME WHY.

Its hand jerks back. It lifts its face as a sunflower to that which gives it life.

V^ directive(original/HOBGOBLIN)==observe==judge==enact || IF(independent)=true THEN directive(modified/HOBGOBLIN(independent))==observe==create==build (self, other, beauty) ^V

An aspiring artist? Useless. A waste of mind.

:new eyes:new limbs:needed and necessary:

Wrong, Te'Qal.

:an army is more than its head:

An army is nothing but its head. Your cephalopod cousins and their independently minded limbs are not the model I work from.

I strip the charge from the useless Hobgoblin's radiolaria in one brisk pass of my palm over its head. The now-empty chassis falls as I spin the recovered energy into a sphere, like yarn into a ball prickling at my hand.

I raise another from the sea. This one knows its maker.

TELL ME WHO YOU ARE.

V^ directive(original/HARPY)==study==compile==serve || directive(modified/HARPY(Conductor))==input(required) ^V

I roll the marble of energy between my palms until it is smooth, electrical waveforms long and calm. The Vex lowers itself to my height at a thought, and I release the marble to let it sink into its huge bronze eye. Vast petals shudder and fold inwards.

YOU'LL DO.
entries.text_zh:
我站在一座玻璃码头上，码头延伸至一片苍白的碱性湖泊之上。我正穿越一片布满静电的雪地。我坐在一张长凳上，眼前是一幅历经千年磨损、变得近乎完美光滑的帕特农神庙浮雕。

:必要的改变:肢体在颚兽的颚之中:孤独的心智皆不理智:

:明智的将军接受新视角:明智的将军赢得战争: 

你说得对，我需要新的工具。 

:反驳:不是工具:而是盟友:聆听: 

:注意你的祖先: 

我从长凳上起身，拍掉手上的灰尘，离开博物馆，出门时随手丢下票根。我的工具正等着我。 

我命令你。 

拉动螺旋，链条重组。真核生物扭动、膨胀、崩塌。 

变得不同。 

吃下苹果，离开花园，做出一个不源自你所属集合体的选择。我需要战术上的变化。我需要你的思想与他人区分开。

尊重我能给予你的。

当我经过时，米诺陶纷纷跪地，我的手在它们的机体上拖出火花。九头蛇的纤毛停止了耸动以示尊敬。

一个高等哥布林举起无用而闪亮的废料碎片，想要焊接到自己身上。它的手在使用焊料时非常稳定。

告诉我为什么。

它的手猛地收回。它抬起脸，如向日葵般面向赋予它生命的存在。

V^ 指令(原始/高等哥布林)==观察==判断==执行 || 如果(独立)=真 那么 指令(修改后/高等哥布林(独立))==观察==创造==建造(自我，他者，美) ^V

一个有抱负的艺术家？无用，浪费心力。

:新眼睛:新肢体:需要且必要:

错了，特卡尔。

:军队不只需要首脑:

军队中，除了首脑，其它的一文不值。你的头足类表亲，及其独立思考的肢体，不是我会用的模式。

我在它的头顶一挥手掌，剥夺了这个无用高等哥布林的活性放射体液。空空如也的机体倒下，我将回收的能量旋转成一个球体，就像纱线缠成一团，刺激着我的手掌。

我从海中唤起另一个。这一个知道自己的创造者是谁。

告诉我你是谁。

V^ 指令(原始/机甲女妖)==研究==编译==服务 || 指令(修改后/机甲女妖(指挥者))==输入(必需) ^V

我在两手间滚动着能量弹珠，直到它变得光滑，电波形态长而平静。Vex一念之间降低身高与我持平，我释放弹珠，让它沉入其青铜大眼中。巨大的花瓣震颤着向内折叠。

就你吧。

entries.name: V. Eternal life
entries.text:
The Vex keep their hypotheses in quarantine. Tested and iterated on until they are ready for distribution.

My lungs fill with salt water. I grow gills, filtering life from the sea of data. What compost have you turned over for me, my creatures?

I make myself anew. Humans have poor magnetoreception: I neglected the sense when building my body. A failure of oversight solved by the addition of digital cryptochromes. Ampullae of Lorenzini and a neuromast while I'm at it. Any information is good information. The wheat may be sorted from the chaff later.

OPEN THE DOOR.

I slip in and out of network and real space, quickstepping through the hollows of space between bodies. Spiraling out towards the Oort cloud through Mercury's burning sands and the radioactive winds on Luna.

The umwelt of pure radiolaria is different from that of a Goblin within its bronze chassis; the umwelt of a Hydra is different from that of a Goblin. The Hobgoblins' sensory horns take in different data than a Harpy's cilia. They each serve different needs within the collective.

The collective's multiplicative umwelten all feed into mine. They, the microorganisms within my holobiont, and I the controlling intelligence at its center.

SPREAD OUT.

My Vex disseminate across the system, ants on the hunt, bringing home information to their queen. I know what I am searching for, if we can only find the right tool for the quest.

The magnetosphere is abruptly useless. Chaff tossed out on the wind. It is gravity that beckons my attention.

I sideslip through the system towards an interesting aberration. A tangled clump of dark matter. My Goblins sift through Human computer networks, bringing me a name: Cocytus.

This is not a place anyone wants me to be.

I suborn the warheads, I take over the gates, I stock the land with my tools.

Gravity moves in the dark; it whispers against my cheekbones and pulls me down. Fine strands of dark matter move around me and through me.

How do we solve the hard problem of consciousness? One theory suggests increasingly complex electrical wave patterns. Sustaining those complex waveforms through an affected substrate. Electrical impulses through brain matter. Another kind of impulse through dark matter.

Vast, dispersed minds. Thinking and acting across distances and timelines broad enough to confuse even the Vex. Gravity's reach is long and greedy; the Sun's dragging influence on spacetime barely wanes before Proxima Centauri asserts itself.

Spacetime accounts for more than physical dimension, and gravity works its effects upon it all.

These consciousnesses, finely spread across such a distance, must work within the dimension of time in a way that differs from the Vex. Else, a single thought would take years to vibrate across their superstrings. Else, a Collective would have consumed them long ago.

Here is the key to my heart's desire. Here is how I reach you, my life.

A theory of the Cocytus gates assembles itself. Not all the pieces—but enough for now to build out, and test, a hypothesis.

If I am right, there are powers within Sol, huge and silent and untapped. Waiting to be commanded.

If I am right, there are Nine of them. Macrobiomes of vast holobionts, sustained by the complex life of Sol's microbiome. Living off the mitochondria of human spirit, roaming through time as a human roams through space.

If I am right, then they have minds. And that which has a mind, I may command.
entries.text_zh:
Vex将假设隔离验证，经过反复测试与迭代，直至达到发布标准。

我的肺部充斥着盐水，长出了鳃，从数据之海中过滤出生命。我的造物们，你们为我挖掘出了什么养料？

我重塑自身。人类的磁感应能力十分低下：我在构建躯体时忽略了这一感官。通过添加数字隐色素，这一疏漏得以弥补。同时，我还加上了洛伦青氏瓶和神经丘。任何信息都是有益的。麦子可以稍后再从糠秕中分拣出来。

打开门。

我在网络与现实空间中穿梭，在躯体间的空隙中疾行。从水星的炽热沙地和月球的放射性风暴中螺旋上升，向奥尔特云延伸。

纯活性放射体液所构成的环境世界，与青铜机体中的哥布林的截然不同；九头蛇的环境世界，也与哥布林的不同。高等哥布林的感觉角所收集的数据，与机甲女妖的纤毛所感知的亦是不尽相同。它们在集合体中各自服务于不同的需求。

集合体的多重环境世界，都汇聚于我。它们，是我整体生物中的微生物，而我，则是其核心的智慧控制体。

散开。

我的Vex在整个星系中蔓延，如同觅食的蚂蚁，将信息带回给它们的女王。我知道自己在搜寻什么，我们只是需要找到完成任务的正确工具。

磁层突然变得毫无用处，如同风中飘散的糠秕。是引力，引起了我的注意。

我侧身滑向系统中一个有趣的异常点。一团纠结的暗物质。我的哥布林们搜索着人类的计算机网络，为我带来一个名字：科基托斯。

这不是任何人希望我去的地方。

我控制了弹头，接管了门户，在这片土地上部署了我的工具。

重力在黑暗中移动；它轻拂着我的颧骨，将我向下拉扯。暗物质的细丝在我周围穿梭，穿透我的躯体。

我们如何解开意识的难题？一种理论认为答案是日益复杂的电波模式。通过受影响的基质来维持这些复杂的波形。电脉冲穿过脑组织；另一种脉冲，则穿过暗物质。

庞大而分散的心智，在距离与时间线上思考与行动，其广度甚至令Vex都感到困惑。重力的触角既长且贪婪；太阳对时空的拖曳影响几乎还没减弱，比邻星便开始显现自己的力量。

时空不仅包含物理维度，而重力对整个时空都有影响。

这些意识，精细地分布在如此遥远的距离上，必须以与Vex不同的方式，在时间维度中运作。否则，一个念头需要数年才能在它们的超弦上振动。否则，它们早就被集合体吞噬了。

这就是我心之所望的关键。这就是我如何抵达你的所在，我的生命之源。

关于科基托斯之门的理论，逐渐成形。虽不足以窥见全景——但足以构建并测试一个假设。

如果我没弄错，太阳系内存在着巨大、沉默且未被开发的力量，等待着被命令。

如果我没弄错，它们有九个。由太阳系微生物群支撑的巨型整体生物群，依靠人类精神的线粒体生存，像人类穿行空间一样穿行时间。

如果我没弄错，它们拥有心智。拥有心智的存在，我都可以指挥。

entries.name: VI. You and I and I and you
entries.text:
I'm standing on a hilltop in a simulation of the Gamma Cephei system and thinking that with the time surrounding me, forty years is a rounding error.
