拉奥：
你手下的灵能士兵在烧毁前，与我维持连接的最长纪录是四十五秒。那点时间连让我开始构建互通的理解都勉强。不把更多心智与我的相联，我就无法形成承受这份负担所需的痛苦汇集器。够了，你要么是在拖延，要么是真的无能。 

你把最强的灵能士兵藏在哪儿？你们执行的任何任务都没有这件事重要；我是我们共同的恩赐者传递力量的通道。那股力量是我通过卢梅转给你的。把你最出色的手下送来与我分担这份重负，否则我会让卢梅撤掉你的总合部，然后把你用作我的主汇集器。

entries.name: Entry 9: Direct Me
entries.text:
It's not working. None of it is working. I can't get them to listen. Lume's Psions are too stuck in their dreams and their delusionary concept of the individual, the self, THEMselves. Arrogant. Selfish. There is a greater movement at work, and they're too myopic to understand the beauty of being a part of it. They are improper tools for the work I intend to put them to; it seems that I will not be able to dismantle the Vanguard with them.

I need you to help me, VI. I need you to speak to me, to speak through me, so that they can see. I would cut off their eyelids to force them to see, but only if you guided my hand. Speak! I need you to speak! Let me be your conduit!

Is this what Guardians feel with the Traveler so still? Do they feel a similar agony when the Light animates them? I have never seen a Guardian in pain—could it be that the Light protects them from that pain, or does it withhold its greater power and deny them a fuller strength?

There is an old word for Guardians who turned from the path of Light. I have seen it in my texts on Darkness: "Dredgen." A word given to the exiled by the preening arrogants that expelled them. I think I should use this word. I should give it a new meaning.

I can't stop trembling, but only the parts of me that have not yet been changed. Only anticipation, an animal's apprehension at a transformational moment of pain. Those that have been made in the shape of his vision are all the better at channeling his power. The agony shaped me from meat to beauty. Gave me meaning beyond a decaying body.

This is the thing Lume's Psions are afraid of: the pain. Only pain. That's so small. A rat fears pain. A frog. Creatures, beasts—these Psions claimed to be the mightiest beings in Sol, but they wither when I share a moment of my agonies with them. Pathetic. They refuse to accept that pain is a pathway into meaning, not merely the spasmodic firing of anguished nerves. Of course transcendence would be excruciating! What did they expect? To meditate themselves into absolute power? To relax into freedom?

Please, VI, direct my hands. Direct my feet. Direct my search to those who would more willingly become my Dredgens. Find me those who can endure the agonies necessary to become open to your power. I am your vessel, but the more I channel your strength without you, the more my own wanes.
entries.text_zh:
不行，全都不行，我没法让他们听话。卢梅的灵能士兵被困于自己的梦中，困在那虚妄的所谓个体、自我、他们自身的概念里。傲慢，自私。有一项更伟大的活动在运行，而他们目光短浅，不懂身为其中一部分的美妙。他们不是我实现计划的合适工具；看来没法靠他们去瓦解先锋。

我需要你的帮助，VI。我需要你和我说话，通过我说话，这样他们才能看清楚。我要割下他们的眼睑逼他们看，但需要你来引导我的手。开口吧！我需要你开口！让我成为你的通道吧！

旅行者沉寂时，守护者就是这种感受吗？光能驱动他们时，他们会承受类似痛楚吗？我从未见到守护者受苦——难道是光能保护他们免于此痛？还是说光能有所保留，不赐予他们更完整的力量？

以前有个词，用于形容那些偏离光能道路的守护者。我在暗影文献中看见过：“德瑞捷”。那些自命不凡的傲慢者用它来称呼被流放者。我觉得我该用用这个词，赋予它新的含义。

我停不下颤抖，但只有那些尚未被改变的部分在抖。那只是预期，是动物在经历转化之痛前的惶惧。那些已被塑成他愿景之形的部分，能更好地传导他的力量。苦痛把我从血肉雕凿为美丽之物，给了我超越朽坏躯体的意义。

这正是卢梅的灵能士兵害怕的：疼痛，只是疼痛而已，何其渺小。老鼠怕痛。青蛙怕痛。生物，禽兽怕痛——这些自称是太阳系最强大存在的灵能士兵，在我与他们分享片刻我的痛楚时就枯萎了，可悲。他们拒绝承认疼痛是通往意义的途径，而不只是抽搐的神经在哀嚎。超越凡世必然撕心裂肺！他们还指望什么？靠冥想通达绝对的力量？靠放松获得自由？

我请求你，VI，引导我的手，引导我的脚，引导我去寻找那些更愿意成为我的德瑞捷的人。助我找到能承受必须之痛、从而接受你力量的那些人。我是你的容器，但我越是在没有你的情况下传导你的力量，我自身就越发衰弱。

entries.name: Entry 1: The Engine of History
entries.text:
There is a level of suffering that I am quite used to, and then there is working with Caiatl's bureaucracy.

Moving this battle rifle platform through Caiatl's latest round of trials has dampened my spirits. Competition against the other foundries typically lifts my spirits, but not this time. I find myself wishing something terrible would happen to me. Maybe I will be struck by a meteor, so I no longer must suffer the signatures they ask of me in duplicate, triplicate, etc., etc. 

The Cabal marched into empire not just because of their legions, but also thanks to their armies of quartermasters, logisticians, factory-masters, armorers, and so on; their soldiers brought the stars to heel, yes, but only because of that greater force that kept them fed, fueled, and stocked with ordinance. One would think the soldiers of the Cabal to be arrogant, but in this twilight age of their state, I've found that the haughtiest and most entitled of the Cabal are the bureaucrats!

They stand in the way of progress, clutching their columns, tables, and limits like a border guard and his rifle. When I want to give soldiers what they ask for, some quartermaster lumbers over to tell me that I must not, for it would be too expensive. Small! Small minds who don't dream, but think in terms of cost, capital, and limits. Discard your limits, factory-masters and accountants. Follow your heart!

Father, when I can get him to emerge from his tinkerer's shed, only mutters about how we must cling to Tex Mechanica's "brand" of old-world class and style. Father's a sentimental dope, and I'm sick of having to wait for his nod of approval.  In the old world, people killed each other with less. They threw rocks. They fought with sticks. It's time for us to make something new. Until I run Tex Mechanica, I will push the firm into the future, despite him. I will follow the voices of soldiers and those who dare. That is how one keeps reverence for what came before, by responding to the will of the masses, who compose the very institutions these moribund leaders claim to represent!

Father eventually will understand. He must. Until then, I find camaraderie in the field. Bracus Lume, my liaison and the commander of the test unit that fields my weapon, understands and agrees. We have spent long hours together discussing many things. He serves as a muse to me: a rogue in uniform. He respects Caiatl, as a soldier must submit to their commander, but through his words, I can pick out the shape of his true intentions. He paints inspiring images of the Cabal before Calus, when they—as Lume so poetically put it—"made an empire in tribute to the sun." Brave Bracus Lume has dreams, like me. Dreams of liberation, of rousing history and leading it forward. Torobatl, their empire—I am moved by his vision, how similar it is to my own.

What weapon would we need to build to realize the aspirations of dreamers like Lume? That is what I ask of my designers and engineers. Imagine a weapon to be carried into the breach and beyond. A tool as mighty as the ones who wield it. Make Lume a weapon that he is proud to carry and let me be the vessel through which it is delivered. Of course, there is marketing in this thought but I don't think of my ask as something that base. We make weapons, not sugary drinks. We give power a body, milling it from inert metal into an implement that shakes the columns of reality itself. The bark of our beasts makes kings and tyrants just as mortal as the lowest of us. I want "Tex Mechanica" stamped on the side of the liberator's gun. I want us to be the engine of history. So, we begin with Lume.  

I will continue to tilt at those bureaucratic windmills, but I think now, at least, I do it with a steadfast squire as company. Together, we'll score a victory over that class of manicured, deskbound elites. They might think they can control the world with the stroke of a pen, a perfected spreadsheet, or the tweak of an allowance, but we'll show them that people with dreams should be the ones to make decisions. People united, individuals of supreme motivation, who wrest the tiller of history away from those who would prefer to crouch on their piles of Glimmer instead. 
It is time for dreamers to lead in a direction of their choosing.
entries.text_zh:
苦难我早已习以为常，但我无法忍受跟查厄托的官僚体系打交道。

把这套战斗步枪平台通过查厄托最新一轮的试行流程，让我心气大减。与其他铸造厂的竞逐通常能让我精神大振，但这次没有。我甚至盼着能有什么可怕的事发生在我身上。也许一颗陨石砸下来，我就不用再忍受他们要我签一式两份、一式三份乃至更多的文件了。 

卡巴尔得以成立帝国，不仅靠他们的军团，也要归功于他们成群的军需官、后勤官、工厂主、护甲商，等等；他们的士兵确实让群星屈膝，但只因那更庞大的力量让他们衣食饱、燃料足、军火丰。若说卡巴尔的士兵骄矜自大，在他们国势衰暮的当下，我反倒发现最骄纵、最自以为是的卡巴尔，是那些官僚！

他们站在进步前，死抱着他们的栏、表、限额，就像边防哨兵攥着步枪。当我想给士兵们他们所求的东西时，总有某个军需官摇摇晃晃地走过来说不行，因为太贵了。狭隘！思维狭隘，没有梦想的家伙，只会用成本、资本、限额来想问题。别总想着限额了，工厂主们、会计们。随心所愿吧！

父亲，只要我能把他从修补棚里拽出来，就会嘟囔我们必须守住特克斯机械那拥有旧世界的格调与风范的“品牌”。父亲多愁善感得傻气，而我厌倦了非要等他点头许可。在旧世界，人们为了一点小事就彼此杀戮。他们扔石头，挥舞木棒彼此争斗。我们该造点新东西了。在我接掌特克斯机械之前，我会不顾他的阻挠，把公司推向未来。我会倾听士兵与敢为之人的声音。对既往致敬的方式，就是回应大众的意志，那些组成了这些行将就木的领袖们声称自己所代表之机构的人们的意志！

父亲最终会明白的，他必须明白。而在那之前，我会在前线寻找同道。十夫长卢梅，我的联络人，试用我武器的部队的指挥官，理解并赞同我。我们畅谈了很多事情。他是我的缪斯：一个身着军装的浪子。他尊敬查厄托，正如士兵必须服从统帅，但从他的话里，我能辨识他真正意图的轮廓。卢梅描绘的卡巴尔——卡鲁斯之前的卡巴尔——以他那近乎诗意的话来说是“为致敬太阳而建立的帝国”。勇敢的十夫长卢梅也有梦想，如我一般的解放之梦，唤醒历史并引领其前行之梦。图罗巴特尔，他们的帝国——他的愿景打动了我，而我的愿景与之何其相似。

为了实现像卢梅这样的逐梦者的抱负，我们需要打造怎样的武器？这正是我对设计师和工程师提出的问题。设想一柄可被携入裂口的武器，与使用者一样强大的工具。为卢梅打造一件他引以为傲的武器，让我成为将其带入世间的容器。诚然，这里面也有市场的考量，但我并不把这诉求视为那样低俗的东西。我们造的是武器，不是饮料。我们为力量铸造一个躯体，把它从惰性的金属铣成足以撼动现实支柱的器具。我们野兽的吠声让王和暴君成为肉体凡躯，与我们中的最卑微者一般无二。我想在解放者之枪的侧面刻上“特克斯机械”，我想让我们成为历史的引擎。所以，我们从卢梅开始。  

我会继续向那些官僚的风车发起冲锋，但如今，我想至少我有了一位忠诚的扈从与我作伴。我们将齐心协力，面对那群修饰得体、困守案牍的精英阶层，拿下一场胜利。他们或许以为能凭笔尖的划动、一份完美的表格，或是额度调整来掌控世界，但我们会让他们见识到，负责做出决定的，应该是有梦之人，团结之人，受到至高驱动之人，从蹲在自己的微光堆上不肯起身的败类手中夺回历史舵柄之人。 
是时候让逐梦者朝他们选择的方向掌舵了。

entries.name: Entry 2: What Mother
entries.text:
I've known Mother to be dead for longer than I knew her alive. I remember small moments: Falling asleep on her shoulder as she carried me home at night after a holiday party. Teaching me to swim. Singing as she washed dishes. I remember feeling safe with her. Even when Father shouted, her voice would silence him. Protecting me. Memories that comforted me.
Until I saw her.

The market at Bonnet Plaza, in the West District. I was getting lunch outside the Mechanica home office. Caiatl's logisticians, Father's lickspittles, hiccups at Factories Three and Four—a miserable day.

I had interred her. She was ash. But in this moment, I saw my mother moving through the crowd with her Ghost flitting around her head. She had been dead for three years at this point. Somehow, the Light had found her. It seems all it needed was ash.

Two others chosen by the Light marched at her side, bristling with weapons, leashed to their puppeteers. The Chosen, on some holy business to save humanity. She glowed, flush with heat, as if the fire that cremated her now animated her from within. I cried out in horror, unable to stop myself. It made sense: of course the Traveler would grant my beloved mother the gift every child in the Last City    dreams of, every dying elder longs for, as they move away from the main of life. Eternal life without fear.

But when I embraced her, crying her name at the center of a cheering crowd, what did my mother do?

She shoved me away.

I felt the searing push of Solar energy in her strength. A sizzling reminder on my chest as I stumbled back and fell. Not a twinkle of recognition in her eyes, just discomfort, the look one gives a clamoring beggar that gets too close. Cold She was cold; she was hideous, a doppelganger, homunculus. Her chirping idiot of a Ghost commanded me to clear the way, and off they went. Bystanders helped me to my feet. Strangers, kinder than my own mother.

Is this the truth of the Light? Is this what it does? Animate the dead and possess them with Ghosts, puppeteers who keep them hooked to life like a fish on a lure? To prey on desperation and transfix the City in this poisoned dream? What miracle makes a mother spit on her child? My memories of her are now curses. Leaden dead weight. Every single one a searing ember.
entries.text_zh:
记忆中母亲去世后的时间，比我与她相处的时间更长。我记得些细碎的瞬间：节日派对后，她把我抱回家，我在她肩头睡着；她教我游泳；她一边洗碗一边唱歌。我记得与她在一起时的安全感。就算父亲吼起来，她的声音也能让他闭嘴。保护着我。这些回忆曾给予我安慰。
直到我看见了她。

那是在博内特广场的集市，西区的那个。我正在特克斯机械总部外吃午饭。查厄托的后勤官、巴结父亲的谄媚者、三号四号工厂的故障——糟糕透顶的一天。

我亲手安葬过她，她化成了灰。但就在这一刻，我看见我的母亲穿过人群，她的机灵在她的头顶盘旋。那时她已经死了三年。光能不知怎的找到了她。看来，只要有灰烬，就能铸造负光者。

还有另外两名被光能选中的人紧随其侧，全副武装，被他们的傀儡师牵着。他们是神选者，肩负着某种拯救人类的神圣使命。她在发光，热气腾腾，仿佛当初火葬时的火焰如今自内而外地驱动着她。我不由自主地惊叫起来。那合乎情理：旅行者当然会将每个圣城孩子梦寐以求、每个垂死老人望眼欲穿的礼物——无惧的永生——赐予我挚爱的母亲。

但当我上前拥抱她，在欢呼的人群中央呼喊她的名字时，我的母亲做了什么呢？

她把我推开了。

我在她的力道里感到了烈日能量的灼烧。胸口被烫得生疼，我踉跄着后退倒下。她眼中没有一丝辨识，只有不适，是人们对靠得太近的叫嚷乞丐会有的那种眼神。冷，她好冷漠；她如此丑陋，是冒牌货，造物。她那只叽叽喳喳的蠢机灵命令我让开，然后他们扬长而去。旁观者把我扶起。那些陌生人，比我自己的母亲还要友好。

这就是光能的真相吗？这就是它所做的？让死人站起来，让他们被机灵附体、操纵，像上了钩的鱼一样被拖拽着活下去？以绝望为食，将圣城困在这场有毒的梦中？什么样的奇迹，会让母亲唾弃自己的孩子？我对她的记忆如今成了诅咒，铅一样沉重，每一段都是灼心的余烬。

entries.name: Entry 3: A Hierarchy of Pain
entries.text:
My dear friend Bracus Lume has been deployed, likely to some miserable theater in Sol as part of Caiatl's efforts to stymie the Hive. If my father had any passion left, I would believe Lume's deployment to be part of a plot to stop me. A favor asked for and granted. A reminder that my efforts, clients, accounts, and so on, are given to me by him. The generosity of an overbearing father: my life, from his largesse.

However, my allies within Tex Mechanica have not been able to source any missives, directives, or dictates from Father's office to stop my project. He spends his time tinkering on museum pieces and Vanguard baubles. I wonder if he even knows the world exists beyond his workbench; his cruelty is bottomless. He is a clever coward, and this retreat from the world is a favorite tactic of his.

I think he wishes for me to rot in the family estate and be quiet again. I was a quiet child and he, a colossus. I would shroud myself and slip through the cold halls of our home, fleeing the muffled sounds of his rage—a phantom by choice, to protect myself. When mother grew ill and died, my father fell silent, listless. This was his first retreat. Father ignored me so profoundly that I truly believed myself to be invisible. It made me think that I had died with my mother. That was even more terrifying than his rage; I was losing my father as well.

But now, I am older and braver. Father may or may not have clipped my wings. I don't care. I will take care of myself. I am used to being alone. But I also have been exploring other ways of being, even those prohibited by the Vanguard. 

There are fascinating texts in this world. Volumes and folios that speak of clarity in purpose and the methods to attain it. I have tried many—meditation, religion, self-actualization—but they all failed, save for one: an old text of assured providence, an exegesis on the sermons of Twin Bird, of the Binary Star. Agony and pain exist, Twin Bird once said, but not all pain is meaningless. Some pain hones. It hammers bladed agony into shape, and an edge is made. Utility formed as a survival mechanism, making the afflicted sharper. 

So I began to run. Thousands of steps, each a moment of pain. Each a nail, pinning me to the present. The pain worked. The pain guided me. The pain led me to power. The Vanguard and Twin Bird both called it Darkness. I call it a new path. 

The Light comes for you in death, and only if it chooses. But Darkness is always there, within, waiting for you to grasp it and pull it to the surface. And so I had a revelation: I needed to attempt communion. I planned routes to run that took me deeper into the City. Down among the people, in their parks, in their streets, full of sound and life and beings—others who did not fear life but made it, composed its raw cacophony, all a part of a pattern so vast, I could not perceive it. But I was, too, one of its parts; the petri dish is a pandemonic universe to the single cell, but utterly still to the human eye.

I think the Light is selfish. To see the state of the Last City below the Vanguard's Olympian refuge is to understand this. The Light sends out its little Ghosts and elevates only the dead whom it deems worthy, never touching the desperate living. It pulls them up to the graceful decks of the Tower, damning the rest to live without its gift. This story is common among the citizens of the Last City. I should know: It happened to me, too.

My mother died and was returned and abandoned me. My father consigned me to the annals of his memory and moved on as if I, too, were already dead. But in the City, the people welcomed me. The dockworkers, the vagrants, the shopkeepers, everyone hurrying on every errand, all denied the Light's gift, but were subject to its rule. I disappeared among them, but I was not consciously forgotten by them. I was not spurned by them. At any moment on one of my excursions, I could stop and talk to someone, to have a moment of connection, to see them as well. I moved among them as one of them, an equal in dreams and aspiration, seen and heard. 
  
The Traveler has the power to shape reality, and yet there are beggars in the low districts of the Last City. There are children that go hungry. The streets are policed. From where do violence and crimes of desperation spring? The individual rendered miserable before their birth, or the great systems above them that maintain the status quo? My own wealth—though it can be stripped from me—is not a shield. It is not a weapon. It is fiat. Exchange, only as long as I play within the bounds of the Light's rules. 

There is a pattern to who the Light picks. I think it chooses based on how jagged the hierarchy of pain will become when it intervenes. I think the Light wants to hurt me. But the Darkness wants me to do something with that pain.
entries.text_zh:
我的好友十夫长卢梅已被派往前线，大概是作为查厄托遏制邪魔族行动的一部分，被丢到了太阳系某个悲惨的战区。如果我的父亲还剩半点热情，我会以为卢梅被调派是为了阻止我——他求来的一份人情，用来提醒我，我的努力、客户、账户等等，都是他给的。专横父亲的慷慨：我的一生，皆出自他的施舍。

然而，我在特克斯机械的盟友没从父亲的办公室里找到任何意在阻止我计划的公函、指示或法令。他把时间都花在摆弄博物馆藏品和先锋的玩意上。我不知道他是否还能感知到工作台之外世界的存在；他的残酷无穷无尽。他是个聪明的懦夫，这种避世之举正是他的拿手好戏。

我觉得他希望我在祖宅里腐烂，再次变得安静。我小时候很安静，而他像座巨像。我会隐蔽起来，穿行在家中阴冷的长廊间，逃离他闷声的怒火——主动选择做个幽灵以保护自己。母亲生病去世后，父亲变得沉默、无精打采，而这里是他的第一个避世所。父亲对我置若罔闻，几乎让我真心以为自己是隐形的，仿佛我和母亲一起死了。那比他的怒火更可怕；我连父亲也失去了。

但现在，我长大了，也更勇敢了。父亲或许剪断了我的翅膀，或许没有，我不在乎。我会照顾我自己。我已习惯了独处。但我也在探索其他存在的可能性，甚至还包括那些被先锋所禁止的。 

这世上有许多迷人的文本。卷帙与册页，论述着明确的目标与达成的方法。我尝试过许多——冥想、宗教、自我实现——但它们都失败了，唯一的例外是一篇许诺天命的古文，阐释了来自双生之星的双鸟的布道。双鸟曾说，苦难与疼痛确实存在，但并非所有痛苦都毫无意义。有些痛苦是磨砺，它把刀锋般的痛苦锤打成形，铸成利刃。功用作为求生机制而生，让受难者更锋利。 

于是我开始奔跑。成千上万的步伐，每一步都是片刻的疼痛。每一步都是一根钉，将我钉在当下。疼痛生效了，引导着我，带我获取力量。先锋与双鸟都称其为暗影，我称之为一条新的道路。 

光能在你死去时才来，还得被它选中。但暗影始终存在于内里，静待你去抓住它，将它拽向表层。于是我顿悟：我需要去尝试交流。我规划了带我前往圣城更深处的奔跑路线，深入群体之中，在他们的公园、街道之中，充满声响、生命和存在——那些不惧生活而是去创造它的人们，谱写出其原始的嘈杂，一切都属于某个宏大的图样，宏大到我无法感知。但我也是其中一部分；对单个细胞而言，培养皿便是喧闹的宇宙，它在人的眼中却静止不动。

我觉得光能是自私的。只要看看先锋的奥林匹斯式高阁下方，圣城的境况，就能明白这一点。光能派出它的小小机灵，只将它认为值得的死者唤起，从不接触那些迫切需要帮助的生者。它把他们拉到高塔那雅致的台面上，拒绝给予其他人恩赐。这种故事在圣城的市民中很常见，我最清楚不过：因为这也发生在了我身上。

我的母亲死而复返，抛下了我。我的父亲把我投进他记忆的年表，继续前行，仿佛我也已经死了。但在圣城里，人们欢迎我。码头工人、流浪者、店主，每个奔忙的人，全都被光能的恩赐所拒绝，却又受其统治。我隐匿其中，但他们并未有意识地遗忘我，没有排斥我。任何一次外出，我都可以停下，与人交谈、获得一刻联系，也看见他们。我行走在他们之间，是他们中的一员，在梦想与愿望上与他们平等，被看见、被听到。 
  
旅行者有塑造现实的力量，可圣城的贫民区依然有乞丐，依然有挨饿的孩子，街道上有警卫巡视。暴力与因绝望而生的罪行从何而来？是个体在出生之前就注定凄惨身世，还是高悬其上的巨大体系维持了既有秩序？我自身的财富——即便可以被剥夺——并非护盾，亦非武器，只是法币。只有我在光能的规则边界内行事，它才具备交换价值。 

光能的选择自有其模式。我认为它的偏好取决于干预后，痛苦层级的剧烈程度。我认为光能想要伤害我，而暗影想要我用那份痛苦做点什么。

entries.name: Entry 4: Paper Histories
entries.text:
Tex Mechanica is a huge, old foundry. At its height, the Mechanica had multiple proving grounds, distribution centers, autofabricators, and other facilities across Sol. We even used to build ships! Though we were never good at it. That was centuries ago, when the tide was high, before the Vanguard determined that contraction and consolidation to the Last City was the prudent move. Squash the frontier, they said. Focus on one stronghold and its satellites.

Father, though he is fantastically wealthy and powerful, is a king at the end of a dynasty. He's the sucker left holding the bag as the house lights come on. What is Tex Mechanica in the age of the Last City? A sporting goods supplier. A widget factory for the Guardians of the Vanguard. A toolmaker for a junta, always building larger and deadlier weapons to face an enemy that is always approaching, never arriving. What do they face next? An arms dealer loves that question because it has no answer—only fear.

I leave my father to figure it out without me. To play weapons-master to undead tyrants. I have a new faith now. A new way forward. The pursuit of freedom and understanding hidden by the Vanguard—this is my task that I take up without guilt and with clear eyes. I am willing to pay any cost; I think of my dear friend Bracus Lume, who has returned from the Hive front terribly wounded by one of their most vicious paracausal weapons. He convalesces in orbit (Father denied him the use of our personal medical suite on campus here) but still insists on fighting to live for a tomorrow he so furiously believes in. I should do the same.

Together, Lume and I make a mighty intellectual and spiritual pair. He, the soldier, and me, the dreamer. Our correspondence sharpens our desire and renders in actual fact the targets of our heady dreams. Father, the Vanguard, and the Guardians are too removed from the people of The City that they might as well oppose their liberation! The current order restrains their growth, restricts them to huddling behind high walls, fearing nightmares beyond them. This ruling elite demands we cow to their dictates and proscribes any group or individual that speaks against them. Caiatl and her Cabal are much the same to Lume and his soldiers, he assures me. Her father twisted what it meant to be Cabal, and though she deposed him, she has not fixed what he broke.

Forces, ideologies, and thoughts opposed to these twin malignancies are deemed evil, dark, and wrong by the institutions they threaten. I ask—what is evil about opposing tyranny? Neither the Vanguard nor Caiatl will abdicate without a fight; liberating the City will take a mass movement, which I don't yet have. However, a small cell that is committed to the cause, acting at the right time and in the most critical places? A bullet is ignited by a firing pin; great movements need a catalyst. The people of The City cry out for one.

I could be the one who brings about the first wave of change. Should I not grasp any weapon, tool, or thought afforded to me to oppose a foe that separates mothers from their children? I have availed myself of the deep records Tex Mechanica keeps hidden in its off-book archives. Paper histories. Nothing that can be searched unless one is physically present. Our guns once barked as vicious dogs across the ruins of fallen Earth. Once, we made tools for seekers on the frontier who used our weapons to carve new paths into the future. According to my research, these weapons became more than their first form.

I, the shunned heir of Tex Mechanica, have scrubbed my name and history from our archives. I go out into the darkness away from home, as our weapons before have. I will find a new name. I will sound out across the frontier and then come home to address the world the Light has built.
entries.text_zh:
特克斯机械是一家巨大而古老的铸造厂。全盛时，公司在太阳系各处都有试炼场、配送中心、自动制造机和其他设施。我们甚至还造过飞船！虽然我们从不擅长。那是几个世纪前，涨潮之时，在先锋认定收缩并整合到圣城才是谨慎之举前。他们说要收紧边界，专注于一个据点然后辐射出去。

父亲虽富可敌国、权势滔天，却是末代君王。灯亮人散后，手里还攥着烂摊子的冤大头。在圣城纪元，特克斯机械算什么？不过是家体育用品供应商，为先锋的守护者提供小器件的工厂，为一个军事体打磨工具的工匠，不断制造更庞大、更致命的武器来对付一个永远逼近、却从未抵达的敌人。他们接下来要对付什么？军火商最爱这个问题，因为它没有答案——只有恐惧。

我把这个问题留给父亲，让他独自去琢磨，去当不死暴君的武器大师。我如今有了新的信仰，新的前行道路。追求被先锋藏起来的自由与理解——这是我无愧承担且有清晰远见的任务。我愿付出任何代价；我想到了我的好友十夫长卢梅，他从邪魔族前线归来，被敌人最凶残的超因果武器重创。他正在轨道上疗养（父亲拒绝让他使用我们在园区内的私人医疗套间），但仍坚持为狂热相信的明天而活下去。我也该如此。

我和卢梅是强有力的思想与精神搭档，他是战士，而我是梦想家。互相通信磨砺我们的渴望，将我们那些激昂梦想之中的目标化为现实。父亲、先锋和守护者远远脱离圣城的民众，可以说是在阻挠人民的解放！当前的秩序束缚了他们的成长，把他们限制在高墙之后，惧怕墙外的梦魇。统治精英要求我们向其法令低头，并将任何反对他们的群体和个人列为禁忌。查厄托与她的卡巴尔，对待卢梅和他的士兵们也差不多是如此，这也是他亲口告诉我的。查厄托的父亲扭曲了卡巴尔的精神，尽管她推翻了他，却没修复他造成的破坏。

与这两个毒瘤对立的力量、意识形态与思想，被它们所威胁的机构打成邪恶、黑暗与错误。我要问——反抗暴政哪点邪恶了？无论是先锋还是查厄托都不会不战而退；要解放圣城会需要一场群众运动，但我尚未推动成形。然而，一个小而坚定的组织，在正确的时机、最关键的地点发动行动呢？子弹由击针点燃；伟大的运动需要催化剂。圣城的人民迫切需要着这样的激发。

我或许能成为掀起第一波变革的人。我难道不该抓住任何可得的武器、工具或思想，去对抗那个让母亲与孩子分离的敌人吗？我研读了特克斯机械机密档案中隐藏的深层记录。那些纸质的历史。除非亲临其处，否则无法检索。曾几何时，我们的枪声如恶犬在陨落的地球废墟中狂吠；曾几何时，我们为边界的探索者打造工具，他们用我们的武器在未来中凿出新路。据我研究，这些武器超越了它们的初始形态。

我这个被特克斯机械所疏斥的继承人，已将自己的名字与经历从我们的档案中抹去。我离开家，投向黑暗，循着我们的武器曾经走过的路。我会寻找一个新名字，让它响彻边界，然后回到家乡，直面那个光能构筑的世界。

entries.name: Entry 5: A Conduit for All Futures
entries.text:
Lume calls his people "Barant": a name once used by and for his kind. One, he says, they are still owed as children of Torobatl. "Cabal" is a name without weight; it is the label, Lume says, of decrepit imperial bureaucrats. A dry moniker.

Lume's Barant are raucous in their new identity. They worship their distant home star, the heroes who once fought in her name, and the dream that they might pile banners of the conquered upon her plazas once more. They strip themselves bare and howl their praise to Torobatl, calling her warrior and queen, boasting so that she might hear and smile upon them. They trample the ground into a migratory temple, ennobling it with the impressions of their feet. They make orbits of worship around their old idols, mighty challenge columns, as their ancestors did on her plains. Though born on an alien world, Lume's Barant are fierce patriots for a homeland they have never once beheld. This fervor inspires me, this clear dream, this grand project.

Lume has given me a gift: an awareness of this type of power. The Vanguard and the Light have their silent deity in the Traveler, but their celebrations are muted. They do not bid the people to exult in their power because they do not want people to realize their power. They want only the Guardians to be powerful, only the Vanguard to be mighty. I want all humanity to be strong. I want us to celebrate alongside the Barant as they do, but with our own undeniable strength.

My teachers—my brother Lume, my long-dead master Twin Bird—both speak of the same thing, which I have now found for myself. Years ago, I exercised my body through rituals of agony. As I write, it appears this new power will do likewise for me. My vision will be made clear, and with that clarity, I will actualize. I will become greater than the gifted.

I had found a place of power on Europa. A trove of artifacts tainted with Darkness. Rumors of real power, hidden deep within a forgotten Praxic temple. I took a maniple of Lume's most fearsome volunteers into that place, losing many to the elements before we even reached its entrance. It was sweltering inside, the air so thick with damp dust that we were burning our filters at thrice the baseline. Lume's warriors chanted liturgical cadences to fill the halls with celebration from the deep organs, but that dead place swallowed all sounds they made. They thought it was a trick of acoustics or some other paracausal phenomenon, and so they armed themselves accordingly. But the closer we approached the heart of the temple, the more I grew assured of the futility of conventional weapons.

I began to hear a voice. A whisper. Not one of us or Lume, who was watching from his convalescing bed aboard our ship. A new voice, just for me.

In the heart of the temple was a great sepulcher that contained a fantastic, glittering crystal. From my studies, I knew it to be a crystal of Stasis, a paracausal manifestation of Darkness, that power to which I had spent years attuning my body and mind. I touched it, and invited power in.

A voice. His voice. Lume still swears it was a devil of unknown power who spoke to me, but I know the truth. Unseen, a voice leaped between his soldiers, possessing them to speak one word at a time. A message born from howling pain that found its final home in me. The agony was unrelenting, the pain immense, but I had prepared for this moment for years. I did not ignite. My soul did not burn out. The devil's voice became my voice, and the devil became me, and I understood: This was not a devil. This was not the Light. It was not even the Darkness. This was a third power. A new thing. My own path.

TO SATURN, the voice and I cried. TO THE RINGS, MY WEAPON.

VI. This was the name of the great one, the third power. VI held my hand and showed me Lume wounded and Lume mighty, myself wounded and myself mighty. VI. This was the power's name. Tombs and temples. We entered a tomb and made it a temple with our cries, as the Barant once stamped migration prayers into Torobatl's dirt, as I once ran through the halls of my family manor fearing and yearning.

In the quiet after, I was alone. Lume bellowed in my aurals, screaming at me in fury for the death of his brethren. He swore to kill me when I returned, but I knew he would not, so I told him, and I began to laugh and made him another promise: I would heal his wound, erase the Hive magic that rotted him from the inside out.

I am happy. I was chosen. I had been right. I was the vessel; my actions—perhaps from even before my birth, but certainly from the moment I became conscious—were guided by these hands that now rested on my shoulders. My explorations of Darkness, my readings and agonies, were indeed the method by which I would attain a power that could be shared among the masses, a counterweight to the Light—but it would have to begin with me. It could only begin with me.

I am, was, and will be the conduit through which all futures flow.
entries.text_zh:
卢梅把他的人称为“巴兰特”：这是曾经被他们用来称呼自己的名号。他说，作为图罗巴特尔的子嗣，他们理当继承这个称号。“卡巴尔”这个名字毫无分量；卢梅说，它只是衰朽帝国官僚的标签，一个干巴巴的称谓。

卢梅的巴兰特因他们获得的新身份而喧腾不已。他们崇拜遥远的故乡恒星，曾以她之名战斗的英雄，那重新在她的广场上堆叠征服旗帜的梦想。他们褪去衣物，对图罗巴特尔嘶吼赞歌，称她为战士和女王，夸耀以盼她听见并对他们展颜。他们将脚下大地践踏成一座迁徙的神殿，以足迹赋予其尊荣。他们围绕古老的崇拜象征——高耸的挑战之柱——虔诚而行，正如其祖先曾在她的平原上所为。虽生于异乡星球，卢梅的巴兰特却热爱着一片从未亲眼目睹的家园。这股狂热，这份清晰之梦，这项宏伟计划，鼓舞着我。

卢梅赠与了我一件礼物：对这种力量的感知。先锋与光能有他们无言的神——旅行者，但他们的庆典寡淡无声。他们不召唤众人共襄盛大的力量，因为他们不愿让人意识到自身的力量。他们只想守护者强大，只想先锋显赫。我想要全人类都强盛，与巴兰特一道庆贺，但要凭我们自身无可置疑的力量。

我的老师们——我的兄弟卢梅，我早已逝去的导师双鸟——都曾提到同一件事，一件我如今也意识到的事。多年前，我以苦痛的仪式锻炼躯体。如今书写之时，我看出这股新的力量将以同样方式起作用。我的愿景将澄明，随之我将得以践行。我将超越那些受到馈赠的人。

我在木卫二找到一处力量的源泉，一批受暗影玷染的神器。传言在一座被遗忘的英勇圣殿深处，藏有真正的力量。我带了一支由卢梅最骁勇的手下自发组成的队伍进入那处所在，尚未到达入口，已折损多人。殿内闷热，空气潮尘稠密，滤芯消耗达基线的三倍。卢梅的战士以宗教圣咏标定步伐，用胸腔深处的声音为长廊注入欢赞，但那死寂之所吞没了他们的一切声响。他们以为这是声学诡计，或是某种超因果现象，于是依此武装自己。但我们越接近圣殿中心，我就越是确信常规武器终将徒劳。

我开始听见一个声音，某种耳语。那既非同行之人，也非正卧于我们舰上病床远程观望的卢梅。是一个新的声音，只有我能听见。

在圣殿中心有一座巨大的石棺，内藏一块奇妙而璀璨的晶体。依我的研究，那是冰影水晶——暗影的超因果显化——是我多年调律身心所追寻的力量。我触碰它，邀力量入体。

一个声音，他的声音。卢梅仍坚称是某个来历不明的魔鬼与我言语，但我知道真相。那看不见的存在，在他的士兵间跳跃，附身于他们，让他们一次只吐出一个字。一个由嚎叫之痛所生的信息，最终在我身上找到了归宿。痛楚毫不松懈，苦难浩大，但我为此刻已准备多年。我没有燃烧起来，我的灵魂没有焚竭。魔鬼的声音成了我的声音，魔鬼成了我，而我随之明白：这不是魔鬼，不是光能，甚至也不是暗影。这是第三种力量，一种新的事物，我自己的道路。

去土星，那个声音与我同呼，去环带，我的武器。

VI，这是那伟大存在、那第三种力量的名字。VI挽住我的手，令我见到负伤的卢梅与强盛的卢梅，负伤的我与强盛的我。VI，这是这股力量的名字。坟与殿，我们踏入坟墓，以呼号将其化作神殿，正如巴兰特昔日将迁徙祷文踏印进图罗巴特尔的泥土，正如我曾在家族宅邸的走廊中奔逃、恐惧和渴望。

寂静落下之后，我孑然一身。我听见卢梅在怒吼，为他同袍之死而对我咆哮。他发誓要在我归去时杀了我，但我知道他不会，于是我如此告知他，而后大笑，又许下一个诺言：我会治愈他的伤，抹去让他自内而外腐烂的邪魔族魔法。

我很快乐，我被选中了，我一开始就是对的。我是容器；我的一切行为——或许自我出生前，至少自我有意识之刻起——皆由如今按在我肩上的手所引导。我对暗影的探索、我的阅读与苦修，确实是获得可在众人间分享之力量的方法，是对抵光能的砝码——但它必须由我开始，也只能由我开始。

我之于所有未来，现在是、曾经是、将来亦是通道。

entries.name: Entry 6: Nine Thoughts out of Time
entries.name_zh: 记录6：时间之外的九个念想
entries.text:
• I can kill Ghosts faster than new Guardians can be raised.

• "There is a world beyond this one."

• The walls that keep us in are feeble. One more push. Take a hammer out and whack away the keystone.

• I have a sword now. Like the dead Ghosts, I took it from the heart of the enemy   and made it to be dim and still and without Light. That makes my sword cut better.  I've killed Guardians. I've killed a couple, and they didn't think I could, but what do they think now? Nothing. They're dead, and I have their Ghosts slapping against my thigh. Kiss my ass.

• I want to go back to the City. I don't want to hurt anymore. I want to be with everyone and have them pick me up. I miss the feeling of hands on me. Among the people, I was never a phantom; I was a moment waiting to be met. The masses were my first love, how much potential a crowd holds, how many dreams.

• Time is a thought that goes backward and forward; that's how VI shares it with me. He promises me things that haven't happened yet and says they have. If they're done, why does he make me wait?

• I wanted to be a Guardian as a kid, and now, I would slap myself for wanting that. I'm more. I'm many things more. Cadmium, lead, metallic hydrogen, platinum. I'm elements you've never seen larger than a milligram. I am more than what I was. Agony and grace.

• To be a Dredgen is to endure this and more. Give me more. I'm not done yet.

• Mother, talk to me. I need to know. VI, if you can hear me, if you are there, I beg you—show her to me again.
entries.text_zh:
• 我杀死机灵的速度，快过新守护者被唤起的速度。

• “在此世之外，别有一界。”

• 禁锢我们的墙壁脆弱不堪。再推一下。取一把锤子，猛砸那枚拱顶石。

• 我有一把刀剑。像那些死去的机灵，我从敌方的核心夺过它，令其昏黯、寂静、无光。那让我的刀剑更加锋利。我杀过守护者，杀过好几个。他们没想到我能做到，可如今他们又作何感想？什么感想也没有。他们死了，而他们的机灵则被我系在腰间，晃来荡去。

• 我想回到圣城。我不想再疼痛难忍。我想与众人待在一起，让他们把我托起。我想念手落在身上的感觉。置身人群，我从不是幽魅；我是一段即将相逢的时刻。大众是我最初的爱恋，群体中蕴藏着多么巨大的潜能，多少梦想。

• 时间是一种向前亦向后的思想；VI与我分享了它。他向我许诺尚未发生之事，说它们已经发生。如果真是这样，那他为什么还要让我等待？

• 小时候我想成为守护者，如今，我会给那个自己一记耳光，以惩戒那个渴望。我如今已超越守护者，远远超越。是镉、铅、金属氢、铂，我是你从未见到超过毫克量级的元素。我已今非昔比，承受着苦难与恩宠。

• 要成为德瑞捷，就是要忍受这一切，甚至更多。给我更多，我还能行。

• 母亲，和我说话，我需要知道。VI，若你能听见，若你还在，我求你——再让我见她一次。

entries.name: Project Proposal, 1961
entries.text:
PROPOSAL DZ-KJIK19RSNP 

…As the Department sets its sights on distant frontiers, we must contend with the problem of survival at extremes. Our colleagues at NASA have seen great success on Project Apollo, but if we are to travel even further afield, we will face conditions even more inimical to human life.

Whether future explorers seek to dive into boiling sulfuric acid or attempt to stretch across higher dimensions, we must equip them for scientific inquiry, communication with native entities—and, above all, their mission to return safely home. 

Dr. Victor Falkner 

IN RE: PROPOSAL DZ-KJIK19RSNP 

Dr. Falkner, ever since I saw you present your work on the Nereida ADS, I knew you were just the sort of man I'd want in the DZ department. I'm glad Purnell agreed—and I'm glad to have you with us. 

We're packed to the gunwales with fancy machinery, but remote-operating some contraption from a cozy cabin is no substitute for putting boots down on the seafloor. You understand that, just as much as you understand that no discovery is worth the life of the person in those boots. 

Your proposal is approved—it's on the books as Project JUNCTION ADVANCE. Assemble your team and requisition what you need. I have high hopes for you. 

Director William Moffat
entries.text_zh:
提案DZ-KJIK19RSNP 

…当我们把目光投向遥远的前沿时，必须直面在极端条件下生存的挑战。我们的NASA同行在阿波罗计划中取得了辉煌成就，但若我们想要探索得更远，就将面临对人类生命构成更大威胁的环境。

无论未来的探索者是要潜入沸腾的硫酸，还是尝试在更高维度间穿梭，我们都必须为他们提供进行科学探索、与原生实体交流的工具——并且，最为关键的是，确保他们能够平安归来。 

维克多·福克纳博士 

回复：提案DZ-KJIK19RSNP 

福克纳博士，自从看到你展示涅瑞达ADS项目的成果后，我就知道你是我想要引入DZ部门的人才。很高兴珀内尔也同意了——更高兴你加入了我们。 

我们这里已经堆满了各种高科技设备，但躲在舒适的船舱里远程操控装置，永远无法替代亲自踏上海底的感觉。你应该明白这一点，也清楚没有任何发现值得以探险家的生命为代价。 

你的提案已经通过——正式立项为联结前进计划。现在你可以组建团队，申请所需的资源了。我对你充满期待。 

威廉·莫法特主任

entries.name: Magnetic Audiotape, 1962
entries.text:
[Portions of tape have been weathered beyond recovery. Label reads: [illegible] Falkner, DZ; Richard Purnell, DZ'.]

PUR: [unintelligible, 12 seconds] bickering about culture and anthropocentrism. They'll be at it for [unintelligible, 4 seconds] 

PUR: What matters to us, to you, is that they recovered three intact survival suits from Diablerets. 

PUR: [inaudible, 12 seconds] questions?

FAL: Many.

PUR: The most pressing, then.

FAL: Will I be allowed to see one of the suits?

PUR: See? Vic, you think [unintelligible, 4 seconds] [laughter] You're getting one of them, tubes and all. Not the wet stuff, Bio snatched that up—some kind of silicone-based micro-organism in suspension, they're saying—leave 'em to it.

FAL: I did not believe it likely [unintelligible, 10 seconds] 

PUR: Oh, don't get me wrong. Chem, Bio, Tech, R&D—even Primes, for some reason—they all want a piece of the pie, and there's not enough slices for all of us.

PUR: Moffat put the kibosh on giving one to Häkke in R&D at least—guns won't do us any good if we're not alive to pull the trigger, and the director's never liked that guy in the first place. Chem and Tech [unintelligible, 2 seconds] other two.

PUR: The Diablerets suits [unintelligible, 3 seconds], but that's a solved problem for humanity already. We're looking at the next frontier. 

FAL: Transdimensional travel. 

PUR: Get your people prepped to receive the materials. And just so we're clear, this isn't charity. I'm expecting great things from you, Vic. 

FAL: I will not disappoint.
entries.text_zh:
[部分磁带因年代久远无法恢复。标签内容显示：[无法辨认]福克纳，DZ；理查德·珀内尔，DZ。]

珀：[难以辨认，持续12秒]为了文化和人类中心主义争论不休。他们得这样[难以辨认，持续4秒] 

珀：对我们，对你而言，重要的是，他们从迪亚布勒雷那里回收了三套完整的生存服。 

珀：[音量过低，持续12秒]问题吗？

福：很多。

珀：那就挑最关键的问。

福：我能看看生存服吗？

珀：看？维克，你以为[难以辨认，持续4秒][笑声]你会直接得到一套，包括所有管线。只是湿的那部分不行，生物科已经抢走了，说是某种悬浮在介质中的硅基微生物…让他们去研究吧。

福：我原本不认为有多大可能[难以辨认，持续10秒] 

珀：哦，别误会。化学、生物、技术、研发…甚至包括首脑，不知出于什么原因，都想分一杯羹，但根本分不过来。

珀：至少莫法特否决了把其中一套给研发部的Häkke——要是活不到开枪的时候，再多枪也没用，而且主任一直看那家伙不顺眼。化学和技术[难以辨认，持续2秒]拿走了另外两套。

珀：迪亚布勒雷生存服[难以辨认，持续3秒]，但对人类来说，那已经不是问题了。我们要瞄准的是下一个前沿。 

福：跨维旅行。 

珀：让你的团队做好接收材料的准备。另外，这不是施舍。我对你期望很高，维克。 

福：我不会让你失望的。

entries.name: Memoranda, 1966
entries.text:
FROM: Dr. Witosław Ostrowski, SU 

Sorry, Vic, didn't mean to leave you hanging. The whole department's been running on too much coffee and too little sleep since it happened—can you blame us? He was one of ours. 

—————————————— 

FROM: Karin Clarke, AC 

This is a notice that Project JUNCTION ADVANCE will be receiving additional funding. A courier will arrive tomorrow with the paperwork. Please be prepared to set aside some time to complete these documents. 

—————————————— 

FROM: William Moffat, D 

Dr. Falkner, I am formally ordering your team to narrow its scope to safeguarding human beings suffused in STRANGE MATTER. This is an internal name for a form of extradimensional exotic matter; you'll be read into our classified projects and studies on the subject shortly. 

Department Lead Dr. Purnell has already been notified, and you should have been allocated additional funds by Accounting. We'll also be providing additional headcount to support this change in direction. Please consult Dr. Purnell and your colleagues in the SM department with any questions. 

If this leaves a bad taste in your mouth, I have it too. I want to make sure you know that this is not standard procedure for projects here. I don't make a habit of ordering experts around their fields. 

Regretfully, the circumstances demand it. The evidence suggests that something took Dr. Davis and Agent Yero through STRANGE MATTER. We need to be able to follow them. 

—————————————— 

FROM: Dr. Yumei Li, SM 

It's the most obvious conclusion. We logged traces of it around the phone. 

—————————————— 

FROM: Dr. Yumei Li, SM 

Scratch that, it's not just the phone. Human Resources and Security narrowed down the intersection where Davis disappeared. There were traces there too. I'm transferring Napier to your team tomorrow.
entries.text_zh:
发件人：维托斯瓦夫·奥斯特罗夫斯基博士，SU 

抱歉，维克，不是故意不理你。自从那件事发生后，整个部门都靠过量咖啡和严重缺乏睡眠硬撑着——能怪我们吗？他曾是我们中的一员。 

—————————————— 

发件人：卡琳·克拉克，AC 

兹通知，联结前进计划将获得追加经费。明天会有一名信使送来相关文件。请预留时间处理这些文书工作。 

—————————————— 

发件人：威廉·莫法特，D 

福克纳博士，现正式命令你的团队将研究范围缩小至：保护被奇异物质浸泡的人体。这是一种跨维度异域物质的内部代号；你将很快被引入我们在该主题上的机密项目与研究。 

部门主管珀内尔博士已获悉此事，会计部也应当已经为你们划拨了追加经费。我们还会增加人手以支持这次研究方向的调整。如有疑问，请与珀内尔博士及SM部门的同事沟通。 

若这让你感到不安，我也一样。我想让你知道，这并非我们这里项目的常规做法。我一向不会随意对专家指手画脚。 

但很遗憾，形势所迫。种种证据表明，是某种东西通过奇异物质带走了戴维斯博士与耶罗特工。我们必须具备追踪他们的能力。 

—————————————— 

发件人：李雨梅博士，SM 

这是最显而易见的结论。我们在电话机周围检测到了它的痕迹。 

—————————————— 

发件人：李雨梅博士，SM 

更正一下，不只是电话。人力资源和安保已经将戴维斯失踪的区间范围缩小了。那里也有痕迹。我明天会把纳皮尔调到你组里去。

entries.name: Pocket Notebook, 1966
entries.text:
Sample degraded within 4 seconds.

If they were alive when they were taken, they would not have stayed that way for more than a few minutes. The director must know this. Perhaps he hopes to at least recover their bodies.

——————————————

I see why Yumei is always in Accounting now. STRANGE MATTER lives up to its name. The process of creating it has a steep price tag, and it is difficult to store for any usable length of time. We can barely coax together enough to stay on a slide. I can test pieces, but for a whole suit, I'll have to join Yumei in the queue.

—————————————— 

I overheard Conway bragging in the cafeteria. Visibility approved another public patent from his team. The fourth this year alone that they've reverse-engineered from their suit.

I asked him for a material sample to test with. Begged, really. I don't care how much he laughs about it later.

Pride is not a result.

—————————————— 

No tests today. I attended the dedication. The director gave the closing speech—about their lives, their work, and the importance of not leaving our own behind. I could swear he looked at me when he said it. I know. I know.

There were unfamiliar faces in the crowd. Not our people. They approached the director as soon as the ceremony closed.

——————————————

Althaus's desk has been cleared. I asked around—poached by DARPA for a weapons program based on the ballistics models they developed from their suit.

I see more unfamiliar faces in the halls every month.

The disappearances aren't just an internal affair. They never could have been. The director believes we will reach out into the void and find friends reaching back. Others do not share his hope.

I didn't need Dr. Purnell to explain this to me. I suppose that can be considered progress? I would rather be making progress on this [expletive redacted] suit.

——————————————

Sample degraded in 9 seconds. At this rate of improvement, even if they are friendly, we will not survive long enough to finish introducing ourselves.

——————————————

There was a scene in the main lobby today. A tall, dignified man in a charcoal suit, speaking with gravitas. Security was trying to escort him out, but the director stopped them.

Now everyone who was within a ten-room radius knows about the lawsuit the Davis family is bringing. Legal must be tying themselves in knots.

Before Mr. Davis left, the director told him, "I will bring them back."

Them. Not their bodies. Them, alive and whole. If the director were anyone else, I'd laugh. But he means it.

The new formulas are running. I will not let them down.
entries.text_zh:
样本在4秒内便降解了。

就算是他们被带走时还活着，也撑不过几分钟。主任心里肯定清楚。或许，他还抱有至少要找回他们遗体的希望。

——————————————

我明白雨梅为何总待在会计部了。奇异物质果然名不虚传。制造它的成本高得离谱，而且几乎无法稳定保存来使用。我们好不容易才凑到那么一点点放在载玻片上。我可以测试碎片，但若要一整套生存服的量，我也得跟雨梅一样去排队了。

—————————————— 

今天在餐厅，听到康威在那里炫耀。他们团队又有一项对外公开的专利获批了，是从那套生存服上反向工程出来的。今年他们就已经拿了四项了。

我向他要了一份材料样本用于测试，可以说是求来的。我不在乎他事后怎么嘲笑我。

自尊不是我们需要的成果。

—————————————— 

今天没有实验。我去了追悼仪式。主任做了闭幕致辞，谈到了他们的生命、工作，以及不放弃团队成员的重要性。我发誓，在说这句话时，他看了我一眼。我知道，我都知道。

人群中出现了陌生的面孔，不是我们的人。仪式一结束，他们就去找主任了。

——————————————

阿尔特豪斯的办公桌被清空了。我打听了一下，他被国防部高级研究计划局挖走了，去参与一项基于他们那套生存服弹道模型的武器计划。

我每个月在走廊里看到的陌生面孔都在增多。

失踪事件已经不再只是内部事务了。其实，它本来就不可能只是内部事务。主任相信，当我们向虚空伸出手时，会有朋友回应。但并不是所有人都认同他的希望。

我不需要珀内尔博士跟我解释这些。我想这也算是一种进步吧？我宁愿是在这套[粗话已隐藏]生存服上取得进展。

——————————————

样本在9秒内降解了。照目前的改进速度，就算对方真的友好，我们也撑不到说完自我介绍。

——————————————

今天主厅里出了场风波。一个高个子、气度不凡的男人，穿着炭灰色西装，讲话声调沉稳有力。安保试图把他请出去，但主任拦住了他们。

现在，方圆十间办公室内的人，都知道戴维斯家正在提起诉讼了。法务那边肯定忙得不可开交。

在戴维斯先生离开前，主任对他说：“我会把他们带回来的。”

“他们”。不是他们的尸体，而是他们本人，活着、完好无损。要是换作别人，我只会嗤之以鼻。但他是认真的。

新配方已经在测试了。我不会让他们失望的。

entries.name: Introduction Letter, 1967
entries.text:
Dr. Falkner,

I'm Dr. Annalise Meyers, lead researcher on Project BLUE DOOR. You may have heard of this project before, as a historical curiosity. In the early days of the Department of External Observation, we were given a mandate to build an interdimensional tunneling device, with the aim of establishing faster-than-light communications without violating causality. Our original tests were inconclusive, and the project was mothballed.

Earlier this year, Director Moffat reactivated BLUE DOOR with a specific directive. He believes that something took Dr. Davis and Agent Yero into another dimension. We've since been concentrating our efforts to creating a path to follow them.

This month, we succeeded. We opened a tear, 15 centimeters across, into another dimension. We project that we'll be able to accommodate human traversal in six months.

However, we have a problem, and Dr. Li said you might be able to help. I understand that JUNCTION ADVANCE is having issues sourcing enough STRANGE MATTER to test with.

Well, right now, we've got too much. The tear flooded our testing room with so much STRANGE MATTER, it must be like air on the other side. There were no casualties, but all our equipment was transmuted into iron filings. We need some kind of shielding.

Interdepartmental cooperation normally involves a lot of paperwork, but it's clear that this project means a great deal to the director—all the red tape's been cut for us. We can start tomorrow, if you like.

What do you say? Let's help each other out.

Dr. Meyers
entries.text_zh:
福克纳博士：

我是安娜丽丝·迈耶斯博士，蓝门计划的首席研究员，你可能当花边新闻听说过这个计划。在对外观察部成立的早期，我们曾奉命建造一台跨维度隧道装置，目标是在不违反因果律的前提下，实现超光速通讯。我们最初的测试结论并不明确，这个计划也就被封存了。

今年年初，莫法特主任下达明确指令，重启了蓝门计划。他认为，是某种东西把戴维斯博士和耶罗特工带去了另一个维度。从那之后，我们便集中精力去开辟一条可以追随他们的路径。

本月，我们成功了。我们开启了一道15厘米宽的裂缝，通向另一个维度。预估六个月内就能达到可供人类通行的宽度。

然而，我们遇到了一个问题，李博士说你或许能帮上忙。我知道联结前进计划正为获取足够的奇异物质用于测试而发愁。

巧的是，我们现在多得用不完。那道裂缝向我们的测试间灌入了海量奇异物质，在那边的世界里，它应该就跟空气一样。虽然没有造成人员伤亡，但我们所有设备都被转化成了铁屑。我们需要某种屏蔽措施。

按照常规，跨部门协作得走一大堆文书流程，但很明显，这个计划对主任意义重大——所有的障碍都给我们扫清了。你同意的话，明天我们就可以开始。

你意下如何？我们互相帮个忙吧。

迈耶斯博士

entries.name: Spiral-Bound Notebook, 1967-1968
entries.text:
EXPERIMENT 1: The tear looked almost innocuous. A floating hole in the curtain of our world. The other side… Dr. Meyers says they are trying to name a new color for it.

20 centimeters. Sample A degraded in 6 seconds. Sample B degraded within 30 seconds. Napier was right: a larger sample mass corrodes more slowly. It doesn't make any sense, but results are results.

Director Moffat was there. He stared at the tear in silence the whole time.

——————————————

EXPERIMENT 6: 24 centimeters. Sample degraded in 159 seconds. Yes. Yes, this is promising. A full-size suit might actually perform far better than our smaller prototypes.

Our current problem is materials. The Diablerets suit's joints were strong but flexible, capable of repeated and extended compression without any loss in tensile strength. R&D cannot replicate it. Told me to "find a [expletive redacted] alien rubber tree or [expletive redacted] off."

A diver in the Nereida couldn't scratch their own back, either. Forget dexterity and haptic perception. In fact, maybe we don't even need a viewport—no, Dr. Meyers will object. If I adapt the polymer structure, can I make it thin enough to coat conventional rubber?

Director Moffat came by again to thank us for our hard work. There were dark circles under his eyes, but he was in a freshly-pressed suit. He must have been on his way to another hearing.

—————————————— 

EXPERIMENT 14: 30 centimeters. Prototype degraded in 8 minutes, 32 seconds. Visor and joints failed first, as expected, but I think I know how to improve the glass, at least. It won't be perfectly clear, but the visibility will be acceptable.

Extensive life support is unfeasible. That's fine; we don't need them to stay for long. Ten minutes, perhaps, to get at least three sets of readings. Double that for safety.

——————————————

EXPERIMENT 25: Annalise and her team made a breakthrough. 162 centimeters. Prototype degraded in 12 minutes, 19 seconds.

BLUE DOOR has held up their end of the bargain; now it is my turn.

——————————————

EXPERIMENT 32: Director Moffat came by the observation room today. He looked at the tear, and told us he would be the first one through.

There was a scattering of nervous laughter. The rest of the team didn't believe him.

Annalise and I, though, we knew. We argued with him for three hours. Long after everyone else had gone home, he finally agreed to have a second. "On belay," he said.

There is not enough budget left in the fiscal year to develop customized suits, and of the team, I am the closest in build to the director. But I would be a poor scientist—indeed, a poor human being—if I would risk someone else's life and not my own.
entries.text_zh:
实验1：裂缝看上去几乎无害，就像挂在我们世界幕布上的一个空洞。另一边…梅耶斯博士说，他们正试图为那东西命名一种新颜色。

20厘米。样本A在6秒内降解，样本B在30秒内降解。纳皮尔说得对：样本质量越大，腐蚀得越慢。这完全说不通，但结果就是这样。

莫法特主任在场。他全程沉默地盯着那道裂缝。

——————————————

实验6：24厘米。样本在159秒内降解。是的，结果令人充满希望。全尺寸的防护服，表现也许会远好于我们的小型原型。

我们目前的问题在于材料。迪亚布勒雷防护服的关节既坚固又柔韧，能够反复、长时间受压而不损失抗拉强度。研发部根本无法复制。他们对我说：“要么去找棵[粗话已隐藏]外星橡胶树来，要么[粗话已隐藏]滚蛋。”

坐在涅瑞达号里，潜水员连自己的背都挠不到，灵巧度和触觉感知什么的就别想了。其实，也许我们甚至都不需要观察窗——不，梅耶斯博士一定会反对。如果我改良聚合物结构，能不能把它做得足够薄，用来包覆普通橡胶？

莫法特主任又过来感谢我们的辛勤工作。他眼下有浓重的黑眼圈，但穿着一身熨帖的西装。他肯定是正要去参加另一场听证会。

—————————————— 

实验14：30厘米。原型在8分钟32秒内降解。护目镜和关节率先失效，和预期一致。不过，至少我觉得自己知道怎么改进玻璃了。没法做到完全透明，但可见度会在可接受范围内。

大规模生命维持系统并不可行。没关系，我们也不需要他们停留太久。也许十分钟，足够获取至少三组读数。为了保险起见，再翻一倍吧。

——————————————

实验25：安娜丽丝和她的团队取得了突破。162厘米，原型在12分钟19秒内降解。

蓝门已经履行了他们的那部分约定，现在轮到我了。

——————————————

实验32：莫法特主任今天到观察室来了。他看着那道裂缝，说他会第一个穿过去。

现场响起了零星的紧张笑声。其他团队成员都不相信他。

但安娜丽丝和我，我们知道他是认真的。我们跟他争论了足足三个小时。等其他人都回家很久以后，他终于同意再加一个人。“作为接应，”他说。

本财年已经没有足够预算开发定制防护服了，而在整个团队里，我的体型和主任最接近。如果我置身事外，拿别人的命去冒险，那我就不是一个好科学家，也算不上一个好人。

entries.name: Magnetic Audiovisual Tape, 1968
entries.text:
[Portions of tape have been transmuted to cesium (inert, despite exposure to air) or burnt through and are unrecoverable. Label reads: EXPERIMENT 33 - DIR. W. MOFFAT & DR. V. FALKNER PARTICIPATING, DR. A. MEYERS RECORDING.]

[A large, mechanical, ring-shaped device sits in the center of a warehouse. A deep, oscillating hum emanates from it. The hum begins to rise in frequency and pitch.]

MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: 40%… 60%… Gentlemen, the test is beginning.

[Two people in large protective suits move towards the device. Each suit has black lettering on the back: the lead suit reads "MOF" while the other reads "FAL." They are tethered by safety lines leading from their suits and connecting to something off camera.]

[A tear opens in the center of the ring. Through the tear, the other side seems to bubble and shimmer, shifting through every color the magnetic tape can capture. Bands of static and visual distortion sizzle across the feed.]

[Visual feed burns out.]

UNKNOWN: [A loud, discordant sound. Though difficult to comprehend at base levels, further analysis has identified audio components drawn from the predator-deterrence call of Dryophytes cinereus, the "gekkering" of Vulpes vulpes, the low-frequency hum of large sand dunes, and Menura novaehollandiae imitating a motor.]

MOFFAT: It's talking to us.

FALKNER: What?

MOFFAT: My name is William Moffat, Director of the Department of External Observations! We mean you no harm. We wish only for the safe return of the humans you took.

UNKNOWN: [A large number of human voices blended into an indistinct chattering crowd.]

MEYERS: Director, this has never happened before. It may not be safe to approach—

MOFFAT: Dr. Nella Davis and Agent Louis Yero have families, loved ones, friends—hoping day after day for their safe return.

MOFFAT: Whatever you need from them, ask it of me instead. They are my subordinates, in my capacity as director—

[The device's hum rapidly changes pitch.]

MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: Gravitational anomalies detected—it's transmuting the gateway!

FALKNER: Already? The shielding, we should have another six minutes—

UNKNOWN: [Roaring.]

[A loud metallic twang. A heavy impact from something large and metallic striking a soft surface. Falkner screams. His scream continues, at the same pitch and volume, for the next three and a half minutes.]

MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: [gasps, stifling a scream]

MOFFAT: Falkner—damn it!

MOFFAT: The line—why won't it—give him back! Give them all back!

MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: Director, oh, God. Director, cut his line and get back! We have to cut power to BLUE DOOR!

MOFFAT: I'm not letting him go!

MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: If you don't, we'll lose you too!

[Visual feed returns.]

[The tear has expanded past the device's boundary; half of the machinery has sunk through it. The air writhes.]

[Moffat stands less than two feet from the tear, feet braced. He grips his own safety line in one hand, and Falkner's in the other. Falkner's safety line leads into the tear. Although the line is taut, Moffat seems unable to pull Falkner back. Instead, he is being dragged towards the tear, inch by inch.]

[Moffat looks into the tear. Falkner's scream continues.]

[Moffat releases his own safety line and plunges through the opening.]
entries.text_zh:
[部分录像带已转化为铯（在空气中仍保持稳定不反应），或已烧毁无法修复。标签写着：实验33 - 参与者：W.莫法特主任及V.福克纳博士，记录人：A.梅耶斯博士。]

[仓库中央，一个大型机械环形装置嗡嗡作响，深沉的声音振荡开来。嗡鸣声逐渐在频率和音高上攀升。]

梅耶斯[通过扩音器]：“40%…60%…先生们，测试开始。”

[两人身着大型防护服，向装置走去。每套防护服背后都印有黑色字母：走在前面的印着“莫”，另一套印着“福”。他们身上系着安全绳，绳子从防护服上延伸出去，连接到画面外的某个装置上。]

[环中央裂开一道缝隙，缝隙那边仿佛在翻滚、闪烁，色彩在录像带能记录的所有颜色间不断变换。静电干扰和影像失真在画面上噼啪闪烁。]

[画面烧毁。]

未知：[一阵刺耳的杂音。尽管在基础层面上难以理解，但进一步分析发现，其中包含的音频成分有灰树蛙捕食者的威吓叫声、赤狐的咯咯叫声、大型沙丘产生的低频嗡鸣，以及琴鸟模仿马达的叫声。]

莫法特：它在和我们说话。

福克纳：什么？

莫法特：我是威廉·莫法特，对外观察部主任！我们并无恶意，只希望你们能安全归还被带走的人类。

未知：[大量人类声音混杂在一起，像嘈杂的人群。]

梅耶斯：主任，这种情况从未发生过，现在靠近它可能不安全——

莫法特：内拉·戴维斯博士和路易斯·耶罗探员都有家人、爱人和朋友，日日夜夜盼着他们安全归来。

莫法特：无论你们需要他们做什么，都让我来吧。他们是我的下属，就我身为主任的职责——

[装置的嗡鸣声突然变调。]

梅耶斯[通过扩音器]：探测到引力异常——它在转化通道！

福克纳：这么快？有屏蔽的情况下，我们还应该有六分钟——

未知：[咆哮。]

[一声金属巨响，某个巨大金属物体撞上柔软表面，发出沉重撞击声。福克纳发出惨叫，持续了三分半钟，音高和音量始终不变。]

梅耶斯[通过扩音器]：[倒吸一口气，强忍住尖叫]

莫法特：福克纳——该死！

莫法特：这绳子——为什么它——把他还给我！把他们都还回来！

梅耶斯[通过扩音器]：主任，天哪。主任，快割断他的绳子，回来！我们必须给蓝门断电！

莫法特：我不会放开他的！

梅耶斯[通过扩音器]：如果你不放，我们也会失去你！

[画面恢复。]

[裂缝已扩张至超出装置边界，一半的机器沉入其中。空气扭曲翻搅。]

[莫法特站在离裂缝不足两英尺的地方，双脚撑着地。他一只手抓着自己的安全绳，另一只手抓着福克纳的安全绳。福克纳的安全绳延伸进裂缝，尽管绳子绷得笔直，莫法特却似乎无法将福克纳拉回。相反，他正被一点一点拖向裂缝。]

[莫法特望向裂缝，福克纳的惨叫仍在持续。]

[莫法特松开自己的安全绳，跳进了那道裂口。]

entries.name: Torn Journal Page, 1968
entries.text:
Dec. 12, 1968 – 21.0°F – 11.6mph, SE – 2.49mi – Overcast

When does heroism become vanity?

I've had a long six weeks to think. Nothing else to do, really—Angie might've trained Medical a little too well, but if I tell her that, she'll put me back on bed rest.

So, when does heroism become vanity? When does determination become mania? When does sacrifice become self-satisfaction? When is enough, enough?

If there's a taller mountain, I have to climb it. Six weeks ago, I called that ambition.

Angie said they won't know if they can discharge Falkner for another ten months. It turned his kidneys to titanium. Heart valve to gallium. Apparently, it treated his early bone cancer though—it's all strontium now.

John told me again that I need to let it go. Angie, too. Stiller, Perlman, Li, Meyers. I know what they're all thinking: Davis and Yero are dead. They have been since the moment they were taken. Nothing of our world can survive in that formless beyond.

I swore I'd bring them back. Is it still for them? Or is it for me?

Fine. Let's say it's just for me, my pride. I don't give a damn. I am never going to let it go. I can't. I won't.

I won't, but Director Moffat, head of the DEO, must. Falkner went with me because I believed, and he believed me. If the only way to get them back is to throw other lives into that tear, let it have them—I won't make that trade. Not ever. I'll unbend the projects I've pointed in that direction. Reallocate manpower and funding. Get back to the mission.

But I'm not letting them go. I will find them, and I will bring them back.
entries.text_zh:
1968年12月12日 - 21.0°F - 东南风11.6英里/小时 - 2.49英里 - 阴天

英雄主义何时会沦为虚荣？

这六个星期过得实在太漫长。基本上也没别的事可做——安吉把医务人员训练得也许过于出色了，可我要是这么跟她说，她肯定会把我重新按回病床上。

所以，英雄主义何时会变成虚荣？坚韧何时会变成狂热？牺牲何时会变成自我满足？足够的界限在哪里呢？

如果有一座更高的山，我就必须去攀登。六个星期前，我把这叫做抱负。

安吉说，他们还要等十个月才能知道福克纳能否出院。他的肾脏被变成钛，心脏瓣膜变成了镓。不过，显然那东西还顺便治好了他早期的骨癌——现在那部分变成了锶。

约翰又一次劝我放手，安吉也是。斯蒂勒、珀尔曼、李、梅耶斯，他们心里怎么想的我都清楚：戴维斯和耶罗已经死了，从他们被带走的那一刻起就死了。我们这个世界的任何东西，都不可能在那一片无形的彼岸存活。

我发过誓要把他们带回来。这誓言现在还是为了他们吗？还是为了我自己？

好，就算这完全是为了我、为了我的自尊。我一点也不在乎。我绝不会放手，我不能，我不会。

我不会，但对外观察部主任莫法特，必须得放。福克纳之所以和我一起去，是因为我的信念，而他相信我。如果把他们救回来的唯一办法，是把更多人往那道裂缝里扔，那是不行的——我不会做那种交换，永远不会。我会把那些项目从那个方向上扭转回来，重新分配人力和经费，回到既定任务上。

但我不会放弃他们，我会找到他们，然后把他们带回来。

entries.name: Lodi, Wisconsin, 1929
entries.text:
I'm four or five years old. Faces, moments, feelings. I'm meeting the world for the first time.

Uncle Tomás says, just wait until you see Jenny.

I think that's a pretty name because it rhymes with Penny, which is my favorite coin because it's the name of my teacher, who is pretty. 

The sound of her rumbles in my chest, like big cicadas. I'm sitting on my dad's shoulders and the summer sun, the band playing loud, hot and itchy sweat down the back of my neck, and then I saw it. 

That biplane is the prettiest thing in the whole world. It sounds like thunder when it flies overhead! A great big bird made out of wood, wire, steel, and canvas. Pop again tells me they named it Jenny. I ask who and he says everyone. I think that means they all can see how pretty she looks, up there, between the clouds, where only birds and angels go.

I say I'd like to be there one day.

Me too, says Ben. He's right next to me.

Uncle Tomás says, sure, kid! It's grand up there. He has a thin mustache and keeps his cap at an angle and wears a silk scarf. They all do that. They all look like they should do that.

Uncle Tomás kneels and puts an arm over Ben's shoulder and points at Jenny in the sky. Anytime you want, I'll take you and Louis up there, Ben. You think it looks grand now, but you can't imagine.

Really?

You go higher than the angels, my uncle says, and you can see what God sees.

What's that, then? My pop asks. Uncle Tomás takes his arm off Ben's shoulder and smiles and says, you know the sound the wind makes, when it's so loud you can't hear anything at all?

I know that sound, my pop says. But hearing ain't seeing. 

That a fact, Benito? 

It's Ben.

Pop hates being called Benito. He hates it so much he named himself Ben, and my brother Junior, he named Ben too. 

Jenny roars overhead again. We all look up.

I like all their names. They stick. Like they're never going to go anywhere. Not without me.
entries.text_zh:
我大概四五岁的时候，开始有了对世界的初步认知——那些面孔、片段和感觉。

托马斯叔叔说：“等你见到珍妮就明白了。”

我觉得那名字真好听，它与佩妮押韵，而佩妮是我最爱的硬币，因为我的老师也叫佩妮，她长得可美了。 

珍妮的声音在我胸口轰鸣，宛如巨蝉，我坐在爸爸的肩头，沐浴着夏日的阳光，耳边是乐队音乐的喧嚣，汗水顺着脖子流淌，痒痒的。就在这时，我看到了它。 

那架双翼机是这世上最美丽的存在。它掠过头顶，声音像雷鸣！那是一只由木头、铁丝、钢铁和帆布编织而成的大鸟。爸爸告诉我，它叫珍妮。我问是谁取的，他说，是所有人。我想，这意味着大家都能见证它的美丽，翱翔于云端，那是鸟儿和天使的领地。

我说，我梦想有一天也能飞上那里。

“我也是，”本站在我身旁，附和道。

托马斯叔叔说：“当然可以，小子！上面壮观极了。”他留着细胡子，帽子总是歪戴，还围着一条丝巾。其他人也是如此装扮，他们就该是这样。

托马斯叔叔单膝跪地，一只胳膊搭在本的肩上。他指着天上的珍妮说：“你什么时候想去，我就带你和路易斯一起飞，本。你现在觉得壮观，但在上面完全不一样。”

“真的吗？”

“你会飞得比天使还高，”叔叔说，“你会看到上帝眼中的世界。”

“那是什么样？”我老爸问。托马斯叔叔从本的肩上移开手，笑道：“你听过那种风声吗？大到让你什么都听不见？”

“听过。”老爸说，“但听见的不等于看见。” 

“是这样啊，本尼托？” 

“叫我本。”

老爸最讨厌别人叫他本尼托，厌恶至极，所以他自称本，还给我哥哥取了同样的名字。 

珍妮再次咆哮着掠过头顶，我们都抬头仰望。

我喜欢他们所有的名字，它们在我心中生根发芽，仿佛永远不会离去，不会留下我一人。

entries.name: Assumption, Illinois, 1938
entries.text:
I'm 13 years old. I stole my pop's old truck, and now I'm driving to see Uncle Tomás. I didn't plan for Ben to come along. And I didn't plan to run out of gas. 

"'Why don't you put some lead in your foot?'" Ben says, his voice high and mocking. He walks behind me, hands shoved in his pockets. "'We're not gonna get there until the '40s, how slow you're driving.'"

"Can it," I snap. "And my voice is deeper than that."

"A big ant is still a little bug," Ben says. He kicks a rock off the highway.

We are somewhere far south of home on Route 51. I lug a gas can. It's my turn since Ben carried it the last mile.

"Think there's a gas station up there?" I ask. Ben doesn't respond. I stop trudging. I look up from the ground, squint against the bright light, look at him, then look at what transfixed him.

"Assumption," Ben says. "Like at mass."

"Weird name for a town," I reply. The town sign is blurry, but I can still read it, for the most part. It's bright.

"Who's that?" Ben says. He points just beyond the sign. 

A silhouette wavers, like heat low over the road, only it isn't hot enough for that. The figure swaggers toward us, limping, then not. Dread nausea swirls like sick in the back of my throat.

"Get behind me, Lou," Ben says. He shoves his hand into his pocket and draws his pocketknife. The blade catches the sun and flashes, and then he stops moving.

Cold air, like what I imagine the sky to taste like. Acrid coal. I feel a buzzing thing shoot through me—a sunburn from the inside out. 

my name is garden and cradle and the mass by which all other bodies are measured and i am your mother
do not be afraid ask me a question before death hastens me from this moment 
screaming is not a question dear one 
ben will be fine you will not cause him insurmountable pain
one more question 
no dear one i cannot blindless is your fate though you will see into the great beyond 

"LOU OH GOD WAKE UP HOLY MOTHER WAKE UP." Ben slaps me, and I wake up screaming.

Ben pulls me into an embrace. I can feel his heart beating against mine. He clutches his pocketknife in a trembling fist, blade stabbing toward Assumption. One day, I'll understand that his fear was not of the thing we saw, but of what it could have done to me.

"Was that the Devil?" Ben whispers.

"It's all right, Ben," I say. "I don't think it was the Devil." We part. I don't think it was something holy either.

I think it was a third thing.
entries.text_zh:
我13岁了，偷偷开着老爸的旧卡车，去见托马斯叔叔。我本没打算带本一起，也没想到会把油开光。 

“你怎么不多踩点油啊？”本模仿着嘲讽的语气尖声说。他走在我后面，两手插兜，“你开这么慢，我们到那都40年代了。”

“闭嘴，”我回敬道，“而且我声音没那么尖。”

“蚂蚁再大也是虫，”本说着，一脚踢飞了公路上的一块石头。

我们在离家很远的51号公路南边，我拎着油桶，上一英里是本拎的，现在轮到我了。

“你说前面会不会有加油站？”我问。本沉默不语。我停下脚步，眯起眼，迎着刺眼的光，看向他，又看向让他呆立的东西。

“升天。”本说，“弥撒上提到过这个词。”

“这镇子名字真怪，”我回答道。镇牌虽有些模糊，但大部分还看得清，亮得晃眼。

“那是谁？”本指向牌子后面的一点。 

一个轮廓摇摇晃晃地靠近，像是公路上的热浪，但此刻并不炎热。那身形一瘸一拐，然后又不瘸了。恐惧在我喉咙深处翻涌。

“站到我身后，路，”本说。他把手伸进兜里，掏出小折刀。刀刃在阳光下一闪，他突然静止不动了。

一阵冷气，像是天空的味道，呛人的煤烟味。我感觉有个嗡嗡作响的东西从我体内穿过，像是从内而外的晒伤。 

我即是花园与摇篮是万物称量的质量是你们的母亲
别害怕在死亡催我离开此刻之前向我发问吧 
尖叫不是问题孩子 
本会没事你不会给他造成不可逾越的痛苦
再问一个问题 
不行孩子我不能失明是你的命数虽然你将注视无垠的彼岸 

“路，天哪，醒醒！”本扇着我的脸，我惨叫着醒了过来。

本把我搂进怀里，我能感受到他的心跳贴着我的。他紧紧攥着小折刀，手在发抖，刀尖指向升天镇的方向。多年后我才明白，他害怕的并非我们看到的东西，而是它可能对我做的事。

“那是魔鬼吗？”本低声问。

“没事的，本。”我说，“我觉得那不是魔鬼。”我们松开彼此。我也不觉得那是什么神圣的存在。

我觉得那是别的什么东西。

entries.name: Holland, Occupied Netherlands, 1944
entries.name_zh: 西海岸，被占领的荷兰，1944年
entries.text:
I'm 20 years old, and I've just been shot down.

I can't really move. My webbing is tangled, hooked on every possible surface inside the cockpit. My left arm is pinned, but my right is free, and I can turn my head. I'm listing to the right and a little down, on account of how my Lightning came to rest.

Low roar. Waves in the distance. Wet, dark sand. I'm on a beach in Holland, or maybe somewhere further north, but certainly on a beach in the Netherlands.

I've been shot down. I can't help but laugh, then gasp. I definitely have some broken ribs. I check myself with my free hand. I have a pistol, a tin of syrettes, four tins of canned rations, a roll of guilders, a signaling mirror, and a pocket phrasebook.

Spanish won't help me, especially when it's in Pop's Jalisco accent. Ben said I should learn Dutch, but I told him that all the Dutch girls I wanted to meet spoke French, and anyways, I didn't plan on getting shot down. But here I am. He's yucking it up in Hawaii, and I'm busted up on the beach with no Dutch. If we see each other alive again, he won't let me live this down.

My knee hurts. I'll stick with French and English if I see anyone. German—I don't know. I know Wisconsin German; I'd sound like a time traveler. 

Someone's got to come running soon. I flew over a few towns on the way here. Yeah. Sure. Someone's going to come soon— 

I wake up. It's nighttime. I'm nauseous. Water runs up and into the cockpit. The tide is coming in. The waves aren't here, but their bitter fingers patter the side of my crashed bird and dribble into my boots.

Hell. I gotta get out. My left arm is cramping, spent too long wrenched in that awkward position. I don't want to drown inside my plane. 

"Help," I shout. "Help! Aide-moi, aide-moi!"

I can hear someone coming. Footsteps, familiar footsteps, sloshing through the surf. I thrash in the cockpit, trying to free my arm, trying to draw my gun. An acrid stink—is that my plane on fire? No, it's coal— 

I wake up to hands on me. Knives flashing in the pale morning light, sawing through my restraints. I stammer something in French about being American, and I'm quickly hushed. 

"You're safe," the men say. "We are friends. You're safe, you're safe."
entries.text_zh:
我20岁了，刚被击落。

我几乎动弹不得，伞带缠在一起，勾住了座舱里的所有地方。左臂被卡死，右臂还能动，脑袋也能转动。我微微向右侧翻着，又往下栽了一点，因为我的闪电就是摔成了这个角度。

低沉的轰鸣，远处的海浪，潮湿的暗色沙子。我在一个海滩上，可能在荷兰西海岸，也可能更北，但肯定是在荷兰的某个海滩。

我被击落了。我忍不住笑了一声，随即倒吸一口凉气，肋骨肯定断了几根。我用还能动的手摸了摸自己，身上有一把手枪，一听注射器，四听罐头口粮，一卷荷兰盾，一面信号镜，还有一本袖珍会话手册。

西班牙语帮不上忙，尤其是我老爸那哈利斯科口音的西班牙语。本曾说我该学点荷兰语，我回他，想认识的荷兰姑娘都会说法语，再说我也没打算被击落。但我现在就躺在这，带着一身伤，一句荷兰语也不会。如果我们还能活着见面，他肯定会笑我一辈子。

我的膝盖疼得厉害。要是真遇上什么人，还是先用法语和英语交流为好。德语？我不太确定。我只会威斯康星那一带的德语，说起来像个穿越时空的怪人。 

应该很快会有人过来的。我驾机飞来途中，曾路过几个小镇。没错，肯定会有人赶来的—— 

又醒来时，夜幕已经降临。我恶心得想吐，海水不断涌进座舱，很明显，潮水涨起来了。虽然浪头还没打到我这里，但咸涩的海水已像手指一样，一下下拍打着我这坠毁的铁鸟，还慢慢渗进了我的靴子。

糟糕，我得赶紧出去。我的左臂抽筋了，长时间卡在那个难受的姿势。我可不想淹死在自己的飞机里。 

“救命！”我喊道，“救命！Aide-moi, aide-moi！”

我听到有人靠近，浪花声中传来熟悉的脚步声。我在座舱里拼命挣扎，想挣脱被卡住的胳膊，还想拔出枪。空气中弥漫着一股刺鼻的气味——是我的飞机着火了吗？不，是煤烟—— 

当我再次醒来时，有人在拉扯我。几把刀在苍白的晨光中闪烁，锯着束缚我的带子。我结结巴巴地用法语说自己是美国人，很快被人制止出声。 

“你安全了，”那些人说，“我们是朋友。安全了，你安全了。”

entries.name: Peenemünde, German Democratic Republic, 1954
entries.name_zh: 皮内明德，德意志民主共和国，1954年
entries.text:
I'm 29 years old, and I'm freezing cold, mucking up from the surf off a rain-swept beach into the woods near Peenemünde, an old V-2 launch site. 

It's nighttime. The Company likes to send me out at night. The boys call me Orlok; the sunlight hurts my eyes. I hate the night shift. It's like I'm walking through a nightmare. But it's my job. It's how we win.

A cluster of concrete buildings damp and dribbling. An airstrip. Old blast pits where V-2s once launched to buzz over the North Sea into England. South, the horizon glows. A city. 

A truck trundles into the base. It stops. Idles. A person gets out, lights a cigarette, and limps into the only standing building. He leaves the door open.

"What the hell?" I mutter. I draw my pistol.

Inside, the rain hammers on the rusted roof. I can hear water churning; whole sections of the building are flooded. This place has been dead for years. Something gravitational draws me deeper in.

"Amerikanisch, Britisch, oder Deutsch?" A voice echoes through the building. Gently accented German.

"Amerikanisch," I answer. I don't holster my gun.

"English fine?"

"If that works for you."

"English is good. I am practicing." 

I follow the voice to the center of the structure. A factory floor, or large warehouse of some kind. Dark but for a single lantern on a solitary table. The man sits in the pool of light, smoking a cigarette. Rain falls through the perforated roof, dribbling on rusted machinery. An empty chair sits opposite him.

"Not much of a space program," I say. 

"No," he says. "Sit, please." He gestures at the table, an unlit cigarette pinched between his fingers. "You smoke?"

I remain standing.

"Are you going to kill me?" I ask him. 

"You're the one with the gun, amigo. Are you going to kill me?"

"No," I say. "Where is Dr. Heuer?"

"Dead."

"What?"

The dark-eyed man mutters a soft, frustrated curse in Russian. "Gone," he says, slowly. "We killed him. Вы понимаете?" 

"Не совсем. Я учусь," I say. "Why?"

"He was a fascist," the Soviet says. "What would we need him for after we captured his rockets? He's been dead since '45."

I sag down into the chair. 

"Sorry to bend your paperclip." He grins. "How is my English, by the way?"

"It's good," I assure him. "How's my Russian?"

"Your pronunciation is fine." 

"Thank my brother," I say. 

"You could continue practicing with me."

The immensity of the offer stuns me. I see a different life, one lonely but wild, in a red world far more ancient than my own. A different tongue, a different set of stars. I am alone, but special. 

"I can't do that," I lie.

"Как жаль," he sighs. "OK. Go now."

"Why?"

Distant, mingled with the driving rain: the thud of approaching helicopters. 

The Soviet stands, leaving the unlit cigarette on the table.

I run.
entries.text_zh:
我29岁，冷得瑟瑟发抖，从风雨交加的海滩浪花中艰难爬出，摸进了皮内明德附近的树林。这里曾是一个V-2火箭发射基地。 

现在是晚上。公司总喜欢在夜晚派我执行任务。男孩们叫我奥洛克，阳光会刺痛我的双眼。我讨厌夜晚执勤，感觉像在噩梦中行走。但这是我的工作，是我们取得胜利的方式。

眼前是一组混凝土建筑，潮湿且渗水。一条飞机跑道，还有旧的爆破坑，曾经V-2火箭就是从那里发射，飞越北海，直冲英格兰。向南望去，地平线泛着光，那是一座城市。 

一辆卡车轰隆隆地驶入基地，停下后怠速运转。一人下车，点燃一支烟，一瘸一拐地走进唯一一幢还屹立不倒的建筑，而且没关门。

“搞什么鬼？”我低声嘀咕着，随即拔出了手枪。

屋内，雨点重重砸在生锈的屋顶上，我能听见水翻滚涌动的声音，整片区域好像都被水淹了。这地方已荒废多年，却有什么东西像磁石一样吸引着我往里走。

“Amerikanisch, Britisch, oder Deutsch？”楼里传来一个声音，是带着轻微口音的德语。

“Amerikanisch。”我回答，没有收枪。

“英语可以吗？”

“你方便就行。”

“英语可以，我在练习。” 

我顺着声音走向建筑物中央，这里应该是个厂房或大型仓库。黑暗中，只有一盏孤灯照亮一张孤零零的桌子。一个男人坐在光圈里，叼着一支烟。雨水从千疮百孔的屋顶落下，滴在生了锈的机器上。桌子对面放着一把空椅子。

“看起来不像是个太空计划，”我说。 

“确实。”他说，“请坐。”他用夹着未点燃的烟的手指朝桌子一指，“你抽烟吗？”

我依旧站着。

“你打算杀我吗？”我问他。 

“拿枪的是你，amigo。你打算杀我吗？”

“不。”我说，“赫伊尔博士在哪里？”

“死了。”

“什么？”

这个黑眼睛的男人用俄语轻轻骂了一句，带着懊恼。“没了，”他缓缓说，“我们杀了他。Вы понимаете？” 

“他совсем. Я учусь。”我说，“为什么？”

“他是个法西斯。”这个苏联人说，“我们把他的火箭都缴获了，还要他有什么用？他45年就已经死了。”

我一屁股瘫坐在椅子上。 

“抱歉，打乱了你的小计划。”他咧嘴一笑，“顺便问一下，我的英语怎么样？”

“挺好的。”我告诉他，“那我的俄语呢？”

“你的发音没问题。” 

“这得感谢我哥哥，”我说。 

“你可以继续跟我一起练。”

这个邀请让我愣住了。我看到了一条截然不同的人生道路，一条孤独又狂野的道路，在一个比我原本世界古老得多的赤色世界里。一种不同的语言，一组不同的星辰。我孤身一人，却又与众不同。 

“我不能那样做，”我撒谎道。

“Как жаль。”他叹了口气，“好，你走吧。”

“为什么？”

远处，在急雨声中，我听到了直升机靠近的砰砰声。 

苏联人站起身，把未点燃的香烟留在桌上。

我奔跑起来。

entries.name: Pine Ridge Reservation, South Dakota, 1960
entries.name_zh: 松树岭保留地，南达科他州，1960年
entries.text:
I'm 35 years old and sweltering. It's summer in South Dakota. The sun hangs in the sky like a man in the gallows. I stand on the deck of an aircraft carrier that has manifested in a lonely ravine.

A major greets me.

"Director Moffat sent you?" she asks.

"Yes." I offer my hand. "Linguistics and Deniable Comms."

"DC? Desks don't usually come out on field trips."

"It's not my first rodeo, Major," I say. "Lead on."

We walk across the deck to a lift, where the corpse of a Hellcat rots. She punches the down button on the lift. I take my glasses off and pull on my respirator.

I follow her deep into the carrier. I can hear muttering from somewhere ahead. Someone moans in the darkness. The major clicks on a flashlight and illuminates the corridor, revealing the air to be thick with particulates.

We follow the voices. I hear two or three speakers. One sounds familiar. I don't wait. I run to the sound of my brother's voice.

Ben is fused to the wall. A saline drip runs into his free arm. His left is lost inside the metal bulkhead with the lower half of his body. A pair of medics attend him. This can't be my brother. Ben is probably having a beer in his barn as he brushes his horses. I take a moment. Compose myself.

"I'm Agent Yero," I say. My mouth is so dry that I cough. I've got to keep distance. This isn't him. "What's your name, Lieutenant?"

"Small world," Ben says. "We got the same last name." He doesn't recognize me with my respirator on. He looks around the hallway, his eyes glazed and wandering. "Really small world. Where am I?"

"South Dakota."

"Pretty far from the Pacific."

"That's where you were?"

"Yeah, three days out from Formosa. Going to wallop Mao's boys."

"How did you get here?"

"One step at a time," Ben jokes. 

"What ship is this?"

"The 'Hornet.' CV-8. Mighty old gal." His gaze wanders over the scene. "You military? That suit looks out of place."

"Army Air Corps. B-17s, then an F-5 during Market Garden."

"My brother died on a B-17," Junior says.

"I'm sorry to hear that, Lieutenant." I make a note that in his world, I am dead. "Does 'Assumption' mean anything to you?"
Ben's idle, pain-killed smile vanishes.

"Who are you?"

"Please, Lieutenant, we don't have much time."

"I saw the Devil there," Ben says. "She walked up and gave me a kiss. Told me I would live for 80 years. I won't die here. The Devil told me so."

I can smell the coal. My Ben may have seen it first, but it chose me.

He only saw the sunrise. I saw the sun.

"Gimme more," Ben groans.

The medics look to the major, who looks to me. I nod: I'm finished.

The major finds me back at camp. My head is swimming.

"He's dead," the major says. "Ten minutes after you left." She tosses a file on my fold-out desk. "You handled that well. Family manifestations are tough."

"That wasn't my brother," I say.

"A doppelganger, like the outbreak in '59."

"No," I reply. "The CV-8 sank in '43, and Ben was never at Formosa." I massage the back of my neck. My head is pounding. Vacuum tube static spreads inkblots across my vision, starting from the left. "This is something else. A, uh, tulpa, maybe."

"But it knew what you were asking it about? 'Assumption'?"

A wave of nausea. "It's a town. Ben and I saw something there as kids. It's a focal moment. Fixed time. Matter is constant—it repeats, and time happens in parallel. Deniable Comms investigates the meaning of those fixed points. We think they have, uh, external meaning."

"Aliens?"

"Could be. Or ghosts. Other times. Other realities." I lean forward on the desk and close my eyes. "I need a constant to help navigate phenomena. Ben is my constant. I know him. That wasn't Ben." He's still out there.

"So, what was that?"

"Chirality. Variegation. Not sure: It depends on where I am observing this from," I say, and for a moment, I am trillions of years old. Understanding backfills, then purges. I forget nearly all of it. I see what happens next.

"Major," I say, "the trash can, please. I think I'm going to be sick."
entries.text_zh:
我35岁，热得难受。南达科他州的夏天，太阳高悬，像个被绞死的人。我站在一艘航空母舰的甲板上，它孤零零地立在这条峡谷里。

一名少校前来迎接我。

“莫法特主任派你来的？”她问。

“对。”我伸出手，“语言学和可否认通信部。”

“可否认通信？坐办公室的人通常不会出来实地考察。”

“这不是我第一次办差了，少校。”我说道，“带路吧。”

我们穿过甲板，来到一部升降机前。有个地狱猫的残骸堆在那里，已经开始腐烂。她按下升降机的下行按钮，我则摘下眼镜，戴上防毒面具。

我跟着她钻进了航空母舰的深处。能听见前方有人嘟哝，黑暗中还传来阵阵呻吟。少校打开手电筒，照亮了走廊，空气里满是悬浮的颗粒物。

我们顺着那些声音的方向走去。我听到两三个人在交谈，其中一个声音听起来特别耳熟。我再也按捺不住，朝着我哥哥的声音跑去。

本和墙壁融为一体了，生理盐水正通过点滴打进他那只还露在外面的胳膊。他的左臂连同下半身都被吞进了金属舱壁里，两名医护兵守在他身边。这绝不可能是我的哥哥。本现在应该正一边喝着啤酒，一边在谷仓里刷马呢。我停下脚步，努力让自己冷静下来。

“我是耶罗探员，”我开口说道，嘴干得要命，忍不住咳嗽。我得和他保持距离，这不是他。“中尉，你叫什么名字？”

“真是巧啊，”本说，“我们居然同姓。”他没认出戴着防毒面具的我，眼神浑浊而游离，环顾着走廊，“这世界可真小。我这是在哪儿？”

“南达科他。”

“离太平洋可真够远的。”

“你原来在那里？”

“是啊，离福尔摩沙三天的航程，准备去狠狠教训一下毛的部队。”

“你怎么到这来的？”

“一步一步走过来的，”本打趣道。 

“这是哪艘船？”

“大黄蜂号，CV-8。老古董一艘。”他的目光在四周游移，“你是当兵的？你这身打扮可不太像啊。”

“陆军航空队的。先是开B-17，后来在市场花园行动里飞F-5。”

“我弟弟死在了一架B-17上，”本说。

“很遗憾听到这个消息，中尉。”我心里暗暗记下，在他的世界里，我已经死了。“你知道‘升天'吗？”
本那种被止痛药弄得有些呆滞的笑容消失了。

“你是谁？”

“拜托，中尉，我们时间不多了。”

“我在那里看见了魔鬼。”本说，“她走过来亲了我一下，跟我说我会活到80岁。我不会死在这里的，魔鬼这么跟我说过。”

我能闻到煤炭的味道。也许是本先看见了它，但它却选择了我。

他只看见了日出，而我看见的是太阳。

“再给我点，”本呻吟着。

医护兵看向少校，少校又看向我。我点了点头：我问完了。

少校在营地里找到了我。我的脑子晕乎乎的。

“他死了。”少校说，“你走后十分钟。”她把一个档案袋扔在我的折叠桌上，“你处理得不错，亲属显现这种事情很难应对。”

“那不是我哥哥，”我说。

“是二重身，就像59年暴发时那样。”

“不，”我回答道，“CV-8在43年就沉了，本也从来没去过福尔摩沙。”我揉着后颈，脑袋疼得要命。真空管的噪音在我视野里像墨迹一样，从左边开始蔓延。“这是别的什么。呃，也许是个意识体。”

“可它知道你在问什么？‘升天'？”

一阵恶心涌了上来。“那是个镇子。本和我小时候在那里看见了一些东西。那是个关键时刻，固定的时间。物质是恒定的，它会重复，而时间是并行发生的。可否认通信部研究那些固定点的意义，我们觉得它们，呃，有外在的含义。”

“外星人？”

“也有可能，或者鬼魂。其他时间，其他现实。”我撑着桌子向前倾，闭上眼睛，“我需要一个常数来帮助自己导航梳理这些现象。本就是我的常数，我了解他。那不是本。”他还活着。

“那，刚才那个是什么？”

“手性，多样化，我也不确定。这取决于我从哪里去观察这一切，”我说。就在那一刻，我感觉自己仿佛有三十万亿年的年纪。理解如潮水般向后灌入，然后又被冲刷干净。我忘掉了几乎所有东西，却看见了接下来会发生什么。

“少校，”我说，“拜托把垃圾桶拿过来，我大概要吐了。”

entries.name: Lodi, Wisconsin, 1962
entries.text:
I'm 37 years old, and my hands are cold. I'm beginning to know what to expect.

Pop's dead and we've got to settle accounts. I've got to let my brother Ben know about everything. All of it. See if that doesn't make an anchor we can both hang on to.

I loiter on the corner of South Main out in front of the bank. I check my watch. Ben's late. Sunset is a rotten orange. Wildfires in Canada, the news said. 

Lodi is quiet. It's been about five years since I've been to the farm. Takes work to make it out there. Logistics of the heart. 

Pop's ancient truck comes rumbling around the corner of Portage Street, and for a sharp moment, I think he's driving it, but that moment passes in a flash of sunset across the windshield. Ben really does look like him now. He pulls the truck to a stop behind my car and greets me with a warm, sad smile. 

"Hey, Lou," he says, stepping out of the truck. He pulls me into a hug. 

I straighten out my suit after we part. "I can't believe that old thing still runs."

The truck is clean, painted a cheery mint green. I stay quiet too long. Ben is a doctor. Good bedside manners. He can read a patient.

"You OK, Lou?"

I lean back against my car and massage the bridge of my nose. I'm 37 years old. Lodi, Wisconsin. Here's where I've got to tell him everything. Ocean between us.

"I don't know how to keep things straight," I say. "How to talk about it."

"Well, we're talking right now," Ben says. He leans on my car next to me. "I'm your older brother. I'm also a damn good doctor with a valid script pad. What's ailing you?"

War. Total war. We split the atom and put our world on a map. Now all the beasts of the dark forest know. They know about me and you. 

"I feel like some mean bastard up there is hammering a wedge between us," I say. "And a different bruiser is whacking that wedge the other way." I shake my head. "I'm sorry. I'm all mixed up."

"I know," Ben says. There's something knowing in his eyes, and I realize part of him has always known about me. The fatigue he carries is the same as the nameless weight I cannot find words for. Maybe in a different language.

"You remember when we stole that?" I ask, pointing to the truck.

"We ran outta gas," Ben says. "Near some small town."

"Assumption." 

"Did we ever actually make it to Uncle Tomás? I can't recall."

"Not yet." 

Ben's back there again. Time to jump in.

"You remember what found us? That third thing."

An epiphany. Ben understands: We are each other's witness. Each other's constant, minted that day on the road to Assumption. He's right here next to me, finally.

"What did it say to you?"

"That everything is gonna be OK."

The bank door swings open, and a young woman steps out. The manager's secretary. She waves us over.

"If you can believe that."

Ben nods. He wipes a tear from his eye. He stands from the car, stuffs his hands in the pockets of his chore coat, and takes a few steps toward the bank. He stops. Turns back.

"Come to dinner tonight."

"Already there," I say.
entries.text_zh:
我37岁了，双手很冷。我渐渐知道接下来要面对什么了。

老爸死了，账得算清楚。我得跟本把所有事情都摊开来说，彻彻底底地谈。看看能不能找到个我俩都能抓住的的锚点。

我在南大街拐角的银行门口来回踱步，看了看表。本迟到了。夕阳西下，天空染上了一种腐烂般的橘色。新闻里说是加拿大的野火造成的。 

洛迪小镇静悄悄的。我已经快五年没回农场了。回去得费一番力气，心里头的后勤活可不好干。 

老爸那辆老掉牙的卡车从波蒂奇街拐角轰隆隆地开过来，有那么一刹那，我还以为是老爸在开车。但那念头随着夕阳在挡风玻璃上一闪就消散了。本现在长得可真像老爸。他把卡车停在我车后，带着一个温暖又有几分悲伤的微笑与我打招呼。 

“嘿，路，”他说着，从卡车上下来，把我拉进怀里。 

分开后，我理了理西装。“真不敢相信这车还能跑。”

卡车收拾得干干净净，还漆成了俏皮的薄荷绿。我沉默得太久了。本是个医生，擅长察言观色，能发觉不妥。

“你还好吗，路？”

我靠在车上，捏了捏鼻梁。我37岁了，在威斯康星州的洛迪。就在这里，我得把一切都告诉他。我们之间仿佛隔着汪洋大海。

“我不知道该怎么把事情理顺，”我说，“也不知道该怎么开口。”

“我们现在不就在说话嘛，”本说。他也靠在我车边上，“我是你哥哥，也是个挺不错的医生，还有合法的处方笺呢。你哪不舒服？”

战争，全面战争。我们将原子劈开，把我们的世界放到了地图上。现在黑暗森林里的所有猛兽都知道了。它们知道我，也知道你。 

“我感觉就像有个坏蛋在天上用楔子往我们中间砸，”我说，“还有个壮汉在另一边使劲敲那块楔子。”我摇了摇头，“对不起，我脑子乱成一团了。”

“我知道，”本说。他眼里有种洞悉的神色，而我意识到，他隐隐约约一直都知道我身上发生了什么。他身上的疲惫，跟我心里那团说不出的重负是一样的。也许在另一种语言里能说得清楚。

“你还记得我们偷这个出去吗？”我问，指了指那辆卡车。

“我们开到没油了，”本说，“在个小镇附近。”

“升天。” 

“我们最后到托马斯舅舅那里去了吗？我记不太清了。”

“还没有。” 

本的心思回到了当时。该跳进去了。

“你还记得找到我们的那个吗？那个别的什么东西。”

本突然明白了，我们是彼此的见证人，彼此的常数，那天在去升天镇的路上铸就的常数。他终于站到了此刻的我的身旁。

“它跟你说了什么？”

“说一切都会安妥。”

银行门开了，一个年轻女人走了出来，是经理的秘书。她朝我们招手，让我们过去。

“如果你相信的话。”

本点点头。他抹掉眼角的一滴泪，从车边站直身体，把手塞进工作外套的口袋，朝银行走了几步。他停下，回身。

“今晚来吃饭吧。”

“没问题，”我说。
